entities.name: Dagon
entities.description:
Dagon is a deity from Mesopotamian mythology who was incorporated into H. P. Lovecraft's fiction in the short story "Dagon", eventually becoming a prominent element of the Cthulhu Mythos, where he is often referred to as Father Dagon. In the stories of Lovecraft and others, he presides over the Deep Ones, a hidden amphibious humanoid race that resides in the Earth's oceans, and is worshipped by the Esoteric Order of Dagon, a secret cult based in Innsmouth. He is the consort of Mother Hydra.

In the real world, Dagon or Dagan was a deity worshipped in Mesopotamia, particularly in what is now Syria. He may have been connected with fertility or grain. He appears in the Hebrew Bible as a leading god of the Philistines, notably in Judges 16, where Samson brings down the temple of Dagon where he is being held captive. The similarity of Dagon to the Hebrew word dag ("fish") led to a depiction of the deity as half man, half fish, like a merman, and to a misconception in Western culture of Dagon as a kind of sea god.

In the Lovecraft story "Dagon," written in 1917, the narrator finds ancient carvings that depict humanoid creatures with webbed hands and bulging eyes, at least one of whom is almost as large as a whale. He then sees a similar creature like that in the flesh--a "vast, Polyphemus-like...monster of nightmares," with "gigantic scaly arms." The creature is never identified as Dagon in the story, though he does seek out a "celebrated ethnologist" to ask "peculiar questions regarding the ancient Philistine legend of Dagon, the Fish-God."

The people of Innsmouth in The Shadow Over Innsmouth worship at the Esoteric Order of Dagon, and according to Zadok Allen are required to take the three Oaths of Dagon. (Allen at one point rants about "Dagon an’ Ashtoreth—Belial an’ Beëlzebub—Golden Caff an’ the idols o’ Canaan an’ the Philistines.") The faithful in the order, Allen says, will not die but instead "go back to the Mother Hydra an’ Father Dagon what we all come from onct." To which he adds, "Iä! Cthulhu fhtagn!". Additionally, Robert Olmstead comes to believe that someday the Deep Ones will "rise again for the tribute Great Cthulhu craved [...] a city greater than Innsmouth next time". This suggests that Dagon functions as a deity in the Innsmouth community, but whether he is supposed to be a distinct entity or merely Cthulhu referred to with a biblical name is unclear.

entities.name: Devourer of the Dead
entities.description:
The Devourer of the Dead is an eldritch abomination from the fictional universe of Marvel by Marvel Comics.

The Devourer of the Dead is a monstrous abomination, which lived in the base of a giant pyramid in the Stygian city of Luxur during the Hyborian Age. It was encountered by Conan and his Zembabwean sorcerer ally Zula, whom were easily overpowered by the abomination. They lit their barge on fire, and sent it into the Devourer, while they escaped with the sarcophagus.

entities.name: Dho-spawn
entities.description:
The Dho-Spawn is a type of Great Old One created for the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

Dho-Spawn are the larval stages of the Great Old Ones, which are invisible and dwell in another dimension.

Category:Species Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Extra-Dimensional Species Category:Great Old Ones

entities.name: Dhumin
entities.description:
Dhumin is a fictional entity created by American author Beecher Smith for his short Cthulhu Mythos story "The Burrower From the Bluff."

Dhumin is hinted at by Chief Russell Two Bears as being a Great Old One, or perhaps a species of colossal worm unknown to modern science (see "Behind the Mythos," below). (: "The Burrower From the Bluff")

One description given by Chief Two Bears is of Native American legends telling of Dhumin being "the most terrible" of the Uktena, "a great snake of the underworld" with "antlers like a deer and wings like an eagle." These creatures are said to inhabit "the deep waters, high places, and caverns beneath the earth … bor[ing] like the earthworm, and travel[ling] freely between the land of the living… and of the dead." (: "The Burrower From the Bluff")

The entity has a dislike of the sun and light in general, although it is only stated to be truly afraid of fire. (: "The Burrower From the Bluff")

entities.name: Dygra
entities.description:
Dygra (also known as The Stone-Thing) is a fictional entity created by American author James Ambuehl for his 1997 short story "The Stalker in the Snows."

Virtually nothing is known of Dygra, other than it possesses a "body of living, jewel-facetted, semi-crystalline" material, "geodic tentacles," and a "glittering polychromatic maw." It has been depicted in the paintings of artist Thomas Jeffries disguising itself as a pile of gems in order to lure in its victims. (: "Correlated Contents")

entities.name: Dythalla
entities.description:
Dythalla, also known as the Lord of Lizards, is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by American author James Ambuehl for his 1985 poem "Dythalla".

Dythalla is a Great Old One that takes the form of a giant reptilian creature with a long serpentine mass of sucker-disced tentacles crowned around its head. Worshipped as a god in the ancient land of Altuas, a temple for worship was built in a courtyard west from the gates of Temme-Kiroth. The temple has an eighteen-foot-tall stone statue of Dythalla, with numerous lizards squirming and scurrying upon every inch of the floor.

During one of his conquests, a ruthless military despot called Parthias the Conqueror raided the temple, torturing and killing the priests on their altar. Further mocking and taunting their god, Parthias urinated on the statue of Dythalla; however, the foul-smelling stream was absorbed into the stone, causing the statue to glow a yellowish hue and transform into a living creature with flesh. Shortly afterwards, Dythalla chomped off Parthias' head, drenching his body in gore. (: "Lord of Lizards")

Category:Great Old Ones Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works

entities.name: Dzéwà
entities.description:
Dzéwà (The White God) is a fictional deity created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Insects from Shaggai".

Dzéwà is a ravenous plant-god that came from Xiclotl to Earth, feared and held in awe by the Shans. It appears as a great white orb hiding an enormous magenta excrescence, an orchid or lamprey mouth with emerald tentacles, tipped with hands emerging from the mass.

Category:Great Old Ones Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works

entities.name: Ei'lor
entities.description:
Ei'lor (also known as The Star-Seed) is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by American author James Ambuehl for his short story "The Star-Seed".

Dwelling in a vast cavern beneath a rural farming village in the United Kingdom, not much is known about the entity named Ei'lor, save for what is briefly mentioned in the occult texts collectively known as The Revelations of Gla'aki. What is known is that it shares many similarities with the Green God; both appear to be composed entirely of vegetable matter, are capable of extruding vine-like tentacles to capture their victims, and both offer some kind of perverse communion to their depraved cults. These two entities also inhabit subterranean lairs in the same region of England, the Severn Valley.

Ei'lor is known to have, via its seedlings, have infested the planet of Kr'llyand - located "near enigmatic Tond and revolving around the green sun of Yifne and the dead star of Baalblo" - with its monstrous growth. After viewing the paintings of one Thomas Jeffreys, Royceton University's Davis Rault fears that this may become the fate of Earth under the fertile attentions of Ei'lor. (: "Correlated Contents")

Ei'lor and its seed are also further discussed in the tome the Ei'lor Fronds. (: "The Star-Seed")

entities.name: Eihort
entities.description:
Eihort, also known as The Pale Beast, is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Franklyn Paragraphs".

Eihort is a huge, pale, gelatinous, oval-shaped monstrosity covered in myriads of eyes and supported by thousands of bony, fleshless legs.

Whenever Eihort encounters a human, it makes a bargain with them. If the human declines, Eihort kills the human. If the human accepts, Eihort implants an undeveloped brood into their body, which will kill the human host when it hatches. According to The Revelations of Glaaki, after the fall of humanity, Eihort's brood will be born into light and replace humanity.

entities.name: Erlik Khan
entities.description:
Erlik Khan is a fictional entity in the Marvel Universe, who first appeared in 1987 in issue #6 of the Strange Tales Vol 2 comic book series.

Erlik Khan is either a Great Old One or a Lesser Old One, who has five arms on each side, of which four pairs are of much smaller than the main pair. He is able to animate the dead, can cross dimensional barriers, and is able to teleport.

He was one of the agents of Shuma Gorath, the lord of the Great Old Ones.

Sometime in the past, the Ancient One was able to imprison him. During the late 20th century, upon the weakening of the mystical barriers protecting Earth, he sent his servants known the Khats to Earth, who then confronted Dr. Strange and his servant Wong.

entities.name: Ghadamon
entities.description:
Ghadamon is a character invented for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game.

Ghadamon is described as being a bluish-brown larval Great Old One made of slime that lives in the stagnant Underworld Sterile Lake east of the Fungus Forest with a colony of its minions. A series of deformed heads can be seen floating and peering from within its form. Its long tentacles give it limited movement over ground by pulling itself along on nearby objects. It emits and absorbs a mix of noxious gas and slime through an ever shifting cycle of pustules and orifices.

Despite having no established cult, its attempted incursion into the waking world was supported by the Deep Ones. It is referenced in the Book of Eibon as a creature "...spawned on the flesh of human brains and secreted beneath a great lake in a fearsome world of darkness where it would lie for eternal ages, feeding, growing, and waiting. This man did claim that Ghadamon is coming and coming soon."

The grimoire of an unnamed sorceress prophesied that in the lake "...Ghadamon shall lie until one shall come for him and Ghadamon shall pass into another realm and there take his place beneath the sea, to grow and wait for the Day. On this day He Who Waits to Spawn will leave his nest and find his terrible cold mate who has awaited him forever. These days, when the Beast shall rampage and dark R'lyeh rise from its watery crypt will see the passage of great Cthulhu..."
entities.short_description: Ghadamon is a character invented for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game.

entities.name: Ghatanothoa
entities.description:
Ghatanothoa (also known as The Dark God) is a fictional entity in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character first appeared in the 1935 short story "Out of the Aeons", ghostwritten by H. P. Lovecraft for Hazel Heald.

In Lovecraft's original story, Ghatanothoa is depicted as a gigantic abomination whose appearance is so hideous that anyone who gazes upon it or its image is petrified into a living mummy. The monster is described as a "hellish god or patron daemon" brought to Earth in prehistoric times by aliens from Yuggoth (identified elsewhere as the home planet of the Mi-Go). They built a colossal fortress atop the mountain Yaddith-Gho in K'naa in the lost continent of Mu, and sealed Ghatanothoa below it beneath a vast trapdoor. When humans arose after the departure of the aliens, they too worshipped the monster out of fear of its frightful power, offering it sacrifices lest it emerge from its crypt and wreak havoc.

Though Ghatanothoa is said to be indescribable, it appears to combine aspects of an octopus and an elephant, and to be both scaly and wrinkled while remaining amorphous.

Victims of Ghatanothoa are permanently immobilized, their skin taking on the consistency of leather; their internal organs are preserved indefinitely, with the brain remaining fully aware. Only the destruction of the subject's brain or the application of a magic scroll can free it from its hellish prison, though the unfortunate is likely to be incurably insane long before the welcomed release.

entities.name: Ghizguth
entities.description:
Hziulquoigmnzhah (sibling) Tsathoggua (offspring)

Ghizguth (The Sound in the Deep Waters) is a fictional entity in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character first appeared in Clark Ashton Smith's family tree of Azathoth ("Genealogical Chart of the Elder Gods").

Ghizguth is one of the Great Old Ones. According to the Parchments of Pnom (Pnom being the chief Hyperborean genealogist as well as a noted prophet), he is a male spawn of Cxaxukluth and the brother of Hziulquoigmnzhah and Tulu. He is also the mate of Zstylzhemghi and the father of Tsathoggua. (: Selected Letters of Clark Ashton Smith)

For a long time, he lived alongside his family on Yuggoth, where he was revered by the Mi-Go (: "The Appeasement of Ghizguth"). However, at an unspecified point in time, they were discovered by his father, Cxaxukluth, who would eventually devour Zstylzhemghi (: "October Surprise").

entities.name: Gi-Hoveg
entities.description:
Gi-Hoveg is a fictional cosmic entity created by James Ambuehl for his Lu-Kthu Cycle.

Ambuehl classifies Gi-Hoveg as a Great Old One in "The Advent of Uvhash", and as an Outer God in "The Stalker in the Snows".

Known as the Aether-Anemone, Gi-Hoveg is a giant spherical being with spongy flesh and spikes protruding from its body, as well as numerous eyes set between its spikes. It is the arch rival of Uvhash, the Blood-Mad God of the Void. (: "The Advent of Uvhash")

Nobody knows where Gi-Hoveg dwells, but some believe "he exists everywhere". (: "The Stalker in the Snows")

entities.name: Glaaki
entities.description:
Glaaki, sometimes spelled Gla'aki, is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Inhabitant of the Lake". It is known to dwell in a lake near the fictional town of Brichester, in the Severn Valley, located in the West Midlands of England.

As old as the stars themselves, Glaaki has a vast reservoir of knowledge, not only of the supernatural entities that exist on Earth, but of those which predate it. Whilst he is aquatic in nature, in his physical form Glaaki resembles nothing so much as an enormous slug with slender spines which appear to be made of matte metal, but which are in fact organic in nature. These quills can inject a substance to ensure its victims' compliance. Those skewered in such a way are granted Glaaki's gift of everlasting life, albeit as an undead puppet. In addition, it is capable of forming tentacles tipped with eyes, so as to keep its true nature hidden whilst observing the world from beneath the water's surface.

Interestingly, although Glaaki is believed to have landed on Earth in the Severn Valley, sightings of it have been reported from many other bodies of water across the globe. How Glaaki is able to achieve this is unknown.

Glaaki's cult, a group of depraved humans both mortal and undead, wrote a series of scriptures known as The Revelations of Glaaki. What these writings contain is for the most part unknown, though it cannot be anything good.

entities.name: Gleeth
entities.description:
Gleeth is an eyeless and deaf lunar entity and is worshipped by the residents of the ancient continent of Theem'hdra as well as in the Dreamlands. He is very similar to Mnomquah, though they are not related.

Category:Great Old Ones Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works

entities.name: Gloon
entities.description:
Gloon, the Corrupter of Flesh, Master of the Temple, is a fictional deity created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The Temple".

Gloon is described as great limacene or slug-like abomination, though it usually hides its true nature through the glamour of a beautiful statue resembling the Greek god Dionysus.

In "The Temple," the crew of a World War I German submarine come into possession of a statue of a deity, which proceeds to drive most of the crew insane before dragging the sole survivor, the submarine's captain, down to the entity's temple on the ocean floor.

Later authors expanded that this deity was a Lesser Outer God (or Other God) named Gloon, who has been imprisoned in his temple, made of dark basalt, since long before the sinking of Atlantis, and supposedly has no purpose other than to cause pain and suffering. There he serves as guardian of a dimensional gate. Accompanying him in the temple are the servants of Gloon, who, unlike him, can leave its confines. There are also statuettes of Gloon (such as the one found by the German crew), depicting him as a nude man adorned with a laurel wreath atop his head, reminiscent of Ancient Greek art. These statuettes inflinct terrible dreams of the the temple in which Gloon resides upon whoever touches them. Eventually, Gloon gleefully sucks their soul into the statuette and then feeds on the soul, delighted in the agony which he causes. (: "The City in the Sea," G. W. Thomas & Lynn Willis, The Encyclopedia Cthulhiana)

entities.name: Gobogeg
entities.description:
Gobogeg, the Twice-Invoked, also known as The Moon-Ladder in one the visions seen by Danforth (: At the Mountains of Madness) is a powerful Great Old One that appears as a colossal pillar of amorphous alien flesh, with a cyclopean head or eye in the center. (: Cthulhu Wars: Great Old One Pack Three)

When summoned in, the deity immediately causes a powerful quake that can be felt throughout the entirety of a country or even continent that it is summoned in.

To make matters worse, once it is summoned Gobogeg literally drags up the entire continent as it ascends upwards, consequently causing the entire world to cave-in on itself. (: Cthulhu Wars: Great Old One Pack Three)

It was Sandy Peterson who greatly expanded on the very vague mention of "moon-ladder" and other visions in H. P. Lovecraft's writings.

entities.name: God of the Red Flux
entities.description:
The God of the Red Flux is a fictional entity created by the late American author Donald Wandrei. It made its first appearance in his 1932 short story "The Tree-Men of M'bwa", later incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by the role-playing game supplement Malleus Monstrorum.

The God of the Red Flux, a.k.a. the Master, is an alien creature from another dimension that came to Earth from the stars in the days before Atlantis. It dwells in a valley within a ring-shaped hill beyond the Mountains of the Moon in Central Africa, between the Congo river and Uganda, its territory shunned by animals and humans alike. The Red Flux, or Whirling Flux, that envelops it, is a "reddish metal structure", possibly a spaceship, which appears to change shape constantly, alternating between a pyramid, obelisk and sphere.

The God of the Red Flux is a mysterious creature with unknown motivations and the power to reanimate the dead. It is served by the virtually indestructible undead M'bwa, whose main task is to gather human victims to be forcibly transformed into vegetable-like beings known as the Tree-Men of M'bwa. If M'bwa is incapacitated (such as by being decapitated), the Master will step outside the Red Flux just long enough to revive him, then return to its whirling abode. One witness who saw it described it as a "titanic lich" with "tatters of vaporous flesh" and "flapping black streamers that whipped from it as it towered to the skies above". (: "The Tree-Men of M'bwa")

entities.name: Gods of Ragnarok
entities.description:
The Gods of Ragnarok are extradimensional entities created by the BBC in 1988 for Doctor Who. They were later identified as Great Old Ones by the Doctor (: All-Consuming Fire).

The Gods of Ragnarok are a trio of Great Old Ones who appear to sentient beings as stone statues. They are entertained by the suffering of others. The Time Lord Rassilon was the one who named them Raag (Father Ragnarok), Nah (Mother Ragnarok), and Rok (Little Girl). He theorized that they created and destroyed numerous universes, even destroying their own. The Gods of Ragnarok kidnap those with individuality and imagination, and force them to entertain them endlessly, demanding bigger and better acts each time. They can fire thunderbolts and create rain, reanimate the dead, manifest simultaneously in different time-phases, and reduce their victims to ashes in a clash of thunder and blinding light.

"Ragnarok" from Old Norse literally means "Reign Wreck", the wrecking of the reign of a king or more broadly in a cosmic sense the destruction of cosmic order and the bringing of utter chaos and ruin.

entities.name: Gog-Hoor
entities.description:
Gog-Hoor (Eater of the Insane) is a fictional entity created by Weston Ochse for his short story "A Spectacle of a Man". The character was later incorporated into the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

Gog-Hoor is a Great Old One that lives in a reverse dimension and can only be visible to humans through reflective surfaces, including puddles of water and mirrors. It is described as being a monster with a bullet-shaped head attached to a body that is inconceivably huge, presumably infinite in size. Gog-Hoor feeds on humans with mental disorders, using its numerous tentacles to drag them into its own dimension and devour their souls. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

entities.name: Gol-goroth
entities.description:
Gol-goroth (The Forgotten Old One) is a fictional deity created by Robert E. Howard for his Cthulhu Mythos stories, and later incorporated into the tales of Lin Carter as a Great Old One. He is first mentioned in Howard's "The Children of the Night", where Professor Kirowan refers to "nameless and ghastly gods and entities as Cthulhu, Yog Sothoth, Tsathoggua, Gol-goroth, and the like." Howard explores the idea further in "The Gods of Bal-Sagoth", where Gol-Gororth is preeminent among the titular entities.

Gol-goroth appears as a titanic, black toad-like monstrosity with an impossibly malevolent glare, or a tentacle covered, scaly, bat-winged entity. However, its physical form may alter to fit the worst nightmares of whoever is viewing it (spider-like to an arachnophobic person, etc.). (: "Dagon Manor")

It is a dark god of Bal-Sagoth (: "The Gods of Bal-Sagoth") and Hyboria, with some modern cults centering around Britain (: "Dagon Manor") and might also be named as the god of the Black Stone in Hungary (: Ye Booke of Monstres), although other sources have challenged this claim (: Ye Booke of Monstres II). It may have been worshipped in Atlantis under the name Golgor in connection with other Atlantean deities such as Valka, Hotah, and Honen (: "The Moon of Skulls").

In the first printing of "The Fishers from Outside", by Lin Carter, Gol-goroth is mentioned in the Book of Eibon as dwelling under Mount Antarktos, at the South Pole, and being the master of the Fishers from Outside (which Carter equates with the Shantaks). However, this has been rectified in more recent printings, as Carter intended to refer to Groth-Golka, not Gol-goroth, having simply confused the names of the two deities.

entities.name: Grace
entities.description:
The Grace are Great Old Ones from the fictional universe of Doctor Who by Big Finish Productions.

The Grace are a benevolent group of Great Old Ones who created the Key to Time. The Black and White Guardians are their agents. They exist outside of time and space, in a state of non-existence. This collective works at keeping the universe together, and when necessary enters reality to prevent its collapse. Beings which are too big to enter normal time and space, the Doctor imagined them as "big, peaceful, pan-dimensional creatures with enormous power". They are in fact entities who can stop time for brief periods and crush the Doctor with a thought. (: The Chaos Pool)

In their native realm, the Grace appear as impish boneless creatures. (: The Prisoner's Dilemma)

Despite their association with the Mythos as putative Great Old Ones, their goodness puts them at odds with the cosmicism of Lovecraft and aligns them more with the benevolent Elder Gods of the Derleth version of the Mythos.

entities.name: Great Intelligence
entities.description:
The Great Intelligence is a fictional cosmic entity created for the science fiction TV series Doctor Who in the 1967 serial The Abominable Snowmen. Some sources in the Doctor Who expanded universe equate this entity with Yog-Sothoth. (: All-Consuming Fire, Millennial Rites)

The Great Intelligence is a malevolent disembodied intelligence perhaps originating from another dimension or universe, although in its original appearances it is explicitly extraterrestrial in origin, "floating about in space". It can take over the bodies of humans and manifest itself as a web-like material. Although its exact motivations are unclear, it desires to conquer Earth, and has employed armies of Robot Yeti to try to subjugate humanity. These robots contain metallic spheres inside their bodies, which provide a direct link to the mind of the Intelligence.

The physical manifestation of the Great Intelligence in our universe (outside of its Robot Yeti and the people whose minds have been possessed by it) usually takes the form of a web-like substance that can be generated on land, sky, or outer space, and is even capable of immobilising a Time Lord's TARDIS in mid-flight. This web also seems to have the biological properties of a fungus.

Additionally, the Great Intelligence can also manifest itself as a slime-like fluid, a dense fog that can engulf and absorb victims, or even as information in a computer network. (: The Abominable Snowmen, The Web of Fear, Downtime)

entities.name: Great Old One
entities.description:
The Great Old Ones are a group of unique, malignant beings of great power in the fictional cosmology of the Cthulhu Mythos. Cthulhu, H. P. Lovecraft's famous creation, is described as a Great Old One. They reside in various locations on Earth, and once presided over the planet as gods and rulers.

Lovecraft uses the phrase "Great Old Ones" in just two of his stories. Unlike his successors, Lovecraft uses the term to refer to the races later writers would identify as the Cthulhi and the Elder Things, not to his pantheon of alien gods.

In "The Call of Cthulhu," it's how the captured Cthulhu cultists refer to the entities they worship:

More information on the Great Old Ones comes from Old Castro, one of the few sane members of the cult:

entities.name: Green God
entities.description:
The Green God is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Horror Under Warrendown" (although it is unnamed), and later incorporated into the Call of Cthulhu horror role-playing game. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

Residing in the underground labyrinth beneath Warrendown in the Severn Valley of England, the Green God appears as a giant statue of a head, similar to those found on Easter Island; however, it is composed entirely of vegetable matter and is capable of extruding lengthy vine-like appendages which it uses to ensnare potential victims or to offer communion to the degenerate cult of mutants who worship it.

An unusual feature of the Green God is its ability to transmute those who eat its flesh. Any who consume the vegetable matter which forms its body will slowly transform into a disgusting, rabbit-like creature, whose sole purpose is to expand the Horror's cult by offering seemingly-innocent vegetables to normal humans, in turn changing them into one of their own.

entities.name: Groth-Golka
entities.description:
Groth-Golka is a fictional creature created by Robert E. Howard for his story "The Gods of Bal-Sagoth", originally depicted as being a giant flightless bird worshipped as a deity. In the expanded Cthulhu Mythos, Lin Carter identified it as a Great Old One and the lord of the Fishers from Outside, although in a case of mistaken identity, the first printing of "The Fishers from Outside" featured Gol-goroth in the place of Groth-Golka.

It has subsequently appeared in the Conan stories of Marvel Comics, and as a monster in the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game. It is sometimes represented as resembling a pterosaur.

In its debut story, Groth-Golka was identified as the last member of a species of prehistoric bird, who has lived for centuries and is worshiped as a god by the people of Bal-Sagoth. The creature's mortality, however, is demonstrated by its death at the hands of the protagonists. (: "The Gods of Bal-Sagoth")

However, in Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, Groth-Golka is now said to reside beneath Antarctica, indicating that it is still alive. Furthermore, one theory adds the interpretation that Groth-Golka and Mnomquah are brothers. (: Malleus Monstrorum: Cthulhu Mythos Bestiary Volume II)

The Guardians of Time, are a group of Great Old Ones whom are masters of reality. Elemental forces which embody various aspects of the cosmos. It's a pantheon within a pantheon, the upper echelon of the Great Old Ones. Though at the top of their hierarchy, in some matters they defer to the Greater Old Ones.

entities.description:
Gurathnaka (also known as the Eater of Dreams or Shadow of the Night) is a fictional entity created by Matthew Grau for the role-playing game CthulhuTech.

Gurathnaka is a Great Old One who appears to be a shadowy, incorporeal entity dwelling in the Dreamlands. It is unknown if Gurathnaka ever had a bodily form, as it exists beyond the wall of sleep in dimensions beyond the physical world, only interacting with the corporeal plane through shadows. Many learned occultists have used bright lights to protect themselves from Gurathnaka's shadows, and the few mortals who worship the entity have lost their sanity while dwelling in the shadows of society. (: CthulhuTech Chapter Fourteen "Parting the Veil")

Gwarloth is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by James A. Gruetzmacher for his 1998 poem "Star Pods".

Gwarloth is a tentacled amoebic horror with multiple hideous eyes, orifices, and a dangling gland forming a cyclopean face. Slithering in the starpools of slime, Gwarloth seeks out innocent victims, devouring unwary souls and supplying nourishment for its hunger. (: "Star Pods")

entities.name: Hastalyk
entities.description:
Hastalÿk is a Great Old One in the Cthulhu Mythos. Its only appearance is in Chaosium's supplement Malleus Monstrorum for their Call of Cthulhu RPG.

Hastalÿk is a gestalt entity composed of millions of microbial parts. It sweeps from planet to planet, amplifying and altering existing contagions as well as causing cellular mutations. It is neither a disease nor carry any disease, but a "mutating force" that forces native species to mutate uncontrollably, enabling diseases to spread throughout the planet.

Humans who caught a disease mutated by Hastalÿk may experience delusional fevers or fevered visions and dreams about other cosmic horrors. In rare cases, their body and voice may be possessed and controlled by Hastalÿk or another Old One.

Not much fact is known about Hastalÿk, only conjectures from scholars and scientists. Whether the mutation and spreading of disease are its goal or only side effects of its presence, as well as whether it moves throughout the galaxy or actually spreads itself on all worlds while remaining dormant on most, are highly contentious. A few scholars even suggest that Hastalÿk's consciousness may be active in many locations at once with varying scopes, thereby causing either global or only local outbreaks.

Hastur the Unspeakable is a cosmic entity in the Cthulhu Mythos. Although the being is associated with H. P. Lovecraft, it is only mentioned in one of his novellas, The Whisperer in Darkness. It was originally the creation of Ambrose Bierce, whose short story "Haïta the Shepherd" describes Hastur as a god of shepherds. Hastur is the name of a city in the Robert W. Chambers short stories "The Yellow Sign" and "The Repairer of Reputations", which appeared in his short story collection The King in Yellow.

Hastur is imprisoned by the Elder Gods in the Lake of Hali, on the shores of Carcosa, a city on Aldebaran. (: "The Lair of the Star-Spawn")

Hastur is the god of the Air element, and the leader of the Air elementals. ("The Cthulhu Mythology: A Glossary" [Francis Towner Laney])

entities.description:
Hecuba is a Great Old One created by Big Finish Productions in 2013 for Doctor Who.

Hecuba is the sister of the Celestial Toymaker who ensnares sentient beings in time related games forcing them to stake their freedom on the outcome.

She has powers similar to the Celestial Toymaker's and appears as a very beautiful woman in a luxurious ballgown. A giant timepiece, the Grand Chronometer, which can manipulate time, stabilizes her pocket universe. She is coy and flirtatious, but takes her amusement from the pain and fear of her victims.

entities.description:
Huitloxopetl is a fictional entity created for the round-robin story to which it lends its name.

Huitloxopetl is the false lure or trickster. It is described as an angel who lures dead souls into its realm (The False Haven). The souls believe they are lead to the afterlife, but they face a horrible truth, and that is a pit of utter darkness. His true form is a demon with four tentacles, horns, wings, goat-like legs, and a head.

In the pit lies the unknown who hungers for souls.

entities.name: Hydra
entities.description:
The Hydra is a fictional creature created by American author Henry Kuttner for his short story "Hydra".

An extra-dimensional deity which feeds on the life essence of its victims, the Hydra requires a portal to be opened to enter universes other than its own; at least as far as the human race is concerned, it utilises cultists who lay honey-traps which grant the ability to project one's astral self. Once the ritual is enacted and the person has projected, a gateway to the Hydra's realm is opened, allowing it to enter our universe and claim its victim, which it does by beheading some poor unfortunate. This person's consciousness is then held in eternal torment whilst the Hydra takes its sustenance from him. The Hydra appears to dwell in the same plane of existence as the slumbering Outer God Azathoth.

Hydra would later be incorporated into Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu role-playing game, where it has been described as a Great Old One (: Malleus Monstrorum) or a minor Outer God (: Cthulhu Handbook [Hiroshi Yamamoto]).

entities.name: Icthultu
entities.description:
Icthultu is an extra-dimensional entity from the fictional universe of the Justice League animated series by DC Comics.

Thousands of years ago, Icthultu once ruled over Thanagar, where the people of that planet worshiped him as their god. Icthultu helped build the foundations of their entire culture including its agriculture, mathematics and philosophy. However, they eventually grew tired of their many sacrifices to Icthultu and stopped worshipping him. Afterwards, Icthultu and the other Old Ones invaded the Earth, nearly wiping out all of humanity before King Poseidon banished them to their home dimension at the cost of sinking the city of Atlantis in the process.

In the present day, Icthultu attempted to invade the Earth again. While Doctor Fate, Aquaman and Soloman Grundy performed a ritual that would prevent Icthultu's return, it was interrupted by the Justice League, causing Icthultu to nearly escape from his dimensional prison. With Icthultu's banishment only being temporary, the Justice League decided to enter his dimension to fight the threat head-on. Icthultu was eventually defeated when Hawkgirl and Soloman Grundy attacked him from the inside of his body, destroying his brain. (: "The Terror Beyond")

The show writers originally intended to use Cthulhu but were under the impression that the character wasn't in the public domain, hence creating their own pastiche.

entities.name: Idh-yaa
entities.description:
Idh-yaa, The Mighty Mother, is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Lin Carter for his short story "Out of the Ages"

Idh-yaa is a deity who gave birth to the Star-Spawn of Cthulhu on a planet in the Xoth Star system, after mating with Cthulhu. She specifically produced the sons of Cthulhu: Ghatanothoa, Ythogtha, and Zoth-Ommog; and a daughter of Cthulhu: Cthylla. Also once called Quum-yaa.

entities.name: Iku-Turso
entities.description:
Iku-Turso is a fictional sea monster, who is deeply rooted in Finnish mythology, most famously appearing in Elias Lönnrot's epic poem the Kalevala. Mikael Agricola, a Lutheran clergyman and de facto founder of literary Finnish, listed Iku-Turso as god of war, while others have tied him to pestilence.

Iku-Turso was later incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by Finnish writer Tuomas Saloranta for his 2012 short story "Mahtavat Ammoiset" (Finnish for "Great Old Ones"). The entity is said to reside somewhere in the waters of Finland.

Iku-Turso was a Great Old One who ruled over the areas of Finland, until he, alongside Kalanpäinen and the other Old Ones, were sung into the swamps by Finnish sages and poets, who had learned these abilities from the Sámi people. Only myths and some of the Deep Ones remained in the country.

Around the 1930s, author Matts W. Cornelius, who was a correspondent of H. P. Lovecraft, wrote stories in which he compared Iku-Turso with the Great Old One Cthulhu.

entities.name: Iod
entities.description:
Iod is a Great Old One in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by the late American author Henry Kuttner for his short story "The Secret of Kralitz", and was later incorporated into Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

The first mention of Iod appears in Kuttner's "The Secret of Kralitz," when Franz Kralitz is learning eldritch lore from his ancestors: "I learned, too, of the unbelievable manner in which Iod, the Source, is worshiped beyond the outer galaxies."

In "The Invaders" (1939), Hayward's experiment teach him that "the first human race dwelt in primal Mu, worshiping strange, forgotten gods"—including "Iod the Shining Hunter."

The most extensive discussion of Iod comes in Kuttner's "The Hunt" (1939), in which the wizard Will Benson "call[s] up an entity which mankind worshiped eons ago as—Iod. Iod, the Hunter":Man had worshiped Iod in older days, under other names. He was one of the oldest gods, and he had come to Earth, the tale went, in pre-human eons when the old gods soared between the stars, and earth was a stopping place for incredible voyagers. The Greeks knew him as Torphonios; the Etruscans made nameless sacrifices diurnally to Vediovis, the Dweller beyond Phlegethon, the River of Flame.

entities.name: Istasha
entities.description:
Istasha is a fictional entity created by American author James Ambuehl for his 1990 Cthulhu Mythos poem "Where Walks Istasha". She is also mentioned in the 1997 short story "The Stalker in the Snows", which identifies her as a Great Old One.

A cat deity similar to Bast but more vicious, Istasha came to Earth long before the rise of humankind, and is worshiped by her Children in the Halls of Ulthar. Her sister is the sylvan Lythalia. (: "Where Walks Istasha", "The Stalker in the Snows")

entities.name: Ithaqua
entities.description:
Ithaqua, also known as the Wind-Walker or the Wendigo, is a fictional entity in the Cthulhu Mythos. The titular creature debuted in August Derleth's short story "The Thing That Walked on the Wind", which was inspired by Algernon Blackwood's 1910 tale The Wendigo.

Ithaqua is one of the Great Old Ones and appears as a horrifying giant with a roughly human shape and glowing red eyes. He has been reported from as far north as the Arctic to the Sub-Arctic, where Native Americans first encountered him. He is believed to prowl the Arctic waste, hunting down unwary travelers and slaying them in a gruesome fashion. He is believed to have inspired the Native American legend of the Wendigo and possibly the Yeti.

Ithaqua's cult is small, but he is greatly feared in the far north. Fearful denizens of Siberia, Canada, and Alaska often leave sacrifices for Ithaqua; not as worship but as appeasement. Those who join his cult are granted immunity to extremely cold temperatures. He often uses Shantaks, a colossal avian "lesser race", as servitors.

Derleth classified Ithaqua as an elemental of air, alongside Hastur, Zhar and Lloigor. However, in at least one of the many conflicts among the Great Old Ones, Ithaqua seems to have sided with Cthulhu against Hastur and Cthugha. (: "The Black Island")

entities.name: Jabberwocky
entities.description:
The Jabberwocky (also known as the Jabberwock) is a fictional creature created by Lewis Carroll for his nonsense poem "Jabberwocky", which was first published in his 1871 novel Through the Looking-Glass.

Zenescope Entertainment later reimagined the Jabberwocky as an Old One for their fictional multiverse, making its first appearance in issue #16 of Grimm Fairy Tales Vol 1.

During the Age of Chaos, a war raged for control of all the realities which threatened to tear the multiverse apart. The Keepers defeated the Old Ones, who were put into a slumber and imprisoned for eternity. Only the youngest of the Old Ones was spared, a child who was placed in the Realm of Dreams. Its real name was unpronounceable, but it became known as the Jabberwocky. It was hoped that it would be cleansed of its evil by the realm of dreams and wonder. They miscalculated and it grew up evil, and eventually doom came to Wonderland, as it twisted the Realm of Dreams into its demented playground, turning it into the Realm of Nightmares. (: Call of Wonderland)

The Jabberwocky has its eyes on Earth, desiring to spread its madness to that world. To prevent this, cults have been offering human sacrifices to the Jabberywocky, children whom are given to him and transformed by Wonderland. Its madness still seeps into the Earth resulting in various atrocities, from serial killers to wars, although refusal to sacrifice a child will cause worse things to happen. In the early 20th century, one father refused to sacrifice his child, and the influence of Wonderland increased on Earth, resulting in the Great Depression and World War Two (: Return to Wonderland). The Jabberwocky has great physical and magical powers, including being able to transform others and make itself as large as a skyscraper, 102 stories high. (: Grimm Fairy Tales)

entities.name: Janai'ngo
entities.description:
Janai'ngo is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Crispin Burnham and Edward P. Berglund for their short story "The Thing in the Library".

Janai'ngo is a crustacean-like, tentacled, half-amorphous marine horror which serves Cthulhu, dwelling in the depths of the Bay of Rhiiklu, somewhere within the eastern coast of the United States.

Janai'ngo can only be summoned on All Hallow's Eve at the stroke of midnight, if a female virgin is sacrificed while placed on an altar outside the great circle enclosing the pentagram. The entity will manifest from the pentagram using the incantation "Iä! Iä! Janai'ngo! Janai'ngo! Mylrtn yh igpstn y'rgo syh'v gt zn drak'lu smr zn dral'ku smr Rhiiklu! Janai'ngo! Janai'ngo! Ai! Ai!" as the sacrifice's blood starts pouring out. The practitioner can contain Janai'ngo for half an hour. Once the time is up, the practitioner must chant "Iä! Janai'ngo! Mylrtn ys igpstn y'rgo dnlq gt zn drak'lu smr Rhiiklu! I command thee!", in order to send Janai'ngo back to his watery dwelling place. (: "The Thing in the Library")

entities.name: Juk-Shabb
entities.description:
Juk-Shabb (also known as God of Yekub) is a fictional entity in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character first appeared in the short story "The Challenge from Beyond", written by H. P. Lovecraft, Frank Belknap Long, Robert E. Howard, C. L. Moore, and Abraham Merritt.

Juk-Shabb is a Great Old One who appears as a huge shining ball of sentient energy, which communicates by changing color and using telepathy. The being is a powerful psionic and has extensive knowledge of magic. Among the Great Old Ones, it is one of the least malevolent.

entities.name: Kalanpäinen
entities.description:
Kalanpäinen is a fictional Great Old One connected with Finland, created by the Finnish writer Tuomas Saloranta for his 2012 short story "Mahtavat Ammoiset" (Finnish for "Great Old Ones"). The author Matts W. Cornelius, a character in the story, compares Kalanpäinen to Dagon (Kalanpäinen means "fish-head" or "fish-headed" in Finnish).

Kalanpäinen was a Great Old One who ruled over the area of Finland, until he, alongside Iku-Turso and the other Old Ones, were sung into the swamps by Finnish sages and poets, who had learned these abilities from the Sámi people. Only myths--and some of the Deep Ones--remained in the country.

Around the 1930's, author Matts W. Cornelius, a correspondent of H. P. Lovecraft, wrote stories that compared Kalanpäinen with the Great Old One Dagon.

The Deep Ones, especially those who live in Lauttasaari, still seek to awaken Kalanpäinen and the Old Ones so they can reclaim the world. (: "Mahtavat Ammoiset")

entities.name: Kassogtha
entities.description:
Kassogtha is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Joseph S. Pulver, Sr. for his 1999 novel Nightmare's Disciple. She is depicted as Cthulhu's sister and mate, and the mother of Nctosa and Nctolhu, who takes the form of a writhing mass of tentacles.

According to some sources, Kassogtha shares some relationship with Great Cthulhu, with more than one tome speaking of these deities creating or unifying to form or breed the known entities Nctosa and Nctolhu. One reference suggests Kassogtha and Cthulhu are "sister" and "brother" (if such terms are applicable). However, the former has no known association with Xoth, said to be the originating planet of Cthulhu and its kin.

This Old One seems to be more like some cosmic parasite, able to merge or join with other significant entities for periods of time, and thereby cause the creation or birth of an "offspring." Thus, at times, Kassogtha disappears (presumably while inhabiting or merging with another being), giving rise to the general opinion that this Old One is rarely heard of or encountered in Mythos lore. For some, this parasitical behavior posits the notion that this deity is characteristically like a disease, and possibly one unwelcomed by the entities it "preys" on. Indeed, Jedediah Pullington, in his "Visions of Crystal and Blasphemy" (New York, 1889), recounts a drug-induced vision where he witnessed the merging of Cthulhu with Kassogtha, which he describes as "tortuous" and "near lethal" and how it took all of Cthulhu's strength to throw off or cast out the other. If something can give such a report credence, it does support the idea of an invading entity, perhaps drawing off some form of sustenance to enable it to create new or altered life.

When not bound with another entity, Kassogtha appears to dwell in a great body of water (or some other liquid matter), poisoned by its presence. A strong association with disease seems evident, amplified by reports of the illnesses suffered by those in the areas where this Old One has manifested. For many scholars, Kassogtha is like a "cosmic sickness" that seeps into life, corrupting and mutating it in foul ways.

entities.description:
Kathulos of the Eternal Lives, the Living Planet ---- Kathulos the Slave-Seer

Kathulos was a fictional character by Marvel Comics and first appeared in Marvel Premiere #8 (May, 1973), written by Gardner Fox and Jim Starlin. Kathulos was also named Kulthas.

Both names were created by Robert E. Howard: The Atlantean sorcerer Kathulos (: "Skull-Face") and the evil deity Kulthas (: "The Curse of the Golden Skull"). Kulthas was invoked in Marvel Comics' Conan stories.

"L'mur-Kathulos" was also listed along with various eldritch entities and locations (: "The Whisperer in Darkness")

entities.name: Klosmiebhyx
entities.description:
Klosmiebhyx is a fictional entity created by Kevin L. O'Brien for his short story "October Surprise".

Klosmiebhyx is the daughter of Cxaxukluth and sister of Zstylzhemghi, Ghizguth and Hzioulquoigmnzhah. Born in a black star in the center of a grand nebula, she travelled with Cxaxukluth and most of her relations to Yuggoth. While there, she and Hzioulquoigmnzhah produced Ysbaddaden and Scathach. (: "October Surprise")

entities.description:
Tsathoggua (cousin) Yog-Sothoth (cousin)|affiliations=Great Old Ones}}

Krang is a fictional entity created by the late American author and H. P. Lovecraft contemporary R. H. Barlow for his 1934 short story "The Tomb of the God".

A monstrous brown, leathery, alien entity, which came to the planet Antanôk when dark magical powers battled for possession of the universe, Krang once slumbered within a gigantic mausoleum lost in the desert-wastes. When the men of Phoor opened this tomb, Krang awakened and ate them. (: "The Tomb of the God") It is said that Krang then joined his cousins, Cthulhu, Yog-Sothoth and Tsathoggua in the star-spaces. (: "The City in the Desert")

At one point Krang encountered and hid from a greater god, Tsathoggua. (: "The Deplorable Voyage") Category:Characters Originating From Lovecraft Circle Works Category:Other Supernatural Beings Category:Great Old Ones

entities.name: Kukulkan
entities.description:
Kukulkan, also written K'uk'ulkan, is the feathered serpent creator god of ancient Maya mythology.

He is believed to embody the sky, wind and rain and provides the energy to sustain life.

The name Kukulkan is formed from the Mayan language words feathered (k'uk'ul) and serpent (kan).

In the Cthulhu Mythos, Kukulkan is considered to be another name for Yig.

entities.name: Kulalu
entities.description:
Kulalu is a fictional entity created by The Asylum for their kaiju film Ape X Mecha Ape: New World Order. The character was inspired by Cthulhu in terms of its name and characterization.

Kulalu is one of the Great Old Ones, a race of extraterrestrial entities who are known to be world destroyers. Millions of years ago, the first specimen of its kind arrived on Earth in a chrysalis, which was thought to be the meteor that killed the dinosaurs, before being awoken and causing the fifth mass extinction event. The substance known as "Sample 7" is actually the blood of Kulalu, with exposure to it causing other lifeforms to experience accelerated growth.

The Johnson Space Center made contact with Kulalu during a mission where they launched a space capsule containing a chimpanzee named Abraham. The space capsule crashed into Kulalu's body, injuring the creature and causing it to lay dormant in the Pacific Ocean for nearly two decades. Kulalu's blood from the accident was responsible for enlarging Abraham into a monstrous King Kong-like ape.

Kulalu was eventually awoken through human sacrifice by Varda, a secretive group of world leaders who worship the Great Old One as their god. The Varda intended to use Kulalu to end humanity's suffering by bringing forth the apocalypse. During its rampage, Kulalu got into some conflicts with Abraham and Mecha Ape. Although Mecha Ape was destroyed, Abraham ultimately defeated Kulalu by dropping the creature into an active volcano. (: Ape X Mecha Ape: New World Order)

entities.name: Lam
entities.description:
Lam is an alien entity, similar to Grey aliens, dwelling in the dark side of the planet Mars.

It is an extraterrestrial intelligence which the occultist Aleister Crowley came into contact with in 1919.

He is said by some to be the Lama of Lêng.

The RPG Malleus Monstrorum supplement linked this occult entity to the Cthulhu Mythos. It is debatable whether or not Grant's occult works count as narrative sources.

entities.name: Leviathan
entities.description:
Leviathan is the name given by some Inuit cultists to a child of Cthulhu: "...the Other Tornasuks left or went to sleep with Him [Cthulhu], except Dagon his servant-creation and Leviathan his son." (: "The Arctic Stone")

It is also one of the primary antagonists of the 2018 video game Call of Cthulhu by Cyanide Studio, based on Chaosium's role-playing game.

The Leviathan is a colossal shark-like or serpentine creature, more than fifty feet in length, that is regarded as an offspring or avatar of Cthulhu — though some sources speculate that it could alternatively be a particularly massive Deep One or Star-Spawn, and others consider it part of an unholy trinity alongside Dagon and Hydra. Its powerful jaws are capable of biting through wood, metal, flesh, and bone with ease, and can gape wide enough to swallow creatures almost as large as a Dark Young whole. Despite being most-proficient at swimming, it is capable of moving on land as well. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

In at least one manifestation, the Leviathan resembles a prehistoric fish with four fins pierced by metallic rings, squid-like tentacles framing its jaws, and a long tail for swimming. It is observed to be two to three times the size of a common whale. It preys upon whales and other large marine animals, but is said to never directly harm humans, instead attempting to psychically corrupt and compel them to worship and unleash its progenitor, Cthulhu. (: Call of Cthulhu)

entities.name: Lloigoroth
entities.description:
Lloigoroth is a fictional entity created by Marvel Comics, which first appeared in Avengers Vol 1 #352-354 "Fear the Reaper".

Lloigoroth is an Old One who was summoned by the supervillain, the Grim Reaper. Seeking revenge against the Avengers, he made a pact with the Old Ones. He swore to reward their generosity with a feast of decay, corruption, and death. Lloigoth empowered him with supernatural powers, giving him the ability to do things that he could not do before; downing an airliner while in flight, walking away from its crash intact, the ability to manipulate time and space, create holographic projections, and re-arrange matter. He was also able to reanimate and control the dead, including former superhumans, who despite being undead, possessed the abilities they had before. Intelligent zombies who hungered for blood and flesh. When the Grim Reaper lost control of the living dead who then turned on him, Lloigoroth appeared and consumed the Grim Reaper.

entities.name: Lythalia
entities.description:
Lythalia is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by James Ambuehl for his 1990 poem "Where Walks Istasha".

Lythalia is a Great Old One who appears as a beautiful woman wrapped in vines and vegetation. She is thought by some to have waylaid Elder God Nodens by dark sorcery and had her way with him, and became mother of the twins Vorvadoss and Yaggdytha. (: "The Star-Seed" (Cthulhu Codex #7, James Ambuehl)

She also has a cat-like sister called Istasha. She is worshipped in ancient Altuas, where temples dedicated to her exist. (: "Lord of Lizards", James Ambuehl)

M'basui Gwandu, also known as The River Abomination, is a fictional entity created by American author Aaron Polson for his short Cthulhu Mythos story "Ngiri's Catch".

M'basui Gwandu is a spider-eyed bat-winged horror which lurks in the depths of the Congo River.

entities.name: M'nagalah
entities.description:
M'nagalah is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Len Wein for DC Comics and made its first appearance in Swamp Thing Vol 1 #8 "The Lurker in Tunnel 13", depicting the entity as a threat to the entire universe.

Soon afterwards, M'nagalah was introduced to the Mythos proper in Ramsey Campbell's short story "The Tugging", and was later incorporated into the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. (: Malleus Monstrorum) In the Second Edition of Malleus Monstrorum, M'nagalah is known as M'guleloc, and two theories are presented regarding M'nagalah. One identifies him as an Old One, while the other identifies him as a lesser deity. It also suggests a connection between M'nagalah and Gla'aki, implying that M'nagalah may be a herald of Gla'aki.

In prehistoric times, M'nagalah ruled over the Tethys Ocean and was described as being "Cthulhu's right-hand man". (: Nightmare's Disciple) Some drawings of M'nagalah were documented in The Revelations of Glaaki, depicted as being a tentacled mass consisting of ropey intestine-like appendages and numerous eyes. (: "The Tugging")

Billions of years ago, M'nagalah and the other Elder Gods were able to roam the universe at will through a cosmic doorway located on Earth, until they were shut off from the cosmos by the Golden Ones. Despite this, M'nagalah and his kind were still able to reach out across the dimensional barriers and touched the minds of learned men, twisting their intellect with visions and corrupting their souls. (: Challengers of the Unknown) M'nagalah claimed to have created all life on Earth and bestowed mankind with the capacity for mindless violence, as well as influencing the minds of some of humanity's greatest scribes, including H. P. Lovecraft, Ambrose Bierce and Edgar Allan Poe. (: "The Lurker in Tunnel 13")

entities.name: M'nthster
entities.description:
M'nthster is a Great Old One from the fictional universe of the animated series The Simpsons. The character first appeared in the opening sequence for the episode "Treehouse of Horror XXIV", directed by Guillermo del Toro, when Bart skateboarded on his tentacles that bursted out of the ground. M'nthster was later featured in the mobile game The Simpsons: Tapped Out, as an unlockable character during the "Cthulhu's Revenge 2019 Event".

M'nthster is the eldest spawn of Cthulhu, who was abandoned by his father as a baby, after being traded in for a pair of designer sunglasses. They continued to be on bad terms for a while, and at least one of their fights resulted in them destroying all of reality. With some help from Marge, Cthulhu was able to eventually patch things up with M'nthster. (: The Simpsons: Tapped Out)

entities.name: Many-Angled One
entities.description:
The Many-Angled Ones are a race of extradimensional entities from the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The term "Many-Angled One" was originally created by Grant Morrison for Zenith, a series published in the science fiction comic magazine 2000 AD by Fleetway Publications. It would later be used for several other works, most notably in Marvel Comics.

The Many-Angled Ones (also known as the Lloigor) exist in a space that contains more dimensions than our universe therefore they appear to humans as "many angled." Therefore when one of them manifests in our universe, it appears to us as the floating disconnected body parts of a larger creature. Unlike most Lovecraftian entities, that often seem to have unknown albeit hostile motivations, the goal of the Many-Angled Ones is to impose on the multiverse a rigid geometrical order thereby making everything run like clockwork.

Many-Angled Ones can only possess superhuman hosts with powers such as superhuman strength and invulnerability. They taught the Nazis how to create superhumans for this purpose.

In the Marvel Multiverse, the Many-Angled Ones (also known as the Great Old Ones) are a group of malevolent entities who exist in the space between the innumerable realities, where they try to spread their corruption and decadence towards those universes. Shuma-Gorath is the most well-known of them all, however, other members include Zvilpogghua, Shub-Niggurath, and Tsathoggua. Despite being one of the Elder Gods of Earth, Chthon is frequently conflated with them. They are referred to as the "Many-Angled Ones" due to them existing simultaneously in many dimensions throughout the Multiverse, and mortals (for example, humans) are unable to perceive their true forms.

entities.name: Mappo No Ryujin
entities.description:
Mappo no Ryûjin is a fictional entity created by Michael Dziesinski for the Call of Cthulhu gaming supplement Secrets of Japan.

Mappo no Ryûjin is a Great Old One, which is currently bound and slumbering in an eight-pointed Elder Sign in the Muvian ruins near the Japanese isles. Currently, it's active in a semi-corporeal form. The last time it visited Earth was 50,000 years ago, when Yig unleashed it to punish the Serpent Men who were worshiping Ghatanothoa and who had joined forces with the island civilization of Mu to create a new hybrid race of humans and Serpent Men. In one night, most of Mu and parts of Lemuria sank beneath the waves. The last act of the dying Muvian wizards bound Mappo no Ryûjin to the Elder Sign.

It is believed that at the twilight of the age of man, when the celestial bodies are in perfect alignment, it will bring forth an orgy of destruction, as the sixth race emerges to take over the world. The Mother of Yig will devour the sun and darkness will reign for 666 days. It is a 1000 ft. long entity with two skeletal wings, a desiccated oriental dragon head, and 666 pseudopods covering its white skin. Each of the pseudopods looks like a giant albino snake, which are used to swallow and consume living creatures, each thick enough to contain a human victim. They are covered with a slimy mucous containing digestive acids.

entities.name: Mhar
entities.description:
Mhar (The World Thunder) is a fictional entity created by Paizo Inc for their role-playing game Pathfinder. The character first appeared in the gaming supplement Spires of Xin-Shalast.

Mhar is a Great Old One whose shape is that of a living volcano with fangs of lava surrounding its caldera and eight crystalline legs coming out of the base. The lava is constantly erupting, afterwards cooling or melting away, bringing it endless pain. It is currently under one of Golarion's largest mountains, the 31,565 feet tall Mhar Massif. The site of the former capital of the ancient realm of Shalast, known for the great carving it has on its face of Karzoug, the last Runelord of Greed.

It was born when the essence of the Planes of Earth and Fire were made to fuse together by a unique planar rift. To alleviate its pain, it traveled the cosmos, settling on hot, molten planets. It would rest within their cores, but eventually their heat wouldn't be enough to keep it asleep. Resulting in its awakening and the destruction of the planet. Numerous worlds were destroyed like this, until it ended up on Golarion.

When the goddess Sarenrae opened the Material Plane to create the Dead Vault, she attempted to put Mhar out of its misery by killing it. She was unable to permanently destroy him, as he was put into a slumber within Golarion. When it awakened, Mhar found itself trapped within Golarion and went insane. Its madness was intensified by his psychic convulsions which rebounded from the planet's surface. The Kodar Mountain range was created by Mhar's convulsions. If Mhar ever breaks free from its prison, it will cover Golarion with magma. Using it as a focus to open a portal to the Plane of Fire. Consuming the Material Plane in lava so that it can finally know peace.

entities.name: Mlok
entities.description:
Mlok is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Gary Myers for his short story "The Priest of Mlok".

Mlok is a creature, possibly a Great Old One, who landed on Earth in ancient times somewhere near the Bnazic Desert, known to devour human victims for sustenance. (: "The Priest of Mlok")

A bloody cult was created around Mlok and it became strong in the city of Drinen. (: "The Gods of Drinen", "The Tomb of Neb")

entities.name: Mnomquah
entities.description:
Mnomquah is a fictional entity created by the American author Lin Carter for his short story "Something in the Moonlight".

Mnomquah is a great reptilian creature with a crown of writhing feelers and empty sockets in place of eyes, although somehow it is still able to see. It is trapped inside the Dreamlands' moon, though how it became stuck there is unknown. In Brian Lumley's version of the expanded Cthulhu Mythos, it is the mate of the disgusting Oorn, and when the Great Old Ones awaken to lay waste to our world, then Mnomquah will be reunited with its repulsive bride.

It is called the Lord of the Black Lake because it rules over the Lake of Ubboth, a great body of water which rests beneath the surface of the moon.

entities.name: Mordiggian
entities.description:
Mordiggian is a fictional deity created by Clark Ashton Smith for his Zothique story "The Charnel God". The entity was later incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos as a Great Old One by Scott D. Aniolowski in his Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game.

Described as swirling darkness, a gigantic shadow, or a worm-shaped column, Mordiggian is worshipped by several human cults and cults of ghouls as a symbol of Death. His name is used in Zothique, Man's last continent.

The name may also find its origins in medieval France, being a corruption of the Latin "Mortician" (to do with the dead). There is also at least some faint echo of the Celtic death goddess The Morrigan in the name, especially since one of her epithets was The Crow That Feasts On The Battlefield.

Mordiggian also seems to be the main subject of The Ghoul's Manuscript and Cultes des Goules.

entities.name: Morrtlgh
entities.description:
Morrtlgh (also known as the Cloud of Knowledge or Devourer of Sons) is a fictional entity created by Anthony Warren for the Miskatonic University Library Association Monograph supplement Kingdom of the Blind, part of a series of fan-driven supplements released by Call of Cthulhu publisher Chaosium.

Morrtlgh is a Great Old One who manifests as a glowing orb which rests at the centre of a swirling vortex of tiny, razor-sharp blades of a metallic appearance. It maintains a small cult of worshippers in rural England, much of its former congregation - located across Western Europe - having disappeared over the ages. Although currently imprisoned, it is still able to manifest itself in a much-diminished form when summoned.

The entity was known to have granted its followers magical boons in the past. To invoke these powers, a sacrifice had to be offered, one which would subsequently be reduced to a fine red mist by Morrtlgh's multitude of spinning blades. It would then use these same blades to inscribe spells upon the living flesh of its supplicants. (: Kingdom of the Blind)

Once free to roam the world and do as it pleased, during the 14th century Morrtlgh was imprisoned beneath a barrow in the English countryside by a coven of white witches. During that time, its power was vastly inhibited, and its worship slowly died out. However, during the 1920s, a team of unwitting scholars, interested in any potential archaeological discoveries which might lie within the barrow, threatened to accidentally set the fearsome creature free. (: Kingdom of the Blind)

entities.name: Mynoghra
entities.description:
Mynoghra, also known as The She-Daemon of the Shadows, is a fictional entity created by the late American author Edward P. Berglund for his 1975 short story "Wings in the Night".

Mynoghra is a cosmic entity capable of manifesting in a variety of forms, including that of a beautiful woman, but in its true form possesses a pair of membranous wings and is highly averse to any form of light. Despite this, Mynoghra has shown to be capable of extinguishing any light sources it encounters, and is usually surrounded by a cloud of inky blackness to protect herself from its effect in any case.

A Great Old One mentioned as a cousin of Nyarlathotep in The O' Khymer Revelations, and the Count de Hammais’ Sorcerie de Demonologie states that of all the Great Old Ones, Nyarlathotep and Mynoghra are the only ones not to be "imprisoned beneath the Elder Sign," and that once summoned, a portal to its dimension is created which may only be closed by the person who opened it.

Mynoghra likes to forge pacts with mortals for an unnamed price, although usually this price is the life-essence of the other party, as the entity finds this to be a particularly delicious repast. The remains of the victim are then fed to Mynoghra's Hell-Hounds, demonic entities only vaguely described but which bear some unspecified connection to the Hounds of Tindalos despite being the offspring of Mynoghra and Shub-Niggurath. In exchange, she may offer boons such as artistic inspiration; these pacts are always brought to a close on All Hallow's Eve. (: "Wings in the Night")

entities.name: N'Gabthoth
entities.description:
N'Gabthoth is a fictional entity created by Marvel Comics, who first appeared in Marvel Premiere #6, written by Gardner Fox and penciled by Frank Brunner.

N'Gabthoth was a Great Old One or Lesser Old One who had been sleeping in a cavern in the ocean near Starkesboro for an unknown amount of time. When Dr. Strange killed Sligguth, one of the spawns of Set and an agent of Shuma-Gorath, N'Gabthoth woke from his slumber. He headed toward Ebora and the Serpent Men of Starksboro, to feed on the human sacrifices which they prepared for him. Who were freed by Dr. Strange during the fighting.

N'Gabthoth had the ability to survive both underwater and on land. N'Gabthoth could fire extremely powerful mystical bolts from his eye, a single one being able to knock Dr. Strange out of the sky. He outmatched Dr. Strange in power, and was able to dissipate magical spells. When the Ancient One added his own power to that of Dr. Strange, the Sorcerer Supreme was able to kill N'Gabthoth.

entities.description:
Nctosa and Nctolhu (also known as The Twin Spawn of Cthulhu) are twin Great Old Ones from the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. They first appeared in the novel Nightmare's Disciple by Joseph S. Pulver.

Nctosa and Nctolhu are the twin daughters of Cthulhu, who are currently imprisoned in the Great Red Spot of the planet Jupiter. They both appear as colossal shelled beings, with eight segmented limbs and six long arms ending with claws, vaguely resembling their half-sister, Cthylla.

entities.name: Nestene Consciousness
entities.description:
The Nestene Consciousness is a Great Old One in the fictional universe of Doctor Who by the BBC.

The Nestene Consciousness is a hive mind race which is both a singular entity and a disembodied life force. It is the offspring of Shub-Niggurath, which spawned it on the planet Polymos. (: Millennial Rites, Craig Hinton)

Nestene exist as energy that can possess plastic. Described by the Doctor as "ruthlessly aggressive and intelligent". The Nestene Consciousness manifests either as a being of pure energy and force or as a mass of solid plastic. It's natural appearance is that of a many-tangled horror which is sort of a hybrid of a octopus, crab, and spider. Which is large enough to dwarf a radio telescope. Due to the stresses of the Last Great Time War, their biology have drastically changed, resulting in a form that is mostly plastic and manifests in a mostly liquid form possessing a humanoid face.

The Nestene Consciousness is able to exist in various places, various plaes, and various times. They travel across space in energy units, which are hollow plastic meteorites that are 8.5 inches in diameter and move across space in "clusters" which are swarm formations. Landing on worlds where they are collected by Autons and then placed into an environment tank where a plastic body to contain the brain is manufactured. Nestenes can absorb psychic energy from willing humans and covert their bodies into energy. A Nestene which had been absorbed into a human mind demonstrated the ability to project energy barriers, teleport, and materializing Autons.

entities.name: Ngirrth'lu
entities.description:
Ngirrth'lu is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by James Ambuehl for his short story "The Stalker in the Snows".

Ngirrth'lu is a ferocious and towering wolf-like humanoid with bat wings. He is served by Werewolf servants known as the Lupine Ones.

After the Elder Gods triumphed in the war against the Great Old Ones, they banished Ngirrth'lu to 'Ykia, Land of the Red Snows, a parallel dimension bordering upon the Earth. (: "The Stalker in the Snows")

entities.name: Nug and Yeb
entities.description:
Nug and Yeb are twin Great Old Ones from the Cthulhu Mythos, who were first mentioned in the short story "The Last Test" by H. P. Lovecraft.

Nug and Yeb were born from the mating of Shub-Niggurath with Yog-Sothoth (: Selected Letters 5.875) and T’yog believed them to be friendly to man. (: "Out of the Aeons")

According to another account by Eibon, the androgynous Cxaxukluth split in two, becoming male Nug and female Yeb. This minority interpretation may just be a textual gloss attempting to harmonize conflicting information. (: "The Second Epistle of Eibon unto his Disciples, or The Apocalypse of Eibon" [Robert M. Price and Laurence J. Cornford])

Nug is the parent of Cthulhu and Yeb is the parent of Tsathoggua (: Selected Letters 4.617). Nug might be known by the name Ptmâk in Hyperborea, as Ptmâk corresponds to the "immediate" parent of Cthulhu. (: letter of Clark Ashton Smith to R. H. Barlow, September 10th, 1935)

entities.description:
Ny-Rakath is a fictional entity created by Chaosium, which features in the Mythos collectible card game.

Ny-Rakath is a Great Old One who resembles a hulking winged bipedal goat with four horns and a serpentine tongue, similar in appearance to the entity depicted on the Devil card of the traditional A.E. Waite Tarot deck.

Its effect was to eliminate and prevent the use of assistant character cards. Its location was listed as Underground.

entities.name: Nyogtha
entities.description:
Nyogtha is a Great Old One in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Henry Kuttner for his short story "The Salem Horror".

Nyogtha is an amorphous mass composed of an unidentifiable sticky black substance. It is capable of extruding tentacles from this mass to manipulate the environment around it. According to the cursed book the Necronomicon, the only way that it can be cast back to its own dimension once summoned is through the use of a ritual combining an ankh, the Tikkoun elixir and the Vach-Viraj incantation (: "The Salem Horror").

Nyogtha is served by a large pack of ghouls which live in the catacombs beneath the city of Arkham. (: "The Anatomy Lesson")

When a man by the name of Carson unwittingly invoked the curse of Abigail Prinn, the body of the witch resurrected itself and attempted to summon Nyogtha through a portal between worlds known as the Witch Room. Luckily, an occultist named Michael Leigh was able to thwart the ritual through use of the method described in the Necronomicon, and both Abbie Prinn and the Great Old One were banished back through the partially opened gateway. (: "The Salem Horror")

Ob'mbu is a fictional entity created by Joseph S. Pulver, Sr. for his novel Nightmare's Disciple, depicted as being a monstrosity that resembles a giraffe-like reptile.

entities.name: Old One
entities.description:
The Old Ones are Lovecraftian-like demons in the fictional universe of the Buffy the Vampire Slayer franchise by 20th Century Fox.

The Old Ones were pure-breed demons that ruled Earth prior to man, during the Primordium Age (liked they ruled many other dimensions). They warred endlessly with each other, were worshiped as gods, and turned Earth into a nightmarish world. Eventually mortal animals emerged, including humans, and the Old Ones were driven from Earth's reality by unknown powers. The Old Ones bred with or infected the mortal animals of Earth, creating hundreds of demon species. Cults were established which worshiped the Old Ones, anticipating their return to Earth which would result in the destruction of mankind.

The greatest of the Old Ones could never be destroyed, and the most one could do was destroy their physical bodies. Their essence would live on though and thereby have the ability to eventually come into being again. Thousands of Old Ones were buried in the "Deeper Well", whose corpses or essences were contained within sarcophagi to prevent their resurrection. It ran across the Earth, nearly 8,000 miles, and could be accessed via an entrance in England and another one in New Zealand.

The concept of the Old Ones as ancient, indestructible beings which ruled the Earth long before the coming of mankind, that were subsequently banished and in the modern day operate through secretive cults while awaiting their time to reclaim the world resonates strongly with H. P. Lovecraft’s depiction of a cosmic pantheon. This connection has been made by many in the fan community, and can perhaps best be illustrated in a quote from Rupert Giles, a scholarly character from the Buffyverse franchise, in the series 1 episode "The Harvest":

entities.name: Old One
entities.description:
The Old Ones are a species or group of demonic-like cosmic beings in the Grimm Fairy Tales multiverse which are based on the Old Ones of the Cthulhu Mythos. They were first identified as Old Ones in issue #2 of the 1st volume of Call of Wonderland in 2012. The first Old One to appear was the Jabberwocky in issue #16 of the 1st volume of the Grimm Fairy Tales in 2007, though he wasn't identified as an Old One till years later.

The Old Ones are incredibly powerful entities that represent the forces of chaos in the cosmos. Their enemies are the Keepers, who represent the forces of order. In ancient times, these two factions waged a war across the realities that threatened to tear the multiverse apart. Defeated by the Keepers, the Old Ones were put into slumber and imprisoned for eternity.

The Keepers spared only one, the youngest of the Old Ones, for all intents a baby, the Jabberwocky, who was put in the Realm of Dreams, to have its evil cleansed, which ended up being a spectacular failure. Early in the 21st century, the Red Knight tried to free the Old Ones, so that they would destroy the world.

entities.name: Oorn
entities.description:
Oorn is a fictional creature created by British author Brian Lumley for his 1987 Cthulhu Mythos novel Mad Moon of Dreams.

Oorn is the mate of the Great Old One Mnomquah, described as a huge tentacled mollusc-like being with appendages which are capable of spraying digestive acids. It is worshipped by both the Men of Leng and the Moon-beasts.

A creature also called Oorn was created by H. P. Lovecraft and R. H. Barlow for their story "The Hoard of the Wizard-Beast". However, as this story was written in 1933 but unpublished until 1994, seven years after the publication of Mad Moon of Dreams, it seems highly unlikely that Lumley would have been aware of its existence when writing about his own creation.
