entities.name: Orgesh
entities.description:
Orgesh (also known as the Faceless God) is a fictional entity created by Paizo Inc for their role-playing game Pathfinder. The character first appeared in the gaming supplement Descent into Midnight.

Orgesh is a Great Old One that has a vaguely humanoid form consisting of a large distended belly, canine legs, and featureless face that has a maw full of shark teeth. Its hunger is endless, requiring a constant supply of sacrifices to placate the voracious god. Its origins lay in the Land of Black Blood, being the first of the Charda to be spawned from the black blood.

entities.name: Othuum
entities.description:
Othuum (The Oceanic Horror) is a Great Old One from the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. It was first mentioned in Brian Lumley's short story "Rising with Surtsey", and was later incorporated into the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

Othuum is an unknown entity who is theorised to resemble a twisting rope-like monstrosity covered in tentacles with a singular alien face in the middle of a squirming, ropy mass. It has been speculated that the entity may be a servant of Cthulhu, dwelling beneath the waves and striving for his master's return. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

entities.name: Paighon
entities.description:
Paighon is a fictional entity which appears in the Lovecraftian fiction of the late American author Walter C. DeBill, Jr.

Described as a "nuclear force-creature" (: "The Barrett Horror"), Paighon is possibly a Great Old One or an Elder God. In "Collector's Item", the earliest of DeBill's works it appears in, Paighon is said to have come from the Andromeda galaxy to the Solar System and settled inside the core of the Earth soon after it formed.

Paighon is the deadly enemy of Ngyr-Khorath and its servitor, 'Ymnar. (: "The Barrett Horror")

entities.name: Pnaklendorf
entities.description:
Pnaklendorf (also known as The Iron Venus or Uterus Mundi) is a fictional entity created by Ricardo Meyer for his short story "Hain", and is later set to play a major role in "The Machine Beneath Our Feet".

Pnaklendorf is the passive counterpart of the "Unbegotten Source," Ubbo-Sathla, and, like it, remains inactive, immersed in a kind of slumber. It is connected to the earth and occasionally manifests through bodies it materializes, perhaps unconsciously. Although these bodies remain dormant, some retain active vital functions, being capable of giving birth—apparently asexually—to creatures resembling luminous spiders.

What may be its primary body lies within the Dreamlands, and its interior has been colonized, becoming the site where the cities of the so-called "Land of Pnaklendorf" have been built. These colonies, originally devoted to mining, experienced rapid growth due to the abundance of resources. However, over time, the rate of extraction surpassed their capacity for regeneration, leading many inhabitants into precarious conditions. Today, it is a nation marked by deep inequalities, and has served as a place of exile for many of the outcasts of the Dreamlands.

Pnaklendorf is described in two esoteric texts. The oldest is the Liber Veneris, which refers to the "Uterus Mundi," hinting at the existence of a Mother Earth. The second is the Manuscripts of Olleros, an anonymous document transcribed by Professor Hidalgo Pintado of the Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer University and published by Agartha Press in Spain.

entities.name: Poseidon
entities.description:
Poseidon is the name of the primary sea-god of Classical Greek mythology. Later, in Roman mythology, Neptune was equated with it. For this reason, this article explains both gods.

Poseidon and Neptune have been mentioned in a handful of stories and poems, both those set in the Cthulhu Mythos and as references to their real-world aspects.

Poseidon was briefly mentioned in "To Greece, 1917," a tribute to the people and mythology of Classical Greece. (: "To Greece, 1917")

Father Neptune once appeared to Thomas Olney, holding a trident and accompanied by scores of tritons and nereids, as well as the primal god Nodens. (: "The Strange High House in the Mist")

entities.name: Ptmâk
entities.description:
Ptmâk is reported in an antehuman text to be the "immediate" parent of Cthulhu (Kthulhut) and his race (the Cosmic Octopi). It appears to have remained dwelling of Vhoorl and is thus quite obscure. Ptmâk has some connection to Nug, and may be another name for Nug.

Ptmâk was created by Clark Ashton Smith in letters to R. H. Barlow. Lin Carter attempted to incorporate some of the information into his work.

The letter is written ambiguously about who is a child of Nug: "The immediate parent of Cthulhu and his race (child of Nug) was Ptmâk". Comparing Smith's letter with his and Lovecraft's Family trees of Azathoth suggests that Ptmâk and Cxaxukluth are the Hyperborean versions of Nug and Yeb.

[http://www.eldritchdark.com/writings/correspondence/59 Smith's letter to Barlow]

entities.name: Q'yth-az
entities.description:
Q'yth-az (also known as The Crystalloid Intellect) is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Scott David Aniolowski for his short story "An Early Frost", and was later incorporated into Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. (: Ye Booke of Monstres)

Q'yth-Az is a Great Old One that lives on a lightless world known as Mthura. It's a stationary entity that extends and absorbs with frost-like tentacles. Anything living that is touched by the crystalline tendrils is transformed into formations of solid minerals. By generating large clusters of sharp, heavy minerals and crystals it crushes victims.

It is able to project its thoughts and influences across the cosmos via mineral formations. Humans that are psychically sensitive who come into contact with crystal formations can pick up its projected thoughts, its influence often manifesting in dreams.

entities.name: Quachil Uttaus
entities.description:
Quachil Uttaus (The Treader of the Dust) is a fictional entity created by Clark Ashton Smith for his short story "The Treader of the Dust". The character was later incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos.

Quachil Uttaus is a Great Old One who can reduce all living tissue he comes into contact with to dust (and is therefore similar to another of Smith's characters, Ubbo-Sathla). Quachil Uttaus is usually associated with age, death, and decay. Summoning this god is considered lethal, if one even subconsciously entertains thoughts of suicide.

It is noted for the acceleration of time that occurs in its presence. Appears as a mummified humanoid with withered, bone-thin arms and unnatural, ever-grasping hands. Also known as "The Ultimate Corruption". It may have been known in ancient Egypt as Ka-Rath, "The Keeper of the Dust".

In Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, although not without limits, it manipulates space-time, capable of speeding up or rewinding the flow of time, moving matter, altering the structure of space, and even creating or destroying matter (for this reason, it is sometimes regarded as an embodiment of one aspect of Azathoth). Currently, it dwells in a limb beyond space and time, but if unleashed upon the real world without restraint, it would burn many stars to ashes and reduce everything to dust. (: Malleus Monstrorum (2020 edition))

entities.name: Quetzalcoatl
entities.description:
Quetzalcoatl is a deity in Aztec beliefs. It is a very inspirational and popular figure in Aztec religion and literature.

The name Quetzalcoatl is formed from two Aztec language (Nahuatl) words, quetzalli, "tail feather of the quetzal bird" and coatl, "snake", creating the compound word Feathered Serpent.

Quetzalcoatl was a major god and usually considered a benevolent one sympathetic to humans. He was one of the major deities of the ancient Mexican pantheon. Originally, Quetzalcóatl seems to have been conceived as a vegetation god, allied with the rain god Tlaloc.

In the Cthulhu Mythos, "Quetzalcoatl" is considered to be another name for Yig.

entities.name: Quoggoth
entities.description:
Quoggoth is a fictional entity created by Marvel Comics for the 2009 comic book Wolverine: First Class #12 "The Substitute".

Quoggoth was created by Shuma-Gorath, lord of the Old Ones himself. Quoggoth served his creator for aeons, until hundreds of millions of years later, he perceived himself to be more powerful than his lord and rebelled against Shuma-Gorath. Although he was unable to destroy his rebellious disciple, Shuma-Gorath imprisoned him within a sunken sepulchre.

Millions of years later, the island upon which the sepulchre was located was brought up to the ocean's surface and used by Magneto as his base, until his defeat at the hands of the X-Men. When they found themselves stranded on the island, Quoggoth brought Cyclops and Shadowcat to the sepulchre. He attempted to make a deal with Shadowcat to get them to release him from his prison but failed to convince Cyclops. They fled and tried to escape, battling the pursuing spawn generated by Quoggoth. Neither Cyclops's optical blasts nor Shadowcat's phasing powers were able to get through the doors that were covered by mystic sigils. Wolverine heard their screams from the other side of the door, and freed them with his claws by prying off the crystal seal. Quoggoth attempted to follow after them but Cyclops managed to close the doors in time with his optic beams as Wolverine put the crystal seal back in place, thereby once again imprisoning Quoggoth.

Not even a telepath of Xavier's power was able to sense him, despite being on the same island. Quoggoth was able to produce spawn from its form, which varied from winged bat-like creatures to one that looked like a little human girl. It's touch was able to shock and stun Shadowcat and it could elongate its tentacles to great lengths. Blasts from Cyclops were unable to wound, much less destroy its tentacles. Considering the fact that Shuma-Gorath's power is such that it's aura-pressure alone could destroy multiple galaxies and it could even destroy a universe with it's most powerful blast, and yet could not destroy Quoggoth only imprison it, Quoggoth must be a cosmic and perhaps even a multiversal threat.

entities.name: Quyagen
entities.description:
Quyagen is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Crispin Burnham and E. P. Berglund for their short story "The Thing in the Library".

Quyagen is the god of Yagothoggua, mentioned in The Black Book of the Skull, which takes the form of an enormous shadowy, horned creature with a mass of tentacles. The god is served by the Y'nathogguans and is worshipped by blood sacrfices, most famously through the "brides of Quyagen". It used the Eye of Zysl'm against the Great Race of Yith until it was imprisoned under the temple at Yagothoggua. It might be related to Othuyeg.

Raandaii-B'nk (also known as The Father of All Sharks) is a fictional entity created by Gregory Nicoll for his short story "From the Deep and Beyond".

Raandaii-B'nk is the god of the Raandeese, and it is said he created sharks in his own image. There is an undersea temple within the Bermuda Triangle, known as the "Cathedral of Raandaii-B'nk".

entities.name: Rhagorthua
entities.description:
Rhagorthua is a fictional deity created by David Conyers for the Delta Green setting of Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

Rhagorthua is a fiery Great Old One similar to Cthugha, who is able to absorb nuclear radiation. The entity is imprisoned somewhere within the subsoil of New Mexico, trapped in a death-like state before being awoken by the Trinity atomic blast of the Manhattan Project. Now partially freed, Rhagorthua sent out radioactive winds as a call for someone to fully free it. Despite still being trapped for nearly sixty years, Rhagorthua patiently waits for its freedom. (: A Handful of Dust)

entities.name: Rhan-Tegoth
entities.description:
Rhan-Tegoth is a Great Old One in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by H. P. Lovecraft and Hazel Heald for their short story "The Horror in the Museum".

Rhan-Tegoth is an entity shaped somewhat like an enormous insect, with a tremendous, barrel-shaped trunk with six appendages ending in claws-like pincers and a near-spherical head covered with hair-like filaments or feelers, a tentacle-like proboscis and three small, beady eyes. The hair-like feelers function as additional mouths that perforate the skin of the creature's prey and secrete digestive acids. Similar to Chaugnar Faugn, Rhan-Tegoth feeds by sucking out the blood and liquefied innards of its victims, the bodies of which are crushed and disfigured by the great strength of the monster.

Despite being a deity of comparatively little power, it is vital for the return of the Old Ones. It lived in the warm seas of Yuggoth before coming to Earth.

Three million years ago, during the Pliocene epoch, it inhabited an area of Alaska before going into a hibernation-like trance. Rhan-Tegoth was the last god to sleep, and was probably meant to be the first to wake. Its body was found by George Rogers and moved to a museum in London, 1926 (: "The Horror in the Museum"), but was then lost track of until It turned up, firstly in Sheffield, UK in the 1980s (: "The Return of Rhan-Tegoth"), and then in Chorazin, New York in the mid-to-late 1980s. (: "Wilbur Whateley Waiting")​ It was worshipped by the prehuman, cannibal Gnophkehs, but few humans know of it in modern times. (​: "The Scroll of Morloc")

entities.description:
Rhogog was said to be created when Cthulhu and Hastur fought above the British Isles and Cthulhu shed blood, which several Star-Spawn put an 'entity' into for unknown purposes. This 'entity' lay dormant, growing in power until it became Rhogog. Rhogog is a great, black oak tree, hot to the touch, and a being of darkness, and unimaginable power.

entities.name: Rokon
entities.description:
Rokon is the god-king of the serpent folk on the planet Zandanua (their place of origin). He is brother to Yig. Rokon and his followers constantly war with Nira and Nodens.

Rokon was created by Llewellyn M. Cabos and expanded upon by James Ambuehl.

With the description of Rokon as "brother" to Yig and the implication that their forms are identical or extremely similar, the further implication from this contribution to the Mythos would be that "Yig" is a member of a race or species and not a unique Great Old One. Following this train of thought, one could posit the same of Cthulhu and Kthanid.

entities.name: S'tya-Yg'Nalle
entities.description:
S'tya-Yg'Nalle (The Whiteness) is a fictional entity created by James Ambuehl and E. P. Berglund for their 1997 short story "Whiteout".

S'tya-Yg'Nalle, also known as "The Whiteness", is an ally or avatar of Ithaqua, stated to be one of the most powerful servitors of the Great Old Ones. Manifesting as what appear to be "snowflakes", they are actually tiny white crawling forms with pincer claws, similar to crabs or spiders. Despite their snowflake-like appearance, the particles actually generate extreme heat.

The Whiteness is said to be a portion of Ithaqua, much like how the Blackness is a portion of Nyarlathotep. Such as with Yin and Yang, the Whiteness and the Blackness are not considered opposites and cannot be used against each other, as they are aspects of space and time as one, consorting as "brothers". The Blackness moves through the stream of time while the Whiteness fills the spaces.

The Whiteness can be summoned using the Nyarlathotep ritual of Ob-ran, the Dark Herald of the Angled Howler, if the name of Ob-ran is interjected with "S'tya-Yg'Nalle". Targeted by the summoner, the rival caster will become a gateway for the Whiteness to enter this dimension, devouring the fabric of the rival caster's flesh from the inside. However, it can also be turned against the summoner, if the rival caster shouts out the Vach-Viraj incantation, a protection spell against the Great Old Ones, while dousing the summoner in the Tikkoun Elixir, also known as holy water, leading to the summoner being devoured instead. Once the feeding is over, the Whiteness will melt away into the body, disappearing as the lifeless shell is reduced to a torn and ragged state. (: "Whiteout")

entities.name: Saaitii
entities.description:
Saaitii is a fictional entity which made its first appearance in William Hope Hodgson's Thomas Carnacki story "The Hog", although it was unnamed in that work. It was given a proper title and classified as a Great Old One in Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game in 1994, incorporating it into the Cthulhu Mythos proper. Later, In the Second Edition of Malleus Monstrorum, Saaitii is described as either Lesser Old One or Unique Entity.

In the original Carnacki stories, the word "Saiitii" (sometimes spelled "Saaitii") is not the name of a single entity, but rather a dangerous class of supernatural manifestations, of which the titular monster from "The Hog" is identified as one. The word first appears in "The House Among the Laurels", and is also used in "The Whistling Room" and "The Hog".

Saaitii is a minor Great Old One that resides in an outer realm, full of darkness and labyrinth tunnels. It manifests as a nightmarish swine, with rhino-like flesh covering its bloated, cadaverous form. Which has a tiny cyclopean eye, at least a dozen cloven-hoofed legs, and three maws filled with boar-like teeth and tusks. Saaitii attacks the souls of its victims, first possessing them and then dragging them into its lair where they are devoured.

entities.name: Satha
entities.description:
Satha is a character created by H. P. Lovecraft’s close friend Robert E. Howard, appearing in the stories "The Scarlet Citadel" (1933) and the "The Valley of the Worm" (1934), Conan and James Allison stories respectively.

Satha first appeared in Marvel Comics in the adaptation of "The Valley of the Worm" in Supernatural Thrillers #3 (April, 1973). "Scarlet Citadel" was later adapted in Savage Sword of Conan #30. He also appeared in Darkhorse Comics (where?).

During the Hyborian Age, Satha dwelt in the southern jungles of the Country of the Worm, terrorizing the Picts. When a tribe of Aesir split from Niord's tribe (as part of their colonization of the place), they migrated to the area, where the eldritch creature known as the Worm killed them, urging Niord, the leader of the tribe who hunted it down and appeared to slay it. In this perspective, he trapped and killed Satha, using his poison to slay the Worm, but died during the battle.

Sometime before or after, Satha lived in Koth where it encountered the powerful sorcerer Tsotha-Lanti to whom it submitted. Conan of Cimmeria would end up in the sorcerer's citadel and encountered it two times, both times surviving though not because of his own actions.

entities.name: Sebek
entities.description:
Sebek is a mythological crocodile-headed god of Ancient Egypt, incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by Robert Bloch. Bloch first mentions the deity in "The Suicide in the Study", published in June 1935; the god himself makes an appearance in "The Secret of Sebek", which appeared in the November 1937 issue of Weird Tales.

Sebek was an Egyptian god worshipped in the form of a Nile crocodile, or of a man with a crocodile's head. He was a god of fertility and war, and was often invoked for protection.

Sebek was worshipped in Egypt from the Old Kingdom (c. 2700 BCE) through the Roman era (until 350 CE), and was a particularly important god during the 12th Dynasty (roughly 2000-1800 BCE). The center of Sebek's worship was the Egyptian region of Faiyum, with its capital at Crocodilopolis.

Sebek's name is also given as Sobek or Sobki; it is spelled SBK in hieroglyphics, and scholars can only guess at the actual vowels.

entities.name: Sedmelluq
entities.description:
Sedmelluq is a colossal glowing worm with a star-shaped mouth dwelling in a subterranean beneath Greenland. It made its first and only appearance to date in Imagon, a German-language Mythos novel by Michael Marrak. Imagon extends the Cthulhu Mythos following the events of H. P. Lovecraft's At the Mountains of Madness.

It is worshipped by the extraterrestrial Mi-Go.

entities.name: Set
entities.description:
Set was a "dark" god (chaos, violence, fire, storms, etc) who was worshiped in historical pharaonic Egypt. In Egypt he was variously worshiped depending on the region of Egypt from which various cults originated as a red-haired storm god and uncle of Horus (Set), the destroyer of life, family and fertility (Sutekh) or as a violent but still ultimately benevolent god-pharaoh who was a member of the godly royal family descended from Ra.

In the Hyborian Age stories of Robert E. Howard, the god Set was originally known as Satha, the venomous giant serpent, who was worshiped by some cultures and demonised by others, becoming known not only as Set, but also as Leviathan and Satan (: "The Valley of the Worm"). He was the dark god / evil god who was worshiped by many of Conan the Cimmerian's sorcerer enemies as well as in the dark kingdom of Stygia. (: "The Phoenix on the Sword", et al)

According to one account, Set is a Great Old One, (: Nameless Cults, Conan: Adventures in an Age Undreamed Of sourcebook) but according to another, Set is the same entity that would later become known as Assatur or Hastur, whose name is derived from "Ah-Set-ur". (: "The Worm of Urakhu")

In the age of Conan, Set had already in times far distant even from that prehistoric era sired "monster-kings" known as the children of Set (: "The God in the Bowl"), described in Marvel Comics stories using Conan as the Man-Serpent species.

entities.description:
Sfatlicllp is the daughter of Zvilpogghua. She is the wife of a Voormi and their offspring is Knygathin Zhaum.

Sfatlicllp was likely born on Kythanil and may have procreated the Formless Spawn once on Earth and probably became their leader (or co-leader). She probably dwells in N'kai with Tsathoggua. Possibly she became the "wife" of Nyogtha, who dwells in Yoth.

A dark-skinned humanoid horror with tentacles sprouting from its head, and glowing red eyes, Shaklatal was worshiped by the earliest African civilizations as the god Amun. It is said to be the rival of Cthulhu.

Shathak (and variants Chushax and Zishaik) were created by Clark Ashton Smith, but not elaborated upon. Laurence J. Cornford correlated some elements.

A shape-shifting, hermaphroditic Great Old One that mainly manifests as a spiny five-legged crab, Shista possesses a spider-like head and wears metallic bracelets on each limb.

entities.name: Shterot
entities.description:
Shterot, also known as The Tenebrous One, is a fictional entity created by Dominique Balczesak for the Call of Cthulhu scenario "Paris, Rêve ou Réalité", featured in the licensed gaming supplement Les Années Folles (1988).

Shterot is a Great Old One who takes the form of a colossal abomination that resembles a starfish. It possesses the ability to replicate when a part of its body is severed, creating duplicates of itself which can connect to and control other beings; while the duplicates are nowhere near the equal of their "parent" in power, the Tenebrous One can create these creatures ad infinitum, potentially granting it a limitless number of followers.

First encountered by humans when it descended from the heavens in long ages past, Shterot proceeded to spawn millions of its duplicates which then attached themselves to fully half of the population of the unfortunate continent that it made landfall upon. This parasitic infestation granted Shterot telepathic control over those infected, and for many years it ruled the land as its regent.

Eventually, however, the Elder Gods took notice and intervened. Rather than killing it, they cut Shterot into many pieces and scattered them across the globe, where these parts continue to live individual existences to this day. It is said that if the pieces unite then Shterot will be whole once more, and free to do as it pleases once again.

entities.name: Shudde M'ell
entities.description:
Shudde M'ell is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Brian Lumley for his short story "Cement Surroundings".

Shudde M'ell is a mile long great grey worm-like creature that burrows through the earth, melting all rocks in its wake. It is believed to be the supreme regent of the Chthonians as well as the largest and most powerful of the race.

Shudde M'ell appears as a colossal worm with tentacles sprouting from its head, and is so large that it can cause earthquakes by simply moving. Although Shudde M'ell is thought to have lain dormant beneath Ethiopia for aeons, it is also suspected to have been the cause of the 1906 San Francisco earthquake.

Millennia ago, when humanity as we know it was a thing still to come, Shudde M’ell sided with the Old Ones in their war against the Elder Gods. When the Great Old Ones were bested, the Elder Gods imprisoned their defeated enemies rather than destroy them. As such, Shudde M'ell found itself locked in a subterranean prison below the sands of Ethiopia, with the Elder Gods using their Star-Stone artefacts to keep them from escaping.

entities.name: Shuma-Gorath
entities.description:
Shuma-Gorath is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. He was first mentioned in a short story by Robert E. Howard from the 1920s (exact date unknown) called "The Curse of the Golden Skull", in which the "iron-bound books of Shuma-Gorath" are briefly mentioned in a single sentence.

He is a character which has been fully developed by Marvel Comics into a cosmic threat. The first appearance of Shuma-Gorath as the primary antagonist was in a story arc within Marvel Premiere #3–14 involving the super-hero Doctor Strange, and it was in issue #10 of that series when he made his first physical appearance in print.

Since then he has appeared in other Marvel comics and, during his incursions into Earth (of the Prime Reality), his manifestations have battled Doctor Strange, the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, the Invaders, and Salem's Seven. His minions have battled various heroes and teams, including the X-Men. Shuma-Gorath has also appeared in Marvel properties in both video games (Capcom and Zen Studios) and role-playing games (TSR).

Shuma-Gorath is a member of the Great Old Ones (also known as the Many-Angled Ones), a race of malevolent cosmic entities that fed on the flesh and bones of mankind's ancestors. He is at least hundreds of millions of years old, having been on Earth at the time of the dinosaurs when he battled a rebellious Many-Angled One of great power whom he had created in the skies over the planet. He claims to be older than the universe itself, which would make him billions of years old. Shuma-Gorath once ruled over Earth, along with the other Great Old Ones, before Sise-Neg (a time-traveling sorcerer from the 31st century) defeated him by putting him to sleep and banishing him into another dimension, after which he destroyed and re-created the universe.

Shuy-Nilh, also known as The Devourer in Darkness or The Devourer in the Earth, is a fictional entity created by American author James Ambuehl for his 1997 short story "The Stalker in the Snows."

Almost nothing is known of the Great Old One known as Shuy-Nilh, although it has been described as an "earth elemental." (: "The Stalker in the Snows")

The entities named the Spawn of Shuy-Nilh are said to have "humped, tentacled forms," although what their relationship is with their (presumed) progenitor may be remains unknown. (: "Correlated Contents")

entities.description:
Sk'tai is a fictional entity created by the late American author Joseph S. Pulver, Sr. for his 1999 novel Nightmare's Disciple.

Sk'tai is said to be the Great Old One Cthulhu's second bride. However, while pregnant with T'ith, her son by Cthulhu, she left Cthulhu to marry Kthanid and became the queen of the Elder Gods. She gave birth to Eppirfon with Kthanid, but was later retaliated against by Cthulhu, who finally came to exact his revenge. (: Nightmare's Disciple)

entities.name: Slorioth
entities.description:
Slorioth is a fictional entity created by Marvel Comics, who appears as the primary antagonist of the four-part story arc "Final Defense", featured in Secret Defenders Vol 1 #22-25.

Slorioth was one of the Great Old Ones, and ravaged the Earth eons ago , until his soul and body were bound to the land by a cabal of sorcerers.

Thousands of years later, a town would be established nearby, in the state of Maine: Starkesboro. Near the end of the 20th century, he corrupted and manipulated the hero Dr. Druid into releasing him from his imprisonment. Slorioth's reemergence was felt throughout the world. Spider-Man's spidey sense went into overdrive. Daimon Hellstrom (The Son of Satan) sensed the disturbance of the Aether, threatening to shift the balance between Heaven and Hell. The powerful telepath Psi-Lord sensed danger everywhere, but was unable to pinpoint its location.

Beneath NY City, subharmonic tremors rippled through the Deviants underground realm. Waves of pure discord threatened to inundate mankind's subconscious minds. Throughout thne United States, reports of extranormal activity rose, building to an unholy crescendo. Upon is emergence, both the Defenders and Secret Defenders fought against him, with no success. The Vishanti arrived threatening Earth with its destruction if they did battle with Slorioth, therefore the Living Tribunal was summoned. Who agreed that Slorioth could not be contained by any dimension and so threatened the entire universe (Earth-616) with destruction, and therefore was drawn away from Earth and its reality.

entities.name: Sodatha
entities.description:
Sodatha, also known as the Slithering God and the Hidden One, is a possible Great Old One by Marvel Comics, (: Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe A-Z #3) and a spawn of the Outer God Yog-Sothoth. (: The Appendix to the Handbook of the Marvel Universe)

Yog-Sothoth is known by the same name. (: "Valley Beyond the Stars")

Sodatha was a great tentacled subterranean monster, which lived within the walled city of Hanghrara in the kingdom of Zamora during the Hyborian Age. The Cult of Sodatha worshiped it as an elder god. It was a creature that possessed great strength, enough to destroy a city and it was capable of borrowing deep and fast. Guarding the tunnels to Sodatha were its spawn, miniature versions of itself. Both Sodatha and its spawn had a maw full of teeth, and many tentacles and eyes. Conan would encounter it in his adventures and during his fighting with its priests, boiling oil ended up on the abomination. Enraged with pain it burst from the ground into the city, toppling buildings and causing the populace to panic. Its inhabitants left the destroyed city in a mass exodus. (: "The Slithering God")

entities.name: Spot
entities.description:
Spot, also known as Thu Thu Hmong and who is later confirmed to be Cthulhu, is a character who appears in Arcana Studio's Howard Lovecraft series of children’s comics. He made his first appearance in the graphic novel Howard Lovecraft and the Frozen Kingdom.

When first encountered, Spot resembles common depictions of the Cthulhi: a large, humanoid being whose lower face is hidden by a mass of tentacles. Later, after his transformation, he takes on a more octopoid appearance, seemingly losing much of his body in the process.

When young Howard Lovecraft accidentally used the Necronomicon to transport himself to the frozen kingdom of R'lyeh, he encountered the Deep One Thu Thu Hmong, who he saved from falling into a crevasse. In gratitude, the creature, who Howard calls Spot as he is unable to remember its full name, pledged itself to his service, and the two helped the citizens of R'lyeh to rid the land of its icy curse. However, the people had been lying to them, and were in fact cultists dedicated to awakening Great Cthulhu. As they conducted their ritual, Spot began to change, and was later revealed to have become Cthulhu.

Later, Spot accompanied young Howard on a series of adventures, travelling to such far-flung places as Antarctica and Yuggoth, and encountering a succession of Mythos luminaries including Dr. Herbert West and Azathoth.

entities.description:
Sthanee is a Great Old One in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was first mentioned in Robert A. W. Lowndes' short poem "Nyaghoggua" (1941), but its physical appearance was first depicted in the pages of Lowndes' comic book feature "When Sthanee Wakes" (pp. 32-33), which was published in Scienti-Comics #2.

Manifesting as a gigantic marine horror with twelve serpentine limbs equipped with suckers similar to those found on an octopus, Sthanee also has a beard of tentacles. It is served by a vicious race of merfolk known as the Children of Sthanee who worship it as a god.

entities.name: Summanus
entities.description:
Summanus is a fictional deity created by British author Brian Lumley for his short story "What Dark God?" (, 1975) and identified as a Great Old One in "The Fairground Horror" (, 1976). It is named after an obscure nocturnal thunder god referred to in the works of Ovid, Pliny the Elder, and Martianus Capella.

Appearing as a grotesque, mouthless humanoid with pale tentacles sticking out from under his robes, Summanus can use these appendages to siphon blood from his victims.

Summanus had a following in Roman times, but if he is worshipped today, his cult is even more secretive. The rites needed for the proper worship of Summanus are found in the Tuscan Rituals.

Brian Lumley based this Great Old One on the Roman deity of the same name mentioned in the poet Ovid's Fasti. It first appeared in the short story "What Dark God?" (1975), and was later incorporated into the greater Cthulhu Mythos by Lumley himself in "The Fairground Horror" (1976). Chaosium included it in the Malleus Monstrorum sourcebook for their Call of Cthulhu () roleplaying game.

Swarog is a fictional entity created for the German-language Call of Cthulhu supplement Berlin: Im Herzen der großen Stadt.

A hideous being appearing as a dark, gigantic, legless bird-like horror swathed in dark flames, Swarog has a long neck topped by a black lump, half of which endowed with a big glowing eye and the other being covered in innumerable tentacles.

It was revered by Slavic and Viking folks as the Solar god Svarog, though sharing almost nothing with the traditional deity.

entities.name: Th'rygh
entities.description:
Th'rygh, also known as The God-Beast, is a minor Great Old One created by Irish games designer Gareth Ryder-Hanrahan, which made its first appearance in his 2002 scenario supplement Verboten! Operation: FAUST for the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game.

Little is known about Th'rygh, other than that it is a monstrous entity which manifests as a horrible patchwork of flesh, soil, and alien matter, and that it is capable of absorbing organic matter - including living creatures - with the slightest brush of its transparent tentacles.

During the spring of 1945, elements of the SS enacting Operation: WEREWOLF under the direct orders of Adolf Hitler attempted to summon Th'rygh using a passage from the Necronomicon. Their goal: to destroy the Red Army which was inexorably driving towards Berlin. When the Allies got wind of this plot, agents of the American Office of Naval Intelligence department Delta Green were parachuted in to thwart their scheme.

entities.name: Thog
entities.description:
Thog the Ancient is a fictional entity created by the late American author Robert E. Howard for his 1933 short story "The Slithering Shadow".

An octopus-like monstrosity of the Hyborian Age, Thog is a man eating abomination which haunts the underground city of Xuthal.

Thog the Ancient is a Great Old One, residing within the subterranean city of Xuthal. It preyed on the city's Black Lotus addicted dreaming inhabitants whom were slowly being consumed by the hungry entity which roamed its dark corridors. They were also prey to its cosmic lusts, as Conan's companion Natala discovered to her horror. Xuthal's inhabitants whom lived for sensual pleasures, lived in terror of it, and would draw lots to see whom would be thrown to Thog to satisfy its lust and hunger.

In the Marvel Multiverse, Thog the Ancient was seemingly the same (including his encounter with Conan, though it is unknown if he was one of the Great Old Ones, or a Lesser Old One.

entities.name: Toad God
entities.description:
The Toad God is a fictional entity, created by Robert E. Howard for his short story "The Thing on the Roof".

The Toad God used to be worshipped by an ancient tribe in Central America, during the pre-Columbian era. A temple was built for the deity, where it laid dormant for thousands of years. However, the temple also contains a mummy wearing a toad-shaped jewel. If the jewel is removed and used to open the hidden door, the Toad God will awaken to curse whoever disturbed it. (: "The Thing on the Roof")

After appearing in their adaptation of the original story, the Toad God was incorporated into the Marvel Multiverse, where it would be established as being either a Great Old One or Lesser Old One. (: Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe A to Z #3; Demons' profile)

Toth is served by humans, such as the one in the story in which it appears, which can send insectoid creatures, the size of normal insects, to sting or bite victims. Once bitten by one of Toth's insectoid servants, a person is slowly possessed by its evil alien intelligence.

The Triple God of Chaos is a supernatural being and Great Old One mentioned in the stories of Thongor of Lemuria by Lin Carter. One of its aspects is Yamath the Lord of the Flames. Another of its three aspects is Slidith, the Lord of Blood.

entities.name: Tsathoggua
entities.description:
Tsathoggua, also known as the Sleeper of N'kai, is a fictional entity in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Clark Ashton Smith for his Hyperborean Cycle.

Tsathoggua (or Zhothaqquah) is described as an Old One, a godlike being from the pantheon. He first appeared in Smith's short story "The Tale of Satampra Zeiros," written in 1929 and published in the November 1931 issue of Weird Tales. His first appearance in print, however, was in H. P. Lovecraft's story The Whisperer in Darkness, written in 1930 and published in the August 1931 Weird Tales.

Lovecraft mentioned Tsathoggua in nine stories, not counting the unfinished fragment that would later become The Lurker at the Threshold. This makes it one of the most oft-mentioned Mythos deities in Lovecraft's fiction, tied with Yog-Sothoth and losing only to Nyarlathotep (ten stories), Cthulhu and Shub-Niggurath (eleven stories each). Of these, Tsathoggua is the only one not created by Lovecraft himself.

Like Shub-Niggurath, however, Tsathoggua never appears physically in Lovecraft's stories, except for a possible appearance disguised as a wax sculpture in "The Horror in the Museum".

entities.name: Ut'Ulls-Hr'Her
entities.description:
Ut'Ulls-Hr'Her is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Joseph S. Pulver for his novel Nightmare's Disciple.

Ut'Ulls-Hr'Her takes the form of a huge faceless creature with various appendages sprouting from her head, a beard of oozing horns, many reddish teats, and fish-like fins sprouting from an egg-shaped body.

Ut'Ulls-Hr'Her's true origins are unknown, although it's been speculated that she has a connection to Shub-Niggurath, possibly being the spawn between Yig and Shub-Niggurath (: Nightmare's Disciple) or possibly an avatar of the Outer God. Others have theorized that she may be the twin sister of Glaaki. She is known to dwell in the Cetus constellation, near the vicinity of a red giant star known as Mira (Omicron Ceti). There have been several claims of her being summoned to Earth but most of these cases remain unconfirmed. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

One manifestation of the entity lives in the caverns below Antioch (a Hellenic colony in modern-day Turkey), where she is worshiped by an all-female cult known as the Daughters of Isolation. Twice a month, they wear masks which are made of flayed human skin and wear sheer gowns. The women lure men to the Paradise of Daphne, promising that they will fulfill their most outrageous sexual desires. The orgy is a cover, and three victims are taken underground, who have been drugged, becoming unable to either speak or move while still being semi-conscious. They are both raped and flayed before being fed to Ut'Ulls-Hr'Her. (: Cthulhu Invictus)

entities.name: Uvhash
entities.description:
Uvhash, also known as The Blood-Mad God of the Void, is a fictional deity created by American author James Ambuehl for his short Cthulhu Mythos story " The Advent of Uvhash".

A gigantic, vampiric red mass of eyes and tentacles, Uvhash is the archenemy of the being known as Gi-Hoveg. It dwells in the realm of Rhylkos, which is linked to the planet Mars, and it is said that whoever summons Uvhash will meet with a terrible fate.

Uvhash seems to have affinities with the Star Vampires and the Hounds of Tindalos, and is rumoured to have been one of the mad Roman Emperor Caligula's eldritch sponsors in the Cthulhu Mythos. (: "The Advent of Uvhash")

In the short story "The Advent of Uvhash", Uvhash consumed the soul of a man who was attempting astral projection under the patronage of its arch-enemy Gi-Hoveg.

entities.name: Vibur
entities.description:
Vibur was created by Chaosium in 1995 for its Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game.

Vibur is a 12 ft tall Great Old One from another plane of existence which has been on Earth for a half-dozen millennia. Whose lumpy pear-shaped body is covered by a fur-like matted black covering. Lacking feet or limbs, it rarely moves but for convenience will shift from one point to another. Small tentacles will occasionally twitch or pass across its body. Radioactive glowing finger-length hexagonal and triangular stones are emitted like feces. Growing on its fur is a blue fungus-like substance which is dangerous to humans. The being's perception and metabolism are those of another universe, and is not fully within the material universe itself. It has incredible psionic abilities, can regenerate itself from a nuclear attack, and is able to teleport itself light years away from a nuclear strike.

Exposure to the fungus risks infection and inhalation of the spores results in infection, which starts with random instances of extreme pain, the loss of physical senses, and experiencing confusing odors, terrible visions, and seeing colors beyond what humans normally see. Vivid nightmares, clinical insanity, and profound depression are common. Eventually the victims loses physical sensation and access to voluntary muscles, and the eyeballs are eaten away by bluish fluid. Becoming a zombie which is completely controlled by Vibur, with the victim's memory and consciousness trapped and helpless within. A third die within 2 weeks, while the majority continue to be transformed by the blue fungus as it locks the consciousness in never ending pain. By this time they are for all intents and purposes dead though the body continues to eat and digest what it consumes. It takes several more months before its tortuous undead life finally ends.

A slimy shape-shifting mass, Volga-Gath can be summoned with mud and the blood of the invoker.

entities.name: Vorvadoss
entities.description:
Vorvadoss (also known as The Flaming One) is a fictional deity in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Henry Kuttner for his short story "The Eater of Souls".

Cloaked in a silvery mist of darkness, only inklings of the face of the entity have ever been visible, described as utterly inhuman and only half-visible features arranged in non-human patterns following alien geometries. Its eyes are clear and black, with tiny green flickering flames seen within them. If inclined to help, despite its passionless alien expression, it can induce reassurance in one who beholds it. (: "The Invaders," Henry Kuttner)

The only known worshippers dwell on Bel Yarnak, the inhabitants of which are only known to be non-anthropoid and utterly unlike mankind in countenance. Vorvadoss has forbidden its own worship to any but the Sindara, the rulers of Bel Yarnak, whom can call upon the deity for advice. Vorvadoss seems to respond in - perhaps manipulative - riddles, as suits its purposes. In fact, it said that "Thou goest to doom, but thy son sleeps in Bel Yarnak, and I shall have a worshipper when thou art vanished." (: "The Eater of Souls," Henry Kuttner)

However, it also said that “Go therefore fearlessly, since god cannot conquer god, but only man who created him.” Simply put, it believes only humans who created god should be the ones to conquer god. (: "The Eater of Souls," Henry Kuttner)

entities.name: Vthyarilops
entities.description:
Vthyarilops (The Starfish God) is a fictional entity created by Dan Perez for his short story "The Likeness".

Vthyarilops is a Great Old One that resembles a starfish but endowed with branching tentacles, spines, a myriad of blue glaring eyes and gaping maws. It is known to dwell in the void of outer space, waiting for victims to consume.

The tattoo artist Cal worked on a full-body tattoo for his female client Mindy, based on an illustration of Vthyarilops from the Necronomicon. When it was completed, Vthyarilops was able to manifest through Mindy and devoured her boyfriend Jake. (: "The Likeness")

entities.name: The Worm that Gnaws in the Night
entities.description:
The Worm that Gnaws in the Night is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Lin Carter for his short story "Shaggai".

The Worm is a massive polychaete worm-like fiend that was observed by the wizard Eibon, who noticed that it was slowly eating away at the planet Shaggai.

The Worm has immense durability and might be one of the most powerful Great Old Ones. The Elder Gods couldn't even handle it and the Worm has survived the radiation from Ghroth, the Outer God who destroyed all life on Shaggai. It was one of the only Old Ones on that planet, with the other being Baoht Z'uqqa-Mogg.

entities.name: Xalafu
entities.description:
Xalafu (also known as The Dread One) is a fictional entity created by Peter Levi for his short story "The Life and Death of Zebros Santiago".

Xalafu is a Great Old One who manifests as a great spherical bubble, shiftingly translucent and opaque, covered in colours of disturbing hue, with one gigantic eye seemingly dominating the whole.

The entity is worshipped by a secretive cult operating in a small village near the Crist'bal Col'n mountain in Columbia. The disciples wear black robes while carrying either torches or long staves, and the wizard is garbed in gaudy white and gold robes. When conducting a sacrifice, a human is tied to an altar as the cult repeatedly chants "Ng'gai'ghl rai uflu ph-ngl dtuu v'hss Xalafu ght gai'lall" numerous times until the human starts incomprehensibly screaming. After being beaten by the staff-wielding disciples, the wizard will perform a hand-waving ritual, and pour out a vial of white power known as Diabolusaerugo to cover the human's body, followed by repeatedly chanting "Omm ug'luh vai Ufalax cn-cns'lgh mngl whglg ssi XALAFU!", before exclaiming the previous chants backwards and stepping back.

When the ceremony is complete, the sky will turn a sickly red and the moon will become purple, as an orangish light gleams from a rift in the sky, allowing Xalafu to enter this dimension. Creeping down from the sky towards the altar, Xalafu smothers the area and gorges on the human sacrifice. Upon finishing, Xalafu slowly floats back into the rift and disappears.

entities.name: Xhamen-Dor
entities.description:
Xhamen-Dor is a fictional entity created by Paizo Inc for their role-playing game Pathfinder. The character first appeared in the gaming supplement Wake of the Watcher.

Xhamen-Dor is a Great Old One whose form is a monstrous hybrid of fibrous, twisted hair-like fungal tendrils and toadstool-like growths which emerges from a mass of bones or a great corpse. It has various incarnations and forms it has taken, one of which is that of a serpentine dragon. It originated in Carcosa, from the residue left behind by Hastur which fused with the remnants of the minds and souls of those consumed by Carcosa. Xhamen-Dor burrows into the minds of those who have learned either its name or the true nature of Xhamen-Dor, spreading within their bodies and turning them into undead servants. It has visited countless worlds, turning their inhabitants into the undead, and feeding them to Carcosa.

entities.name: Avatar
entities.description:
An avatar (: "The Haunter of the Dark") (/ˈævəˌtɑr, ˌævəˈtɑr/; Hindustani: [əʋˈt̪aːr] from Sanskrit अवतार avatāra "descent") is a concept originating in Hinduism. It is a deliberate descent of a deity to Earth, or a descent of the Supreme Being (e.g., Vishnu for Vaishnavites), and is mostly translated into English as "incarnation", but more accurately as "appearance" or "manifestation".

Within the Cthulhu Mythos, an avatar generally holds the same meaning. An Elder God, Great Old One, or an Outer God may decide to appear in a physical or spectral manifestation to humans or their inhuman brethren. The reasons for why an otherworldly entity may need to manifest an avatar are varied. Most deities and entities of power in the Cthulhu Mythos do not or cannot exist in mundane, three-dimensional space. Alternatively, they may be otherwise separated by vast distances of space, sequestration in a secret location, or by virtue of living in another universe or dimension. Manifesting an avatar is often the only way such a being can communicate and interact with its worshippers or have physical agency in a particular location.

Most avatars are exponentially weaker but require a considerable effort of will on the part of their deity to manifest. Some avatars may be capable of being harmed, killed, or confounded by mortals, though to a cosmic entity, such interference is likely less than the buzz of a fly.

Often referred to as the God of a Thousand Faces, Nyarlathotep has more known avatars than any other entity in the Mythos.

entities.name: Guardian Pillar
entities.description:
The Guardian Pillar is a fictional avatar created by Chaosium for the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. It is loosely inspired by the description of the Elder Gods in "The Lair of the Star-Spawn", by August Derleth and Mark Schorer, as well as the "pillar of flame" featured in The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath, by H. P. Lovecraft.

The Guardian Pillar is a living flame, identified as an avatar of the Elder Gods, which dwells in the Cavern of Flame with the bearded priests Nasht and Kaman-Thah. It guards the gates to the Dreamlands, and enables Nasht and Kaman-Thah to contact the Great Ones, which are the only beings capable of commanding the Guardian Pillar to leave the Cavern of Flame. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands)

The portrayal of the Guardian Pillar as an avatar of the Elder Gods, which is controlled by the Great Ones might be a reference to the Dreamlands stories penned by Gary Myers, in which the Elder Gods and the Great Ones are actually the same species. However, this interpretation is not supported by the Call of Cthulhu RPG in general. In most iterations of the Mythos, the Great Ones are protected by the Elder Gods' enemies, the Outer Gods. entities.name: Amaterasu
entities.description:
Amaterasu is a sun goddess of Japanese mythology, and the cheif deity of the Shinto cosmology. She was first recorded in the Kojiki, an early Japanese chronicle of myths, legends, hymns, genealogies, oral traditions, and semi-historical accounts.

Amaterasu was later incorporated into Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, where she is classified as an Elder God. However, it was stated that this classification should be taken loosely and used as a basis of comparison with Cthulhu Mythos creatures.

Amaterasu is a Sun Goddess, whose manifestation is that of a luminescent Japanese woman of unfathomable beauty. She is dressed in a dazzling white kimono. The ancient island civilization of Mu worshiped her. (: Secrets of Japan)

entities.name: Angerboda
entities.description:
Angerboda is a giant in Norse mythology, the mother of the most famous Norse monsters. The Marvel adaptation was created in 1985 by Walt Simonson. Making its first appearance in issue #360 of the 1st volume of Thor.

Angerboda is a descendant of the Elder God Set. She is the offspring of Varcolac and Set's granddaughter Echidna. Angerboda is a giantess of Jotunheim, who is also a witch. She mated with Loki the Asgardian trickster god, and like her mother and grandfather, gave birth to several monsters of legend. Siring both the Midgard Serpent and the Fenris Wolf, and its alleged Hela, the Asgardian goddess of death. In addition to her magical knowledge, she possesses superhuman strength and is able to shapeshift into animals.

entities.name: Bast
entities.description:
Bast, also known as Bubastis, is a goddess from Egyptian mythology, incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by Robert Bloch's short story "The Suicide in the Study".

Another spelling of her name is Bastet, but due to the way the Egyptian language works, it does not change the pronunciation. The additional 'et' ending is added merely to emphasize the t in her name which denotes that she is female.

Bast is the Egyptian goddess of cats and in legend the daughter of Isis. (: "The Brood of Bubastis") She is an Elder God and the queen of all cats on Earth. However, her authority does not extend to the cats of Saturn and Uranus. The cats of these planets are associated with different deities. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

Bast is also linked with ghouls by some Saracen sorcerers, who call her "the Chewer of Corpses". A ghoul-cult to Bast fled from the Middle East to Cornwall, where they established a secret temple. (: "The Brood of Bubastis") It is believed that this was orchestrated by Nephren-Ka and that a false doctrine was spread to revive the worship of Nyarlathotep. (: Cathulhu)

entities.name: Bodhisattva
entities.description:
The Bodhisattva are part of the Buddhist cosmology, and were later incorporated into Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. (: Secrets of Japan)

The Bodhisattva are entities who have refrained from reaching full enlightenment and therefore ascending to Nirvana, so they can assist other mortals in becoming enlightened. They are the messengers of Lord Buddha, carrying out his will. Each of them has its own particular promise or concern on which it focuses its energies. They have a 99% understanding of how the universe works, and therefore have great power.

Bodhisattva manifest in consecrated temples to those whom have fasted or meditated for hours, and appear as shining beings of golden plasma energy who usually tower over mortals. Depending on the natural inclination of the supplicant is the gender it takes, and usually as they are rendered in paintings or statues. In its manifestation, supplicants see their own truth, therefore they may confuse the being with something from their belief system (e.g. angels).

entities.name: Buddha
entities.description:
Buddha is a historical figure from ancient India who is part of the Buddhist cosmology which was first used by Chaosium in 2005 for its Call of Cthulhu role-playing game as an Outer God. However, it is stated that this classification should be taken loosely and used as a basis of comparison with Cthulhu Mythos entities.

In fact, the Buddha is considered to be the yin-yang balance of calmness, order, and consciousness that counteracts Azathoth's perpetual state of eternal mindlessness and infinite chaos. For this reason, it is stated that the Buddha, as the guardian of the Dharma, is not affiliated with part of Azathoth’s court, but rather a counterpart, an invisible entity to the heartless Outer Gods. (: Secrets of Japan)

The Cosmic Buddha is a timeless entity who exists beyond time and space, where it appears as a statue. Changes such as a facial expression or a new hand position are instantaneous with no visible movement from the old to new position. On Earth a mortal on a path to enlightenment awakened to the cosmos true nature. He became the Cosmic Buddhas's physical incarnation on Earth, the Body of Manifestation (Nirmâna-Kâya), the Living Buddha. Upon his death, he ascended to the Outer Realm of Nirvana, where he merged with the Cosmic Buddha's Absolute Body (Dharma-Kâya).

Just as the multiverse has an infinite number of dimensions, so there are an infinite number of Buddhas, each of which watches over a specific dimension. Every 3000 years, a mortal becomes the Living Buddha thereby renewing the teachings of Dharma on Earth. After which it ascends to merge with the Cosmic Buddha. When the Lord Buddha manifests on Earth, it is usually to those whom are on the path to enlightenment, appearing as glowing man who is in the lotus seating position. Behind the hovering man is a spectral purple flame. Often the unmoving man is surrounded by a court of swirling devas and bodhisattvas. (: Secrets of Japan)

entities.name: Celaeno
entities.description:
In Greek mythology, Celaeno (; Ancient Greek: Κελαινώ, romanized: Kelainṓ, lit. 'the dark one', also Celeno or Kelaino, sometimes Calaeno) was the name of several figures.

Celaeno, one of the Pleiades. She was said to be mother of Lycus and Nycteus, of King Eurypylus (or Eurytus) of Cyrene, and of Lycaon, also by Poseidon

Celaeno, one of the Harpies, whom Aeneas encountered at Strophades. She gave him prophecies of his coming journeys.

Celaeno, one of the Danaïdes, the daughters of Danaus. Her mother was Crino. She married and killed Hyperbius, son of Aegyptus and Hephaestine. She was also believed to have had a son Celaenus by Poseidon.

Celaeno, a Phocian princess as the daughter of King Hyamus of Hyampolis, son of Lycorus. Her mother was Melantheia (Melantho), daughter of Deucalion. Celaeno or her sister Melanis became the mother of Delphus by Apollo.

Celaeno, daughter of Ergea by Poseidon. She was the mother of Lycus and Chimaereus by Prometheus.

Celaeno, an Amazon. She was killed by Heracles whilst he was undertaking the ninth labour.

entities.name: Cerberus
entities.description:
The Cerberus is a monster of Greek mythology, which fought Hercules. The Marvel Comics adaptation was created in 1966 by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby and made its first appearance in issue #130 of the 1st volume of the Thor comic book series.

In Chaosium's roleplaying game Call of Cthulhu, Cerberus appears as a creature. It was originally a Unique Entity, but was later reclassified as a species in 7th Edition. (: Cthulhu Invictus)

The Cerberus is a descendant of the Elder God Set. It was sired by Set's granddaughter Echidna who mated with Typhon, one of the Titans. A multi-headed large dog with a scorpion tail which guards the gates of Tartarus. It can shapeshift into a larger dog or into a minotaur-like humanoid. When in humanoid form it's able to transmute objects into weapons, carries a warhammer, and fires blasts from his helmet.

The Chimaera is a monster in Greek mythology, a fire breathing creature that merges elements of three different animals (which depending on the version is lion/snake/goat or lion/dragon/goat).

The Chimaera is a descendant of the Elder God Set. It's the offspring of Set's granddaughter Echidna who mated with Typhon, one of the Titans.

Chimaera is introduced as a creature species in the 7th Edition. (: Cthulhu Invictus)

entities.name: Coatlicue
entities.description:
Coatlicue (The Serpent Skirted One) is a goddess from Aztec mythology. The character was originally incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by Stanley C. Sargent in his short story "The Rattle of Her Smile".

Not much is known about the deity known as Coatlicue, former mate of the Snake God Yig. An enormous creature, she is said to be humanoid in form with a reptilian nature, her head is actually a pair of serpents which face each other, and she wears a skirt created from living snakes, hence her epithet.

In the days that Coatlicue spent with Yig, the pair ruled the crimson cavern of Yoth beneath the subterranean land of K'n-yan where they were venerated by the Serpent People. This arrangement came to an end when the Serpent Men abandoned Yig to instead worship Tsathoggua. The ancient Aztec civilisation, and later Mexican Indians, also worshiped Coatlicue, and the Aztecs created a great statue in her honour which now resides in Mexico City's National Museum of Anthropology.

"Coatlicue" Cōātlīcue ("Snakes Skirt") is a Nahuatl goddess revered by Nahuatl speaking peoples of the region now known as Mexico and other regions further south where that language group was once dominant. There are certain mounds in North America that may have been built by colonisers from Mexico centuries before white settlement.

entities.name: Indrid Cold
entities.description:
Indrid Cold, also known as The Smiling Man or The Grinning Man, is a pop culture figure who has been incorporated into the expanded Cthulhu Mythos by American author Josh Reynolds.

A tall, thin man with abnormally long limbs and an over-wide smile which never leaves his face, Indrid Cold has pale skin through which can occasionally be seen a wriggling movement or an unnatural twitch. He is also a telepath who appears to be immune to conventional weapons. Indrid Cold's real nature has not been confirmed, but it is heavily implied that he is an extraterrestrial creature from the Cthulhu Mythos in the disguise of a human.

Indrid Cold is infamous in conspiracy theory circles for being connected to sightings of unidentified flying objects and the Mothman of Point Pleasant, with his appearance being reported since as early as 1966. He is also commonly associated with the so-called Men in Black, a government agency purported to be heavily involved with covering up UFO phenomena. It is in this last guise that Reynolds most closely portrays the Cthulhu Mythos iteration of Cold: an alien entity working with the United States government.

entities.name: Echidna
entities.description:
Echidna is part of Greek mythology. Echidna is a monster in Greek mythology, depicted as half-woman and half-snake, known as the "Mother of Monsters." She was the mate of Typhon and the mother of many famous mythical creatures, including the Hydra and Cerberus, representing chaos and danger in ancient stories.

While there is no direct reference to Echidna in the Cthulhu Mythos created by H. P. Lovecraft and later authors, several parallels can be drawn.

In Chaosium's roleplaying game Call of Cthulhu, while Echidna herself does not appear directly, her relatives—such as her mother Ceto, her mate Typhon, and her offspring Cerberus—do make appearances. (: Cthulhu Invictus)

Echidna is the granddaughter of the Elder God Set born to his son Phorcys who mated with Ceto, a sea monster. She has sired many of the monsters of Greek mythology, most of which the heroic demi-god Hercules has battled. Most of them were sired with Typhon, one of the Titans, except for Angerboda who she sired with Varcolac and the Snakes of Many Colors.

entities.name: Elemental
entities.description:
Elementals are supernatural creatures from Medieval thought that became a popular part of the belief systems of demonology, alchemy and ritual magic in the Renaissance era. They were incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by August Derleth and other writers.

Elementals are living beings composed of one of the Classical Elements. The Classical Elements were theorised by the Ancient Greek philosopher Empedocles and defined as being Air, Earth, Water and Fire.

Each of the four Empedoclean Elements has a corresponding type of Elemental: Sylphs for Air, Gnomes for Earth, Undines for Water and Salamanders for Fire.

Paracelsus in particular popularised them and wrote about them in the 16th Century. Paracelsus wrote A Book on Nymphs, Sylphs, Pygmies, and Salamanders, and on the Other Spirits, in which mythological creatures and beings were assigned a classification based on one of the four Elements. This meant that all mythological or supernatural beings fell into one of the Elemental categories.

entities.name: Fenris Wolf
entities.description:
The Fenris Wolf (also known as Fenrir) is a giant wolf deity from Norse mythology. It was first mentioned in the anonymous narrative poem collection Poetic Edda, which describes the entity as the one destined to kill the god Odin during Ragnarök. The Marvel Comics incarnation was created in 1965 by Stan Lee and Jack Kirby, making its first appearance in Journey into Mystery Vol 1 #114.

The 17th century Danish sorcerer Axel Holm learned about "Loki the Sly One and the accursed Fenris-Wolf" in his occult studies. (: "The Trap")

The Fenris Wolf is a descendant of the Elder God Set and the offspring of Set's great granddaughter, the giantess Angerboda, after she mated with the Asgardian god Loki.

It is an Asgardian Wolf God, approximately 15 ft tall, which has the intelligence of a human and is capable of shapeshifting, to a large-sized wolf or a wolf-like humanoid. It also possesses god-like strength, speed and regenerative abilities.

entities.name: God
entities.description:
God is, according to the Abrahamic religions, creator and ruler as well as the sustainer of the Universe.

"God" is used in interjections by William Dyer, (: At the Mountains of Madness) Marinus Bicknell Willett, (: The Case of Charles Dexter Ward), Henry Armitage and Francis Morgan, (: The Dunwich Horror) the reanimated Eric Moreland Clapham-Lee, (: Herbert West--Reanimator) Zadok Allen, (: The Shadow Over Innsmouth) Henry Wentworth Akeley, the Speech-Machine and Albert Wilmarth, (: The Whisperer in Darkness) Francis Wayland Thurston, (: "The Call of Cthulhu") a Boston surveyor and Ammi Pierce, (: "The Colour Out of Space") an addicted narrator, (: "Dagon") Robert Blake, (: "The Haunter of the Dark") a poet narrator, (: "He") a grave-robbing narrator,(: "The Hound") Davis and a doctor colleague, (: "In the Vault") a monster-hunter narrator , (: "The Lurking Fear") Sheehan, (: "Old Bugs") the outsider, (: "The Outsider"), Richard Upton Pickman and a narrator, (: "Pickman's Model") Delapore and the oldest man of his party, (: "The Rats in the Walls") Harley Warren, (: "The Statement of Randolph Carter") Edward Derby and Daniel Upton, (: "The Thing on the Doorstep") Jervas Dudley, (: "The Tomb") a migrant narrator, (: "The Transition of Juan Romero") Carter, (: "The Unnamable") Lovecraft, (: "The Very Old Folk") Powers Meredith, (: "Bothon") Dr McNeill and a Native American ethnologist narrator, (: "The Curse of Yig") Alonzo Typer, (: "The Diary of Alonzo Typer") a resurrected leper narrator (: "The Disinterment")

Obed Marsh mocked Innsmouth inhabitants for praying to him. (: The Shadow Over Innsmouth)

A de la Poer was allegedly 'cursed of God', (: "The Rats in the Walls") and "An Act of God" is a legal term. (: "Bothon")

entities.name: Graeae
entities.description:
The Graeae ("Gray Ones") are three Titan sisters in Ancient Greek mythology. They are hags or witches in Greek mythology. They were described as sharing only one eye, one tooth and one tongue, having to share use of these three grisly detachable body parts to communicate or take action.

In the Marvel fictional universe it is mentioned they are the offspring of Echidna but they have not yet made an appearance in Marvel Comics.

In the Marvel fictional universe, the Graeae are granddaughters of the Elder God Set, as the offspring of Set's son Phorcys who mated with Ceto, a sea monster. The sisters are witches that look like ancient women (hags) and they share one eye and one tooth. Whose names are Enyo, Deino (or Dino), and Pemphredo (or Pephredo).

They have also been called the Grey Ones of Hellas and were individually known as Pephredo, Enyo and Deino. In this version they are an avatar of Our Ladies of Sorrow. (: Our Ladies of Sorrow) They were the oracle of men, but that role was then taken over by the keeper of secrets. They tried to retake that role through their daughter, clashing against the Harlot. (: Hexed: The Harlot and the Thief)

entities.name: Huitzilopochtli
entities.description:
Huitzilopochtli was the Aztec sun god and patron god of the city of Tenochtitlan. It is also a god of war and associated with hummingbirds, its name originating from the Nahuatl words for "hummingbird" and either "south" or "left". It's commonly represented as a humanoid figure, sometimes blue-skinned, wearing a feathered hummingbird helmet, and holding the fire serpent Xiuhcoatl. Human sacrifices were performed to Huitzilopochtli, as the Aztecs believed that blood gave it strength and nourishment.

Huitzilopochtli (spelled as "Huitzilopotchli") was mentioned in H. P. Lovecraft's early story "The Transition of Juan Romero" and first incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos in "The Electric Executioner", a collaboration between Lovecraft and Adolphe de Castro. In the works of August Derleth, this entity is associated with Cthulhu.

Juan Romero, while entranced by an inexplicable force or spell, repeatedly cried out this god's name as he descended into a deep chasm inside a mine shaft. On the next day, Romero was found dead in his bunkhouse, with no signs of having left it during the night, and the entrance to the abyss disappeared during a massive cave-in caused by a storm. (: "The Transition of Juan Romero")

The deranged inventor Arthur Feldon believed that Huitzilopochtli and the other Aztec gods were about to return, and that Feldon would rule the world with them with the power of his invention: a portable electric executioner. When another man pretended to be an emissary of Huitzilopochtli in order to play along with Feldon's mania, the inventor was so impressed that he pledged his servitude while mentioning the names of Tonatiuh-Metztli and Cthulhutl. (: "The Electric Executioner")

entities.name: Hydra
entities.description:
The Hydra is a fictional entity whose origins lie within Classical Greek mythology. It has been mentioned in a number of Cthulhu Mythos stories, as well as in other related works through its real-world aspect.

The Hydra is a creature that lurks in the deepest parts of the Mesopotamian Sea. It takes the form of a many headed serpent that harbours a bitter hatred for surface dwellers, spitting acid and poisonous venom at unsuspecting travellers.(source?)

The Lernean Hydra was a descendant of the Elder God Set, sired by Set's granddaughter and mother of many prominent mythological monstrous figures Echidna, who mated with the Titan Typhon.

The Hydra was multi-headed reptilian monster who could grow two heads when one was removed, and whose blood was venomous. The Hydra became stuff of legends in Greece, and was one of the "labours" assigned to the demigod Hercules.

entities.name: Hypnos
entities.description:
Hypnos is the Greek god of sleep incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by H. P. Lovecraft's eponymous short story. It is speculated that he is an Elder God (: Malleus Monstrorum), appearing as a youthful man with a bearded face, "immense, sunken and widely luminous eyes", and a crown of poppies.

Hypnos is the Greek/Roman God of Dreams and appears in Lovecraft's short story "Hypnos", where he met a nameless man who would soon be his friend by chance. Hypnos begins to enlighten his new friend on the nature of reality and shows him realms which exist beyond all concepts of space, time and dimensions. This happens over a period of time where the two travel further beyond. Transcending limitless realms of existence countless times, going further and deeper each time they transcend the previous plateau of existence.

The Lord of Dreams soon becomes confident that he can become the King of all reality, and ascends even further with his friend, eventually reaching a massive clump which they seemingly cannot pass through, unlike all the other previous levels of existence. His friend gives up and awakens from his sleep and waits for Hypnos to wake up as well. However, Hypnos manages to get past his obstacle, only to be driven insane by what he experienced afterward, and by the sound of a flute.

Hypnos is the Elder God said to guard the boundary between the real world and the Dreamlands. If people attract his attention through reckless behavior in the Dreamlands, they will incur his wrath. He can freely alter the appearance of dreamers. This power can be used as either a blessing or a curse. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

entities.name: Jade Emperor
entities.description:
The Jade Emperor is a deity from the mythology of Chinese traditional religion (aka, Folk Religion) and is part of the Taoist cosmology. The entity was later incorporated into the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game by Chaosium, appearing as an Elder God in the Secrets of Japan supplement; however, it is stated that this classification should be taken loosely and used as a basis of comparison with Cthulhu Mythos creatures.

The Jade Emperor is an Elder God who sits on the Jade Throne within the Citadel of the Taoist Immortals. He is at the head of the Taoist court, the personification of Yin (dark) and Yang (light). The cosmic forces which exist in the cosmos. He is an entity of pure Tao, unmanifested reality. He gives breath to all of creation and flows through all life.

The Jade Emperor is an incredibly powerful entity who follows the "way of achieving action through minimal effort", and therefore he rarely intervenes. Being the embodiment of the cosmic force of probability, he is able to alter probability. He can also restore the balance of the primal life force in any being and bestow immortality. (: Secrets of Japan)

entities.name: Jinn
entities.description:
The Jinn (singular: Jinni) were part of pre-Islamic Arabia's mythology which were later incorporated into Islamic theology.

R. H. Barlow wrote an anthology called Annals of the Jinns about a humanoid species of ancient times. He suggested that they came from Antanôk, a planet now blown to asteroids, and Yaksh could not be habitable by them. (: Clark Ashton Smith letter to R. H. Barlow, 10 September 1934)

Ludvig Prinn encountered "djinns and efreets" in the years he spent as a captive in Syria, having been captured during the Ninth Crusade. (: "The Shambler from the Stars")

According to occultist Edward Barnes Halpin, the Jinn are alien creatures that ruled the Earth before humanity. On Earth, they became nearly extinct during the ice ages, in part due to the adverse conditions, combined with fighting among themselves. However, some Jinn remained active on the planet until the time of King Solomon, who found a way to magically imprison them in objects, such as jars. Due to fundamental differences in metabolism, it's not possible for a human to actually kill a jinni, so imprisoning them is the only way to defeat them. (: "Out of the Jar")

entities.description:
Jupiter, also known as Jove and Zeus, was an important Greco-Roman god, who appeared in several of the works of H. P. Lovecraft, such as the story "Poetry and the Gods".

entities.name: Khephren
entities.description:
Khephren (c. 2600-2532 BCE) is a real-life pharaoh of Ancient Egypt in the 4th dynasty who was incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos via H. P. Lovecraft's fiction (: "Imprisoned with the Pharaohs"), which took some liberties with the historical facts.

Khephren (also Chephren) is the Greek form of the pharaoh's name, which is more properly Khafre or Khafra. He is not to be confused with Khephnes, a fictional Egyptian possessed by a Yithian, who by Lovecraft's chronology lived a thousand years later.

Khafre is credited by some with building the Second Pyramid and the Great Sphinx, whose face is thought by some to have been carved in his likeness. His statue in the Egyptian Museum in Cairo is "one of the most important and iconic surviving sculptures from ancient Egypt."

According to Lovecraft (: "Imprisoned with the Pharaohs"), Khephren built the Second Pyramid shortly after 2800 BCE. He restored (rather than constructed) the statue of the Great Sphinx; its face was "probably altered to form a colossal portrait" of Khephren, "that men might look at the colossus without fear." He also built the Temple of the Sphinx, a "yawning gateway temple" in which was found a life-size diorite statue of Khephren that was moved to the Cairo Museum.

entities.name: Legend Horror
entities.description:
The Legend Horror also known as the Kraken is a colossal talking creature resembling an octopus. It battles the Fawcett Comics' superhero Captain Marvel in the final issue of Whiz Comics #155, from 1953. The story uses many Cthulhu Mythos terms such as "gibbering" as well as noting that had the alter ego of Captain Marvel, Billy Batson, been able to make sound he would have screamed in the process of going insane at the sight of the Legend Horror. Very obviously, and given the strong shift to horror content that had recently taken place in American comic books, this was inspired by Mythos stories and in particular the entity Cthulhu.

The Legend Horror is abducting humans then keeping them to devour later by stacking them in a larder resembling a giant frozen food section from a supermarket.

The Legend Horror even has servitors: gigantic intelligent vampire bats that swoop in and easily grab human victims, carrying them off to the lair of the Legend Horror.

entities.name: Lilith
entities.description:
Great Ones (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands) Old Ones (formerly)

Lilith is a demonic entity from Jewish mythology, incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by H. P. Lovecraft's short story "The Horror at Red Hook". Since then, she has been reused by other authors in stories and role-playing game material.

Traditionally, Lilith is described as an ageless woman of sinister beauty, known for visiting sleeping men, with whom she then engages in somnambular sex. However, Lovecraft changes her appearance, depicting her as an entity with "leprous limbs" and phosphorescent skin (: "The Horror at Red Hook").

According to one account, she is an avatar of Our Ladies of Sorrow (: Our Ladies of Sorrow), but according to others, she is either a Great One (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands) or an Ancient One that can also assume the form of a female gug in our material plane (: Cthulhu Dark Ages). In the Malleus Monstrorum, it is said that she was originally an Ancient One (2006 edition) or Old One (2020 edition), but was banished to Earth's Dreamlands at some unknown time and became a Great One. It is said that she will someday regain enough strength to escape from the Dreamlands (: Malleus Monstrorum).
