entities.name: Magna Mater
entities.description:
Magna Mater is referenced as Cybele in the H. P. Lovecraft story "The Rats in the Walls".

The Miskatonic University Library Association Monograph supplement The Pastores identifies the Magna Mater as an avatar of Shub-Niggurath, held in worship in medieval France by an extensive cult of powerful humans and other supernatural entities.

Magna Mater is a Latin phrase meaning 'Great Mother' and was used historically as a title in Ancient Rome for both Cybele, a middle eastern cult with transvestite and eunuch priests and ecstatic public rituals and processions involving ritual slashing and blood spilling, and more generally in ancient syncretic religious beliefs as being the female principle in its highest and most powerful form, that of the giver of life, who impliedly could also take it away. In this sense it is cognate with the "Earth Monster" from South American ancient religion or the Amazonian Yacumama. More simply, a humanoid personification of Mother Nature as both the mother of us all, and the soil to which we will return.

entities.name: Mormo
entities.description:
Mormo is a shapeshifting female entity known for having three forms: The first form, is a mocking vampire-like maiden who may or may not be wearing Victorian Era style clothing; Second, a gorgon-like creature with tentacles for hair instead of snakes; And lastly, a large toad-like creature with tentacles for a face, akin to her servitors the Moon-beasts.

In the story The Horror At Red Hook, H. P. Lovecraft directly connected Mormo to Lilith. He referenced Hippolytus, but put a more sinister twist upon the worship of Mormo.

As the chant closed, a general shout went up, and hissing sounds nearly drowned the croaking of the cracked bass organ. Then a gasp as from many throats, and a babel of barked and bleated words - 'Lilith, Great Lilith, behold the Bridegroom!' More cries, a clamour of rioting, and the sharp, clicking footfalls of a running figure.|H.P. Lovecraft, "The Horror at Red Hook"}}

In the story "Hydra", Henry Kuttner equates Gorgo, Mormo, the Thousand-Faced Moon and the Magna Mater with Hydra.

entities.name: Nodens
entities.description:
Nodens (also known as Lord of the Great Abyss) is a healing god from Celtic mythology, incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by H. P. Lovecraft's short story "The Strange High House in the Mist". The character is generally depicted as being an inhabitant of the Dreamlands and the master of the night-gaunts, a servitor race of flying creatures.

Later writers, starting with August Derleth, refer to Nodens as an Elder God. (: "A Note on the Cthulhu Mythos") Lin Carter suggested that Nodens is likely the leader of the Elder Gods (it is considered to be either Nodens or Kthanid). (: "The Necronomicon: The Dee Translation")

Nodens is an "archaic" god served by the night-gaunts. He seems to be somewhat benevolent, opposing the frightening Nyarlathotep, and helping Randolph Carter to find his way back to the waking world, along with S'ngac. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

Nodens is also described with "...the grey and awful form of primal Nodens, Lord of the Great Abyss". He appeared to Thomas Olney and the One, along with the ocean god Neptune and a procession of tritons and nereids. Nodens was riding a "vast crenulate shell" carried by dolphins. He extended a hand to help Olney and the One board the shell carriage and took off "into the limitless aether". (: "The Strange High House in the Mist")

entities.name: Nyx
entities.description:
Nyx is an fictional deity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character's background was developed by Yuke Kabula in the Shangri-La 93: Ghizguth Mythos anthology, while her first appearance would be in the short story "Erebus".

She is thought to be an adaptation of Nyx, the goddess of the night in Greek mythology, incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos.

In Greek mythology, Nyx is the goddess and personification of the night. In Hesiod's Theogony, she is the offspring of Chaos, and the mother of Aether and Hemera by Erebus.

Nyx was originally an Elder God that embodies the primordial Night as an active cosmic force. She is described as the daughter of the Darkness and granddaughter of Azathoth, the Blind Idiot God, but also as the mother of Hypnos, Thanatos and the race of moonborn. She manifests not as a fixed being but through avatars, objects (like a green pearl), songs, rituals, dreams, and even crystalline or slimy substances. Nyx is considered a renegade among Elder Gods. She once allied with Ghizguth to seal away Ab-T'bohugha, but later turned against him, creating cosmic tension between abyssal and celestial waters. Her most prominent avatar is Petra, a beautiful young woman (appearing around 20) with brown hair, emerald-green eyes that obsess those who gaze into them, and a distinctive green pearl earring.

entities.name: Odin
entities.description:
Odin is a deity in Norse mythology, the ruler of Asgard and chief god of the Æsir tribe of deities.

A more Lovecraftian-like depiction of Odin appears as the main antagonist of Robert E. Howard's short story "The Cairn on the Headland".

During the Dark Ages, Odin frequently appeared on Earth to his worshippers, either to accept human sacrifices or assist them in battles as a Norse warrior. Due to him taking the form of a human, Odin was subjected to many of the limitations of humanity and could be harmed by certain weapons. After being fatally wounded in the Battle of Clontarf near Dublin, Ireland, Odin's body was buried with the stones of the cairn by Red Cumal, an Irish warrior who was fighting against the pagan Viking invaders. Thereafter, Christianity became triumphant over his religion, with Odin eventually being forgotten to time.

Hundreds of years later, Odin was dug up to be resurrected by the touch of holly. The human-like body was altered in horrific transmutation, now taking the form of a "slavering monster" with "shadowy tentacle-like arms outspread." Odin confronted James O'Brien, the reincarnation of Red Cumal, who managed to defeat him with the cross of Saint Brandon, banishing the heathen god back to the stars where it came from. (: "The Cairn on the Headland")
entities.short_description: Odin is a deity in Norse mythology, the ruler of Asgard and chief god of the Æsir tribe of deities.

entities.name: Pan
entities.description:
Pan is an ancient Greek god often associated with pastoral scenery, music and fertility. He is typically represented as a humanoid figure with the legs and horns of a goat, similar to the mythic fauns. His name is the origin of the word panic.

In ancient times, the god Pan was said to dwell in Mount Maenalus, in Arcadia, and was accompanied by strange creatures named Panisci. (: "The Tree")

Later on, Pan and the other gods entered a death-like sleep, but shall wake up and reclaim their domains someday. (: "Poetry and the Gods")

In The Great God Pan, by Arthur Machen, the titular deity is unseen, but plays a pivotal role by impregnating a woman who took part in a scientific experiment to see beyond the fabric of reality (similar to H. P. Lovecraft's "From Beyond"). This union results in the birth of a deceptively human child named Helen Vaughan, who grows up to commit terrible acts (: The Great God Pan). In Lovecraft's "The Dunwich Horror", Henry Armitage mentions Machen's story in connection to the case of Wilbur Whateley.

entities.name: Phorcys
entities.description:
Phorcys is a monster from Greek mythology. The Marvel Comics incarnation first appeared in the 2nd issue of the comic book miniseries X-Men vs Agents of Atlas by Jeff Parker and Gabriel Hardman.

In the Marvel version of mythology, Phorcys is the son of the Elder God Set. Like his father Set, the sea god Phorcys is known to have spawned many monsters, ones known to humans in their mythologies and which are involved in the histories of the Olympians and Asgardians. He is 200 ft tall, possesses super strength, and the ability to regenerate. It has clawed hands and several long tentacles surrounding its mouth. It can psychically control the Sirens.

entities.name: Jacques Roulet
entities.description:
Jacques Roulet is a historical figure from 16th century France who is mentioned in H. P. Lovecraft's story "The Shunned House"; the story implies that Jacques is the ancestor of the story's fictional villains, Etienne and Paul Roulet.

The story's narrator, discussing the history of Providence's Roulet family, recalls an "ominous item in the annals of morbid horror": the creature Jacques Roulet, of Caude, who in 1598 was condemned to death as a daemoniac but afterward saved from the stake by the Paris parliament and shut in a madhouse. He had been found covered with blood and shreds of flesh in a wood, shortly after the killing and rending of a boy by a pair of wolves. One wolf was seen to lope away unhurt.

Compare this to the nonfiction account given in a blog on social history in central France:One werewolf trial took place in the Touraine in Angers in 1598. In that year two hunters came across two wolves feeding on the body of a dead 15 year old boy. As they chased the wolves into the forest they came across Jacques Roulet with his clothing in tatters, his hands drenched in blood, and with shreds of human flesh under his fingernails. Roulet was dragged before the court in Angers where he was charged with murder. During his questioning, when he may well have been tortured, Jacques Roulet claimed that he had been a werewolf ever since using a salve his parents had given him years before....

Roulet was sentenced to death on the grounds of murder, werewolfism, and cannibalism. He eventually appealed to the Parliament of Paris and his sentence was revoked and reduced to two years in a mental institution on the grounds that his testimony was taken under duress and during a time that he was not of a sound mind.The narrator notes the "queer significance as to name and place", since the story's Roulet family also comes from Caude. He speculates that if the "Providence gossips" had "generally known of it...the coincidence of names would have brought some drastic and frightened action."

entities.short_description: Saturn (also known as Cronus) is a god in a human form, first appearing in the H. P. Lovecraft poem "Simplicity: A Poem"'. He is a god in Ancient Roman mythology and is known for devouring his children.

entities.name: Sphinx
entities.description:
The Sphinx was an ancient entity known, among other places, in Egypt.

The famous Great Sphinx of Giza was patterned after the true Sphinx, but the face was later replaced with the human one of the Pharoh Khephren. It seems that it was something close to life-size, for the real Sphinx's paws were the size of hippopotami. (: "Imprisoned with the Pharaohs")

The real Sphinx's paws were covered in yellow fur, and each toe was equipped with a retractable claw. Harry Houdini, who caught sight of the paw, but not the rest of the creature, mistook each of the five toes for a head, and the claws for rigid tentacles that extended forward to consume food. (: "Imprisoned with the Pharaohs")

The Sphinx-statues of Sarkomand resembled vast winged lions. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath) However, the Great Sphinx of Giza has no wings.

entities.name: Taranushi
entities.description:
Taranushi (also known as Lord of the Jinn) is a jinn from North African mythology. It was later incorporated into the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game by Chaosium. (: Cthulhu Invictus)

Taranushi is an Outer God who was summoned to Earth by Simoon, a Saharan sorcerer. Easily breaking free of his spell, Taranushi coerced Simoon to bring the jinn to Earth. Which Taranushi let loose on the peoples of the Arabian desert and eastern Libya.

For decades, the Earth was their playground, traveling back and forth from their home dimension. Upon Simoon's death, they found themselves unable to return home. Enraged, the jinn rebelled against Taranushi, who was able to fight them off, but lost control of the jinn. He is both worshiped and hated by the jinn.

His giant form appears insubstantial as if made of smoke. One with greyish skin and tusks coming out of its mouth. Taranushi can take a form that is human in shape, jinn, or a combination of the two.

entities.name: Tiráwa
entities.description:
In the real world, Atí'as Tirawa, a.k.a. Tirawahat, is a creator deity from Pawnee mythology. In the Cthulhu Mythos stories of H. P. Lovecraft and Zealia Bishop, this deity is known as Tiráwa, and is venerated by the Wichita people of Oklahoma.

Tiráwa is a protective god worshiped by the Wichita. His worshipers believe that Tiráwa is the father of men, just as Yig is the father of snakes, and may be called to protect his children against the wrath of Yig. (: "The Curse of Yig")

According to Grey Eagle, Yig and Tiráwa dwell in the underground with the K'n-yanians (: The Mound) Since the K'n-yanians worship idols of Yig and Cthulhu, and believe that the latter brought the ancestors of humanity to Earth from the stars, it is possible that Tiráwa might be associated with Cthulhu.

entities.name: Yaldabaoth
entities.description:
Yaldabaoth, The Demiurge is a deity associated with Platonism and Gnosticism sects. According to some creeds of Platonic roots, at first matter did not exist and everything was spirit. However, Yaldabaoth, a proud and jealous god, tried to structure everything by recreating the spirit in a material world and confining everything on that plane. But he only succeeded in fabricating an imperfect world, a crude imitation of the original spirit. His arrogant personality prevented him from admitting his mistake.

Yaldabaoth, presumptuous and stupid, hates men because, unlike him, they have souls, which he lacks and which he wishes to obtain by any means, although it is impossible for him. Therefore, he mistreats, punishes and represses mortals to take revenge on them. (: Apocryphon of John, On the Origin of the World, Hypostasis of the Archons)

"Samaël" is one of the mystical words used by occultist Robert Suydam, along with "Sephiroth" and "Ashmodai". (: "The Horror at Red Hook") According to one account, Samael is an avatar of Nyarlathotep. (: "What Dark God?")

The term "Yaldabaoth", the name by which it is usually known, tends to be associated with the meaning son of chaos, although there is great controversy regarding this.

entities.name: Yamata no Orochi
entities.description:
Yamata no Orochi (sometimes spelled Yamatano Orochi) is a titanic dragon/serpent of Japanese mythology. It was first recorded in the Kojiki, an early Japanese chronicle of myths, legends, hymns, genealogies, oral traditions, and semi-historical accounts.

In Marvel Comics, Yamata no Orochi was first mentioned in the comic book issue Black Axe Vol 1 #2, but would not officially appear until Storm Vol 5 #11. In the Marvel Multiverse, Yamata no Orochi is the offspring of the Elder God Set. It was a colossal serpentine dragon with eight heads and eight tails, whose length extended across multiple mountains. The Japanese god Susa-No-O-Izumo slayed the dragon, and afterwards found within its belly, the perfect sword, the Grasscutter.

Yamata no Orochi is also mentioned several times in the Japanese version of the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu.

In The Twilight Angel, a scenario written by Jun Arisaka and published by HobbyJapan, Yamata no Orochi is resurrected from the Pyramid of Lake Shinji by the mastermind Ranko Yūdomari toward the end of the story. Yamata no Orochi is depicted as a ten-headed fiery dragon, and its true form is a massive mass of energy from another dimension. It is approximately 546.8 yards long, and each of its heads can incinerate an area with a diameter of about 0.62 miles using heat rays reaching 18,032°F. While the NPCs Yuri Katagiri and Yūko Katagiri hold it back, the player characters fight Ranko Yūdomari.

entities.name: Ysbaddaden
entities.description:
Ysbaddaden, is a fictional extraterrestrial being created by American author Kevin L. O'Brien for his short Cthulhu Mythos story "October Surprise".

According to The Book of Merlin, Ysbaddaden and its sibling Scathach were the offspring of Hzioulquoigmnzhah and Klosmiebhyx on distant Yuggoth. When the cannibalistic Cxaxukluth came in search of nourishment, Ysbaddaden and Scathach were whisked off to Cykranosh by Hzioulquoigmnzhah. What became if it afterwards is not recorded (: "October Surprise").

Ysbaddaden, Chief of Giants is the name of a character from Welsh mythology which is loosely related to the legend of King Arthur. According to the folklore, Ysbaddaden was killed by a nobleman named Goreu after it killed many of his siblings.

entities.name: Derek Adams
entities.description:
Derek Adams is a character created by Scottish author William Meikle for his Midnight Eye Files series of occult detective stories. He made his first appearance in the 2005 novel The Amulet, and has since appeared in at least fifteen different stories.

Adams is a hard-drinking, heavy-smoking private detective based in Glasgow, Scotland, he is a man with an open mind and a certain experience in dealing with the supernatural. His encounters with the bizarre include foiling the plans of Cthulhu cultists to bring their master to Earth, a run-in with brain-snatching Mi-Go, and a team-up with Arkham private dick Frank Nardi while on the case of mysterious signals from the great beyond.

Once a student at Glasgow University studying Organic Chemistry and Molecular Biology, while in attendance Adams met and fell in love with a woman named Liz. During the course of their occasionally-stormy relationship Liz, unbeknownst to Adams, became pregnant; during a drunken row where she attempted to explain her situation to him, Adams left Liz alone and returned to the bar. During his absence, Liz committed suicide.

Attempting to reestablish his life, Adams took a course in journalism, eventually landing a menial position on a local rag. However, this failed to hold his interest, and he began to drink heavily.

entities.name: Wendy Adams
entities.description:
Wendy Adams, the Urchin, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games who appears in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos.

When Wendy was very young, her Mama used to let her play with her old necklace, a piece of unusual design featuring an eye surrounded by a shiny star. Wendy was always fascinated by this bauble.

However, her childhood happiness ended when they received word that her father had been lost at sea. This caused a change in Wendy's Mama, and she began to scrawl bizarre symbols all over their house in white chalk, and read books with evil-sounding names. Soon, the authorities took notice, and Wendy's Mama was carted off to the asylum, while Wendy was sent to an orphanage, but not before her Mama gave her a parting gift: the necklace with which she had been so besotted as a child.

Spending several years in the orphanage, Wendy became completely disillusioned with the care given her and, deciding that she would be better off on her own, snuck away to live her life on the streets. Times were difficult for a little girl running with a pack of street kids, but somehow she made it work.

entities.name: Ahtu
entities.description:
Ahtu is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by David Drake for his short story "Than Curse the Darkness".

Ahtu is one of Nyarlathotep's countless avatars, worshipped mainly in central and southern Africa. It manifests in the form of a black column of viscous matter, around fifty feet in diameter, erupting from below the ground. Several golden tentacles sprout from its central mass.

Dame Alice Kilrea likens this entity to a "cancer" that permeates and mutates its environment into an imitation of life which, if allowed to grow unchecked, would eventually cover the entire Earth and transform the planet into "a ball of viscid slime hurtling around the sun", and then stretch its tentacles towards Mars. (: "Than Curse the Darkness")

It is believed that Ahtu can be called only at certain special locations in Africa, such as in the Congo Free State, although others may exist. To contact Ahtu with a spell, a special golden amulet depicting a three-lobed eye wreathed by flames is necessary. (: Arkham Unveiled)

entities.name: Aiueb Gnshal
entities.description:
Aiueb Gnshal (The Eyes Between Worlds) is a fictional entity created by Kevin T. McKinnon and Dylan K. Sharpe for the Call of Cthulhu scenario "The Eyes Between Worlds", which was published in the Miskatonic University Library Association Monograph Strange Tales of Dread and Wonder.

Aiueb Gnshal is a mysterious Lesser Other God who has made his home in a long-lost temple in Bhutan, as well as many other temples. He appears as a formless black void with seven orb-like eyes. It is mainly worshipped by Ghouls who worship him in a defiled cult spoken of in the Cambuluc Scrolls of the wizard Lang-Fu. Looking into the eyes of this horrid being, after a disgusting and awful ritual, will allow you to see into the Court of Azathoth, in which he resides simultaneously as he does across his temples.

In the Cthulhu Mythos, it is said that the Mongolian warlord Temujin, better known as Genghis Khan, had the favour of Aiueb Gnshal.

entities.name: Aku-Shin Kage
entities.description:
Aku-Shin Kage (悪心影, meaning "malicious shadow" and with alternate spelling "Akushin Kage", "Aku-Shin-Kage" or "Akushin-Kage") is one of the avatars of Nyarlathotep. Its first appearance was in the Secrets of Japan supplement for the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

Aku-Shin Kage's field of action is the territory of Japan. Throughout the history of the country, it has caused many wars and confrontations. In fact, it is believed that the warlord Oda Nobunaga was one of the Aku-Shin Kage's human incarnations known as the "Dark Warlord".

Dark Warlord is said to have dictated the work known as "Kuragari no shūkai" (in English, "Manual of the Shadows") to a ninja clan with supernatural powers that carried out a multitude of killings and served the Dark Warlord from the late 12th century to the early 18th century.

In more modern times, due to a long and close affinity with Oda in life, it can take on the human form of the ghost of Nobunaga, appearing age 40. In this guise, the avatar of Nyarlathotep urges on one or more deranged leaders of ultra-right nationalist groups. Nowadays, it resembles a Yotsubishi Heavy Industries businessman advocating a golden age for the Japanese empire in boardrooms.

entities.name: Al Azif
entities.description:
Al Azif is a fictional entity in the Demonbane Mythos. The character was originally created by Jin Haganeya, appearing as one of the main heroines for the visual novel Deus Machina Demonbane.

Al Azif is the humanoid avatar of the Necronomicon, taking the form of a petite young girl with silver hair and jade green eyes in a white dress. Behind her are a pair of small, floating book-like wings composed of grimoire pages. In Magius Style, she accompanies her master in a much smaller, chibi-like form with a black outfit replacing her white dress, while her head grows a pair of black wings that can change into a hat.

As a thousand-year-old grimoire, Al has a high sense of pride and can be arrogant at times. She clashed with Hadou Ruri on multiple occasions because the latter could not tolerate her personality and called her an old book, although their relationship was drastically improved as the story progressed.

Regardless, Al is fundamentally a kind-hearted person who cares deeply about the well-being of those who are close to her. In the past, Al has gone through many different masters, where every single one of them suffered a horrific death after battles against evil forces. This put heavy burden on her as she felt a tremendous guilt over their demise. After her encounter with Daijuuji Kurou, Al slowly opened her heart until she finally developed romantic feelings for him.

entities.name: Aletheia
entities.description:
Aletheia is a fictional deity created by comic book author Tiziano Sclavi for Dylan Dog issue #374 "La Fine dell'Oscuritó" (Sergio Bonelli Editore, November 2017).

Aletheia appears as a large loosely interconnected grouping of enormous hands in the sky, jutting out of clouds and darkness, with each hand having a large eye in the center of its palm. Untold amounts of much smaller but thick cords or threads of metallic flesh extend from the surface of its hands and fingers - the threads of Aletheia.

A thread of Aletheia will interconnect with a human victim at the base of their spine. Attempting to remove the thread - which is about as thick as the spine it attached itself to - with sufficient force will cause the entire spine of the victim to be violently pulled out, leading to an explosively gory demise.

Once connected, a being will at some point experience the call of Aletheia, approaching its summoning point, which will be engulfed in blinding light. Those not called, at Aletheia's disgression, are violently expelled with a painful, but non-lethal searing burn, which flings them back from the light.

entities.name: James Ambrel
entities.description:
James Ambrel is a self-insert character of prolific Cthulhu Mythos author and editor James Ambuehl.

Although little is known of Ambrel, he appears to be an author specialising in occult and paranormal literature. It is possible that he lives in, or near to, Braving, Minnesota.

entities.name: Arkham Detective
entities.description:
The Arkham Detective is a fictional character created by American author and filmmaker Byron Craft for his eponymous series of Cthulhu Mythos stories. The Detective, whose name is never revealed, made his debut appearance in the 2015 novella Cthulhu's Minions.

A hard-boiled detective in the employ of the Prohibition-era Arkham Police Department, the Detective spends his time working for the department's Mythos Division, a subdivision of that agency dedicated to combatting the many and varied supernatural threats which plague the small New England city of Arkham. Despite his lack of jurisdiction outside of his home town, he has been known to travel to other notable Lovecraft Country locations, including Innsmouth and Dunwich. He has been stated to have lost two different partners in the twelve months leading up to the first story.

The Detective was once married with a son but, due to the long hours he spent on the job and with his drinking buddies in the town's many Speakeasies, his wife left him, taking the child with her. He has not spoken to either of them since.

During one of his investigations, a murder-kidnapping which took him to the coastal town of Innsmouth by the sea, the Detective rescued a seven-year-old girl named Allison. The terrors they experienced that night created a strong bond between the two, and he soon adopted the girl. While he is at work his landlady, an elderly, good-natured woman by the name of Mrs. Trumble, takes care of Allison, and has even gone so far as to convert her spare room into a play area for her.

entities.name: Armandra
entities.description:
Armandra is a fictional character created by the late British author Brian Lumley for his Titus Crow series of Cthulhu Mythos stories. She has an important role in Lumley's novel "In the Moons of Borea".

Daughter of the Great Old One Ithaqua, Armandra is a powerful sorceress and priestess who wages war against her parent. She uses magic, but is also telepathic. A highly strung but heroic character, she assists the human protagonists of the Titus Crow series and other interlinked stories against Ithaqua and other Mythos entities until final victory.

entities.name: Azathoth's aliases
entities.description:
As one of the most prominent elements in the Cthulhu Mythos, the Outer God Azathoth has gone through many different aliases over the years. This page offers a guide to the various names of Azathoth, including the avatars employed by this eldritch abomination.

entities.name: Agnes Baker
entities.description:
Agnes Baker, the Waitress, is a fictional character who first appeared in Fantasy Flight Games' Second Edition of Arkham Horror, but who has since gone on to feature in other Arkham Horror Files lines of Cthulhu Mythos-related games and fiction.

Once nothing more than a waitress at a small-time Arkham diner, when changing a light bulb one day, Agnes fell from the ladder and hit her head, an event which changed her life forever.

Upon awakening at the hospital, she found that the trauma to her head had unlocked memories of a past life untold millennia ago in a strange place called Hyperborea. There, she had been a powerful spellcaster, able to bend the winds of magic to her will. However, the memories also told her that she had been eventually slain by a creature of nightmares.

Finally plucking up the courage to try out one of the spells for herself, to her astonishment she found out that they actually worked. Afterwards, Agnes spent her time quietly developing these new abilities, although she was always careful to do so well away from the prying eyes of others.

entities.name: Tony Balnco
entities.description:
Tony Balnco is a minor character created by American author C. J. Henderson for his Frank Nardi series of short stories.

A police officer for the NYPD, upon retirement Balnco partnered with three other former detectives including Frank Nardi to form the Arkham Detective Agency, a private investigations company which specialised in cases with a supernatural aspect.

Whilst providing security for an exhibit on ancient Egyptian culture at Arkham's Miskatonic University, Balnco encountered a mysterious entity who had visited the display for reasons of its own. Inadvertently insulting the being, he suffered a gruesome fate at its hands, being turned into a great gobbet of living, suffering flesh. At the request of Frank Nardi, who seemed to have gained a measure of respect from the entity, he was transformed back to a human corpse upon his death (: "Cruelty" by C. J. Henderson).

Some months later the entity, now confirmed to have been the Outer God Nyarlathotep, returned to Balnco and gave him new life, encouraging him to seek out Frank Nardi and murder him. Why it chose to do this is not revealed. Luckily for Nardi, however, he was able to turn the tables on his would-be attacker and ended Balnco's life for good, granting his former friend the closure he so desperately sought (: "Closure" by Glynn Owen Barrass).

entities.name: Roland Banks
entities.description:
Roland Banks, the Fed, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror series of Cthulhu Mythos publications. He made his first appearance in the 2009 expansion Innsmouth Horror.

As can be gathered from Fantasy Flight's various flavour texts, Roland is known for being something of a stickler for the rules. On occasion, however, in extraordinary circumstances, he is shown to be willing to throw procedure out of the window in the interests of serving justice, as seen when he tackled the case of a murdered orchestra (see "History," below).

Banks had been a model agent for his entire career, but during one particular investigation had the bad luck to get caught up in a local situation in which corrupt local authorities had struck a deal with local bootleggers to supply their town with illegal hooch. Although Banks tried to bring the authorities to justice, it transpired that at least one of the perpetrators had had connections high in the federal bureaucracy. Immediately removed from the case, he was reassigned, and word went out within the bureau that Banks was now blacklisted.(: The Dirge of Reason)

Banks was subsequently assigned to investigate a case in the jurisdiction of Arkham, the case of a murdered orchestra which the Bureau had been pressured to solve by yet more meddling higher-ups, and which his superiors believed would be unsolvable - adding yet another black mark to his record. As it turned out, Banks was far more resourceful and open-minded than his superiors had counted on, and discovered that the orchestra's conductor had been putting ancient Sumerian texts to music, accidentally summoning an otherworldly entity which destroyed them all. Banks managed to defeat the being and close the gate torn open by the orchestra's music, and file a report which seemed plausible yet contained no mention of the supernatural causes which would have had him labelled as a kook.(: The Dirge of Reason)

entities.name: Newt Bardhoff
entities.description:
Lieutenant Newt Bardhoff is a character created by American author Brandon Berntson for his Lovecraft Mysteries trilogy of Cthulhu Mythos novels. He made his debut appearance in 2018's The Night of Dagon.

Bardhoff is a thin man who is usually clean-shaven, who is described as being "pleasant, easy to talk to". A lieutenant in the Innsport Police Department, he is married to a shy bookstore owner named Amelia, and is good friends with the protagonist of The Lovecraft Mysteries, private investigator Devlin Macky. Prior to his marriage, Bardhoff had a "harmless, innocent crush" on Macky's secretary Millie Von Clydesburgh.

Although single at the beginning of the series, at the end of The Night of Dagon Bardhoff is introduced to a shy bookstore owner named Amelia; by the time of the events described in The Lurker at the Threshold, the two have been married for around two years.

After being assigned the case of an artefact stolen from the Innsport Natural History Museum, Bardhoff and his partner Inspector Duke Givens found themselves investigating a missing persons case on the estate of cultist Mordred Haddonfield. Captured by Haddonfield and his undead servant Borgas, they were destined to be sacrificed to the recently-awoken Dagon: the timely intervention of Macky and Millie Von Clydesburgh saved them from this fate, and the pair returned to Innsport to begin an evacuation ahead of Dagon's murderous rampage (: The Night of Dagon).

entities.name: George Barnaby
entities.description:
George Barnaby, the Lawyer, is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games as a playable Investigator for their Arkham Horror Files range of Cthulhu Mythos-related content.

Always one with a strong desire for control over his situation, George spent a month in prison for a crime of which he was innocent. The experience instilled in him a need for justice, and this pushed him into the decision to become a lawyer.

Being a highly charismatic and intelligent man, he proved to be extremely well suited to his chosen profession and, after a long and successful career, retired to spend time with his wife Maria. Their dream was to buy a boat and sail the seven seas in their old age.

However, George's life was shattered when, not long after retiring, Maria was murdered by assailants who wore occult jewelry. Vowing revenge, he tracked the men down to the small city of Arkham, where he prepared his final act of justice.

entities.name: Jenny Barnes
entities.description:
Guinevere "Jenny" Barnes, the Dilettante, is a fictional character created by Chaosium for the first edition of the Arkham Horror cooperative board game. Her character has since been extensively expanded on by Fantasy Flight Games after they acquired the Arkham Horror franchise, appearing in both game expansions and Arkham Horror Fiction releases.

A strikingly attractive woman, Jenny is independently wealthy due to a generous allowance given to her by her father, a professor of Arthurian studies. It was as result of her father's vocation that she was named Guinevere, which she dislikes intensely, choosing to be known as Jenny. She prefers to dress in clothes which are the height of fashion, appears to be very up to date with cultural trends, and carries a pair of nickel-plated .45 automatic pistols. She is well-educated, likely as a result of her upbringing and her travels through Europe (: Hour of the Huntress).

During the Roaring Twenties, Jenny spent a long period attempting to help her sister Izzie overcome mental health problems for which she was committed. Finally, after experiencing burnout from her efforts - which she believed were her parents responsibility - she took the plunge and moved to Paris, desperate to start living her own life. Unfortunately, this caused a rift between the sisters, with Izzie believing that her sibling had abandoned her. With time this breakdown began to be repaired, and Jenny and Izzie's correspondence increased as the two embarked on the long process of reforging their former bond (: Hour of the Huntress).

When Izzie disappeared in the New England town of Arkham, Jenny made her way to Massachusetts in search of the missing woman. There, she discovered that Izzie had first been manipulated into joining, then coerced into assisting, a cult dedicated to the worship of the Outer God Shub-Niggurath. With the assistance of a ragtag group of allies, including tomboy mechanic Lonnie Ritter, Miskatonic University professor Tilde Félix, and Arkham PD officer Galeas Morgan, she managed to thwart the cult's efforts to summon a Dark Young, although the High Priestess was able to make her escape with Izzie as a hostage (: Hour of the Huntress).

entities.name: The Beast
entities.description:
The Beast is a fictional entity created by Keith Herber for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

The Beast is an avatar of Nyarlathotep worshiped in Egypt. It is, in fact, one of the avatars associated with the Sphinx of Giza, the others being the Black Lion, destroyer of Egypt, and the Faceless God. (: The Fungi from Yuggoth)

entities.name: Belasco
entities.description:
Belasco is a supervillain in the fictional Marvel universe, who was created in 1982 and has been an enemy of the X-Men throughout his history.

Belasco is one of Earth's most powerful sorcerers with an encyclopedic knowledge of occult spells from a number of books. He has a superhuman demonic form, is immortal, and has superhuman durability. He was a 13th century sorcerer from Florence, Italy who contacted the Elder Gods and made a pact with them. He kidnapped Dante's beloved, took her to Pangea, and raped her to produce a new race of demons. When she died giving birth, an enraged Dante attacked him and during the fighting he ended up being placed in suspended animation.

In the late 20th century, the volcanic mountain became active, releasing Belasco. During his attempt to repeat history with Ka-Zar's wife Shanna, he ended up trapped in Limbo when Ka-Zar hurls the Bloodstone locket into the volcano. Belasco conquered the demonic pocket dimension of Limbo and then kidnaps 7-yr old Illyana Rasputina (Magik), to use her mutant powers to open a gateway to the Elder Gods and make her his apprentice. The X-Men attempted to rescue her but failed and she remained trapped in Limbo, where he turned her into a demon sorceress. She turned on him, drove him from Limbo and became its ruler.

Belasco became the ruler of the Cat People and later regained control of Limbo. He attempted to wipe out mankind, but his pawn was killed by the Punisher. He later had a contest with the fear-demon D'Spayre to see if they could corrupt the mutant Cable but failed. Later with the aid of the N'Garai, Belasco fought the X-Men but they emerged victorious with Magik's assistance. He later returned to Limbo and regained his domain. Belasco is obsessed with Magik, not only because of her powers but because he has also fallen in love with her.

entities.name: John Bell
entities.description:
John "Johnny" Bell is a character created by American author Jeffrey Thomas as a recurrent protagonist in his Punktown series of dystopian science fiction stories. He made his first appearance in the 1995 short story "The Bones of the Old Ones".

Bell is described as "a man of thirty-one, with sandy short hair neatly cut and brushed back from his forehead. His eyes were blue and far-spaced, his lips too full for his taste though his ex-wife had called them sensuous"; "[t]here was to his face, oddly, both a boyish quality and a prematurely wasted, haggard aspect."

When first introduced, he is working as a Detective Inspector for a local police force; later appearances show him to have an affinity for jobs involving the protection of others.

In the extra-terrestrial colony of Paxton, Oasis, Bell was involved in the investigation of mass murders and cult activities which eventually led to his involvement in the thwarting of a scheme to return the Old Ones to this plane of existence (: "The Bones of the Old Ones").

entities.description:
Mark Berkenwald is a supporting character created by the late American author C. J. Henderson for his Arkham Detective Agency series of hard-boiled/Cthulhu Mythos stories. A founding partner in the supernaturally-focussed Arkham Detective Agency, Berkenwald is portrayed as neither as senior nor as outspoken as the series' main protagonist, Frank Nardi.

entities.name: Black Buddha
entities.description:
The Black Buddha is an avatar of Nyarlathotep who first appeared in Masayuki Shuno's 2001 novel Kuroi Hotoke.

According to legend, the Black Buddha statue washed ashore at Akuhama in 877 CE, having been part of the cargo of a ship that sank at sea. Its survival was taken as a sign of divine favor, and a Buddhist monk later built a temple around it, which came to be known as Anranji. There, the figure was worshipped as the bodhisattva Kurochier Kanzeon, or simply Kuromi-sama.

Over time, the statue came to be associated with a series of unsettling and supernatural events said to have plagued Anranji for centuries, as well as with Japan's Tendai Buddhist sect.

In the novel, Detective Isurugi was hired to locate a Tang dynasty treasure linked to the 9th-century Tendai monk Enzai, believed to have been lost in a shipwreck. His investigation leads him to Anranji, where Kuromi-sama is venerated, and the case soon takes a darker turn with the discovery of an unidentified corpse. As the mystery unfolds, it is revealed that the Black Buddha is in fact an avatar of Nyarlathotep, whose hidden influence lies behind the temple's long history of inexplicable horrors. (: Kuroi Hotoke)

entities.name: Black Whore
entities.description:
The Black Whore (also known as Abigail Dexter) is a fictional character created by American author Kevin L. O'Brien for his 2006 short story "October Surprise".

After merging with Doctor Ambrose Dexter and turning him into a new avatar for himself, Nyarlathotep impregnated Dexter’s wife with his own seed; the resultant child, Abigail Dexter, would therefore be Nyarlathotep's avatar from birth.

As an adult, Abigail earned her doctorate in nuclear physics and took a post with the United States government. She then masterminded a plot to detonate a nuclear weapon underwater to destroy a Deep One city; this fulfilled the schemes' primary goal of cracking an Elder Sign which held the Great Old One Cthaeghya in imprisonment. (: "October Surprise")

Abigail Dexter's current whereabouts are unknown.

entities.name: The Blackness from the Stars
entities.description:
The Blackness from the Stars is an extraterrestrial entity in the Cthulhu Mythos. Its only appearance is in Chaosium's supplement King of Chicago for their Call of Cthulhu RPG.

The Blackness from the Stars is an immobile blob of living, sentient darkness, torn from the primal fabric of the cosmos at the center of the universe. It is distinguishable in darkness only as a vaguely shimmering, oily patch.

The Blackness is immune to physical threats, and can regenerate itself upon harm by magical threats. Heat, cold, acid, and electricity have no effect. The entity can't endure light: direct sunlight will sear it to dust; even the dimmest light source (such as a candle) can still damage it.

The thing can enthrall nearby victims and make them slaves. Creatures within twenty miles of it can also suffer nightmares of the entity; those with histories of mental instability are most susceptible and therefore often targeted. To defend itself, it can also manipulate the air to create a vortex that spirals from itself to nearby areas.

entities.name: Henry Stephenson Blaine
entities.description:
Dr. Henry Stephenson Blaine is a fictional character created by Lin Carter for his Xothic Legend Cycle.

Henry Stephenson Blaine, Ph.D., was the curator of the Manuscripts Collection at the Sanbourne Institute of Pacific Antiquities in Santiago, California (: "The Dweller in the Tomb"). He once studied Semitic Languages under George Gammell Angell (: "Out of the Ages").

In 1928, Dr. Blaine was in charge of making an inventory of the collection of artifacts and manuscripts that formerly belonged to the late Prof. Harold Hadley Copeland. Among Copeland's possessions was a carved jade idol of Zoth-Ommog and a copy of the Yuggya Chants. The idol gave Blaine nightmares and affected his mind, showing him images of the submerged Zoth-Ommog and trying to influence Blaine to remove the Elder Sign that kept the god imprisoned. At night, Blaine was afflicted with episodes of somnambulism in which he would walk to the beach at Wexton Pier with a paper containing an incantation copied from the Yuggya Chants. One night, he was found sleepwalking into the sea. Upon being awakened by the cops who located him, Blaine caught sight of at least one Yugg diving into the water. After that episode, Blaine was committed to Mercy Hospital Psychiatric Emergency under the care of Dr. Robinson Dambler. For the next two months, Blaine spoke nothing other than repeating the word "Yugg" and tried to blind himself 11 times. (: "Out of the Ages")

He was succeeded as curator by his friend and former assistant Arthur Wilcox Hodgkins. (: "Out of the Ages", "The Horror in the Gallery")

entities.name: William Blake
entities.description:
William Blake is a recurrent character in the works of British author David Hambling, and the primary focus of a story cycle to which he lends his name.

Born in the early 20th century, by the 1920s Blake was one of the Bright Young Things, a term given to the post-World War I generation of the London party scene. While studying for his PhD, he made a living by tutoring promising lower-achievers, at that time renting a room in the house of an older couple by the name of Hall (: "The Dulwich Horror of 1927").

Blake was never to finish his degree, however, as a result of an encounter with an extra-dimensional entity; the same encounter left him with near-fatal injuries, killing most of his friends and putting the two other survivors forever beyond his reach (: "The Dulwich Horror of 1927").

Later in life, Blake would become a teacher, living a semi-itinerant life and moving regularly in an effort to leave his past behind him (: "The Monsters in the Park").

entities.name: Bloated Woman
entities.description:
The Bloated Woman, also known as the Goddess of the Black Fan, is a fictional entity created by American games designer Scott David Aniolowski for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu role-playing game. She made her first appearance in the critically acclaimed 1984 scenario supplement Masks of Nyarlathotep.

An avatar of Nyarlathotep active in and around China, the Bloated Woman is described as "a 600 pound, seven-foot-tall being vaguely resembling an obese human female, with tentacles in place of arms and nose, five perfect cupids-bow mouths made hideous by clusters of protruding tangs, and wearing a yellow-and-black tunic of a material resembling fine silk, in the belt of which hang six sickles and the mystic Black Fan". However, the fan allows her to project the appearance of a beautiful young Asian woman: without it, she reverts to her "natural" appearance.

She is worshipped by the Order of the Bloated Woman, a historical organisation which has been in her service for millennia.

entities.name: Bones
entities.description:
Bones (real name unknown, but used the alias of Bobby Anderson) is a fictional character created by American author Armand Rosamilia for his Keyport Cthulhu series of Mythos stories.

A heavy-set former gang member, Bones has a tremendous capacity for violence, but has also displayed great compassion when dealing with those in need. He possesses a seemingly supernatural ability to judge the character of others, although he believes it only works on around 25% of those he meets.

In the first book of the series, Bones stole a mysterious artefact which his biker club had been hired to obtain before going on the run from his former associates under a false identity. He eventually found himself in the degenerate town of Keyport where he discovered the sinister Esoteric Order of Dagon, which was trying to awaken the Great Old One Cthulhu. Joining forces with a ragtag group of people who were fighting back against the cult, he succeeded in saving a girl named Tina from becoming a human sacrifice, but his own life was hanging in the balance at the book's conclusion.

entities.name: John Henry Booth
entities.description:
John Henry Booth is a character created by C. T. Phipps for the eponymous series of Mythos novels Cthulhu Armageddon.

John Henry Booth is a middle aged African American man with grizzled features and is a physically imposing specimen. He prefers to dress in the weather beaten attire of a New Arkham Ranger or those of a cattle rancher.

John is a former Ranger that led Gamma Squadron for the Council of Leaders in New Arkham. He spent many years traveling and charting the Wasteland outside of his city-state in hopes of helping humanity's pockets of survivors. Unlike the majority of his fellow Rangers, John held little animus to mutants or members of human-related races like the Deep Ones or Ghouls.

John was raised as the son of Marcus Booth and Winifred Booth. When he was a boy, his father murdered his mother and attempted to kill him before being killed by John in return. The reason for this was becasue Marcus Booth had discovered John was not his biological son. He was in fact conceived by an unknown inhuman father (at the behest of magician-scientist, Alan Ward).

entities.description:
C'thalpa is a fictional entity created by Dominique Balczesak for the Call of Cthulhu scenario "Paris, Rêve ou Réalité", featured in the licensed gaming supplement Les Années Folles (1988).

Almost nothing is known of this entity other than that it has some kind of relationship to the entity known as Shterot. Its only mention consists of a single of line in the scenario "Paris, Rêve ou Réalité", which says "SHTEROT, defeated, has returned to the bosom of C'THALPA..."

entities.name: Creighton Capshaw
entities.description:
Creighton Capshaw is a fictional character created by American author Brandon Berntson for his Lovecraft Mysteries trilogy of Cthulhu Mythos stories. He made his debut appearance in the first book in the series, 2018's The Night of Dagon.

The curator of Innsport's Natural History Museum, Capshaw is described as "a short, portly man with a salt and pepper beard and mustache" with "tiny round spectacles on a boyish, cherubic face … his eyes … beady but bright blue."

Capshaw has an inveterate interest in ancient artefacts, which is likely what brought him to the academic position which he holds in the series.

Before the events of The Lovecraft Mysteries, Capshaw had been a long-time friend of the wealthy antiquarian Mordred Haddonfield, but over the years their relationship deteriorated into a bitter rivalry. At the beginning of the series, Capshaw's museum came into possession of the Silver Bluebell, also known as the Shadow of Dagon. Haddonfield, by this time a devoted cultist of that dark god, hired private eye Devlin Macky to steal the artefact from Capshaw's office (EXP: The Night of Dagon).

entities.name: Carsai the King
entities.description:
Carsai the King is the leader of the Citadel of the Black. It is an enigmatic being who's always covered in smoke and whose clothes or burning eyes are rarely seen. He frequently invites people to the place, whether they are victims, followers of the Great Old Ones, or people from Golarion who simply grab his attention. It is a neutral zone between the Old Cults and the Dominion of the Black, and Carsai attends to both sides.

The powerful immortal leader Carsai the King is the closest thing the planet-god Aucturn has to a ruler and whose true form and nature are unknown. A High Priest of Nyarlathotep, he has ruled the Citadel of the Black for centuries. However, he does so autocratically, and the citadel is not a theocracy. He is suspected of being an avatar of the Empty Traveler, who is in turn an avatar of Nyarlathotep. There are also those who comment that it could be the Black Pharaoh.

He tends to appears in public frequently. Each of his appearances gathers multitudes of cultists who esteem him. His charismatic speeches are often broadcast on the Pact Worlds, frequently causing jubilant screams and spontaneous ecstatic suicides. Aucturn's defense facing the Dominion of the Black and his being a reasonable figure on an alien planet caused the Pact Council to accept Aucturn as a protectorate of the Pact Worlds, if only out of necessity and proximity. While this means that he may have a representative on the council (usually Carsai or his associates), he does not have much power on planets or moons in the system.

Interestingly, the media leader's portrayal of an anti-hero (a handsome rebel protecting the Pact Worlds from terrible horrors) has increased devotion to Nyarlathotep and the Outer Gods in the Pact Worlds.

entities.name: Cgfthgnm'o'th
entities.description:
Cgfthgnm'o'th is a fictional monster created by Brian Lumley for his novel The Burrowers Beneath.

A creature of gargantuan proportions, Cgfthgnm'o'th's actual appearance was unknown, although it is described as a Chthonian and thus presumably resembles the other members of its species. From underground soundings conducted on the area where its body dissolved was estimated to have been nearly a quarter of a mile long and a third that distance in width. It was known to have been capable of extruding enormous grey tentacles with crimson mouths at the tips, which it used to consume any humans unfortunate enough to come within its reach.

When the Wilmarth Foundation, a group of humans with knowledge of the Cthulhu Cycle Deities and who were dedicated to destroying them, launched the Great Britain Project, their telepaths located Cgfthgnm'o'th in an undisclosed locale beneath the British countryside, possibly somewhere in Scotland. Cgfthgnm'o'th, a child of Ubbo-Sathla and one of the lesser minions of the Great Old Ones who appeared to be directly affiliated with Cthulhu himself, had been imprisoned there aeons ago by the Elder Gods, who held it there through the use of their Star Stones.

The Wilmarth Foundation planned to use an enormous modified drilling rig with an explosive-tipped harpoon to reach and destroy the creature deep in its subterranean lair and, although their plan was ultimately successful, lost a great deal of their equipment and a number of their personnel during the operation, including one of their valuable telepaths, a man named Gordon Finch.

entities.name: Lily Chen
entities.description:
Lily Chen, the Martial Artist, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for inclusion in their vision of H. P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos.

The day after Lily's birth on mainland China to a pair of impoverished peasants, a group of mysterious monks arrived on the doorstep. Claiming to be searching for a “child of prophecy,” they told Lily's parents that their child was the one they sought. Despite their obvious shock that the babe was female, the monks expressed their desire to take her away and train her for a task of great importance; after receiving assurances that Lily would be well looked after, her parents agreed.

From the time she could take to her feet alone, the monks trained Lily in every combat technique they knew, and even went so far as to bring in instructors from across the globe. Lily absorbed all of their teachings with ease, and in the process achieved a state of harmony between her mind and body that few ever attain.

Then, in 1926, one of the monastery monks leapt from his meditations screaming “the Great Eye is opening! The final days are upon us!” before dropping down dead. Taking this as a sign that her purpose was near at hand, Lily made her way to Arkham, where she searched for clues on how to defeat whatever ancient evil was threatening existence.

entities.description:
Chig is an entity first made mention of in The Revelations of Glaaki, which appears to have been its only reference to date (: "The Inhabitant of the Lake"). It is apparently some form of deity worshipped by the alien yarkdao, whose Priests of Chig undertake devotional rituals lasting three-and-quarter years in length.

entities.name: Chorazin
entities.description:
The Chorazin is an avatar of Cthulhu created by Chaosium for their role-playing game Call of Cthulhu.

The psychic manifestation of Cthulhu's will, the Chorazin appears as an ethereal representation of its "parent" entity, but can only make its presence known through the dreams and nightmares of those nearby. Using this method to spread madness and chaos, the Chorazin will slowly absorb the insanity it creates and, once it reaches a critical mass, explodes into our dimension in a flash of raw energy. This mass will gestate over the course of the next twelve hours, until finally a full-size representation of Cthulhu with all of its powers and abilities emerges. Once manifested in this way, the Chorazin is only vulnerable to electricity and certain types of magic.

entities.name: Harold Clemmens
entities.description:
Harold Clemmens is a character created by C. J. Henderson as part of his Arkham Detective Agency series.

At the time the stories are set, Harold Clemmens is the president of Miskatonic University, Arkham's premier higher-learning institution. C. J. Henderson describes him as:

Despite his appearance, he is portrayed as being something of a visionary, making such decisions as retaining the services of a private detective agency: not only as physical security, but to monitor Arkham's underworld for rumours of any criminal activities directed towards the university. Highly intelligent, he also appears to have at least a rudimentary knowledge of the gods and monsters of the Mythos, as shown in the short story "Cruelty".

entities.name: Cloud-Thing
entities.description:
The Cloud-Thing is a fictional entity created by American author and games designer Kevin A. Ross for the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. It first appeared in "Thunder in the Blood", a scenario included in the supplement End of the World (Triad Entertainments, 1994).

The Cloud-Thing is one of five Lesser Other Gods from the Court of Azathoth that appeared during a summoning of Azathoth near San Lucas. It appears as a cloudy mass with shimmering bursts of purplish light emanating from within it, as well as a funnel-like extension that reaches almost to the ground beneath, which it uses to suck victims into itself. It leaves behind a light rain of purplish crystals in its wake. (: End of the World)

Its power is weaker than that of other deities, and while it is sometimes summoned by Azathoth when Azathoth appears, it cannot leave the area on its own, even after Azathoth has departed. Furthermore, destroying it is difficult for humans, but not impossible. For this reason, it is extremely timid. In fact, if it feels threatened or if any kind of “Bind” or “Dismiss” spells are cast on it, it flees into the clouds. (: Malleus Monstrorum, 2006 edition)

Category:Outer Gods Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works

entities.name: Harold Hadley Copeland
entities.description:
Prof. Harold Hadley Copeland is a fictional character created by Lin Carter for his Cthulhu Mythos short story "The Dweller in the Tomb".

Prof. Copeland was an eminent archaeologist, one of the world's leading authorities on ancient civilisations of the Pacific area. He co-founded the Pacific Area Archaeological Association and was, at some point, president of it, prior to his compulsory resignation in 1911. While his earlier works were lauded as brilliant, Copeland's interest in unorthodox hypotheses, such as touching upon the existence and worship of Cthulhu and particularly about the existence of the lost continent of Mu, led to the gradual decline of his reputation.

His Prehistory in the Pacific: A Preliminary Investigation with Reference to the Myth Patterns of Southeast Asia (1902) was universally admired and acclaimed. Polynesian Mythology, with a Note on the Cthulhu Legend Cycle (1906) was more controversial, but still regarded as "a massive work of scientific research". However, after reading the Ponape Scripture, Copeland became obsessed with finding the tomb of Zanthu, a hierophant who escaped the destruction of Mu, and the legendary Zanthu Tablets. His next published book, The Prehistoric Pacific in the Light of the Ponape Scripture (1911), resulted in his being asked to resign from the Pacific Area Archaeological Association.

After his academic fall from grace, Copeland organised the Copeland-Ellington expedition to central Asia, which penetrated the Plateau of Tsang in 1913 to search for the tomb of Zanthu. Ellington died of red-water fever only a few days after the party's departure from Sangup-Koy, leaving Copeland as the solo leader. Deep into the inhospitable deserts of Tsang, other members of the expedition deserted or were taken one by one by the Mi-Go. Copeland felt an inexplicable familiarity with the Plateau, as if he had seen it before in a previous life or in dreams. When confronted by a Mi-Go, he was even more surprised to find that the creature appeared to recognise him, and it was the Mi-Go who was scared of him, rather than vice-versa.

entities.name: Cotoaahd
entities.description:
Cotoaahd is a fictional monster created by Philip José Farmer for his Cthulhu Mythos short story "The Freshman".

According to the folklore of the extinct Tamsiqueg people who inhabited the Miskatonic River area, Cotoaahd was the chief of a group of "evil giants" who battled against the heroes Mikatoonis and Chegaspat. After Chegaspat was killed, Mikatoonis turned the giants into stone with a magical club, thus creating the Tamsiqueg Hills that now stand next to Arkham's Miskatonic University. One of these "curiously shaped" hills is known as Cotoaahd.

It is also said that every few centuries, Cotoaahd manages to free himself from the spell and walk around for a while, before returning to his "rocky slumber". A colossal creature, he can flatten houses and trees under his feet. When Roderick Desmond summoned Cotoaahd with a spell to kill his mother, witnesses reported that the house his mother was in collapsed suddenly "like a giant foot stepped on it", but no one reported seeing the monster, which might suggest that Cotoaahd is invisible.

Miskatonic University's Committee of the Occult Arts and History Department (COTOAAHD), at one point headed by the wizard R. Layamon, appears to be named after this entity. (: "The Freshman")

The Crackling Energy Mass is one of five Lesser Other Gods from the Court of Azathoth that appeared during a summoning of Azathoth near San Lucas. It appears as a large mass of crackling black energy from which ebony lightning lashes out. (: End of the World)

entities.name: Crawling Dead
entities.description:
The Crawling Dead was an eldritch abomination from the fictional universe of Marvel from Marvel Comics.

The Crawling Dead lived in the abandoned ruins of an Atlantean city during the Thurian Age. It was a fleshy throbbing mass of living putrescence with a brain. Centuries earlier, the city's inhabitants had dumped their dead into a communal tomb. Where eldritch forces kept the falling flesh alive, and eventually the corpses began to meld and grow. Until an eldritch abomination arose, one with a brain which was insatiably hungry for more flesh, to further expand.

It used a spell to lure King Kull of Valusia to its lair. The enchanted Kull saw and followed a beautiful women into the city's dark catacombs. Lorkar his bestial humanoid companion was unaffected by the spell and saved Kull's life, at the cost of his own as he was enveloped and digested by the mass. It then tried to consume Kull whom killed the abomination. Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Other Supernatural Beings

entities.name: Titus Crow
entities.description:
Titus Crow is a fictional character created by Brian Lumley for the eponymous Cthulhu Mythos series Titus Crow.

Originally an occultist with a vast knowledge of the history, creatures, and motivations of the in-universe Mythos, Crow also had in his possession a number of artefacts related to the topic. He has displayed an unwavering resolution in stopping the schemes of the Great Old Ones and their minions, even to the point of apparent self-sacrifice.

Later rebuilt to be better in every way after a catastrophic accident, Crow became a persistent nemesis to the Cthulhu Cycle Deities, and Ithaqua in particular.

Lumley's 1987 short story "Inception" reveals the Crow's vast mystical knowledge to stem from being unwittingly baptised in a mind-expanding liquid.

entities.name: Jim Culver
entities.description:
Jim Culver, also known as the Musician, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Files series of Cthulhu Mythos releases. He made his debut appearance in the Dunwich Horror expansion for the second edition of Arkham Horror.

A young black man from New Orleans, Jim Culver inherited a trumpet from his father, one which has caused him no end of trouble: despite being a talented trumpeter, playing the instrument allows him to commune with the dead, and even, on occasion, raise them to life. He also appears to be accepted by the graveyard ghouls, and has been known to exchange information with them.

Since his debut, Culver has appeared in several Fantasy Flight releases, including Eldritch Horror (Horrific Journeys expansion), Elder Sign and Arkham Horror: The Card Game. In 2010 a pre-painted plastic miniature of the character was released as part of the Arkham Horror Premium Figures line, but this has since been discontinued.

entities.name: Cybil
entities.description:
Cybil is a hero in the fictional Army of Darkness universe which expands the world of the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was created in 2009 by Mike Raicht. She first appeared in issue #22 of the 2nd volume of Army of Darkness by Dynamite Entertainment.

Cybil is a woman who was adopted as a child and in her early teens became possessed by a demon which used her as a gateway for other demonic spirits who had escaped hell and possessed others in her community. She was incarcerated in an asylum along with the other possessed patients. Ash Williams and the werewolf Brad searching for the Protectors of the world, identified her as a fellow Protector. They were able to free her and the others from demonic possession.

Cybil joined them in their mission to find other Protectors, becoming a member of the League of Light. Alongside her fellow superheroes, she fought the forces of the Necronomicon. Having failed to prevent the Apocalypse and the end of mankind, the team built a time machine to send two members back in time (Cybil and Brad) with Ash's spirit. They were successful in preventing the possession of Ash by Hell's Prophet thereby altering the timeline. Cybil and Brad disappeared, and the new timeline's Cybil was freed of her demon and the asylum years earlier by this timeline's Brad.

entities.name: D'endrrah
entities.description:
D'endrrah, also known as The Divinity, is a fictional entity created by Pierre Zaplotny for the Call of Cthulhu scenario "La Terza Bocca di D'endrrah", featured in issue #46 of the French role-playing magazine Casus Belli. The character also played a pivotal role in Bryn Fortey's 2021 short story "Beneath the Pimple", published in Vol 5, Issue 4 of the Lovecraftiana zine.

D'endrrah is a shape shifting Outer God who possesses a great hunger for living worlds. It often manifests in the form of a gigantic squid-like monster or a cloud of heavy, smoky, organic matter with millions of teeth, which wanders the cosmos endlessly to devour any world it stumbles across.(source?)

D'endrrah was defeated by Cthulhu when it threatened to devour Earth sometime before the time of ancient Egypt. Stories are also told of the Egyptian god Ra, the god of the sun, who fought this monster in its guise as Apep from his flying chariot.(source?)

Another story tells of how D'endrrah acted on behalf of Yog-Sothoth in a plan to expose and imprison the duplicitous god Olkoth, sealing it beneath a hill in rural Wales. (: "Beneath the Pimple")

entities.name: Damballah
entities.description:
Damballah is a fictional character from Marvel Comics. He was created in 1975 by Roy Thomas, Gerry Conway, and John Buscema and Made his first appearance in issue #152 of the 1st volume of the Avengers comic book series.

Damballah, is the offspring of the Elder God Set. He had worshipers in Zembabwei during the Hyborian Age and in modern day Haiti. When in spirit form, Damballah can travel to Earth where it manifests as a humanoid serpent or a huge snake. It is able to possess serpents and transforms them into versions of its form, and is also able to control snakes. It is able to possess or control others, even those with training in the mystical arts.

entities.name: Daoloth
entities.description:
Daoloth is an Outer God in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Render of the Veils".

Daoloth is an entity that dwells beyond the three dimensions known to humans. Worshipped on Yuggoth and Tond, and formerly in Atlantis, his astrologer-priests are said to be able to see the past and the future, and even how objects extend into and travel between different dimensions.

Daoloth's indescribable shape causes viewers to go mad at the sight of him; thus, he must be summoned in pitch-black darkness using the Daoloth formula, and is known to take a small amount of blood from the summoner. If not held within some kind of magical containment, such as the Pentacle of Planes, he continues to expand and expand — perhaps even to an infinite size. Those enveloped by the god are transported to utterly bizarre and remote worlds, usually perishing as a result. Daoloth's worship is rare on Earth.

One request that can be made to Daoloth, magically contained, is to view things as they really are, not as our veiled senses perceive them. The sight is usually more than one can bear. (: "The Render of the Veils")

entities.name: Daoth-Yhol
entities.description:
Daoth-Yhol is an enigmatic figure created by Ross F. Bagby for his short story, "The Arctic Stone". Older than R'lyeh, it has lived on Earth long before Zagguwa arrived and the Ubbo-Sathla sloughed, and it is considered to be Cthulhu's deadly enemy. It can be summoned by an elliptical grey stone, which was stolen by a shaman from a dark tower run by three-toed eyeless creatures. This stone was eventually inherited by his great-grandson, the shaman of an Inuit tribe in the West Greenland coast that worshipped Cthulhu, whom kept it in a box out of fear and regarded it as an object of taboo. (: "The Arctic Stone")

entities.name: Dark Man
entities.description:
The Dark Man is a character created by American author Ron Shiflet for his Cthulhu Mythos fiction. He made his first appearance in the short story "The Dark Man's Assassin", published in the April 1998 edition of Edward P. Berglund's online fanzine Nightscapes.

The Dark Man manifests as a looming figure made entirely out of a black, smoky substance, standing in excess of seven feet in height. Although its only consistently-visible facial details are a pair of fiery red eyes, it occasionally reveals the barest hints of shifting features, and is possessed of a smile which chills the recipient to their very core.

Although the Dark Man likes to enact Byzantine schemes to gain material power, he also appears to be a somewhat capricious creature, occasionally granting boons to mortals in exchange for their service, and visiting upon them a terrible vengeance when they betray him.

entities.name: Dark Sargassum
entities.description:
The Dark Sargassum is a fictional monster from the Cthulhu Mythos featured in the role-playing game supplement The Bermuda Triangle.

Classified as a "Unique Entity", the Dark Sargassum is a colossal organism spread over a large area within the Bermuda Triangle, in the Atlantic Ocean. This marine terror originated as a Dark Young of Shub-Niggurath which sank with the lost continent of Atlantis and adapted itself to a new environment, mimicking the form of seaweed and feeding off marine life in the area. Now over 11,000 years old, it has grown into a humongous beast that looks and smells like a floating mass of sargassum.

Hidden within its body are over a hundred rope-like tentacles, which are used to capture prey and drag it towards the creature's toothed maw, located near its centre. Due to its size, the Dark Sargassum can encircle and crush ships weighing up to 200 tons. Few people are aware of the monster's real nature, save for the local Deep Ones and the organisation known as the Cult of Sargath, the latter of which congregates every All Hallow's Eve to offer human sacrifices to it. (: The Bermuda Triangle) Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Other Supernatural Beings

entities.name: Chandler Davies
entities.description:
Chandler Davies is a fictional character created by Brian Lumley. The character is a British weird artist who first appears in Lumley's Titus Crow story "An Item of Supporting Evidence" (1970). He is subsequently mentioned in a handful of Lumley stories, making one more brief appearance in "The Fairground Horror" (1976).

Davies, though introduced in "An Item of Supporting Evidence" as a "weird-artist," originally appears as a skeptic of the idea that there is a reality behind the eldritch horrors in Lovecraftian fiction. He is invited by Titus Crow to Blowne House after writing a letter "commenting upon the negative effect which [Crow's] short story 'Yegg-ha’s Realm' had had on him."

As a "gourmet of such tales," Davies objects that the story--a "Lovecraftian piece" published in the magazine Grotesque that was "set during the time of Rome’s rule over England and involving the worship of an 'outside God'”--had depicted “so thoroughly unbelievable a God” as "existing in such a well-known period of England’s history that even an average student of our country’s antiquities could hardly miss the obvious impossibility." "I must admit that blunders like yours irk me considerably," Davies complains.

More generally, Davies insists that "Mythological-Fantasy was ‘out;’ that the Cthulhu Mythos’ fabled lands and creatures and Cimmeria’s scintillating citadels and dark demons should have been allowed to die a sad but certain death along with their respective originators." The "constant culling from those tales...was weakening the impact of the original works," Davies feels.

entities.name: Henri-Laurent de Marigny
entities.description:
Henri-Laurent de Marigny is a fictional character created by Brian Lumley as a companion for Titus Crow, a time-travelling adventurer engaged in a long war with the Cthulhu Cycle Deities about whom Lumley wrote an extensive series of stories. Lumley presents him as the son of a character featured by H. P. Lovecraft and E. Hoffmann Price in "Through the Gates of the Silver Key".

Born to noted occultist Etienne-Laurent de Marigny some time in 1923, upon the death of his father Henri inherited an extensive library of mystic knowledge amongst other things. After making the acquaintance of Titus Crow, another man with a deep understanding of the occult, the pair proceeded to embark on a course of action which would bring them into direct conflict with many Mythos entities (which they refer to as the Cthulhu Cycle Dieties), Ithaqua in particular appearing to consider them something of a nemesis.

Throughout the course of their conflict with these beings, de Marigny has fought several Mythos beings -- alone, by the side of Crow, and as part of the Wilmarth Foundation -- has travelled to places unknown to the general populace, including Earth's Dreamlands, and has mastered the use of the time travelling device left to him by his father known as de Marigny's Clock.

Although an accomplished occultist in his own right, de Marigny is usually overshadowed by the understanding possessed by his companion Crow; however, this does not seem to overly concern him. The only Lumley story in which de Marigny serves as a main character without an appearance by Crow is "The Mirror of Nitocris".

entities.name: Dee
entities.description:
Dee is a recurrent character in the Cthulhu Mythos works of the late American author Michael Shea.

An attractive 55-year-old gay woman, Dee is described in her first appearance as having

She often carries a heavy walking stick, although she acknowledges that this is for aesthetic and self-defence purposes, rather than as a result of any mobility issues. She has given it the ironic nickname of "Rod".

Dee enjoys walking in the hills surrounding her home in San Francisco, where she has taken in a lodger, a young woman who calls herself Scat. She is also the co-owner of a small independent bookstore named Treefrog - where she first came across Scat - and drives an aged Volkswagen Bug when she needs to.

entities.name: Roderick Desmond
entities.description:
Roderick Desmond is a fictional character, the protagonist and title character of Philip Jose Farmer's 1979 short story "The Freshman".

Desmond is a well-known writer of horror novels from Busiris, Illinois, who, despite being 60 years old, is enrolling as a freshman at Miskatonic University. By entering college, he hopes to escape the control of his domineering mother, but he worries that she will follow him even there.
