entities.name: Diabolique
entities.description:
The Diabolique is a fictional character in the prime reality of the Marvel universe of Marvel Comics. Diabolique was created in 1993 by Chris Cooper and Rurik Tyler, first appearing in issue #9 of the 1st volume of Darkhold: Pages from the Book of Sins.

Diabolique is a demon/human hybrid that has ties to both the Darkhold and the Cult of the Darkhold. It appears as a 6 year old child, but is far older though she acts as a bratty child, a twisted sadistic one. She is constantly seeking out surrogate parents, who she later kills when she decides to move on to a new set of parents.

The demonic child possesses a number of magical powers. She gains the form of those she kills and their bodies and souls are fused into an entity called Playmate. Which at it's smallest is the size of a mouse which can grow to massive size and slaughters everything that's in its path, growing in power as the number of victims that it absorbs increase. It smothers, renders, strangles, and engulfs its victims. The entity projects heads, tentacles, and limbs with claws and teeth. Diabolique's power increases as the power of the Playmate grows, but if it's destroyed she is temporarily made powerless.

At full power, she can open dimensional portals, manipulate and absorb hellfire, tear apart victims, mentally control others, and practice sympathetic magic (e.g. voodoo dolls). She uses a spider called Zoroaster, which is the size of a small tarantula and she treats as a pet (Zoro). It is immune to hellfire, possesses superhuman strength, is able to regenerate it's limbs, and can increase its size to that of an automobile.

entities.name: Matthew DiNardo
entities.description:
Matthew DiNardo is a minor recurrent character in Armand Rosamilia's Keyport Cthulhu story cycle.

An aspiring young author, Matthew writes extreme horror stories with the intent to shock and disgust. He is a devious character, willing to say or do almost anything to get women to sleep with him.

When Matthew took his new girlfriend Tina out on a date to nearby Keyport, the two had an argument about his writing and broke up. As the Esoteric Order of Dagon were conducting their plans to raise great Cthulhu from his watery slumber, Matthew was not allowed to leave town, and ended up falling into the clutches of the deformed children which roamed the subterranean labyrinth beneath Keyport, where he was tortured and killed.

entities.name: Deputy Dingby
entities.description:
Deputy Dingby is a character who features in Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Files series of games and fiction. He was a member of the Arkham County Sheriff's Department.

A number of Encounter cards from Arkham Horror Second Edition feature interactions with the Deputy, in which he is usually portrayed as more than a little inept.

Dingby assisted Sheriff Engle in his interview with reformed cultist Diana Stanley after she attempted to break her ties to the Silver Twilight Lodge. His subsequent disappearing act hints that he may have been in league with the cult, or perhaps on their payroll.

When Professor Norman Withers informed Sheriff Engle of the abduction of his colleague Claus Schmidt by a Hound of Tindalos, Dingby investigated the scene, finding a torn-off fingernail.

entities.name: Raymond Dirk
entities.description:
Sheriff Raymond Dirk is a character created by American comic book creator Michael Alan Nelson as one of the primary protagonists for The Gray Man story arc of his Mythos series Fall of Cthulhu. He made his first appearance in issue #11 in March 2008.

A well built man somewhere in his late thirties, Dirk is Sheriff of the Arkham Police Department, and as of the end of the Gray Man story arc, apparently one of the last. He is a tough but fair officer with an open mind, and is well aware of the flaws of those who work for him.

Several years prior to the events of The Gray Man, Dirk lost his beloved wife in a car accident; his actions in trying to help the people of Arkham resulted in him losing all memory of her very existence.

Dirk comes from a family with a tradition of holding the title of Sheriff in Arkham, being at least the third in his line to occupy that position; the officers under his command expect that if Dirk ever has a son, then he too will take up the role.

entities.name: Charles Dodgson
entities.description:
Charles Dodgson is a wealthy man who has been involved with Wonderland for over a century. Born in the early 19th century, he contracted an incurable disease. To prevent his death, he made a pact with the Jabberwocky. In exchange for the restoration of his youth and health, making him immortal, he sacrificed humans to Wonderland, usually children and the majority of them having come from his extended family.

During the early 21st century, guilt overwhelmed Charles as he witnessed the devastation that Wonderland inflicted on the real world. Charles went into Wonderland, committing suicide by provoking Johnny Liddle into murdering him.

Dodgson also appears in the series' Cthulhu Mythos crossover Call of Wonderland, where he is an antagonist-turned-ally of H. P. Lovecraft. Dodgson's son, Howard Philips Dodgson, first appeared in issue #3 of Beyond Wonderland, and seems to have been named after Lovecraft.

entities.name: Andrew Doran
entities.description:
Dr. Andrew Doran is a fictional character created by American author Matthew Davenport for his Cthulhu Mythos series to which he lends his name. An action-archaeologist in the style of Indiana Jones, he made his first appearance in the novel The Statement of Andrew Doran in 2013.

An athletic man with a thick crop of unruly brown hair and matching beard, Doran is a proficient user of magic, although he claims that his internal reserves are small and exhausting to use. He is an alumni of Miskatonic University who, at the series beginning, is working as a field archaeologist in Mexico, but later returns to his alma mater to take up the position of Dean.

Doran is accompanied by a "woman" named Olivia who is stated to be an aspect of his psyche self-manufactured to protect him from the horrors which he has witnessed. Through Olivia, he is able to perform actions which would shatter the sanity of a normal person: this would seem to suggest that rather than an aspect of Doran's psyche, she is an entirely separate personality, or has perhaps even become her own entity.

Prior to 1941, Doran had spent a year living amongst a tribe of Night Gaunt-worshipping natives named the Night Watchers in Mexico. For some unspecified reason, they sentenced him to death, but were unsuccessful in their execution (: The Statement of Andrew Doran).

entities.name: Dositheus
entities.description:
Dositheus is a fictional character, based on the historical figure Dositheos, who is a recurring character in the Simon of Gitta stories of Richard L. Tierney. His first appearance was in "The Sword of Spartacus", published in Swords Against Darkness #3, published in 1978.

Dositheus appears as a Samaritan wizard who serves as a mentor to Simon of Gitta, though at times Simon has to rein in Dositheus when his plans for revenge against Rome go too far. Dositheus has an apprentice named Menander and a crow familiar named Carbo.

Dositheos, who probably lived in the first century AD, was the founder of a Samaritan religious sect with Gnostic teachings. He is said to have known John the Baptist and to have been either a teacher or a rival of Simon Magus, the figure that Simon of Gitta is based on.

Dositheus appears in Tierney's stories "The Sword of Spartacus", "The Fire of Mazda", "The Seed of the Star-God" and "The Throne of Achamoth", and in his novel The Drums of Chaos. His death is referred to in Tierney's story "The Dragons of Mount Fractus".

entities.name: Ursula Downs
entities.description:
Eldritch HorrorMansions of MadnessArkham Horror: The Card GameCult of the Spider Queen

Ursula Downs, the Explorer, is a character who features in Fantasy Flight Games Arkham Horror Files range of Cthulhu Mythos-related games and fiction.

Never one to follow the pursuits usually associated with young women of the time, Ursula enjoyed climbing trees, digging in the mud and exploring all of the places where others didn’t want to go. After showing a natural aptitude for languages, the sciences and history, she enrolled in Boston University where she graduated first in her class at Archaeology.

Using her inheritance to finance her trips across the globe, Ursula set about exploring the remnants of lost civilisations and the ritualistic practices of remote tribes which had never before seen a westerner, selling the pieces she wrote about these expeditions to various magazines and scientific journals in order to fund future excursions. In this manner, Ursula became the world's premier female archaeologist, and one of the few people on the planet able to make boasts such as having climbed a mountain on every continent and stolen a priceless relic from a savage tribe of cannibals.

entities.name: Dragon of the Moon
entities.description:
The Dragon of the Moon is an eldritch Lovecraftian entity from the fictional universe of Marvel by Marvel Comics. It was created in 1984 by Peter B. Gillis and Don Perlin, making its first appearance in issue #138 of the Defenders comic book series.

The Dragon of the Moon originated on Earth, The offspring of the Elder God Set, it originated on Earth, but later headed out into space to explore the cosmos and spread its evil beyond Earth. The Dragon has claimed to be responsible for committing various evils but it is a great liar, and thus many of its claims are difficult to verify. It is most infamous among the superhumans of Earth for corrupting the hero Moondragon.

The Dragon has the power to reshape reality and can manipulate forces on a planetary scale. If a mortal is worthy, it will offer them its power, seducing them by appealing to their insecurity and/or greed. The greater the acceptance of the victim, the greater the Dragon's power within the material universe. The Dragon of the Moon manifested as an amorphous centipede-like presence, which grew in tandem with its power.

entities.name: Dwarf
entities.description:
The Dwarf is a fictional demon in the prime reality of the Marvel universe of Marvel Comics who was created in 1992 by Chris Cooper and Richard Case, first appearing in issue #28 of the 3rd volume of Ghost Rider.

The Dwarf is a demon which serves the Elder God Chthon. It delivers pages of the Darkhold in black envelopes to people, sometimes giving them little to no inkling of what it contains or what it's for and other times promising much if they use the page.

It can magically transport itself to anywhere it wants. Usually appearing wherever a Darkhold page is found. To get people to use a Darkhold page and thereby damn their souls, it influences them. The Dwarf prefers manipulating others to directly attacking them.

entities.name: Finn Edwards
entities.description:
Finn Edwards, the Bootlegger, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games who appears in several of their expanded Cthulhu Mythos lines.

The advent of Prohibition was nothing less than a godsend for small-time drifter Finn Edwards: until that point, he had been simply meandering through life, scratching out a living wherever he could, but the new demand for alcohol on the streets of America gave him the opportunity to make some serious money and, more importantly, feed his craving for danger.

All of this ended one night when, after a botched supply run, Finn found himself tearing through the woods one moonlit night, just a little ahead of the deranged cultists who wanted to sacrifice him to their dark god.

Narrowly escaping, and shaken to his core, Finn gathered up all the cash, firearms and supplies he could lay his hands on, resolving to make those lunatics pay for giving him the fright of his life.

entities.name: Eligos
entities.description:
Eligos is a fictional demon created by Sean Clements in 2015 for the STARZ series Ash vs Evil Dead.

Eligos is a minor demonic entity summoned by the Necronomicon, which is a "Demon of the Mind". The demon is able to control and manipulate individual's minds, can inhabit the body of a mortal without displaying physical evidence of the possession, is able to teleport short distances, and has telekinetic abilities.

One such demon was summoned by Ash to find out how to undue what the Necronomicon had wrought. During the interrogation, the binding circle was accidentally broken, releasing the demon. It overpowered them, then unknown to the others it possessed Kelly, after which it manipulated its companions, fought them, and before it was exorcised killed Pablo's uncle.

Nathaniel Elton is a fictional character created by Chaosium for their horror-roleplaying game Call of Cthulhu, making his first appearance in the supplement The Complete Dreamlands

Nathaniel Elton is the grandson of Basil Elton, the protagonist of H. P. Lovecraft's 1919 short story "The White Ship." In the expanded Cthulhu Mythos of Call of Cthulhu Elton, with the help of fellow dreamer Ward Phillips, was able to navigate the one safe path through the Basalt Pillars of the West to reach Cathuria. (: The Complete Dreamlands).

entities.name: Sheriff Engle
entities.description:
Sheriff Engle is a character who features in Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Files series of games and fiction. He is the head of the Arkham Police Department.

Engle made his first appearance as a Blight card for the Arkham Horror Second Edition expansion The King in Yellow.

When unwilling cultist Diana Stanley attempted to break her ties with the Silver Twilight Lodge, she went to see Sheriff Engle in an attempt to blow the whistle on the cult's activities. At first, Engle seemed to believe her story, but soon mysteriously abandoned the case, and in doing so hinted that he may have in fact been in the pocket of Carl Sanford, the Lodge's high priest. (: Feeders from Within)

After Professor Norman Withers told Engle the story of how his colleague Claus Schmidt had been abducted by Hounds of Tindalos, Engle agreed to launch an investigation, but only under the condition that Withers change his statement to something more mundane. Engle further hinted that he knew about the strange goings-on in Arkham, but was unwilling to write about these occurrences in a report. (: Ire of the Void)

entities.name: Esch
entities.description:
Esch is an extraterrestrial avian creature who appears in Brian Lumley's Titus Crow series of novels, making his first appearance in the 1975 novel The Transition of Titus Crow.

Like the rest of his species, the Dchichi, Esch is a tall humanoid with the head and lower limbs of a terrestrial bird. He sports a beautiful set of feathers similar to that of a bird of paradise, and wears a cloak and shoes crafted from fine gold mesh. (: The Transition of Titus Crow)

When Titus Crow first set foot outside of his Time Clock upon Elysia, he was greeted by Esch. At first Esch attempted to communicate with him in alien languages which the Earthman did not understand, but as soon as Crow tried to tell him this, Esch replied in plain English. Esch then informed Crow that there was a Lithard on its way to collect Crow, before disappearing into a Time Clock of his own. (: The Transition of Titus Crow)

entities.name: Eva
entities.description:
Eva is a hero in the fictional Dynamite universe, who was created in 2006 by James Kuhoric. She is Dracula's daughter, who has fought against him her whole life.

Upon the death of Vlad Tepes's wife, he made a pact with what he believed to be god's envoy in exchange for her life. In reality a demon, Vlad Tepes was turned into a vampire and his wife didn't return to life as he was promised, but a part of her returned as Eva, his baby daughter. Who was deliver by wolves to a monk. Eva possesses a preternatural ability to find evil influences among men and wipe it out, and has been destroying Dracula's influence ever since.

Eva fought alongside Ash Williams against her father and his army of monsters, when he tried to use the Necronomicon to bring about eternal night on Earth. She later was part of a coalition of warriors and supernatural beings which included her father Dracula, that fought against the Hyborian sorcerer Kulan Gath in the early 21st century. In one possible post-apocalyptic future, she was allied with Ash Williams, her father, and the remnants of the human, witch, vampire, and werewolf races against the Deadites.

entities.name: Malachai Farrow
entities.description:
Malachai James Farrow, whose Christian name has also been spelled 'Malachi,' was a fictional character who first appeared in Peter J. Evans' 2013 Arkham Horror Fiction novel Feeders from Within.

Farrow was a soldier who served in the Pancho Villa Expedition of 1916-17 alongside his friend Mark Harrigan. When their squad was separated from the main force and pursued by Villistas, they took refuge on a rocky hillside. While looking for a means to escape, the squad came across an unusual opening in the side of the hill and investigated, hoping to find a route which lead away from the Villistas.

Delving deep into the cave, the group came across a cavern which was home to a bizarre machine attended by a number of Mi-Go who promptly attacked. Fending them off and destroying the machine, Farrow and Harrigan were able to escape, although all of the other soldiers were apparently killed.

Returning to the United States, Farrow was institutionalised in Arkham Asylum where he was treated by Dr. Eric Hardstrom for two years and seven months with little progress. After his discharge he travelled to Providence, Rhode Island, where he lived for a few years before checking himself into the Lemarchand Institute with what little money he had for more psychiatric help. Dr. Carolyn Fern treated him, and slowly discovered his fear of monsters with knives for hands.

entities.name: Father-of-All-Sharks
entities.description:
The Father-of-All-Sharks is an avatar of Cthulhu created by Bruce L. Priddy for the 2006 edition of Malleus Monstrorum, a monster manual supplement for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu horror role-playing game. Priddy created the creature as part of a competition run by Chaosium, with the top three entries being included in the book; the Father-of-All-Sharks came in second place.

The Father-of-All-Sharks manifests as a colossal glowing white shark resembling the ancient extinct species Megalodon, but twice the size. It has been theorized to have been the inspiration for the biblical Leviathan.

The Deep Ones know the correct rituals required to summon the Father-of-All-Sharks, but are wary of doing to, as their mystical skill does not include the knowledge on how to control the being once it has manifested: thus, they only ever resort to deploying the creature during the direst of circumstances, such as when one of their cities is under threat, or some terrible transgression must be punished.

The Deep Ones are known to worship the Father-of-All-Sharks, and some other non-human species are believed to do so as well. It has no human cult as such, although various Polynesian and Hawaiian islanders venerate the creature, having made sacrifices to it in the past in hopes of appeasing the beast and avoiding its terrible attentions.

entities.name: Feaster from Afar
entities.description:
The Feaster from Afar is a fictional entity created by Joseph Payne Brennan for his eponymous short story.

The Feaster from Afar is an avatar of Hastur the Unspeakable and a fearsome predator that moves through interstellar space. At some point, a branch of the Whateley family seems to have summoned it down to Earth, where it has remained, inhabiting the hills outside Granbury, New England, turning them into a barren waste completely devoid of animal life.

The Feaster from Afar glides over the terrain, unaffected by gravity, and might be able to pass through solid objects as well. It appears as a black, shriveled creature, with knife-like claws at the tips of its tentacles, which are used to perforate the skull of its victims and suck out their brains. Victims are invariably found dead with their heads riddled with holes.

Like many other entities of the Cthulhu Mythos, the Feaster from Afar can manifest itself in dreams. Its approach is accompanied by a sharp drop in temperature. (: "The Feaster from Afar")

entities.name: Joachim Feery
entities.description:
Joachim Feery is a fictional scholar of the occult, created by Brian Lumley, who frequently cites him as an authority in his Cthulhu Mythos stories. He is first mentioned in Lumley's "Cement Surroundings," which debuted in the 1969 Arkham House anthology Tales of the Cthulhu Mythos. Lumley's fullest discussion of the character occurs in the short story "Aunt Hester" (1975).

Feery appears as the author of limited-edition commentaries on books of eldritch knowledge, such as his Notes on the Necronomicon, which was first referenced in "Cement Surroundings", and Notes on the Cthaat Aquadingen, which Lumley cited in "The Fairground Horror". The existence of a more complete first edition of Notes on the Necronomicon--known as the Original Notes on the Necronomicon--was revealed by Lumley in "Name and Number". Other sources cited by Feery include Unspeakable Cults and De Vermis Mysteriis.

Feery's books were published in limited editions, mostly at his own expense, and the vast majority of copies were "bought up and destroyed as fast as they appeared" by "religious and other authorities"--making the surviving examples exceedingly rare.

While Lumley's occultists find Feery to be a valuable resource, they also urge caution. Titus Crow cautions that Notes on the Necronomicon is "hardly what one could call a reliable guide," and Thomas Millwright warns that "Feery’s reconstructions and translations were often at fault or fanciful in their treatment of the original works." Hester Lang notes that Feery's "quotes, while apparently genuine and authoritative, often differ substantially when compared with the works from which they were supposedly culled," because "Feery claimed that most of his occult knowledge came to him ‘in dreams’!”

entities.name: Carolyn Fern
entities.description:
Carolyn Fern, the Psychologist, is a character created by Chaosium as an investigator character for their Cthulhu Mythos-inspired board game Arkham Horror.

Gaining her degree at Rhode Island Hospital during the 1920s, Carolyn spent a further year training as an allopathic psychiatrist at Butler before taking up a residency position at the Lemarchand Institute under the supervision of physician Dr. Spencer. (: Feeders from Within)

When one of her patients, one Malachai Farrow psychologically damaged by experiences he underwent while in the US Army, was murdered in exactly the same way he had been dreaming of, Carolyn took a leave of absence from the hospital and travelled to Arkham to look into Farrow's psychological history. (: Feeders from Within)

What she found there was a plot by both human cultists and the alien Mi-Go to bring madness to the world. Fortunately, Carolyn made the acquaintance of Henry Armitage, Mark Harrigan and Diana Stanley, unique individuals with knowledge of the occult, and the group were able to thwart the conspiracy against mankind. (: Feeders from Within)

entities.name: Jacqueline Fine
entities.description:
Jacqueline Fine, the Psychic, is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games as part of their Arkham Horror Files line of Cthulhu Mythos gaming material.

Plagued by terrible nightmares her whole life, Jacqueline dreams of a time when the world will be plunged into a thousand years of horror by dread creatures from another dimension. Having recently learned to control her "curse", she has discovered that they are in actuality visions of a future not yet come to pass. As a result, she now works to decode the meaning behind the dreams and, perhaps, prevent the coming apocalypse.

Jacqueline Fine was first introduced in the Arkham Horror supplement Dunwich Horror. She has also appeared in Eldritch Horror and Arkham Horror: The Card Game. Additionally, a plastic gaming accessory was released as part of the Arkham Horror Premium Figures line in 2010.

entities.name: Dancy Flammarion
entities.description:
Dancy Flammarion is a fictional character created by Caitlin R. Kiernan, an albino teenager from the backwoods of Florida who hunts monsters at the direction of a Lovecraftian angel. First appearing in the novel Threshold (Roc/New American Library, 2001), Dancy was subsequently featured in a series of short stories collected in the volumes Alabaster (Subterranean Press, 2006) and Comes a Pale Rider (Subterranean Press, 2020). She also appears in a number of graphic novels written by Kiernan.

In their notes for Threshold, on September 16, 1998, Kiernan mentions a “creepy little ‘Boo Radley’ albino girl”--their earliest reference to the character who became Dancy Flammarion. (Boo Radley is a reclusive, offputting, ultimately heroic character from Harper Lee's novel To Kill a Mockingbird.) The name Dancy comes from a small town in Alabama, in Pickens County near the Mississippi state line, that Kiernan passed through while collecting Upper Cretaceous fossils in July or August 1998; "the name stuck in my head, as names often do," they later wrote.

entities.name: Floating Horror
entities.description:
The Floating Horror is an avatar of Nyarlathotep which is usually associated with Haitian voodoo.

The Floating Horror appears as a colossal airborne jellyfish shot through with scarlet veins. During its incubation phase it parasitically occupies the body of a living human being.

This avatar of Nyarlathotep can be summoned by using voodoo magic to make the offering of a human host body. Once the ritual is complete, the Floating Horror will enter the body of the "chosen one" and begin its incubation period. Once this phase is complete, the host will die and the Floating Horror will emerge to begin its work: the capture and consumption of living human beings.

entities.name: Henry R. Flynn
entities.description:
Henry R. "Hank" Flynn is a fictional character created by American writer Josh Finney for his Mythos/noir Casefile: Arkham comic book stories. He made his first appearance in the graphic novel Casefile: Arkham- Nightmare on the Canvas in February 2016.

Flynn is a cynical New Englander who works as a private investigator to pay the bills. A former marine, he sustained an injury amidst ancient ruins on an unspecified island, seems to have given him some connection to a mystical force which he can tap into in times of great stress, although he seems entirely unable to control its effects. He is in love with a woman named Glynda, a self-styled witch with a deep, if bookish, knowledge of the occult.

Flynn served as a marine in the Pacific theatre during the Second World War where he suffered head trauma from an artillery blast which left him with a piece of shrapnel embedded in his skull. After being invalided out of the service, Flynn returned to his home town of Arkham, where he set himself up as a private investigator.

In 1946, Flynn was hired by a woman named May Derlith to find missing artist Richard Upton Pickman, to whom she was both benefactor and lover. However, Pickman had gone insane, murdering those who had in his human life denied his talent, and eventually turned his rage on Derlith before being shot and killed by Flynn.

entities.name: Abigail Foreman
entities.description:
Abigail Foreman is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their contributions to the Cthulhu Mythos.

A library intern at Arkham's Miskatonic University, Abigail discovered something unusual in an old book in her care: the pages changed when significant events occurred, but the text always indicated a countdown to a certain date. Joining forces with sailor Silas Marsh, the pair were able to uncover a plot by the folks of Innsmouth to awaken a dread entity and thwart it (: The Deep Gate).

Abigail Foreman has appeared in several Cthulhu Mythos contributions by Fantasy Flight, including the Arkham Horror expansion The King in Yellow, Chris A. Jackson's novella The Deep Gate and Arkham Horror: The Card Game.

Abigail made her first appearance in The King in Yellow expansion for Arkham Horror, where she appeared as a Blight card representing characters harmful to the "heroes" of the game. Despite this, she is portrayed as very much the secondary protagonist in the novella The Deep Gate.

entities.name: Fractal Yog-Sothoth
entities.description:
The Fractal Yog-Sothoth (also known as Lord of the Fractal Realm) is a fictional entity created by Scott David Aniolowski for Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, depicted as being an avatar of the Outer God known as Yog-Sothoth. (: Ye Booke of Monstres II)

Appearing as an agglomeration of coruscating rainbow-coloured geometric shapes surrounding a central mass of tentacles, the Fractal Yog-Sothoth is rarely encountered in the real world; nevertheless it is occasionally stumbled across by unwitting computer users. When its bizarre dimension is accessed, the Fractal Yog-Sothoth immediately forces its way through the user's now-destroyed computer screen and grows to a terrifying size, lashing out with its appendages: any living being touched by the Fractal is instantly absorbed by it.

Being an entity composed entirely of energy, the Fractal Yog-Sothoth cannot be harmed by any physical means. However, it is vulnerable to energy-based weapons and effects, and the switching off or restarting of the computer which it used as a gateway may act to cast it back to its own dimension. (: Ye Booke of Monstres II)

It has been suggested that entities other than Yog-Sothoth possess fractal avatars in this other dimension, although if any of them have been encountered by humans there have been no survivors left to tell the tale.

entities.name: Roland Franklyn
entities.description:
Roland Franklyn is a fictional character created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Franklyn Paragraphs". As part of the Campbell's Severn Valley setting, Franklyn is considered part of the expanded Cthulhu Mythos.

Roland Franklyn (died 1967) was the leader of a cult in Brichester, England, in the mid-1960s. The core of his cult's theology is that "the number of souls in the universe is limited...and that humanity must therefore acknowledge an infinite number of simultaneous incarnations." In January 1964, he published his cult's dogma in We Pass From View (True Light Press). Among the claims made in the book is that the deceased must be cremated in order for the soul to be reincarnated. Otherwise, the "burrowers of the core may drag off his body from the grave with him still in it to the feast of Eihort." After his death, Franklyn himself, alas, was not cremated. (: "The Franklyn Paragraphs")

entities.name: Gazira
entities.description:
Gazira is a fictional monster created by Michael Dziesinski for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

Gazira is a colossal monster whose existence and activities the Japanese government has kept a secret, resulting that most believe it to be a fictional monster created by the media (known to the West as Gadzella). Nuclear radiation wakes it from hibernation, as does strong seismic activity. It's a courageous beast though not a particularly intelligent one.

After going on its rampage, Gazira returns to its hibernation site. Its rampages are covered up as the result of typhoons or earthquakes, with the locals generously paid off. It considers Japan to be its turf and will battle creatures which are of similar size, including various Great Old Ones. The being has the ability to exhale a column of radioactive fire. (: Secrets of Japan)

Gazira is a clear nod to the iconic kaiju Godzilla, with its nuclear and seismic plot devices being identical to those portrayed in the original run of films. Even the names Gazira and Gadzella are near-carbon copies of the real world names given to the creature (Gojira and Godzilla, respectively).

entities.name: Ghattambah
entities.description:
Ghattambah, the Insect-God, is a fictional entity created by Mark McLaughlin with input from Michael Sheehan, Jr. for the Cthulhu Mythos humor and bawdy tales collection Best Little Witch-House in Arkham.

Ghattambah exists outside of time and space, and is said to be able to gift those it deems worthy with fantastic powers.

The High Priest of Ghattambah's human cult, Azmael Mondrago, has shown no compunction in destroying those who trespass within its chapel, and is suspected of being responsible for the disappearance of several children in his time, suggesting that Ghattambah requires blood sacrifice (: "In The Chapel Of Ghattambah").

At some point in Earth's future Ghattambah served Nyarlathotep in the Outer God's plots to lay waste to the human race. (: "The Spawn Of Ghattambah").

entities.name: Ghroth
entities.description:
Ghroth is an Outer God in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Tugging", which depicts the entity as being a living planetoid.

Ghroth is an Outer God that resembles a rust-colored moon with a single gigantic red eye that it closes to avoid detection. It's made up of molten iron, ash and gas, and splitting the surface are cracks or faults. Below its crust are vast seas, which are used to form a giant eye.

It drifts throughout the universe while singing its siren song, The Music of the Spheres. Any Great Old Ones or Outer Gods sleeping on a planet it passes is awakened by its call. Ghroth destroys planets as well and has destroyed the home of Baoht Z'uqqa-Mogg, forcing it to flee and take up residence on Earth. As Ghroth gets closer to a world, the planet experiences natural disasters in the form of erupting volcanoes, tidal waves, earthquakes, changing tides, and horrific storms.

The Death Star, one of Ghroth's many aliases, is also the name of the planet-destroying space station constructed by the Galactic Empire from the Star Wars franchise.

entities.name: Duke Givens
entities.description:
Inspector Duke Givens is a fictional character created by American author Brandon Berntson for his Lovecraft Mysteries trilogy of Cthulhu Mythos novels. He made his debut appearance in 2018's The Night of Dagon.

A "portly man with jowls", Givens prefers to dress in suits which are always clean and neatly pressed. An inspector in the Innsport Police Department, he is married to an unnamed woman, and has a love/hate relationship with the protagonist of The Lovecraft Mysteries, private investigator Devlin Macky.

After being assigned the case of an artefact stolen from the Innsport Natural History Museum, Givens and his partner Lieutenant Newt Bardhoff found themselves investigating a missing persons case on the estate of cultist Mordred Haddonfield. Captured by Haddonfield and his undead servant Borgas, they were destined to be sacrificed to the recently-awoken Dagon: the timely intervention of Macky and Millie Von Clydesburgh saved them from this fate, and the pair returned to Innsport to begin an evacuation ahead of Dagon's murderous rampage (: The Night of Dagon).

Later, Givens was heavily involved in the battle against the Mad Arab Abdul Alhazred, the Outer Gods, and their legions of monstrous minions after Macky accidentally kickstarted Alhazred's plot to bring about the return of his dark masters (: The Lurker at the Threshold).

entities.name: Glynda
entities.description:
Glynda (second name undisclosed) is a fictional character created by Josh Finney for his Casefile: Arkham Mythos stories. She made her first appearance in the 2016 graphic novel Casefile: Arkham- Nightmare on the Canvas.

Glynda is a beautiful woman of indeterminate age whose body has been modified by the Outer God Shub-Niggurath to make her more appealing to the opposite sex. She owns and operates a shop named Rare Books which deals in antique books, and has a sideline in occult writings. She is currently in a relationship with private eye Hank Flynn.

As a former devotee of Shub-Niggurath, Glynda possesses certain magical powers, and her abilities specialise in protective invocations.

Given by her mother to the service of Shub-Niggurath at a young age, Glynda underwent a mystical transformation at the hands of her god which was intended to give her physical characteristics desirable to men. She was then sent out into the world under orders to seduce and have children with as many men as possible; these children were then sacrificed as a blood offering to the Black Goat.

entities.name: Glyph
entities.description:
Glyph (real name unknown) is a primary character and main protagonist in Ian Davey's Bh'Yhlun series. She made her first appearance in "An Incarceration in Bh'Yhlun," published in the September 1997 edition of Edward P. Berglund's online fanzine Nightscapes.

A 13-year-old British girl, Glyph found herself orphaned in the aftermath of the coming of Bh'Yhlun. She has spent the time since then living by any means necessary in the ruins of the world, dodging the various monstrosities which patrol the now-twisted countryside.

After a brief period of imprisonment in the living tower of Bh'Yhlun, Glyph began the long journey to Glastonbury when some previously-unsuspected magical ability told her that her destiny lay in that ancient place (: "An Incarceration in Bh'Yhlun").

Glyph subsequently joined up with an older couple named Helen and Aaron and, later, a pregnant woman named Lucy who had borne witness to the genesis of this new world. Eventually arriving at Glastonbury, the group were confronted by Stanley Pickman, an avatar of Nyarlathotep. When the Outer God fully manifested, a magical ritual was able to banish it, and restore the world to the way it was before the coming of Bh'Yhlun (: "The Epiphany of Dissolution").

entities.name: Gloria Goldberg
entities.description:
Gloria Goldberg, also known simply as The Author, is a fictional investigator character created by Richard Launius for Chaosium's Cthulhu Mythos board game Arkham Horror in 1987. Since Fantasy Flight Games' acquisition of the property in 2005, they have significantly expanded on her history and exploits. However, it is possible that Chaosium still hold rights to the character, as Gloria does not appear in the latest edition of Arkham Horror (third).

Unlike many of the investigator biographies from Arkham Horror, Gloria Goldberg's backstory has remained largely consistent over the years. She has suffered from nightmarish, apocalyptic visions of sinister entities from beyond our reality destroying the world for as long as she can remember. Over the years, medical and psychiatric treatment has helped her channel these dreams into her fiction, and this has earned her a reputation as a highly-inventive horror writer with a successful career.

In Graham McNeill's 2012 novel Bones of the Yopasi, Gloria is encountered by a group of investigators on the trail of a Cthulhu cultist while on tour in Kingsport promoting her latest book. Although the group keep her in the dark about their true agenda, an invitation to her latest reading - at a local historical society - allows the others to examine occult materials which they would not have otherwise had access to.

Since her first appearance in 1987, Gloria has appeared in most Arkham Horror-related work, including Eldritch Horror, the Arkham Horror Premium Figures line, and Arkham Horror Fiction. A more complete list is given below.

entities.name: Gray Man
entities.description:
The Gray Man is a supernatural character created by American comic book creator Michael Alan Nelson for the Fall of Cthulhu story arc named for the character. The Gray Man made his first appearance in issue #11 of that series in March 2008.

A seemingly unkillable creature of unknown origin, the Gray Man manifests as a humanoid male dressed in the manner of a stereotypical Hispanic gangster, complete with tailored suit and Portuguese language. He possesses a ceremonial knife which he prefers to use to kill his victims, but is not necessary for use on mortal beings. However, it has been hinted that this artefact is intended for use against targets far more powerful than mere humans…

The Gray Man was summoned by persons unknown to kill an unidentified target. Although the young thief Lucifer stole his knife and spirited it away to Arkham, the Gray Man tracked it down and embarked on a murderous rampage in his efforts to retrieve it. Although several civilians and police officers died during the slaughter, Sheriff Raymond Dirk and Lucifer managed to imprison him in one of the Harlot's boxes, saving Arkham, at least for a short while.

entities.name: Salome Gray
entities.description:
Salome Gray is a fictional character by Dan Wickline for the comic book Grimm Fairy Tales Presents: Call of Wonderland Vol 1 2, published by Zenescope Entertainment in 2012.

Salome Gray is a tattoo artist that runs a tattoo parlor called Anarchy Ink. She and her friend Julie Sands were inadvertently drawn into an attempt by the forces of Wonderland to invade Earth. They vanquished their foes and returned to Earth, but were soon drawn back into Wonderland by the power of the Queen of Spades, who needed them to fill the role of the Queen of Hearts in Wonderland.

entities.name: Gtuhanai
entities.description:
Gtuhanai the Insatiable is a fictional entity created by author J. B. Lee for his 1999 short story "Forces of Change."

Manifesting as a whirling conglomeration of helical metal structures, Gtuhanai is capable of absorbing any metals in its vicinity into its body, in turn increasing its own mass and power. What the upper limits to this ability are remain unknown, but are implied to perhaps be limitless. (: "Forces of Change")

According to the Necronomicon, Gtuhanai is worshipped by a species of metal beings known as the Aartna, which inhabit the region of space around the Pleiades star cluster. (: "Forces of Change")

Gtuhanai is the "brother" of Cthulhu and the "son" of Yog-Sothoth; it has also been described as being somewhat similar to Glaaki, although whether any "familial" relationship exists between the two entities is unknown. It was first summoned to Earth by the sorcerer Mezamalek (perhaps the same being as Zon Mezzamalech of Hyperborea) who used its power on his enemies, obliterating all who stood against him before the entity turned on Mezamalek and consumed him. (: "Forces of Change")

entities.name: Gyyagin
entities.description:
Gyyagin is a fictional monster created by Stephen King for his short story "Jerusalem's Lot". A giant extraterrestrial worm that transforms its human followers into undead servitors, Gyyagin is itself identified as a servant of "Yogsoggoth" (possibly Yog-Sothoth), and is heavily implied to be the titular Worm that the grimoire known as De Vermis Mysteriis (English: Mysteries of the Worm) alludes to.

Gyyagin is a massive worm that burrows under the ground in the area around the town of Jerusalem's Lot, Maine. Descriptors and sobriquets include "the Worm from beyond space", "Star-Eater" and "Blinder of Time". Its body is segmented, at least 5 ft. wide, grey in colour, and produces black slime as it moves around its tunnels. Wherever it crawls over, the ground's vegetation withers and turns white. Its mere proximity seems to have a noxious effect on the local inhabitants, precipitating the birth of eyeless or noseless children.

Like many Mythos deities, Gyyagin demands bloody sacrifices. Its victims are apparently killed by constriction, as the gargantuan worm squeezes them until their blood vessels are ruptured.

Gyyagin is perhaps most notable for transforming its human followers into undead creatures (referred to at one point as nosferatu) which live in its tunnels with it. Blood relatives of these cultists seem to be subtly attracted to the area that the Worm inhabits, but it is not known whether this psychic link is formed by Gyyagin or by the undead relatives themselves.

entities.name: Hagarg Ryonis
entities.description:
Hagarg Ryonis, also known as The Lier-in-Wait, is a fictional entity created by Sandy Petersen for the Call of Cthulhu gaming supplement H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands.

Hagarg Ryonis is one of the Great Ones, the gods of Earth that reside in Kadath. She appears as a huge reptilian monster with black scales, six irregularly spaced eyes, and obsidian claws and teeth.

Although Hagarg Ryonis is not evil, when the unbelief and depravity of Dreamland’s inhabitants become so severe that they disturb the emotions of the Great Ones, she carries out a massacre until the people repent. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands)

In Hyperborea, Hagarg Ryonis was regarded as the guardian of tombs and homes, meting out justice to the unjust. (: Wizards of Hyperborea)

entities.name: James Joseph Hanley
entities.description:
James Joseph "J.J." Hanley is a character created by American authors James Ambuehl and Robert M. Price for their Braving, Minnesota contributions to the greater Cthulhu Mythos.

Hanley is an intelligent man who works as a reporter for the Braving Bulletin, a local Minnesotan newspaper. He appears to cover primarily human-interest pieces (and has his own column titled "Meet the People of Braving") but also claims to have unearthed a number of stories which have been deemed "ultimately unprintable", hinting that they may have been supernatural in nature.

entities.name: Harlot
entities.description:
The Harlot is a character created by American comic book creator Michael Alan Nelson for the Boom! Studios Mythos series Fall of Cthulhu. She made her debut appearance in the very first issue in 2007.

The Harlot is a large humanoid creature who dresses in a gaudy burlesque style offset by her appearance, which appears to be degenerate to the point of resembling a corpse. A resident of the Dreamlands, she operates a brothel of sorts, trading her secrets for less savoury payments, such as body parts or memories.

The Harlot is a powerful creature in control of her own dream-realm, and has been seen to destroy several Nightgaunts with little effort. Although she is not a match for a being such as the Elder God Nodens, she has stated that she would be capable of making him work for his victory, should such a confrontation come about.

The Harlot chose to help the bereaved dreamer Cy Morgan, even to the point of challenging the Elder God Nodens for the possession of him. She later imprisoned him in one of her boxes at his own request, as he wished to forget the death of his fiancé, which he believed to have been his own fault (: Fall of Cthulhu Volume 1: The Fugue).

entities.name: Mark Harrigan
entities.description:
Mark Harrigan, the Soldier, is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games who has appeared in several of their Arkham Horror Files range of Cthulhu Mythos-related products.

There are three separate origin stories given for Harrigan, each one slightly different from the others.

The first backstory stated that Harrigan had joined the United States Army and fought in Europe during the First World War, where he saw monsters killing men in the trenches. Upon returning home, he finds that his partner Sophie has one of the monsters inside her, and the creature consumes her soul.

This version is largely similar to the Arkham Horror story, but Sophie is confirmed to have been Harrigan's wife, and after her death he travels to Helsinki, where he had seen some of the monsters posing as German soldiers during the war.

entities.name: Stuart Hartwell
entities.description:
Dr. Stuart Hartwell is a fictional character created by American author Peter Rawlik for his Cthulhu Mythos stories, making his debut in the episodic novel Reanimators (2013, Night Shade Books).

Hartwell was a student and protégé of celebrated Miskatonic University physician Dr. Allan Halsey. When Halsey's corpse was reanimated by the misguided Herbert West, Hartwell's parents fell victim to the crazed beast during its murderous rampage. In the aftermath Hartwell, having deduced the cause of Halsey's condition, swore revenge on West.

In the following years, Hartwell obtained his medical degree and established himself as a respected practitioner, primarily through an association with neighbour Nathaniel Wingate Peaslee. However, this relationship soon soured when Peaslee's body was inhabited by the Yithian Mr. Ys, who coerced him into acting as his agent, and pressing him into his service with such other Mythos characters as Dr. Muñoz.

Despite these distractions, Hartwell remembered his vow and, although his zeal in pursuing his vengeance waxed and waned several times over the years, it was always in his mind. To this end, he developed an proficiency in the reanimation process; although this was initially solely for thwarting West, he soon came to be an accomplished practitioner in the art, his own versions of the reagent surpassing West's (although this may have been at least partially due to the acts of sabotage Hartwell enacted when West was absent from his laboratories).

entities.name: Hasuta
entities.description:
Hasuta (also known as Hastur) is an extraterrestrial entity from the fictional universe of the Haiyore! Nyaruko-san series.

Hasuta was a childhood friend of Nyaruko and Kuuko. His father is the owner of the Carcosa Computer Entertainment corporation and Hasuta was initially sent to Earth to help their gaming company win the extraterrestrial console wars. Although, after he failed the mission, Hasuta joined the Space Defense Agency and remained on Earth to help protect a human boy named Mahiro Yasaka. Hasuta quickly fell in love with him and, despite Mahiro not being interested in him romantically, the two of them are generally in good terms. Kuuko initially wanted them to be together so she can have Nyaruko all to herself, until she set her sights on having a threesome with both Mahiro and Nyaruko.

Hasuta takes the form of a young feminine boy with blond hair, however, he is capable of transforming into his "King in Yellow" super mode where he appears to be more masculine and mature. His species was the inspiration for the character "Hastur" from the Cthulhu Mythos. He is physically stronger than Nyaruko and Kuuko, and in combat, he uses the power of wind manipulation.

entities.name: Patrice Hathaway
entities.description:
Patrice Hathaway, the Violinist, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games, appearing as a playable character for several of their Arkham Horror Files lines of games including Arkham Horror itself.

Always a natural with the bow and string, as Patrice grew up it became clear to all that she was something of a musical prodigy. Immersing herself in her sublime violin symphonies, upon reaching adulthood, her fame grew to worldwide proportions, and she played in venues across the globe.

However, something had always nagged at the back of Patrice's mind when she played, the thought that something was watching her and listening to her harmonies. And so it was that when she found herself playing a few melodies with an old gypsy woman one day, the crone's revelation that she was being stalked by something malignant was not as much of a shock as it should have been; she took notice and decided to do something about it. Thus, Patrice took her first steps on the path which would ultimately lead to the knowledge that there really are monsters lurking in the abyss beyond human sight.

Although initially conceived as a character for the Innsmouth Horror expansion of Arkham Horror Second Edition, Patrice has also made appearances in several of Fantasy Flight's companion games including Eldritch Horror, Arkham Horror: The Card Game, and Elder Sign. In 2010 a plastic figurine designed to replace the cardboard tokens included with the games was created for her as part of the Arkham Horror Premium Figures line, although this is no longer in production (all ).

entities.name: Lola Hayes
entities.description:
Lola Hayes, the Actress, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for inclusion in their Arkham Horror Files line of games and fiction set within the greater Cthulhu Mythos.

After her last show - a bizarre play full of ritualistic chanting and disturbing masks - Lola decided to admit herself into a sanatorium; the nightmares had just been too much to bear, and she feared for her mental wellbeing.

However, when she read the article in the newspaper about how the director of that play had hung himself, she decided that she needed to look into things for herself. So, once again securing herself a role in the production, she surreptitiously strapped on her derringer and went back to work.

Although first created for Fantasy Flight's Kingsport Horror expansion for their Second Edition of the Arkham Horror board game, she has since appeared in other games of theirs related the Mythos, including Eldritch Horror and Arkham Horror: The Card Game. In addition, a plastic miniature intended to replace the cardboard counters included in the game boxes was released as part of their Arkham Horror Premium Figures line, but production of this has since been halted (all ).

entities.name: Hellhound
entities.description:
The Hellhound is a fictional demon in the prime reality of the Marvel universe of Marvel Comics. It was created in 1992 by Chris Cooper, first appearing in issue #2 of the 1st volume of Darkhold: Pages from the Book of Sins.

Hellhounds are summoned by the Darkhold. It tracks down what you summoned it to find and once that's done it gets at the page which summoned it so it can go back home. The Hellhound won't stop until it does. The Hellhound is the size of a large pig with teeth the size of daggers, possesses superhuman strength and speed, and is incredibly tough, being able to survive being hit repeatedly by laser defenses.

entities.name: Tisha Hewitt
entities.description:
Tisha Hewitt is a fictional character created by American author Lee Clark Zumpe for his Cthulhu Mythos stories.

A woman somewhere in middle age, Tisha is a native of Arkham, Massachusetts. A former investigative journalist for the Arkham Gazette, she left this profession to author books on real-life ghost sightings, a field in which she became well respected. As well as writing, she founded a successful ghost tour business in her home town and still accepts the occasional contract as a freelance journalist. In addition, she is on the books of the Arkham Detective Agency as a consultant.

Tisha had a brother, Alex, five years older, who disappeared when he was seventeen. In her later life, she discovered that he had been sacrificed by a cult on the outskirts of Arkham.

entities.name: Charlene Hines
entities.description:
Charlene Hines is a fictional character created by Canadian author Troy Young for his Nyarlathotep Cycle series of Cthulhu Mythos stories.

A twenty-eight year old woman with an extensive criminal record, at the time of her introduction Charlene is serving a lengthy jail sentence for murder. Her only distinguishing feature is a mole on her chin, which she rubs when she is anxious.

Once a promising student from a wealthy family, Charlene's life was destroyed after she was abducted by a clan of inbred cultists who promised her as a bride to the Great Old One Hastur. Despite making an escape, she ran away from home, falling into a life of drugs and prostitution on the streets. After her pimp mistreated her once too often, she killed him, and was sentenced to prison time.

After five years in jail, Charlene was approached by Harjit Singh of the Department of Extraordinary Phenomena at the suggestion of Adele Kramer. Singh recruited her into the organisation and partnered her with senior investigator Malcolm Mayweather.

entities.name: Brad Hollins
entities.description:
Brad Hollins is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games as part of the backstory for Investigator "Skids" O'Toole in the board game of Lovecraftian Horror, Arkham Horror.

While doing time for the murders of nine people, Brad made the acquaintance of small-time criminal "Skids" O'Toole due to the fact that the two were cellmates. While Skids was mostly harmless, Brad was crazy as a junkyard dog, claiming that aliens made him do what he had done, and constantly ranting and raving about the Ancient or Old Ones. Where he came about this knowledge is anybody’s guess - he sometimes claimed it came to him in dreams - but Brad was determined to get to Argentina to put a stop to them.

All of this came to an end, however, the night Skids heard his cellmate chanting in a strange tongue. Looking over, he was just in time to see Brad's body erupt into a blazing inferno, killing him instantly.

It was this experience which prompted Skids to travel to Arkham upon his release in order to get to the bottom of what had happened to Brad.

entities.name: Horsemen of Nyarlathotep
entities.description:
The Four Horsemen of Nyarlathotep, also known as simply the Horsemen of Nyarlathotep, are a demonic quartet of supernatural beings who serve the messenger of the Outer Gods, Nyarlathotep. They are part of the "Million Favoured Ones". They are supporting antagonists of Fall of Cthulhu, a supernatural horror comic book series published by Boom! Studios in 2007.

entities.name: Wendell Hunt
entities.description:
Wendell Hunt is a character created by American author David Kenney for his Lost Archivist series of Cthulhu Mythos stories. He made his first appearance in the 2019 short story "The Lost Archivist."

Hunt is the chief archivist of Miskatonic University's Armitage Memorial Library. In this capacity, he encounters a variety of supernatural forces, including covetous necromancers amongst the faculty and zombies, amongst others. He is assisted in his tasks by his boss Dr. Clara Pedrick and the insane researcher Dr. Shattuck, both of whom have extensive experience in the field.

During the course of his duties, hunt has suffered some serious and permanent physical disfigurements, including the loss of an eye on one occasion, and an ear on another.

During his investigation of theft and murder at one of the library’s most dangerous departments, Storage Area B, Hunt confronted and defeated a magic-wielding professor and his zombie minion. He is able to overcome the threat and restore balance to the archives, but loses his ear to the zombie's hungry jaws in the process (: "Gnashing Whispers")

entities.name: Ialdagorth
entities.description:
Ialdagorth is a fictional entity created by Kevin Eric Sheridan for his short story "Servants of the Coils".

Ialdagorth is a cousin and servitor of Azathoth. He appears as a black, shapeless and malevolent mist. The sight of the monstrousity is said to be unnerving, if not traumatizing.

entities.description:
Iaon-Thamungazoth, Lord of Chaos is a Great Old One worshiped in ancient Lemuria, one of the three primal lords of Lemuria and an aspect of the Triple God of Chaos.

entities.name: Rocco Ignacio
entities.description:
Father Rocco Ignacio is a fictional character created by American author Armand Rosamilia for his Keyport Cthulhu series of Mythos stories.

A man in his twilight years, Father Rocco has ministered to the steadily dwindling parish of the Keyport Church of God for decades. Despite the Esoteric Order of Dagon's attempts to run him out of town and his flock's loss of faith, he himself remains a devout servant of his Lord.

In the first book of the series, fugitive criminal Bones arrived in Keyport and he and Father Rocco joined forces to combat the sinister Esoteric Order of Dagon's scheme to awaken Cthulhu, recruiting the help of others along the way. Although badly beaten by cultists at the story's conclusion, Father Rocco clung to life as a terrifying monstrosity rose from the depths of Keyport Bay.

entities.name: Ilyth'la
entities.description:
Ilyth'la is a fictional entity from the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was first mentioned in Fred Pelton's occult text "The Sussex Manuscript".

Ilyth'la is a woman created by Cthulhu and Nyarlathotep who founded her own cult among humans in prehistoric Virklyu. According to The Sussex Manuscript, many cultists consider themselves her children. Later, Daniel Harms identified her with the Hebrew demon Lilith. (: The Encyclopedia Cthulhiana)

entities.name: Intelligent Mollusk
entities.description:
Intelligent mollusks are a telepathic race of creatures which inhabit the seas of Venus in the distant future. They are mentioned in Brian Lumley's Cthulhu Mythos novel The Transition of Titus Crow.

In the same book Titus Crow further states that ten million years later all life on Venus has died but it is unclear if the mollusks still survive elsewhere.

entities.name: Ishiti
entities.description:
Ishiti is a fictional character from Marvel Comics who was created in 1982 by Gil Kane and Bruce Jones. She made her first appearance in issue #134 of the first volume of the Conan the Barbarian comic book series.

Ishiti is an offspring of the Elder God Set. She had the ability to "freeze" time for everything except serpents and any living being which had been bitten and poisoned by a serpent, and anything that person was carrying. In her serpentine form, she had the body of a giant snake with a humanoid head that had fangs and a gorgon-like spread of writhing serpents.

In her semi-humanoid form, she had the upper torso of a woman and was able to extend her two long snake-like arms which would draw a victim into her dimension. Conventional weapons (for example, swords) were unable to harm Ishiti due to her scaly hide. She could also project powerful mystical blasts from her mouth, which with repeated strikes could turn a human into Serpent Man. Her mouth had fangs and was able to swallow a fully grown man.

entities.name: Pete Ivalu
entities.description:
Sergeant Pete Ivalu is a fictional character created by Troy Young for his Nyarlathotep Cycle series of Cthulhu Mythos short stories.

A 6-year veteran in the Canadian Army Rangers, an organisation purposed with maintaining a military presence in the Arctic Circle, Pete Ivalu was a small man with an infectious smile. He was of Inuk (Inuit) descent, a trait which aided him during his deployment in the tundra.

After his squad was tasked with the investigation of a missing tribe in the far north of Canada, Ivalu was assigned to assist Dr. Adele Kramer in preventing them from completing their purpose: awakening a malevolent entity trapped in the ice floes. In the aftermath of this operation, he was seconded to the Department of Extraordinary Phenomena, a black-ops government agency dedicated to protecting humankind from "The Other".

Ivalu's first mission saw him partnered with Joe Mills, an Inspector in the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, and the two successfully eliminated a Nyarlathotep cult.

entities.name: Jack Russell
entities.description:
Jack Russell (aka, Werewolf by Night) is a superhero in the fictional Marvel universe, who was created in 1972, a C-list hero with a few comic book series.

Jack Russell is a werewolf , the son of a Transylvanian nobleman and baron. One descended from a family which had been cursed by the Elder God Chthon. It was the curse of lycanthropy which remained dormant until his father activated it by reading a passage in the Darkhold. On his 18th birthday, he turned into a werewolf.

Ever since he has been trying to find a cure (and for his sister who also became a werewolf though she was later cured by a sorcerer who took the curse upon himself) and until then ways to control or minimize the curse. An adventurer who lives off the trust fund established by his mother through the sale of his father's estate, he has fought the evil forces of the supernatural (including the Cult of the Darkhold and the Wolf Lord Varcolac) both individually and as a member of the Midnight Sons.

entities.name: Doyle Jeffries
entities.description:
Doyle Jeffries is a fictional character who appears in Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Files line of Cthulhu Mythos-related games and fiction. He is the editor of the Arkham Advertiser, Arkham's local newspaper in the Fantasy Flight Games version of the Cthulhu Mythos.

Doyle Jeffries first appeared in the Arkham Horror Second Edition expansion The King in Yellow as a Blight, a character which imparts negative effects onto the players.

In Richard Lee Byers' 2018 novella Ire of the Void, Professor Norman Withers approached Jeffries at the offices of the Advertiser requesting access to their archives in an effort to find others which had suffered the same fate as his friend Claus Schmidt, who had been abducted by a Hound of Tindalos. Jeffries obliged this request, on the condition that Withers later give him an exclusive interview on the event. Jeffries did indeed get his exclusive, but it was a heavily-edited version of the tale which featured no supernatural events.

entities.name: Bob Jenkins
entities.description:
Bob Jenkins, The Salesman, is an investigator character for Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Cthulhu Mythos board game, making his first appearance in the Second Edition Core Set. Since then, he has appeared in many of Fantasy Flight's Arkham Horror-related products, and was even given his own plastic miniature in the first wave of Premium Figure releases.

As with all of the Arkham Horror investigator backstories, Jenkins' history and motivations are not entirely consistent. However, unlike many, the essence of his motivations remain the same: he is on a quest to locate the source of some mysterious gold coins in an effort to finally make his "big score."

entities.name: K'thugguol
entities.description:
K'thugguol, a.k.a. the Slime-Thing or the Grand Shoggoth, is a fictional character created by Lin Carter for his short story "The Descent into the Abyss". It is the oldest and mightiest member of the shoggoth species, the first of its kind to have been created, and a servant of the entity Ubbo-Sathla, who the shoggoths adopted as their god.

Like a typical shoggoth, K'thugguol is described as a large, gelatinous, amoeboid creature with myriads of eyestalks. It dwells deep in the subterranean realm of grey-litten Y'qaa and guards the entrance of the pit inhabited by Ubbo-Sathla. entities.name: Kaajh'Kaalbh
entities.description:
Kaajh'Kaalbh is a fictional entity created by Jeff Beney for the Call of Cthulhu scenario "Full de Drames", featured in the French fanzine Backstab #9. The character is depicted as being a servant of the Outer God known as Azathoth.

Kaajh'Kaalbh is an entity of pure chaos, usually dwelling in the realm of Chaos. It has no true stable form, and is brought to the Earth dimension through summoning magic. This summoning by black magic requires the assistance of a Dimensional Shambler to succeed, due to the requirement to find and access the correct dimension of Chaos in which Kaajh'Kallbh dwells.

Once summoned, the form taken by Kaajh'Kaalbh is stable when on Earth. However, what that form may be is random- anything from a colossal puddle of goo to a rocky dinosaur-like monster. Formless and fearless, Kajh'Kaalbh is immensely powerful.

entities.name: Kaalut
entities.description:
Kaalut is a fictional character created by J. B. Lee for the short story "Genuine Article" (January, 1998).

Kaalut is a gigantic insectoid larva-like horror, dwelling in the nebulous realm of K'gil'mnon, along with the Gharoides, its parasitic insectoid servants. It also likely has human worshipers.

Kaalut, the Gharoides, and K'gil'mnon were all created by J. B. Lee before he ever read H. P. Lovecraft. Upon discovering the Cthulhu Mythos, Lee decided to incorporate his inventions into the pantheon, mentioning Kaalut along with Yog-Sothoth, Nyarlathotep, Azathoth and Shub-Niggurath in "Genuine Article" (January, 1998).

entities.name: Kandar the Destroyer
entities.description:
Kandar the Destroyer is a fictional demon created by Sean Clements in 2018 for the STARZ series Ash vs Evil Dead.

Kandar the Destroyer is a demon which was unleashed by the Dark Ones. Prophesied to battle the Prophesied One to test mankind's mettle. It wreaked havoc and not even the US military could stop it despite calling in air strikes and deploying armor against the demon. It was finally killed by Ash who fired the Kandarian Dagger into it's mouth.

It was impervious to all types of attacks (e.g. bullets, explosives), except for the Kandarian Dagger which could kill it. The demon increased its strength by absorbing the damage inflicted by fighter jets and tanks. If a nuclear weapon had been used its strength would have been increased exponentially. The demon could also breathe fire.

entities.name: Kandarian Demon
entities.description:
The Kandarian Demon is a fictional demon created by Sam Raimi in 1981 for the movie, "The Evil Dead", though it would not appear in physical form till 1987 in the sequel, Evil Dead 2.

The Kandarian Demon is the creator of the Deadites, though it's unknown if it was created by the Dark Ones or they got it to do their bidding. Sometime in the past, it was placed into a slumber by a spell within the Necronomicon. To summon the Kandarian Demon requires the reciting of passages in the Necronomicon. Known sightings of the Kandarian Demon include in medieval England (circa 1300 AD), the United States in Tennessee (1980s), and again in the United States in Michigan (early 21st century).

It is able to turn nearly anything into a Deadite, including plants, humans, and inanimate objects. When it comes to humans, it will focus on a specific target. Going so far as to chase the target, until it "infects" the victim. In its non-corporeal form the Kandarian Demon has the ability to apply physical force, and can fly long distances several feet over the ground.

entities.name: Charlie Kane
entities.description:
Charlie Kane, the Politician, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for inclusion in their Arkham Horror Files line.

Charlie Kane is a man on a mission, a politician determined to clean up Arkham. Like many politicians, he made whatever promises he needed to to get elected, but unlike most, he actually did what he could to help the city once he came to power. Charlie has had to do things that he doesn’t like to think about, but all of his actions have most definitely been for the public good.

Being a man with his finger on the pulse, Charlie's contacts slowly began to feed him the parts of a sinister picture in Arkham, one which he didn’t like one bit. However, he couldn’t tell anybody about it; nobody would believe him for one thing, and for another he couldn’t be causing panic in the streets. So, gathering his meagre evidence together, Charlie went to see an old acquaintance, Professor Grant, at Miskatonic University.

Standing dumbfounded over Professor Grant's horribly mutilated corpse in a university office whose walls were stained crimson, Charlie took his first steps down the road to ridding the streets of whatever threat has befallen them, whatever the cost.

entities.name: Ernst Kant
entities.description:
Baron Ernst Kant is a fictional character created by Brian Lumley as a recurring background element in his Cthulhu Mythos stories. He is first mentioned in Lumley's story "The Mirror of Nitocris" (1971).

Kant is described as a "witch-hunter" or "the witch-hunting Baron." He was the putative owner of a silver-plated revolver accompanied by silver bullets, later sold to occultist Henri-Laurent de Marigny; there is an "ornately inscribed 'K' on the weapon’s butt," but de Marigny acknowledges that there is not "a single shred of evidence" that the pistol actually belonged to Kant.

Kant is said to be the father of occultist Joachim Feery--though Feery was "illegitimate," and thus not eligible to inherit Kant's title.

Kant suffered a "hideous and inexplicable death in a Westphalian Bedlam." According to "a comparatively modern work on singular foreign mental cases," Kant believed that "his every insane action [was] controlled by a creature he called Yibb-Tstll," which he described as “huge and black with writhing breasts and an anus within its forehead, a black-blooded thing whose brains feed upon its own wastes….”

entities.name: Karakal
entities.description:
Karakal, also known as Karakal of Flames, is a fictional entity created by Sandy Petersen for the Call of Cthulhu supplement H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands, depicted as being one of the Great Ones, the gods of Earth that reside in Kadath. He is believed to be the lord of fire and is said to have a handsome face, to be bare-chested, and to be enveloped in blazing flames.

He is primarily worshipped by magicians and is served by a species known as the Minions of Karakal. He also occasionally leaves Kadath and travels in disguise. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands)

He might also be the same being as Zo-Kalar.(: "The Crawler of Pnoth") However, both are usually regarded as independent deities. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands)

entities.name: Wade Kearney
entities.description:
Wade Kearney is a fictional character created by American author Ron Shiflet for his Cthulhu Mythos stories. He made his debut appearance in the short story "Unfinished Business" in July 2006.

Kearney is a tough, hard-drinking private detective based in Arkham, Massachusetts. Despite having no desire to look into such matters, many of the cases which cross his desk involve supernatural elements: as a result, he is occasionally sought out by clients who have heard of his experience with occult investigations.

In addition to his detective services, Kearney has also been known to provide security services, although he appears somewhat reluctant to engage in such employment.

In his story notes for the 2017 edition of Looking for Darla: Stories of Mythos Noir, creator Ron Shiflet states that "The truth is that there was an ongoing mental tussle at the time as to whether I should focus on [Bill] Sweetan or Wade Kearney as an ongoing character in my fiction. They are pretty much the same person but I eventually seemed to settle on Kearney."

entities.name: Keeper of Dreams
entities.description:
The Keeper of Dreams is a fictional monster created by Gary Myers for his Dreamlands short story "Passing of a Dreamer".

The Keeper of Dreams is a living creature disguised as an idol that squats on an altar made "of what the unimaginative think are merely human bones", behind a secret door in a hidden alley in the dream town of Ulthar. Its appearance is similar to a salamander with "improperly placed" eyes, flabby claws and "fretted wings". Whatever it has "in lieu of a mouth" made ex-priest Snireth-Ko scream when he saw it.

The Keeper of Dreams is known for its ability to grant wishes, or more accurately sell them. What it demands as payment for its clients' desires is unknown, but ominous, apparently involving the death of the client, whose bones are afterwards added to the Keeper's altar. The fees are kept in a mysterious painted box, so the Keeper may someday use them when the Old Gods awaken to reclaim the Earth, either as a form of blackmail or "to purchase unspeakable favours" from them. (: "Passing of a Dreamer")

In the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, the Keeper's is payment is revealed to be its clients' souls, kept in silvery globes inside the box. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands) Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Other Supernatural Beings Category:Extra-Dimensional Characters

entities.name: Keeper of the Cage
entities.description:
The Keeper of the Cage was an enormous once-human monstrosity who dwelt deep within the Dreamlands in the H. P. Lovecraft-inspired Cthulhu Mythos. As his name might suggest, he was the guardian of an enormous cage filled with beings who were to be sacrificed to the Great Old Ones. His first appearance was in the novel The Clock of Dreams by Brian Lumley.

A colossal, hairless, humanoid creature whose skin had the whitish pallor of the grave, the Keeper claimed to be both near-immortal and near-omniscient. Formerly a mortal man who had been remade by the Great Old Ones after they caught him trying to use their own power against them, the Keeper had been stripped of all self-interest save that required to survive, and posted as a sentry next to the great pit into which their sacrifices were to be cast.

When interdimensional time-traveler Titus Crow journeyed through the Dreamlands his love, the Lady Tiania, was abducted by one of the servants of his enemies, a great Night-gaunt. Following the creature back to its nest, he found her in the hands of the Keeper. After freeing the creatures held in the cage, Crow attempted to do battle with the Keeper but was completely outmatched. Only the intervention of Crow’s friend, Henri-Laurent de Marigny, swung things in Crow‘s favour, with de Marigny at the helm of a machine outfitted with a weapon of awesome power by the Elder Gods. This weapon made short work of the Keeper, and the trio, along with all of the those imprisoned in the cage, were able to make their escape.

entities.name: Keeper of the Moon-Lens
entities.description:
The Keeper of the Moon-Lens is an avatar of Shub-Niggurath created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Moon-Lens".

The Keeper of the Moon-Lens is a massive creature that appears like a towering white mass of gelatinous flesh. Its legs have several joints, and the feet are shaped like circular pads. Instead of arms, it has three spines that can be used to hold onto the ground to facilitate movement. Its head is formed by thick coils of semi-transparent flesh. The face consists of "a huge toothed beak" and a number of yellow eyes that peer in many different directions. It speaks with a sibilant high-pitched voice.

This avatar is worshiped by the inhabitants of the English town of Exham in the Severn Valley, who can summon it using a gigantic lens mounted atop a high pylon to create a beacon of concentrated moonlight and open a door to the interior of a hill, from which the Keeper will emerge. Chosen "sacrifices" will be engulfed by the monster's coils of gelatinous flesh before being expelled. Those who go through this ritual begin to experience a gradual transformation, both physical and mental, turning them into the Goff'nn Hupadgh Shub-Niggurath (a.k.a. the Blessed of Shub-Niggurath). These are creatures reminiscent of the legendary satyrs and dryads, whose flesh, at least in some cases, is tough and wood-like, and who become immortal once the transformation is complete.

Inside the hill, the Keeper inhabits a subterranean world of catacombs built with alien geometry and strange angles. The ancient Romans worshiped it as the Magna Mater, while modern cultists seem to refer to it with male and female pronouns interchangeably, suggesting that the entity might be androgynous. Like many beings associated with the Great Old Ones, the Keeper of the Moon-Lens can be repelled by the star-signs. (: "The Moon-Lens") Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Avatars of Shub-Niggurath
