entities.name: Annie Knowby
entities.description:
Annie Knowby is a fictional hero in the Evil Dead franchise. The character was originally created by Sam Raimi for the 1987 horror/comedy film Evil Dead 2, and would later be featured in the comic book series Army of Darkness.

Annie Knowby arrived at her parents cabin with her boyfriend and two locals, to show them lost pages of the Necronomicon that she found, only to find evidence of a slaughter and a bloody Ash Williams. At first they believed Ash to be the murderer, but soon discovered the horror of the Deadites. One by one the members of her party were killed, till only she and Ash remained. As she read the Necronomicon to banish the Deadites, she was mortally wounded by Evil Ash's dismembered hand, dying as she spoke the final words of the incantation.

An alternate version survived the events in the Cabin and ended up in hell when it swallowed the cabin. With the help of a simulacrum of Ash, she freed her parents souls. After the two of them escaped from Hell, they would go on killing Deadites back on Earth. Eventually they would end up in the Mirror Dimension.

entities.name: Koth-Serapis
entities.description:
Koth-Serapis is a fictional sorcerer who features in Robert M. Price's stories set in Robert E. Howard's James Allison story cycle.

An evil magician of the Hyperborean age, Koth-Serapis penned the occult script which came to be known as the Black Rituals of Koth-Serapis when alive.

At the moment of his death, he cursed the Vanir warrior Bane to live forever through multiple incarnations until such time as the two could meet again and he could take his revenge upon the savage. However, in the 1930s Bane, now in the form of a Texan man named James Allison, met the sorcerer and defeated him, breaking the curse and earning his final rest.

After Koth-Serapis' death in Hyperborea, he somehow transformed into a colossal worm-like creature which inhabited the Dreamlands and consumed the souls of the dead. How this fits with his confrontation with James Allison in the 1930s is unclear.

entities.name: Adele Kramer
entities.description:
Dr. Adele Kramer is a character who features in Troy Young's Nyarlathotep Cycle of Cthulhu Mythos stories.

A woman in her early 30s, Adele Kramer is a marine biologist, formerly working at Dalhousie University, currently employed in the service of the Department of Extraordinary Phenomena, an agency which stands in opposition to "The Other": a catch-all term given to the forces of the Cthulhu Mythos.

After an encounter with an entity and its human thrall in the Canadian Arctic Circle on her first assignment for the agency, Adele was wounded: she later sported a bite scar across her cheek and was missing the ends of her left ring and pinky fingers.

Adele briefly possessed a wide range of extremely powerful psychic powers as a result of spending time in proximity to Azathoth, but saw this as more of a curse than a blessing. These abilities were later removed by the Outer God Yog-Sothoth as a reward for her service.

entities.name: Kthanid
entities.description:
Kthanid is an Elder God in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by the late British author Brian Lumley for his 1975 novel The Transition of Titus Crow, the second in Lumley's Titus Crow series.

Reputed to be the “brother” or "cousin" of the Great Old One Cthulhu, Kthanid is physically identical to his sibling - a colossal humanoid with stubby bat-wings and sporting a growth of octopoid tentacles from his lower face - in every way but one: his eyes are a deep gold in colour. Said to be as good as Cthulhu is evil, Kthanid radiates an air of benevolence to all who those in his presence. He is the head of the pantheon of Elder Gods who oppose both the Great Old Ones and Outer Gods, and resides in a vast crystal palace at the centre of the realm of Elysia, home of the Elder Gods.

Kthanid summoned the cosmic time-traveller Titus Crow after the latter became lost in the infinite depths of the multiverse, seeking a champion to aid him in his battle against the Great Old Ones. He then introduced Titus to his daughter Tiania, and the two fell instantly in love.

The Elder God then sent Crow on a mission to Earth’s Dreamlands in order to defeat the threat of the Great Old Ones which had begun to fester there, claiming to be unable to travel to that reality himself.

entities.name: Kulan Gath
entities.description:
Kulan Gath is a fictional character in the Marvel universe who first appeared in 1972 in issue #14 of the 1st volume of Conan the Barbarian. He also has starred in the Red Sonja line of comics published by Dynamite Entertainment.

Kulan Gath was an incredibly powerful sorcerer, whose power approached the level of the Sorcerer Supreme, Doctor Strange. His power was amplified by human sacrifices and his N'Garai masters. Kulan Gath was able to transform NY city and its population into Hyborian Age analogs, project mystical lasers, summon demonic entities, and manipulate flesh and bone.

During the Hyborian Age he was Stygia's dominant sorcerer. He waged war with his bitter rival the sorceress Vammatar of Hyperborea, but then formed an alliance with her. They married and attempted to free the imprisoned Shuma-Gorath from Mount Crom. Who they then attempted to subjugated, and were overwhelmed by the Old One. Each though the other dead, and both headed back home. Kulan Gath returned to Stygia where he had been displaced by Thoth-Amon. For a while he apprenticed uner him, but was later forced out of Stygia due to his blasphemous sorcery. He would later clash with the sorceress (and mutant) Selene Gallio, and had multiple encounters with the barbarian Conan in various kingdoms of the Hyborian super continent.

He returned to life in late 20th century Earth by possessing the body of a worker who found his necklace. Kulan Gath transformed NY City and its inhabitants into a city of the Hyborian Age, enslaving the Morlocks, X-Men, New Mutants, and Avengers. While Selene and Kulan Gath restarted their old feud, the heroes regained their memories and turned on him. Using the mutant Magik, Doctor Strange reversed time to undo Gath's spell. Later a fisherman found his necklace and was himself possessed. Kulan Gath traveled the world and ended up in South America where he took over an indigenous village. In his attempt to ascend to godhood, he attempted to sacrifice a goddess his agents captured to the N'Garai. The Avengers foiled his plans therefore the N'Garai feasted on him.

entities.name: Kuuko
entities.description:
Kuuko (also known as Cthugha) is an extraterrestrial entity from the fictional universe of the Haiyore! Nyaruko-san series.

Kuuko was a childhood friend of Nyaruko before they graduated from space school. Many years later, Kuuko was hired by Nodens as a bodyguard for his plans of human-trafficking in the theme park of R'lyeh, where she eventually reunited with Nyaruko and confessed her romantic feelings towards her. Nyaruko rejected Kuuko's advances due to a human boy named Mahiro Yasaka being her true love. Seeing him as an obstacle between them, Kuuko tried to kill Mahiro, leading to Nyaruko defeating her in battle. Despite this, Kuuko later moved to Earth to help protect Mahiro so she can stay close to Nyaruko. Over time, Kuuko also developed feelings towards him, showing interest in having a threesome with both Mahiro and Nyaruko. When her cousin Kuune tried to be in an incestuous relationship with her, Mahiro pretended to be in an engagement with Kuuko in order to convince Kuune to leave her alone. Kuuko continued to try to get together with Nyaruko, much to Nyaruko's annoyance. She is also big into otaku culture and loves playing video games.

Kuuko is capable of shapeshifting and takes the form of a red-haired slender human girl. Her species was the inspiration for the character "Cthugha" from the Cthulhu Mythos, and is considered to be archenemies with Nyaruko's. (likely a reference to August Derleth's short story "The Dweller in Darkness") Although, she is physically weaker than Nyaruko, Kuuko is still a very competent fighter. In combat, she uses the power of pyrokinesis as well as a plethora of weapons including a crowbar, lasers and swords.

entities.name: Lady with the Red Parasol
entities.description:
The Lady with the Red Parasol, whose real name is Tzu San Niang, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Cthulhu Mythos setting.

The Lady is a beautiful woman of apparently Asian descent, who is never seen without her signature red parasol, which is likely one of the powerful magical artefacts known as "Keys." She is a senior member of the Red Coterie, a secret society dedicated to obtaining the Keys as part of an unknown agenda.

Although capable of wielding significant mystical powers, such as the ability to psychically reach through walls and attack her enemies (: "City of Waking Dreams"), she is not immune to magic herself, as seen when a blast from the Key known as the Xiamen Bi left her visibly shocked and unwell (: "A Forty Grain Weight of Nephrite").

The Lady is known to be a formidable figure in the Shanghai criminal underworld, as well as amongst its upper echelons (: "City of Waking Dreams"), but has been seen to operate in as diverse locations as Cuba (: "Brother Bound") and San Francisco, California (: "A Forty Grain Weight of Nephrite").

entities.name: Marie Lambeau
entities.description:
Marie Lambeau, also known as the Entertainer and the Smoky Velvet, is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Files line of Cthulhu Mythos releases. She made her first appearance in the Dunwich Horror expansion for Arkham Horror in July 2006.

A young black woman from New Orleans, Louisiana, Marie Lambeau is an extremely talented singer. Her grand-mére was regarded by many as a witch, and some believe that Marie carries a touch of magic in her blood as a result.

Shortly after moving to Arkham, Marie's grand-mére passed, and the girl began to hear songs and rhymes in her head. What they mean, Marie is yet to find out.

Since her debut, Marie has appeared in several other Arkham Horror Files releases including Eldritch Horror and Arkham Horror: The Card Game. In 2010, a pre-painted plastic miniature was released as a gaming aid as part of the Arkham Horror Premium Figures line, although this is no longer in production.

entities.name: R. Layamon
entities.description:
R. Layamon is a fictional character who appears in Philip José Farmer's short story "The Freshman". Layamon is a professor at Miskatonic University, the chairman of the Committee of the Occult Arts and History Department and a powerful wizard. He is affiliated with the Lam Kha Alif fraternity.

Farmer provides a description of Layamon:

Throughout the story, Layamon is pushing the new student Roderick Desmond to cross a moral line, to eliminate the "defects of character" that would keep him from fulfilling his arcane potential.

entities.name: Le Novar
entities.description:
Le Novar is a character created by author J. B. Lee for his Cthulhu Mythos writings. He was first made mention of in the 1998 short story "Genuine Article".

Le Novar claims to be a cosmic time-travelling alien from Xandra the Asteroid Planet, currently occupying the body of a human being - an elderly black man named Nick Calvert - although whether this is actually the case is uncertain. He is the author of the fictional book The Stars Are With You!, a "paperback mishmash of [Erich] von Daniken, Madame [Helena] Blavatsky and H. P. Lovecraft", in which he reveals the truth of his origin.

Le Novar owns an artefact, dubbed the Clawed Crystal, which allows its user to travel through space and time, and even to affect events in the past. He has also been shown to be willing to loan the Crystal to others in exchange for favours, as seen when he allowed Robert Clarke the use of its abilities in exchange for the theft of a manuscript from Miskatonic University.

Despite there being no mention of Xandra the Asteroid planet in the works of Lovecraft, Le Novar being a body-swapping, time-and-space travelling alien suggests that he may be of the Great Race of Yith.

entities.name: Roy Leakey
entities.description:
Roy Leakey was a fictional character created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Moon-Lens".

Once a bookish man who enjoyed antiquarian pursuits, Roy Leakey had heard that there were many second-hand shops in the town of Exham in the Severn Valley, which he had never visited. One day he decided to take the train to Exham, although he had to do so via a very contrived route, as the town had only a single line which made its journey infrequently.

Upon reaching Exham, Leakey was tricked into thinking that there were no trips back out until the next day and so decided to spend the night in a local hotel. The hotel had only a single room on the second floor, one which overlooked an unusual hill fronted by a strange device resembling a tall, pylon-mounted lens.

Later that evening, whilst locked in his room by the hotel manager - a cultist of the Black Goat of the Woods, Shub-Niggurath - he saw an enormous monstrosity emerge from what Leakey saw was a door in the hillside. He was then offered the chance to become one of Shub-Niggurath's servants. However, he saw an opportunity to escape, and shimmied down the outside wall whilst the townsfolk lay prostrated in front of the aperture.

entities.name: Thomas Lee
entities.description:
Thomas Lee is a character created by British horror author Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Inhabitant of the Lake".

Born some time before 1865, Thomas Lee was a Brichester resident who, as an adult, became a servant of the Great Old One Glaaki, and the leader of his cult. In this capacity Lee commissioned a row of houses, later known as Lakeside Terrace, in a remote part of the Severn Valley next to the body of water in which his master dwells. He and his fellow cult members were responsible for transcribing the volumes known as the Revelations of Glaaki.

Having succumbed to the Green Decay, Lee is no longer able to tolerate the touch of sunlight, and now appears to spend his days inside one of the many stone sarcophagi which dot the landscape surrounding Lakeside Terrace.

entities.name: Emma Legrasse
entities.description:
Emma Legrasse was created by Dan Wickline in 2012, first appearing in issue #3 of the 1st volume of Grimm Fairy Tales Presents: Call of Wonderland by Zenescope Entertainment.

Emma Legrasse is a female police officer who finds herself dragged into the madness of Wonderland. Abused as a child she grew up to become a detective in the police force. While investigating a murder, her primary murder suspects (Julie Sands and Salome Gray) disappear. She then opens a new murder investigation, believing their disappearance is tied to the previous murder case. Emma becomes consumed by H. P. Lovecraft's journal and comes under the influence of the Mad Hatter's hat.

entities.name: Lesser Old One
entities.description:
The Lesser Old Ones is a designation coined by Lin Carter to refer to a category of beings who serve the Great Old Ones and lead their servitor races. Apart from their hierarchical rank in the Cthulhu Mythos, a notable difference between Great Old Ones and Lesser Old Ones is that the former have been (for the most part) imprisoned by their enemies, the Elder Gods, while the Lesser Old Ones remain (for the most part) free.

Although the concept appears in several other works, the term "Lesser Old One" is not always used. The role-playing game Call of Cthulhu refers to most of these beings as Greater Servitors, and a few of them as full-blown Great Old Ones. At the same time, the Second Edition of Malleus Monstrorum defines Lesser Old Ones as “deities in the process of developing into Great Old Ones, or Secondary deities to the Great Old Ones.” This definition includes Nctosa and Nctolhu, Pharol, Saaitii, Sebek, and Yegg-Ha. In the Demonbane Mythos, entities like Dagon and Mother Hydra are classified as Lesser Gods.

The concept of the Lesser Old Ones appears to be based on the works of August Derleth, specifically The Trail of Cthulhu series, which establishes that the Great Old Ones are served by two kinds of beings. Their ordinary servitors are species such as the Deep Ones, the Mi-Go, and the Tcho-Tcho people, which can be repelled by the five-pointed star-stones of Mnar. The second kind consists of the Great Old Ones' "immediate servitors". These are far mightier creatures, identified as "superior beings [...], against whom the five-pointed star is powerless". At least one of them is described as a giant, tentacled frog-like creature. (: "The Watcher from the Sky")

In the stories of Lin Carter, the expression "Lesser Old Ones" is used by Prof. Copeland (: "The Horror in the Gallery") and Abdul Alhazred (: "Behind the Mask") to denote a group of immortal beings who are several times more powerful than the servitor races they lead, but still nowhere close to the Great Old Ones they serve (: "The Descent into the Abyss"). They thus stand at an intermediary level between the Great Old Ones and their common servitors. Unlike their imprisoned masters, however, the Lesser Old Ones still roam the world, trying to find ways to free their overlords (: "The Horror in the Gallery").

entities.name: Calie Liddle
entities.description:
Carroll Ann Liddle was created by Raven Gregory and Daniel Lester in 2007, first appearing in issue #1 of the 1st volume of Grimm Fairy Tales: Return to Wonderland by Zenescope Entertainment. She is the primary protagonist of the Wonderland saga, appearing as the protagonist in the majority of the story arcs and mini-series.

Carroll Ann Liddle is Alice Liddle's daughter who grew up with a mother who slowly but steadily went insane. One day, Calie was given the task of watching her mother (to guard against the threat of suicide) but her mother demanded that she find a white rabbit which had escaped. Calie searched for the rabbit and eventually found it in the basement, in a previously unknown hole in the basement floor.

She fell through and her own adventures in Wonderland began. Calie would end up fighting and running from the Madness of Wonderland for decades, both in the Realm of Nightmares and on Earth. Fighting alongside her mother's aspect in Wonderland (Lacie) against the madness of Wonderland, battling her insane brother Johnny Liddle, trying to change Wonderland for the better, defending Earth from its madness, and trying to save and then protect her daughter Violet Liddle.

Calie evolves throughout the three series, and her evolution is tied to her own abilities, and especially those in Wonderland. Upon her second trip to Wonderland, while seeking to reclaim her daughter Violet, her physical abilities are all enhanced dramatically. Once the portal is destroyed she reverts to her ordinary capabilities as this was a result of her learning that she had control over the dimension by learning she had control over the madness which sought to infect her. In this mentality, she also proves adept with using martial weapons, most often a sword or a battle ax.

entities.name: Johnny Liddle
entities.description:
The Mad Hatter was created by Lewis Carroll in 1865, first appearing in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland. In 2008, the character was reimagined as Johnny Liddle for Zenescope Entertainment's Grimm Fairy Tales fictional universe, in the issue #1 of the 1st volume of Grimm Fairy Tales: Return to Wonderland.

Before Johnny Liddle, there were two other men who had the title of the Mad Hatter, with the first being Jack the Ripper and the second was Alice Liddle's brother, Drake Liddle, who corrupted his nephew, Johnny Liddle, molesting the child. He grew up into a sociopath who was fascinated with death and killed small animals. What finally broke his mind was his mother's suicide. After finding out that Alice committed suicide because of his father's infidelities with a prostitute, he murdered his father. Upon learning this, his sister Calie Liddle, sent her brother through the Mirror to Wonderland, where he was transformed into one of Wonderland's most feared inhabitants, an insane killer who sometimes serves the Jabberwocky.

entities.name: Violet Liddle
entities.description:
Violet Annabelle Liddle was created by Raven Gregory in 2009, first appearing in issue #1 of the 1st volume of Beyond Wonderland by Zenescope Entertainment.

After Calie Liddle escaped for the first time from Wonderland, she ran away to New York City with her boyfriend Brandon Price while already being pregnant. Violet was eventually born and joined her family's history of a connection to Wonderland, as it influenced her with its madness via the Mad Hatter's hat. Later she fought side by side with her mother, both in Wonderland and on Earth against the forces of the Realm of Nightmares.

entities.name: Teddy London
entities.description:
Theodore "Teddy" London is a fictional occult detective created by the late American author C.J. Henderson.

London is a two-fisted detective in the tradition of the original pulp magazines who is turned to by people who fall foul of Cthulhu Mythos-related problems and threats. He is sometimes assisted by overweight janitor Paul Morcey. London is armed with a pistol and a knife to which he has given the names Betty and Veronica respectively.

entities.name: Lrogg
entities.description:
Lrogg is a fictional deity created by Ramsey Campbell for his short story "The Insects from Shaggai", which portrays it as the main god worshiped by the L'gy'hxians, the native inhabitants of the planet L'gy'hx, known to humans as Uranus.

In the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, it is identified as an avatar of Nyarlathotep. (: Ye Booke of Monstres II)

Described as a "relatively insignificant deity" (compared to Azathoth), Lrogg is a two-headed bat-like creature worshiped as the main god on L'gy'hx. Its cult is regarded as comparatively agreeable, as Lrogg confers benefits to its believers and demands nothing more than an annual ritual that involves the removal of the limbs of a chosen native. Cultists are willing to tolerate other faiths, if not provoked. Their enemies are executed by having acid poured into their brains. The fact that these practices pale in comparison to the atrocities committed by the cult of Azathoth speaks volumes about the cruelty of the latter. (: "The Insects from Shaggai") Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Avatars of Nyarlathotep

entities.name: Lu-Kthu
entities.description:
Lu-Kthu, otherwise known as Lew-Kthew or the Birth-womb of the Great Old Ones, is an Outer God who first appeared in James Ambuehl's short story "Correlated Contents", published in 1998. Ambuehl is an American horror writer who has expanded H. P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos with the creation of the Lu-Kthu Cycle or Pantheon of Lu-Kthu.

Lu-Kthu is described in the book called The Rituals of Glaa-Dith.

The innumerable ovoid pustules on the slimy surface of the enormous creature are both inside and outside these tunnels and are in fact biological incubators. How often the larvae inside the incubators mature and spawn forth is unknown.

Lu-Kthu is the primary deity of the Lu-Kthu Cycle and the origin from which the gods of the Pantheon of Lu-Kthu were born. The true form of Lu-Kthu is unclear; theories have been proposed suggesting that Lu-Kthu is a physical entity, a star, a nebula, a separate entity possessing all of these characteristics, or a "Great Vortex". The depiction shown above is based on a painting featuring Lu-Kthu. (: "The Stalker in the Snows", "Correlated Contents")

entities.name: Lucifer
entities.description:
Luci Jenifer Inacio Das Neves, who goes by by the name of Lucifer, is a character created by American comic book creator Michael Alan Nelson for the Gray Man story arc of his Mythos series Fall of Cthulhu. She made her first appearance in issue #11 in March 2008.

A pretty young woman in her late teens or early twenties, Lucifer lived her early life as an orphan thief on the streets of Brazil. There, she encountered an occultist named Walter McKinley who took her in, making use of her talents as a thief in exchange for food and board. Under his tutelage, she gained a degree of mystical knowledge, including how to use protective wards and travel to the Dreamlands.

As an adult, Lucifer continues to use her talents to combat the supernatural threats which threaten humanity, despite the recent loss of her mentor.

Lucifer has, during the course of her activities, stolen a precious artefact from the supernatural creature known as the Harlot. Although she has been punished for this transgression, she remains in the Harlot's debt.

entities.name: Lucy
entities.description:
Lucy is a character created by author Ian Davey as one of the protagonists in his Bh'yhlun series of Cthulhu Mythos stories. She made her first appearance in 1997 in "Black Letter Day".

Lucy was, in the time before the coming of Nyarlathotep, a regular woman in a relationship with a man named Georgio, a gifted filmmaker. Georgio decided to create a piece based on an old book he had come across, Feery's Notes on the Necronomicon, and thus began the end of the human race, an event which Lucy was uniquely placed to witness.

After the fall of humankind Lucy, alone and pregnant, preserved her sanity through the careful use of certain drugs while she made her way to Glastonbury, following a psychic pull which promised safety.

Eventually reaching Glastonbury, Lucy, a girl who called herself Glyph, and older couple Helen and Aaron defeated an avatar for Nyarlathotep and managed to restore the world to its former condition- mostly…

entities.name: Luminous Transparency
entities.description:
The Luminous Transparency is a fictional entity created by American author and games designer Kevin A. Ross for the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. It first appeared in "Thunder in the Blood", a scenario included in the supplement End of the World (Triad Entertainments, 1994).

The Luminous Transparency is one of five Lesser Other Gods from the Court of Azathoth that appeared during a summoning of Azathoth near San Lucas. It appears as a constantly shifting and self-reconfiguring conglomeration of transparent blue-white pyramid shapes. During this process it encloses nearby objects within itself. (: End of the World)

entities.description:
The Lurker in the Star Pool is a fictional entity created by American author A. A. Attanasio for his 1980 short story "The Star Pools."

The Lurker in the Star Pool is one of the Million Favoured Ones, beings granted a new form by Nyarlathotep. It is described as a massive translucent blob full of a red gas with multiple heads resembling sharks and squids as well as gangly limbs and bat-like wings.

It dwells in the Star Pools, a collection of thousands of green ponds in Haiti.

entities.name: Devlin Macky
entities.description:
Devlin Fredelin Macky is a fictional character created by American author Brandon Berntson for his Lovecraft Mysteries trilogy of Cthulhu Mythos novels, for which he is the series protagonist. He made his debut appearance in the first book in the series, The Night of Dagon.

A private investigator in the East Coast city of Innsport, Macky is used to taking on any kind of job just to pay the bills, usually missing persons cases, or looking into spouses suspected of cheating. He operates a small office for his business in one of the more nondescript areas of the city, and drives a somewhat beaten-up, but still perfectly serviceable, coupe. He has an aversion to fire, deep water, heights, guns, and dogs, although none of these are crippling fears. Macky also drinks and smokes too much, character flaws which he freely admits to.

Macky was married in the past, to a woman named Veronica, who he nicknamed Posh-posh. Sadly, Veronica was diagnosed with cancer a month after their first meeting; she died two years later, after losing her battle against the disease.

Macky and his secretary Millie Von Clydesburgh have something of a complicated relationship: despite having shared a few kisses, Macky seems reluctant to commit, despite Millie having been quite blunt about her feelings for him.

entities.name: Jacob Maitland
entities.description:
Professor Jacob Maitland is a fictional character created by American author Robert M. Price as part of his Cthulhu Mythos writings. As noted by occult detective Anton Zarnak, he is a highly intelligent man, and later in life develops an extensive knowledge of the forces of the supernatural.

As a young graduate assistant working towards his doctorate at the Sanbourne Institute of Pacific Antiquities, Maitland aided Anton Zarnak with a matter regarding the acquisition of occult texts.

Later, as a senior faculty member at Sanbourne, with the aid of his star pupil and the Bimini Glyphs, Maitland decoded the mysteries of the R'lyeh Text. Whatever he learned from the translation, it pushed him to destroy the Text to protect humankind.

entities.name: Aphra Marsh
entities.description:
Aphra Marsh is the protagonist of the Innsmouth Legacy books by Ruthanna Emrys. She is a Deep One woman who has lived in San Francisco since her release from an Oklahoman concentration camp after World War II. She works in a bookstore and, less officially, for the FBI. She is the leader of a small magical coven, known as a confluence, following the Aeonist teachings she was raised in.

Aphra is a woman in her late thirties that consistently refers to herself as "ugly." She has the "bulging eyes, thick neck, and receding hairline" associated with her Innsmouth heritage. Despite this, cover art and several characters show attraction to her in-universe. She is assumed to be of a white ethnicity despite the mixed heritage of the Deep Ones.

Aphra Marsh was born in 1910 in Innsmouth, Massachusetts to Kezia and Silas Marsh. She was ten years old when the Innsmouth Raid occurred and she was interred along with her family, far away from the ocean. Despite this, she was already fluent in both Enochian (the language of the Yithians), English, and R'leyian (the language of the Deep Ones). While interred, their camp was later filled with Japanese victims of the real-life Executive Order 9066. While the majority of Deep Ones and Innsmouth residents died as a result, Aphra and her brother, Caleb Marsh, survived and were released with the Japanese residents in 1946.

Aphra would live with a Japanese family, the Kotos, in San Fransisco until 1949. She would work as a bookstore clerk for a minor occultist named Charlie Day. Aphra would keep her true nature secret from him even as she helped him in translating some of the occult works there. Later, she would be recruited by FBI agent, Ron Spector, to investigate Aeonist activity. While initially extremely reluctant, the FBI agent sharing the documentation of her mother's torture and dissection by the US government convinces her to cooperate. Aphra would investigate a minor Cthulhu cult led by Osmin Wilder and companion, Mildred Bergman, who had unwittingly been drowning their members by sending them out in parodies of the Deep Ones return to their homelands. She reluctantly has Ron Spector send the leaders of the cult to asylums for their safety. Aphra also takes her boss on as a magical apprentice. (: "The Litany of Earth")

entities.name: Harrison Marsh
entities.description:
Harrison Marsh is a character created by American author Armand Rosamilia for his Keyport Cthulhu series of Mythos tales.

At the beginning of the cycle, Harrison appeared as a youngish man with no distinguishing features. As his Innsmouth heritage began to assert itself, he gradually came to resemble his kinfolk, losing most of his hair and his skin taking on an unhealthy pallor.

It is worth noting that although Harrison comes from Innsmouth stock, he is considered of "weak blood" by those of the Esoteric Order of Dagon. Why this might be the case is not explained.

After coming to Keyport with his wife Nicole to settle his grandfather's estate, Nicole was abducted by the local chapter of the Esoteric Order of Dagon and used as a sacrifice to awaken Great Cthulhu. Despite Harrison's best efforts, he was unable to rescue her, and quickly began to assume the traits of his blood, the proximity to others of his kind apparently being the catalyst.

entities.name: Jeb Marsh
entities.description:
Jeb Marsh is a character created by American author Armand Rosamilia for his Keyport Cthulhu series of Mythos stories. He made his first appearance in the short story "Ancient" in 2012.

A distant descendant of the Innsmouth Marshes, Jeb carries the curse of his blood and is now almost completely inhuman. Upon his change, the Keyport branch of the Esoteric Order of Dagon locked him up in his secluded cottage, likely due to their belief that he was not of a like mind with them. However, he has managed to tunnel his way through the basement, and is now able to come and go as he pleases. It is implied that he roams the streets of Keyport at night, attempting to help those who might fall victim to the monstrous creatures which lurk beneath the town.

entities.name: Nicole Marsh
entities.description:
Nicole Marsh is a minor recurrent character in the Keyport Cthulhu series of Mythos stories by Armand Rosamilia.

Nicole is the young wife of Harrison Marsh, a descendant of the Keyport branch of the Marsh family.

When she and her husband travelled to Keyport to settle old Jeb Marsh's estate, Nicole was kidnapped and used as a sacrifice to awaken the Great Old One Cthulhu. However, the being found her to be unworthy, and although she was not killed in the process, the encounter left her in a catatonic state.

entities.name: Silas Marsh
entities.description:
Silas Marsh, the Sailor, is a character who features in many of Fantasy Flight Games' Cthulhu Mythos-related games, and who has also appeared in some of their fiction.

Growing up, Silas had always displayed a natural affinity for water, and for the ocean in particular. It therefore came as no great shock to anybody who knew him when he decided to pursue a career as a sailor. Signing up to a merchant shipping company, Silas took his leave and set off to explore the oceans.

As Silas sailed the world, visiting ports the world over, he began to have strange dreams, visions in which he walked through undersea cities and conversed with fish-like beings of nightmarish properties. Upon one of his rare trips home, he resolved to discover the source of these dreams, and was directed to the main branch of the family in Innsmouth.

First appearing as an Investigator for the Second Edition expansion of Arkham Horror, Innsmouth Horror, Silas has since made appearances in Eldritch Horror, Arkham Horror: The Card Game and Mansions of Madness, in addition to the novella The Deep Gate by Chris A. Jackson, which is centered on the character. In 2010, Fantasy Flight released a plastic miniature of Silas as part of their Arkham Horror Premium Figures line, but this is no longer available.

entities.name: Malcolm Mayweather
entities.description:
Malcolm Mayweather is a character created by Canadian author Troy Young for his Nyarlathotep Cycle series of Cthulhu Mythos stories.

Mayweather is a tall, physically fit black Canadian man, likely in his late twenties or early thirties. Since a violent encounter with a magic-using Nyarlathotep cultist, he is missing his left arm. He is capable of utilising minor magic, but the effects of this appear to consist solely of the ability to keep away the effects of the nightmares caused by exposure to the entities of the Cthulhu Mythos.

Mayweather was exposed to radiation in a temple to Nyarlathotep which caused him to develop a highly-aggressive form of cancer. It has been speculated that this is a magical affliction, which Nyarlathotep is capable of accelerating, halting, and perhaps even reversing.

A relationship had begun to form between Mayweather and junior agent Charlene Hines; this was cut short with the death of both parties.

entities.name: Dora McCain
entities.description:
Dora McCain is a character created by American author Ron Shiflet for his short story "Seduced".

Dora is a beautiful young girl with long blonde hair who is apparently in her middle teens. She dresses in cheap, dirty clothes, is poorly educated (at least by the standards of the modern world), and lives in a rickety old country shack with her father and at least four siblings.

A typical backwoods hillbilly from a degenerate West Virginia family, Dora's mother died when she was aged twelve, and a few weeks later she made the acquaintance of Mother Shub, a crazy old woman who lived deep in the forest and was widely believed to possess magical powers. Over the years, Mother Shub taught her how to mix potions, make prophecies and even command the animals of the woods on occasion.

When she was around fifteen, Dora was raped by three boys, brothers from a neighbouring family. She went to Mother Shub for help, who gave Dora her own power before passing on. Gathering her strength, Dora assembled the ingredients for a dark elixir and cast the spell she had been taught. Answering her call, Shub-Niggurath sent its servants to slaughter the brothers for her.
entities.short_description: Dora McCain is a character created by American author Ron Shiflet for his short story "Seduced".

entities.name: Meikumi Urushibarao
entities.description:
Meikumi Urushibarao is a fictional entity created by Kouichi Azakawa for his light novel series Makai Shoujo R'lyeh Lulu.

Meikumi Urushibarao is an avatar of Nyarlathotep, who takes the form of an attractive female human with glasses; however, she has no true form, possessing the ability to exist in multiple different forms at the same time and can summon other manifestations, including the Black Pharaoh and the Great Calamity. As an entity from a transcendent superdimension, Meikumi is not bound by any concepts from all other universes and dimensions, as well as dwarfing gods like Cthulhu and Hastur in terms of power.

Posing as an air-headed Japanese teacher in Rhymegasaki City, Meikumi's true goal is to release chaos and destruction from the Shining Trapezohedron. (: Makai Shoujo R'lyeh Lulu)

entities.name: Messenger of Azathoth
entities.description:
The Messenger of Azathoth is a fictional monster created by Gary Myers for his short story "Passing of a Dreamer", where it is encountered by the dreamer Snireth-Ko on the dark side of the Dreamlands' moon.

This creature has also been incorporated into the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, where it is portrayed as a "seed" destined to "fertilize" and destroy the Dreamlands' moon.

The Messenger of Azathoth is a "seed" drifting through the Dreamlands towards the moon. When it comes in contact with the satellite, it will melt through the ground and lodge itself in its core, where it will begin to grow, boiling the Lake of Ubboth and consuming Mnomquah in the process. While burrowing, it will radiate an intense green light that causes those who come near it to undergo a gradual deterioration until their bodies finally dissolve into living "pools of protoplasm". The Messenger can't be destroyed by physical means, only by magical artefacts. If allowed to reach maturity, it will eventually break free, destroying the Dreamlands' moon with cataclysmic consequences not only for the dream realm, but for the sanity of all the Waking World's population as well. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands)

In the works of H. P. Lovecraft, Nyarlathotep holds the role of Azathoth's messenger (: Fungi from Yuggoth) and is known to operate from the dark side of the Dreamlands' moon with his Moon-beast allies (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath). It's not known whether Myers intended the creature from "Passing of a Dreamer" to be Nyarlathotep, but the RPG classifies it as a distinct servitor race, apparently unconnected to the Crawling Chaos.

entities.name: Mh'ithrha
entities.description:
Mh'ithrha (The Arch-Lord of Tindalos) is an Outer God in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Bruce Ballon for the Call of Cthulhu gaming supplement Unseen Masters.

The master of the Hounds of Tindalos, Mh'ithrha is the mightiest member of that strange species. Although invisible to the human eye, its physical form is said to be that of a gargantuan wolf, somewhat resembling the beast Fenrir from Norse mythology.

Mh'ithrha has been engaged in a war with Yog-Sothoth for all of eternity; stories of this conflict are the stuff of legend in the Cthulhu Mythos, and the fact that it has not been annihilated by such a being gives a hint to the true extent of Mh'ithrha's power. (: Unseen Masters)

entities.name: Father Michael
entities.description:
Father Michael is a fictional character who appears in several of Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Files series of Cthulhu Mythos-related games and fiction. He is the pastor at Arkham's South Church, and works alongside investigator character Sister Mary.

Father Michael first appeared as a Blight card in the Arkham Horror Second Edition expansion set The King in Yellow, although he was mentioned on Sister Mary's Investigator card from the Core Set.

In the novella by Richard Lee Byers, Father Michael made a brief appearance when the protagonists, Professors Norman Withers and Claus Schmidt, visited South Church as part of their research.

entities.name: Million Favoured One
entities.description:
The Million Favoured Ones are a mysterious group first mentioned in "The Whisperer in Darkness" and expanded upon in the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game.

The Million Favoured Ones are not a true species, but in fact a catch-all term for any entity who has been granted a new, more powerful form by Nyarlathotep as a reward for their patronage.

The Million Favoured Ones include individuals such as the Lurker in the Star Pool and the Horsemen of Nyarlathotep.

entities.name: Joe Mills
entities.description:
Joe Mills is a character created by Troy Young for his Nyarlathotep Cycle series of Cthulhu Mythos stories.

Mills is a tall, broad-shouldered man somewhere in his early thirties. As a trained law enforcement professional, he generally has a calm demeanour and is able to function well in high-stress situations.

As a Corporal with the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Mills was sent to investigate a strange creature which had washed up on the shore of a small fishing community in Canada named Gallou Cove. Whilst there, he met marine biologist Dr. Adele Kramer, and the two of them attempted to perform an ad hoc autopsy on the beast. However, when they cracked open its shell, a bizarre side-effect of whatever the creature was composed of awakened a psychic ability in them, allowing them to sense when elements of "The Other" (a catch-all term for the forces of the Cthulhu Mythos) are nearby. Shortly afterwards, the creature's mother appeared, and the town was closed down by a mysterious government organisation which also recruited them into its ranks.

Ostensibly promoted to the rank of Inspector in the RCMP and transferred to the other side of the country, Mills was in fact seconded to the agency under the orders of a man named Harjit Singh, who proceeded to send him on a variety of assignments across the country. He has since encountered (and defeated) several elements of The Other including both a Cthulhu worshipper and his summoned abomination and, in partnership with an agent named Pete Ivalu, an entire cult devoted to the Outer God Nyarlathotep.
entities.short_description: Joe Mills is a character created by Troy Young for his Nyarlathotep Cycle series of Cthulhu Mythos stories.

entities.name: Minh Thi Phan
entities.description:
Minh Thi Phan is an Investigator character created by Fantasy Flight Games for inclusion in their Cthulhu Mythos-related games and fiction.

Minh Thi Phan has had two differing biographies released, one in the Innsmouth Horror Deluxe Expansion to Arkham Horror Second Edition, and the other in Eldritch Horror.

Minh's family fled their home in Korea to escape persecution from the Japanese; making their way to the United States, the family settled down to build themselves a future. Being hard workers, they were able to pay for Minh to attend community college where, despite experiencing her own share of racism and harassment, she completed her degree before heading out into the wider world to find a job.

Landing a position as secretary at a small firm in Arkham, Minh's main concern was that her new boss might act inappropriately towards her, but luckily Mr. Thompson wasn’t that kind of man, and Minh settled into her new job comfortably.

entities.name: Mlandoth
entities.description:
Mlandoth is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. The character was originally created by Walter C. DeBill, Jr. for his short story "Where Yidhra Walks".

Mlandoth is a primal entity or force, not dissimilar to the Nameless Mist or Darkness, although it is uncertain if it is a place, conscious being, or an inconceivable maelstrom of unknown forces and properties outside the perceptible cosmos. It is mentioned in Uralte Schrecken as a kind of prime archetype from which all mythical god-heads are derived. It is paired with the equally primordial Mril Thorion.

According to the cycle surrounding these beings, they are a sort of cosmic yin and yang, whose meeting resulted in the creation of all things (although Azathoth is usually attributed to this). Their joinings routinely create and destroy matter and entities. One of the beings created in this way was the inimical Outer God Ngyr-Khorath. (: "Where Yidhra Walks")

It is said that Mlandoth and Mril Thorion manifested from Yidh Nak as a result of the titanic explosion at the beginning of the universe. Mlandoth, together with Mril Thorion generated a "vortex" by being omnipresent throughout all time and space and continuously intersecting with one another; this vortex gave rise to all. (: "Prologue: Collector's item")

entities.name: Monstrosity
entities.description:
The Monstrosity is a fictional demon in the prime reality of the Marvel universe of Marvel Comics, created in 1993 by Chris Cooper, first appearing in issue #13 of the 1st volume of Darkhold: Pages from the Book of Sins.

The Monstrosity is a demon released by the Darkhold, which the press called "Monstrosity". It possessed superhuman strength, durability, and speed. Able to easily life a tall muscular man with both hands above its head and throw him. Its claws could easily tear human flesh and bone, and rip through a car's roof. The demon siphoned the lifeforce of humans via its mouth, killing them. Usually it left a shriveled corpse.

For every lifeforce that it consumed it gave the one who used the Darkhold page the lifeforce to heal another being. Victoria Montesi for a short period was able to heal her hospitalized lover because she used one of the pages of the Darkhold, not realizing that it released a demon which was killing and stealing their lifeforce for her use. Many were killed before she discovered the truth and rejected the Darkhold.

entities.name: Cy Morgan
entities.description:
Cy Morgan is a fictional character created by American comic book creator Michael Alan Nelson for his Boom! Studios Cthulhu Mythos series Fall of Cthulhu. He made his debut appearance in the first issue in 2007.

Cy is an average American man who as an adult studied at Arkham's Miskatonic University. He previously lived with and was engaged to a woman named Jordan, but their relationship ended with her supernaturally-motivated suicide.

Cy and his sister Sarah were raised by their uncle Walt after the death of their parents at a young age, and was fortunate enough to be accepted to study at Miskatonic University.

Later in life, Walt killed himself in front of Cy and his fiancé Jordan, leaving little but questions and a stack of occult artefacts in his wake. This prompted Cy to investigate what had happened to Walt, a journey which took him to the Dreamlands, led to a confrontation with the evil Mr. Arkham and, eventually, resulted in insanity and incarceration in a mental health facility. (: Fall of Cthulhu Volume 1: The Fugue)

entities.name: Galeas Morgan
entities.description:
Officer Galeas Morgan is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Fiction series of Cthulhu Mythos stories. He made his first appearance in the 2017 novella Hour of the Huntress by Dave Gross.

A junior officer in the Arkham Police Department, Morgan is a tall fellow but almost painfully thin, to the point where Jenny Barnes, on their first meeting, guessed that he skipped meals. Although prone to a certain social awkwardness, he has shown himself to be a brave and resourceful individual. (: Hour of the Huntress)

Morgan appears to be in a developing relationship with tomboy mechanic Lonnie Ritter, Lonnie seemingly possessing deep feelings for the officer, feelings which may not be entirely reciprocated. (: Hour of the Huntress)

Morgan assisted globetrotting dilettante Jenny Barnes in her quest to find her missing sister Izzie in the town of Arkham. Along with Lonnie Ritter and Miskatonic University anthropology professor Tilde Félix, Morgan fought a cult dedicated to the Outer God Shub-Niggurath, facing down and banishing the Dark Young which they had summoned during a sacrificial ritual. (: Hour of the Huntress)

entities.name: Tony Morgan
entities.description:
Tony Morgan, the Bounty Hunter, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Files and appears in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos.

One day, while hard on the trail of a particularly elusive bounty, Tony cornered his quarry out in the countryside, near a large river. However, this time his prey turned out not to be human.

A humanoid creature covered in scales and coated in slime, the monster stank of the ocean, rotted fish and the offal of the unfortunate farm animals which it had slaughtered and devoured. Upon realising that it had a pursuer, the thing immediately made for the river, throwing itself straight in. Having never let a target escape, Tony shrugged off his revulsion, drew his knife, and went to work.

Everything from then on had gone by in a blur; Tony had a vague recollection of the nightmarish beast trying to tear his arm off at the shoulder before everything went black, and he passed out.

entities.name: Jedidiah Mortonson
entities.description:
Jedidiah Mortonson is a character created by author C. J. Henderson as an antagonist in his Frank Nardi series of short stories.

Born over three hundred years ago, Jedidiah Mortonson was hung by the citizens of Arkham for child sacrifice and the practice of black magic, before they appropriated his house to, ironically, convert it into an orphanage. What the locals had failed to realise was that Mortonson had already lived far beyond his natural span through the use of his blood magic, and an extension of the spell allowed him to transfer his consciousness into the walls of his former home upon death.

Mortonson spent the next one hundred and fifty years inhabiting the bodies of those who dwelt within the house, draining their life's essence to fuel his own, until the closure of the orphanage. The departure of the inhabitants caused him to wither, and with no life force to drain, he began to die.

This state of existence continued until the property was purchased by Edward and Julie Douglas in the present day. Mortonson promptly began his psychic draining of the couple, but was eventually thwarted and killed by the intervention of Frank Nardi and the Arkham Detective Agency. Upon his death, the old house imploded, leaving nothing but a great hole in its place.

entities.name: Mother of Pus
entities.description:
The Mother of Pus is a fictional entity created by games designer Richard Watts for the Call of Cthulhu scenario "Behold the Mother", an adventure which was included in the 1998 supplement Dead Reckonings.

A Lesser Outer God composed of eyes, slime, tentacles and mouths, the Mother of Pus was spawned from the mating of Shub-Niggurath and a human. When summoned, she seeks refuge in pools of foul water. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

entities.name: Mother Shub
entities.description:
Mother Shub is a fictional character created by American author Ron Shiflet for his short story "Mother's Little Helper". Whether this was the character's name, an affectation, or her title, is unknown.

An ancient woman at the time of her death, Mother Shub lived in a ramshackle, single-room hut in the West Virginia forests known to the locals as Shub's Woods. There, she plied her trade as a local witch doctor, providing the nearby hillbilly families with basic medical care and potions with a variety of effects amongst other seevices in exchange for goods and services. She also operated a moonshine still near to her home, and kept a small number of scrawny black goats.

Although the locals feared Mother Shub and the powers she possessed, they appeared to be unaware that she was in fact a cultist devoted to the worship of Shub-Niggurath, from whom she was granted her gifts. When the time came for her to be with her god, she passed her power on to young Dora McCain, a local girl apprenticed to Mother Shub since the death of her ma.

Later, it is shown that rather than die, Mother Shub was instead transformed into a seductive inhuman entity which inhabits another dimension and accepts the gifts of male souls from her former apprentice in the name of her dark god (: "Mother's Little Helper").

entities.name: Mr. Arkham
entities.description:
Mr. Arkham is a character created by American comic book creator Michael Alan Nelson for the Boom! Studios Mythos series Fall of Cthulhu. He made his debut appearance in the very first issue in March 2007.

Manifesting as a well-spoken, distinguished gentleman in his late middle age, Mr. Arkham hides a dark secret: he is in fact an avatar of the Outer God Nyarlathotep. To maintain a cover while he enacts his schemes, he operates the Arkham Boarding House, an antiquated, and somewhat dilapidated, establishment which charges high prices for maintaining its residents' privacy.

Mr. Arkham is served by a human man named Connor, and a creature resembling a common housecat named Nemesis, who is in fact a former Atlantean sorcerer.

Mr. Arkham was responsible for unearthing the corpse of the mad Arab Abdul Alhazred, whom he subsequently reanimated as part of his scheme to initiate a cosmic war. He then befriended first Walt McKinley, and later his nephew Cy Morgan, in his schemes to retrieve a mystical dagger, before driving the latter insane with the revelation of who he really was (: Fall of Cthulhu Volume 1: The Fugue).

entities.name: Mril Thorion
entities.description:
Mril Thorion is an Outer God who, along with Mlandoth, serve as Yin and Yang. (: "Where Yidhra Walks")

Mril Thorion, together with Mlandoth generated a “vortex” by being omnipresent throughout all time and space and continuously intersecting with one another; this vortex gave rise to all. (: "Prologue: Collector's item")

Mlandoth and Mril Thorion were created by Walter C. DeBill Jr., but were suggested years earlier by Clark Ashton Smith.

entities.name: Tommy Muldoon
entities.description:
Tommy Muldoon, the Rookie Cop, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for inclusion in their Arkham Horror Files range of Cthulhu Mythos-related products.

Straight after passing out of Boston City's police academy, Tommy found himself immediately sent out on secondment to the Arkham Sheriff's department.

At first, Tommy didn’t mind this, but the realities of working in Arkham were soon brought home to him, with bizarre reports of monsters stalking the outskirts of the city and horribly mangled corpses turning up all over town making him realise that there was something deeply wrong with the place.

However, Tommy had sworn an oath to protect and serve and so, with his trusty rifle Becky at his side, he set about the dirty business of cleaning up Arkham, whatever the personal cost might be.

entities.name: Mupp
entities.description:
Mupp is a character created by Mark McLaughlin and Michael Sheehan, Jr. for their Egyptian Cthulhu Mythos stories.

Severely deformed from birth - as a result of interference from the Outer God Nyarlathotep at the time of conception - Mupp is described as "large, red-faced … with an oversized skull, a cleft lip, a slight chin, a stunted arm, and overly large, malformed hips. His crooked spine ended in a vestigial tail. His left foot resembled the flipper of a turtle, while his other foot and hands all featured the wrong numbers of fingers and toes." His most distinctive feature is that he is a cyclops, with a "huge single eye nestled above … flaring cheekbones. Even at birth, a thick arc of black brow curved over the eye, which regarded the world with seething wrath. The iris of this eye was composed of three reddish-gold lobes, centered around the irregular black circle of the pupil."

He is also a gifted magic user with the ability to cause blood to gush from the ears of others with but a whisper, see in total darkness, and project blasts of green fire from his hands.

Despite being born to the pharaoh Tutankhamen, Mupp's hideous appearance meant that he was exiled to the catacombs beneath the royal palace. There, he formed his own cult to Nyarlathotep before one day stumbling across the undying followers of Azathoth. He learned from these shrivelled mummies how to reanimate the dead, and commanded them to bring him more corpses with which to create his own army. However, before his plans could come to fruition, he was slain by the creature Setek after displaying a burst of childish petulance.

entities.name: Dylan Murphy
entities.description:
Dylan Murphy is the primary human antagonist in Keyport Cthulhu, the first book in Armand Rosamilia's Keyport Cthulhu story cycle.

A bald, heavyset man, Dylan has a mean temper. He is the head of the Keyport branch of the Esoteric Order of Dagon and the eldest son of his family, at least the ninth to take the name of Dylan Murphy. He owns the Broad Street Pub, the de facto headquarters of the Order.

Dylan may or may not be a human/Deep One hybrid; his appearance is suggestive of such ancestry, but his contempt for the deformities present in others of this kind suggests otherwise.

While growing up, Dylan saw the mistakes that his forbears had made in their attempts to awaken great Cthulhu, and new that he could do better.

entities.name: Rex Murphy
entities.description:
Rexford T. Murphy, also known as The Reporter, is a fictional character in the Arkham Horror series by Fantasy Flight Games.

An investigative reporter for the Arkham Advertiser, Rex had looked into many strange reports in his time, but had always managed to lose any evidence before these stories had gone to press. His photographs from Innsmouth had blown out to sea in a gust of wind, the bizarre tracks he found in Dunwich had washed away in a freak storm before anyone was able to verify them, and those were most certainly not the only incidents.

On Rex’s most recent excursion, this time to Lithuania, he had gone to see an old gypsy fortune teller, who had screamed him right out of her home, claiming that he was cursed. Soon afterwards, the diary that he had uncovered concerning cult activity in the area had mysteriously gone missing.

Returning to Arkham empty-handed, Rex quickly went to work trying to uncover what he believed was a global conspiracy.

entities.name: N'h'll
entities.description:
N'h'll is a fictional entity created by Peter A. Worthy for his short story "Sweet Despise".

N'h'll is a mysterious entity or force worshiped at least by one insane killer who escaped from Arkham Asylum. Information about N'h'll is apparently only to be found in the Song of Yste. While there is almost nothing known about N'h'll, it is probably the void for all, including the Great Old Ones, and even such as Mlandoth. (: "Sweet Despise")

entities.name: N'tse-Kaambl
entities.description:
N'tse-Kaambl is an Elder God from the expanded Cthulhu Mythos, who first appeared in Gary Myers' short story "The House of the Worm".

N'tse-Kaambl is a powerful Elder God, who is primarily worshipped in the Dreamlands and was responsible for the creation of the Elder Sign. She is known to combat the Great Old Ones and Outer Gods. Although her ultimate goal is to defeat the evil gods, she is indifferent towards humanity as a whole. Referred to as a goddess "whose splendor hath shattered worlds", N'tse-Kaambl usually takes the form of a beautiful woman wielding a spear and shield. Her spear is capable of firing blasts of powerful energy, while her shield is emblazoned with an Elder Sign and protects anything that is behind it. (: Malleus Monstrorum)

N'tse-Kaambl was most likely inspired by Athena, a goddess from Greek Mythology.

entities.name: Naggoob
entities.description:
Naggoob is the Father of Ghouls and the free lead servant of Nyogtha, according to the Unaussprechlichen Kulten. (: "The Horror in the Gallery")

As such, he might be related to Nug, Feaster Among the Tombs, who the Book of Eibon identifies as the grandfather of all ghouls who serve Nyogtha. (: "The Descent into the Abyss") However, in later references, Nug is depicted as Yeb's twin, and Naggoob is identified as the father of ghouls. (: Encyclopedia Cthulhiana, H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands)

Naggoob was created by Lin Carter for his 1976 story "The Horror in the Gallery", and classified as one of the Lesser Old Ones.

In Chaosium's role-playing game Call of Cthulhu, Naggoob is the leader of the ghouls who serve Nyogtha and continues to appear as the “Father of Ghouls.” However, in this setting, it is said that he earned this title because he frequently mated with witches, resulting in the birth of many half-human, half-ghoul children. (: H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands)

entities.name: Frank Nardi
entities.description:
Franklin "Frank" Nardi is a fictional character who appears in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. He was originally created by author C. J. Henderson for his short story "The Idea of Fear", but has since been expanded upon by others including Josh Reynolds and Robert M. Price.

Originally of Italian descent, Frank is outwardly a stereotypical hard-boiled New York detective, although he possesses a strong moral compass and is fiercely loyal to his friends. He is somewhere in his late middle age and, although still solidly built for a man of his years, has gained a certain amount of excess weight since leaving the force.

After serving with the New York Police Department - where he attained the rank of detective - Frank chose to take early retirement. Subsequently, he contacted three other former police officers and partnered with them in the Arkham Detective Agency, a private-investigations firm which they established in the supposedly-sleepy town of Arkham, Massachusetts.

Soon after setting up business the group realised that, far from being an ordinary place, Arkham was in fact home to many strange and inexplicable occurrences. In order to exploit this, the Agency branched out from regular detective work into paranormal investigations, a side business which has proven to be extremely lucrative, if at times hazardous.

entities.name: Narrathoth
entities.description:
Narrathoth is a fictional extradimensional entity created by Robert Silverberg for his short story "Demons of Cthulhu".

Narrathoth is an entirely white creature covered in scales. It is larger than a man, and has a bulging head with a single three-lobed eye. It speaks in a deep bubbling voice that sounds as if it was coming from the depths of the sea, and has a peculiar odor suggestive of extreme antiquity. It describes itself as "one of the lurkers at the threshold of the universe", and as one of the followers of Cthulhu, who waits for the time its master will return and reconquer the worlds he once ruled.

In the Necronomicon of Abdul Alhazred, Narrathoth is identified as a servant of the "Old Ones", although he shares the power of his dormant masters. Like them, Narrathoth lies asleep beyond the Great Gate. However, he can be summoned to our realm by a simple ritual, which can be easily performed even by the most amateur occultist. Only "six or seven" ingredients are needed, including a woman's undergarments and the blood of a male cat. A chalk pentagram must be drawn to keep the entity contained. The summoning chant also mentions Cthulhu and Shub-Niggurath.

Once summoned, Narrathoth can be forced to serve its summoner by the uttering of the phrase "I have called you by your True Name, Old One, and I command you to do my bidding". Its powers enable it to conjure up anything its summoner asks for, creating objects out of the fabric of spacetime itself, and although it serves grudgingly, it is forced by the spell of obedience not to harm its summoner in any way with the conjurations. In spite of all this, Alhazred still warns his readers that Narrathoth is wrathful and dangerous, and that "pity be upon him who summons him and loses control". (: "Demons of Cthulhu") Category:Other Supernatural Beings Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Extra-Dimensional Characters

entities.name: Nemesis
entities.description:
Nemesis, whose name as a mortal was Hadron, is a character created by Michael Alan Nelson for his Fall of Cthulhu series of Mythos comic books. Nemesis made his first appearance in the very first issue of Fall of Cthulhu, titled "Harlot", although he played little part in the events of the main story arc, his character being fleshed out somewhat in the prequel spin-off Fall of Cthulhu Volume 6: Nemesis.

Hadron was the D'harin, or high priest of Vesh, in Atlantis in the days leading up to the sinking of that once-proud civilisation. He was blindsided by the Oracle Sysyphyx, who was herself in league with the Outer God Nyarlathotep, and tricked into overthrowing his brother, the King, through a series of complex schemes.

Ultimately, the Oracle's prophecy bore fruit: Hadron was the last of his people, bore witness to the destruction of his civilisation, and later became immortal like a god when Nyarlathotep transformed him into an undying housecat for his own amusement (: Fall of Cthulhu Volume 6: Nemesis).

In the modern day Hadron, now going by the name of Nemesis, assisted Nyarlathotep's avatar Mr. Arkham by stealing the Gray Man's knife from the Arkham Police Department lockup. In the aftermath of the war between Nyarlathotep and Nodens he declared himself the victor, as he was the only "god" left undefeated. However, he played no part in the actual war and, being in effect a housecat, had nothing to gain from this declaration, nor any way to force his will upon the world.

entities.name: Nezaral
entities.description:
Nezaral is a fictional character from Marvel Comics created in 1995 by Ian Edginton. It first appeared in issue #8 of the 1st volume of Blade: The Vampire-Hunter comic book series.

Nezaral is a demon who is an agent of the Elder God Chthon. It is a giant demon able to swallow a human whole. The demon is immortal, possesses an endless hunger for souls, has superhuman strength, and is able to empower others with demonic abilities.

entities.name: Mindy Nguyen
entities.description:
Mindy Nguyen is a character created by Canadian author Troy Young for his Nyarlathotep Cycle series of Cthulhu Mythos stories.

A tall, good-looking Asian woman with long black hair which she usually wears tied back, Mindy is trained in the combat techniques of Krav Maga.

Formerly an investigative reporter, Harjit Singh recruited Mindy into the Department of Extraordinary Phenomena around 2018 after her fiancé was tortured and killed by 'winged shrimp with legs' (most likely Mi-Go) whilst on a hiking trip.

A little over a year later, one of her assignments caused her to cross paths with an alien life form and its collection of exotic flora. This encounter left her with a heightened ability to sense the presence of otherworldly entities and influence.

entities.name: Ngyr-Khorath
entities.description:
Ngyr-Khorath (also known as The Ultimate Abomination, The Dream-Death, and The Mad God of the Void, among other titles) is an entity featured in the Mlandoth Cycle by Walter C. DeBill Jr. It has existed in the area now home to the Solar System since before the Sun and planets formed. It appears as a red or deep blue-green mist which causes a sense of terror as it approaches. Once close, an eye of flame forms within. When life arrived on Earth, it became enraged. A cult to Ngyr-Khorath exists. Its legend (part of the so-called Mlandoth Cycle) appears in the Book of Thoth, The Chronicles of Thrang, the Uralte Schrecken, and The Texts of Mloeng. Von Könnenberg suggests that it is a form of the entity Mlandoth, and itself has an avatar, 'Ymnar.

It spawned by fission the Great Old One (or its avatar) 'Ymnar, and its nemesis is the Elder God Paighon.

entities.name: Niggurab
entities.description:
Niggurab, or Nigguraab, is an entity created by Polish comic book creator Len Kaminski for his stint on long-running superhero series Avengers. It was first mentioned in issue #353 in September 1992 .

Niggurab was one of the deities invoked by the supervillain Grim Reaper, who required power to create his Legion of the Undead, an army of zombie-villains with the sole purpose of destroying the Avengers (: Avengers #353) .

It has been speculated that Niggurab is merely another name for the Outer God Shub-Niggurath, rather than its own unique entity .

entities.name: Samuel Nightingale
entities.description:
Samuel Nightingale is a fictional character who appeared in Peter J. Evans' 2013 novel Feeders from Within. It was his first and only appearance, having died during the story’s finale.

A slight and wiry man, Nightingale nevertheless had a coldness in his eyes which caused all who met him to be instantly wary; psychiatrist Dr. Carolyn Fern instantly recognised him as a sociopath with no regard to the fate of others. He worked for businessman/bootlegger Phillip Avery as his second-in-command and enforcer (and had been nominated to succeed Avery) until the two died in November 1926. He was also a member of the Silver Twilight Lodge, although doesn’t appear to have been particularly advanced in the hierarchy. (: Feeders from Within)

Nightingale was responsible for dispatching the assassins who attempted to kill Carolyn Fern, and he himself tried to kill Mark Harrigan, but was interrupted by the arrival of Diana Stanley. When the group of Silver Twilight Lodge members travelled through Mr. Stone's portal to N'kai, he was one of the few lucky or cunning enough to make it back after the Formless Spawn attacked. In a fight shortly afterwards, Nightingale was killed by Diana who stabbed him through the neck. (: Feeders from Within)

entities.description:
Northot is a mysterious entity related to Yog-Sothoth, Shub-Niggurath, and possibly even to Azathoth. It manifests as a faun-like humanoid with color-changing hair or as a glowing halo of unknown color. The faun-like traits may be a hint of its lineage due to both it and Shub-Niggurath's ungulate-like features of the goat and deer respectively.

entities.description:
Nuja of Lomar is a ficitonal character created by American author Jason Scott Aiken and included in several of his sword-and-sorcery short stories. She appears to have been at least partially inspired by the Robert E. Howard character Red Sonja.

Nuja is a statuesque and beautiful warrior-woman hailing from the ancient land of Lomar. She wears her red hair long, carries a steel greatsword, and dresses in silver armour. She also appears to be a protector of sorts for her homeland, and may be somehow affiliated with the Great Old One Tsathoggua.

entities.name: Nya
entities.description:
Nya is a fictional entity in the Demonbane Mythos. The character was originally created by Jin Haganeya, appearing as the overarching antagonist for the visual novel Deus Machina Demonbane.

Nya is an avatar of Nyarlathotep, who takes the form of a tall, black-haired woman wearing glasses and a purple dress suit. Depending on the circumstances, she can assume many different forms, such as the Black Pharaoh or Father Nye; however, her true form is a burning smile with the three-lobed eye. She owns a bookstore that contains many grimoires including the Key of Solomon, the Lemegeton, the Grand Grimoire, the Black Pullet, the Book of Dzyan, and the Book of Loagaeth.

Nya's characterization is shown to be cunning and manipulative, as she enjoys toying with everyone. But most of all, she is an Evil God who claims that true evil is no different than love, resulting in her loving humanity but in the most twisted way possible.

She was responsible for creating a time-looped world called the Infinite Spiral, also known as the Klein Bottle, forcing Daijuuji Kurou and Master Therion to relive their battle countless times. Her ultimate goal was to break the Shining Trapezohedron and free the Court of Azathoth, allowing the Outer Gods to consume all of reality and sink everything into primordial chaos. (: Deus Machina Demonbane)

entities.name: Nyar
entities.description:
Nyar (also known as Nyarlathotep) is a fictional entity created by Juan Gotō for his manga series Alicia Y.

Nyar is an avatar of Nyarlathotep, who resembles a dark-skinned man wearing clergy attire. When accompanied by Alicia Y Armitage, he often transforms into a black cat, and can also take the form of the three-lobed burning eye. Nyar has been shown to have several supernatural abilities, including flight and teleportation; however, his powers are limited due to him merely being a projection of a god in this world. In addition to spending time on Earth, he appears to have a secret lair, located in the Cydonia region of the planet Mars.

Thousands of years ago, Nyar was the god worshipped in Egypt, who granted a dying wish to the Great Pharaoh Nephren-Ka, teaching him magic and bestowing him with the power of clairvoyance. Nephren-Ka spent his last days painting future events on the walls of his catacomb, which was concealed in fabric by the priests out of fear, only taking a look into the future little by little. According to Nyar, Nephren-Ka is destined to be resurrected in the future but will suffer in a world where there are no humans left to rule.

In the present day, Nyar took the role of Alicia's guardian after the death of Mr. Whateley, changing her surname to "Armitage" instead of Whateley. At the behest of John Dee, Alicia was trapped underneath a giant star-shaped stone by a descendent of the priests who guarded the catacomb of Nephren-Ka, a woman claiming to be a servant of Nyarlathotep. Soon afterwards, Nyar got into a confrontation with the woman, ultimately killing the self-proclaimed servant by crushing her head. Nyar eventually figured out that he needed the Silver Key to save Alicia, with Randolph Carter arriving for assistance; despite being on bad terms with Nyar, Carter agreed to help due to the dire circumstances.

entities.name: Nyarlathotep's aliases
entities.description:
Nyarlathotep used many aliases, some being dedicated to specific avatars. It should be noted that although he is referred to as the God of a Thousand Forms, this is likely only a metaphor: as he is known to visit planets across the cosmos and other dimensions, it is likely that he employs far more forms than a mere thousand.

This list also includes humans who have been impersonated or possessed by Nyarlathotep.

entities.name: Nyarlathotep's Half-Brother
entities.description:
Nyarlathotep's Half-Brother is a fictional cosmic being created by Walter C. DeBill, Jr. for his short story "In 'Ygiroth".

Little is known about this entity, which is described as Nyarlathotep's "half-brother and other face", possibly indicating that it might be an aspect of Nyarlathotep himself, as opposed to a literal relative.

It is also described as "a ravenous and by no means sane entity", and has the power to spread fear "like a poisonous vapor", causing all in its proximity to panic in sheer uncontrollable terror. (: "In 'Ygiroth")

Since Nyarlathotep's only known parent is Azathoth (: Selected Letters of H. P. Lovecraft), which reproduces asexually by fission (: "The Family Tree of the Gods"), the idea that he could have a "half-brother" seems unusual, although it opens up the possibility that Azathoth might be able to reproduce sexually as well, and that either Nyarlathotep or his Half-Brother (or both) were born from such a union. entities.name: Nyaruko
entities.description:
Nyaruko (also known as Nyarlathotep) is an extraterrestrial entity from the fictional universe of the Haiyore! Nyaruko-san series.

Nyaruko is a member of the Space Defense Agency, an alien organization dedicated to stopping intergalactic crimes. Nyaruko was sent to Earth to protect Mahiro Yasaka, a human boy that she fell in love with. Mahiro constantly rejects Nyaruko's advances towards him, usually with violence (i.e. stabbing her with forks) due to her persistence. Despite this, he does genuinely love her back but is often turned off by her behavior. Nyaruko would later be joined by her childhood friends Kuuko and Hasuta, the former of which is madly in love with her despite Nyaruko expressing zero interest in return and the latter is in love with Mahiro, making both of them an inconvenience for Nyaruko's relationship.

Nyaruko is capable of shapeshifting and takes the form of a silver-haired petite human girl, as her true form would cause people to lose their sanity. Her species was the inspiration for the character "Nyarlathotep" from H. P. Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos. In combat, she uses a plethora of weapons including a crowbar, grenades, swords and chainsaws.

It is later revealed that, as an incarnation of the character, Nyaruko is protected by the Story of Nyarlathotep, preventing anyone from truly defeating her. The final volume of the light novel series features a parody of Demonbane's Athleta Aeternum, where the Story of Nyarlathotep summons an army of infinite Nyarlathoteps from popular culture to save Nyaruko.

entities.name: Nyctelios
entities.description:
Nyctelios is a fictional entity created by Patrick Bosquet for the Call of Cthulhu scenario "Le Regard Dans L'Abime", featured in issue #87 of the French role-playing magazine Casus Belli.

Nyctelios was originally one of the Elder Gods, but was punished by Nodens for transgressions against his brethren, ultimately becoming an Outer God who was imprisoned under the Mediterranean Sea. He takes the form of a grotesque, muscular cyclops-like humanoid, whose body is infested with hideous worms. One day, he will rise from the abyssal citadel he was ensnared in and seek revenge upon the Elder Gods.
