entities.name: Danny O'Bannion
entities.description:
Danny O'Bannion is a fictional character created by Keith Herber for the first edition of Arkham Unveiled, published by Chaosium in 1990 for the Call of Cthulhu role-playing game, where he is presented as the owner of Lucky Clover Cartage Company, a front for O'Bannion's bootlegging operations. O'Bannion's name is Herber's homage to the American screenwriter and director Dan O'Bannon (who co-wrote the screenplay of Dark Star (1974) and wrote the screenplay of Alien (1979) among other films), according to correspondence between Herber and fellow Call of Cthulhu writer Richard Watts during the development of Arkham Unveiled. Most recently, O'Bannion reappears in Chaosium's Arkham (2023), the first of several releases planned for the 'Arkham Unveiled' line (formerly known as 'Lovecraft Country') for the 7th edition of the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game.

O'Bannion has also appeared in publications from Fantasy Flight Games (establised 1995) for their Arkham Horror Files series of Cthulhu Mythos-related releases. Although primarily appearing in the now-discontinued Call of Cthulhu Living Card Game, he has also been referenced in other media, such as Peter J. Evans' franchise tie-in novel Feeders from Within.

Danny O'Bannion is a major player in the shady underworld of 1928 Arkham, heading the organised crime coalition dubbed The Syndicate, a powerful group with an interest in every illegal activity in town. Conducting much of his business from the Clover Club, a shady den of iniquity, his group is at constant war with the Sheldon gang, bootleggers plying their trade in opposition to the Syndicate.

O'Bannion has a daughter, a beautiful young woman named Naomi, who also works for the Syndicate.

entities.name: Naomi O'Bannion
entities.description:
Naomi O'Bannion is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Files line of Cthulhu Mythos-related releases. She has appeared in both Call of Cthulhu: The Card Game and Arkham Horror: The Card Game.

A beautiful young woman, Naomi works for her father Danny's criminal organisation The Syndicate in the Arkham of 1928, seeming to spending much of her time in the Clover Club, a shady speakeasy. Although generally seen as an antagonistic character, she has been known to assist others in their battles against the forces of the Cthulhu Mythos.

entities.name: "Skids" O'Toole
entities.description:
"Skids" O'Toole, the Ex-Convict, is a fictional character conceived by Fantasy Flight Games as part of their Arkham Horror Files range of Cthulhu Mythos-relates games and fiction.

Whilst Skids had never really wanted to be a criminal, needs must when the devil calls, and he was in desperate need of cash. Never really seeing himself as a bad person, Skids did what it took to come up with the money; protection rackets, robbery, even bank jobs were not out of the question, but he prided himself on the fact that he’d never actually killed anybody.

When the law finally caught up with Skids and he explained that he needed the dough to finance treatment for his sick mother, the cops simply laughed in his face and booked him anyway. Clearly, that excuse had been used one too many times.

After his Ma died from her illness when Skids was only two years into his time, he didn’t get any other visitors. To keep himself from going stir crazy, he decided to make real friends with his cell mate, a strange fellow named Brad Hollins. Brad constantly muttered and rambled about how the “Old Ones” were coming and told stories of the things he had learned of in his dreams, but Skids stuck with him anyway and the two became real friends.

entities.name: Olkoth
entities.description:
Olkoth, also known as The God of the Celestial Arcs, is a fictional entity created by user Danto for the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game website Tentacules.net, which first appeared in the scenario "The Voice of Christ". The character was later given an in-print publication, being featured as the antagonist of Bryn Fortey's 2021 short story "Beneath the Pimple", published in Vol 5, Issue 4 of the Lovecraftiana zine.

Olkoth is an Outer God who appears as a demoniacal deity with the ability to manifest in the form of a human if certain conditions are met, such as in proximity to an eyeless, grotesque statue of the Virgin Mary. It is described as a cautious being, one which always waits to see which way the wind is blowing before taking sides in any conflict.

Olkoth has always played on the sidelines, aligning itself with whatever being it deems to be the potential victor. However, the Outer God Yog-Sothoth, losing patience with Olkoth's machinations, set in motion a plan to trick it into taking the wrong side and thus allowing Yog-Sothoth to wreak its vengeance upon it. This plan, enacted with the aid of D'endrrah and involving Mh'ithrha, resulted in Olkoth being imprisoned beneath Twymbarlwm, a culturally significant hill in Wales. (: "Beneath the Pimple")

entities.name: Akachi Onyele
entities.description:
Akachi Onyele, the Shaman, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Files range of Mythos-related content.

Trained by one of the elders of her small Nigerian village from a young age to be the tribe's next shaman, Akachi learned English along with the ways of the outside world from a Christian missionary. Whilst she ignored his attempts to convert her - she already knew far too much about the world which is hidden from the eyes of most mortals - she took all of his other teachings in her stride.

Finally, upon reaching adulthood, the elder called her to him, telling the young woman "Akachi, I have seen that a great trial is coming for you. You must go to the United States, to a city called Arkham. There, you will have to face one of the old creatures, using the things that I have taught you." Thus Akachi made her way to America, finally landing on the shores of New England, and preparing for her greatest test.

The backstory given in Eldritch Horror varies from that given in Arkham Horror. Rather than being sent to Arkham, Akachi travelled Africa teaching others the ways of the shaman, before beginning her quest in Cape Town.

entities.name: Johnathan Orton
entities.description:
Johnathan Orton, who later went by the name Phillip Avery, is a character who appears in Peter J. Evans' 2013 Arkham Horror Fiction novel Feeders from Within.

A sergeant in the United States Army, Orton was part of the abortive 1916-17 Pancho Villa Expedition to the Sierra Madres. Whilst separated from the main force, Orton's squad discovered a cave in which a group of Mi-Go were working on a bizarre machine. During the ensuing battle between the soldiers and aliens, he was badly wounded and presumed dead by the survivors.

In the aftermath, the Mi-Go who would come to be known as Mr. Stone rebuilt Orton using parts from both the alien and human dead, and while Orton could now pass as human by concealing his body beneath heavy clothing, his face was hideously disfigured. Orton and Mr. Stone then travelled to Arkham, Massachusetts, where he took the name Phillip Avery.

Establishing a successful import business specialising in esoteric artefacts with the ulterior motive of gathering equipment and supplies for Mr. Stone, Avery became a highly-influential figure in Arkham, and soon joined the Silver Twilight Lodge, a cult dedicated to the service of dark gods.

entities.name: Othuyeg
entities.description:
Othuyeg is an entity that appears as a great tentacled eye similar to Cyäegha, but much more similar to the monster featured in the horror movie The Crawling Eye. He currently dwells within the subsoil of Kansas, in the fabled Seven Cities of Gold.

Othuyeg has as its servitor species miniature versions of itself known simply as the Spawn of Othuyeg. Since there is also a Mate of Othuyeg the Spawn may literally be its children.

An Elder God, Oztalun is symbolised by a seven-pointed star, which is its personal seal.

entities.name: Pantha
entities.description:
Pantha is a hero in the fictional Dynamite universe, who was created in 1974 by Carl Wessler. She was a character for Harris Publications before Dynamite Entertainment. Pantha was originally an alien shapeshifter from the planet Drakulon, the same world as Vampirella, who was later retconned into an ancient cursed Egyptian shapeshifter.

Sekhmet was a high priestess of Ra in ancient Egypt whom was given the ability to turn into a panther and was worshiped as a minor deity. When Egypt was inflicted with famine and drought, bloodlust took over and she killed and devoured many, including her own son. For her crimes, she was condemned by Ra to walk the Earth for eternity. In the modern era, she has been a friend and ally of Vampirella.

One version fought alongside Vampirella, Red Sonja, Eva, Dracula, Athena, Herbert West, and Ash Williams against the sorcerer Kulan Gath and the Army of Darkness. Pantha is able to turn into a panther or half-panther. In her possession is the scarab of Atum-Ra, an object that only women can touch. Which protects her and is able to open doorways to other worlds.

Category:Other Supernatural Beings Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Humans Category:Extraterrestrial Characters

entities.name: Pandora Peaslee
entities.description:
Pandora Peaslee is a fictional character created by American author Peter Rawlik for his Cthulhu Mythos fiction.

Pandora is an unspecified descendant of the Peaslee line, which includes Nathaniel Wingate Peaslee and Wingate Peaslee, characters who made their first appearance in H. P. Lovecraft's novella The Shadow Out of Time.

A former Central Intelligence Agency operative, Pandora later came to work as a government liaison to Mister Ys, a member of the Great Race of Yith, thousands of whom were living quietly among us in the build up to a calamitous event. In the aftermath, Pandora found purpose in becoming a resistance fighter against the Yithians who had harnessed a biological weapon and used it to subjugate the human race.

Pandora was present at the fall of the human race, when an experimental biological weapon was unleashed on the populace, causing an outbreak of zombie plague. Fortunately for some, a recent influx of Yithians, come to witness the end of the world, had made preparations for a select group of humans with particular skill sets to have a chance at survival, Pandora amongst them (: "Time Flies").

entities.name: Harrison Peel
entities.description:
Major Harrison Peel is a fictional Australian Army Intelligence officer created by David Conyers for a series of Cthulhu Mythos stories centring on the character. Peel has since been expanded on, primarily by Conyers, but on some occasions by and with other authors, including Brian M. Sammons, C. J. Henderson, John Goodrich, David Kernot, and John Sunseri.

Peel is a former Australian Army Intelligence officer in the employ of America's National Security Agency as an independent contractor. As well as more mundane human opponents, his missions regularly bring him into conflict with the forces of the Cthulhu Mythos, including such entities as Shoggoths and the Dark Young of Shub-Niggurath.

Note: unless otherwise stated, all stories are by David Conyers

entities.name: "Ashcan" Pete
entities.description:
"Ashcan" Pete Washburne, the Drifter, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Files line of Cthulhu Mythos content. He made his first appearance in the Core Set of Arkham Horror Second Edition.

Pete is a drifter, travelling the country with his trusty dog Duke and his guitar. He has roamed the length and breadth of the United States, but his nightmares have finally led him to the New England town of Arkham, where he hopes to put an end to the bad dreams.

Since his debut in Arkham Horror Second Edition, Pete has appeared in a number of Arkham Horror Files works, including the Arkham Horror: The Card Game expansion The Dunwich Legacy, the Eldritch Horror expansion Cities in Ruin, and the Mansions of Madness expansion Recurring Nightmares. He also made a cameo appearance in Graham McNeill's 2011 novel Ghouls of the Miskatonic, and in 2010 a pre-painted plastic miniature of the character was released as part of the Arkham Horror Premium Figures line.

entities.name: Ward Phillips
entities.description:
Ward Phillips is the name of several characters in the Cthulhu Mythos, all derived from the name of Howard Phillips Lovecraft.

There is a Ward Phillips in "Through the Gates of the Silver Key" (1934), described as "an elderly eccentric of Providence, Rhode Island." This "Providence mystic," who "enjoyed a long and close correspondence" with Randolph Carter, is said to be "lean, grey, long-nosed, clean-shaven, and stoop-shouldered.

The Rev. Ward Phillips is "Pastor of the Second Church in Arkham in the Massachusetts-Bay" in August Derleth's The Lurker at the Threshold (1945). He is the author of Thaumaturgical Prodigies in the New-English Canaan, published in Boston in 1801, and he has a vitriolic debate over the book with Alijah Billington in 1808.

Joan Stanley, in Ex Libris Miskatonici, says the Miskatonic University library was created in 1693 when another Ward Phillips--great-grandfather of the reverend--donated his library of 127 mainly religious books to the fledgling college.

entities.name: Stanley Pickman
entities.description:
Stanley Pickman is a fictional character created by Ian Davey for his short Cthulhu Mythos story "Black Letter Day". At the culminations of the events of "The Epiphany of Dissolution", he is revealed to be an avatar of Nyarlathotep.

At first appearing as an older man who claims a professorship in an unknown subject, after the fall of mankind and return of the Old Ones, Stanley Pickman looked considerably younger, as if the global catastrophe has somehow rejuvenated him. Later, in a confrontation with Glyph and Lucy, Pickman was obliterated when Nyarlathotep fully manifested and called forth his fellow Outer God Yog-Sothoth.

entities.name: Psuchawrl
entities.description:
Psuchawrl is a fictional character created by Charles R. Tanner for his 1941 Cthulhu Mythos short story "Out of the Jar".

One of the alien Jinn who came to the Earth in prehistory, Psuchawrl cannot be killed by humans, but was instead imprisoned in a jar by King Solomon, and can only be freed by breaking the jar's seal. Their physical appearance is that of a 9 ft tall humanoid with an eyeless sea anemone-like face, a beaked grinning mouth, and a pronounced ridge running from the forehead to the nape of the neck. (: "Out of the Jar")

entities.name: Ptar-Axtlan
entities.description:
Ptar-Axtlan (also spelled Ptar-Aztlan) is a fictional entity created by Gerald W. Page for his Cthulhu Mythos short story "Confession in Darkness".

Known as the Leopard That Stalks the Night, Ptar-Axtlan is a mysterious entity associated with cats. Like Cthulhu and other similar beings, Ptar-Axtlan can grant gifts of immortality and eternal youth to its followers. However, while Cthulhu's followers assume the traits of fish, Ptar-Axtlan's have a more feline appearance. Even a sadistic practitioner of the dark arts shuddered to think about what an entity like Ptar-Axtlan might ask in return for its gifts of unaging beauty. (: "Confession in Darkness")

entities.name: Queen of Clubs
entities.description:
The Queen of Clubs is a character in the fictional Grimm Fairy Tales pastiche universe, who first appeared in 2013 in issue #13 of the 1st volume of Wonderland. The character was created by Patrick Shand & Raven Gregory. Despite the name of her home universe, the character is inspired by characters from the Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and Through the Looking-Glass, and What Alice Found There books by Lewis Carroll, and not the fairy tales compiled by the Brothers Grimm.

The origins of the Queen of Clubs is unknown. The Queen of Clubs and the Queen of Diamonds are lovers, and enemies of the Queen of Spades. After their most recent battle with her, they finally became free of Wonderland, retreating to Los Angeles, California.

entities.name: Queen of Diamonds
entities.description:
The Queen of Diamonds is a character in the fictional Grimm Fairy Tales universe, who first appeared in 2013 in issue #13 of the 1st volume of Wonderland. The character was created by Patrick Shand & Raven Gregory

Adina was a church girl who was sacrificed to Wonderland. Surviving her arrival in the Realm of Nightmares, she was later accidentally murdered by the Mad Hatter. Adina was later revived by Keres, the Goddess of Death who made her the Queen of Diamonds.

The Queen of Clubs and the Queen of Diamonds are lovers, and enemies of the Queen of Spades. After their most recent battle with her, they finally became free of Wonderland, retreating to Los Angeles, California.

entities.name: Queen of Spades
entities.description:
The Queen of Spades is a character in the fictional Grimm Fairy Tales universe, who first appeared in 2010 in Tales from Wonderland: The White Knight. The character was created by Raven Gregory, Troy Brownfield, Ralph Tedesco, and Joe Brusha.

Alone in the Realm of Dreams, the Jabberwocky desired companionship. He took down a sky whale, and ate the sacred, ancient entity. Its death shook the foundations of the realm, resulting in the birth of a new entity, the Queen of Spades which emerged from the Jabberwocky's shadow. An entity who controlled the shadows and desires to conquer all of Wonderland, the Queen of Spades has displayed both good and evil tendencies.

entities.name: Quumyagga
entities.description:
Quumyagga is a fictional monster created by Lin Carter for his Cthulhu Mythos fiction. The first and oldest member of the Shantak species, it is the leader of all the Shantaks who serve Groth-Golka. As such, Quumyagga is considered the prototype of the race and one of the Lesser Old Ones. (: "The Descent into the Abyss", "The Fishers from Outside", "The Horror in the Gallery")

Quumyagga is a giant bird-like creature covered in both feathers and scales, with a single eye and a single leg, as well as a hooked beak. (: "The Descent into the Abyss")

According to the Book of Eibon, Quumyagga dwells either in the high peaks of the Plateau of Leng or in the chasm beneath Mount Antarktos. (: "The Fishers from Outside")

The original versions of the stories that mention Quumyagga claim that it is a servant of Gol-goroth, but this was later changed to Groth-Golka. Carter always intended it to be Groth-Golka, but confused the name of the two deities due to the fact that both were featured in "The Gods of Bal-Sagoth", by Robert E. Howard. entities.name: Illyana Rasputina
entities.description:
Illyana Rasputina (aka, Magik) is a superhero in the fictional Marvel universe, who was created in 1975, a B-list hero with a few comic book series.

Illyana Rasputina is a mutant who also possesses magical abilities. She is the younger sister of Colossus of the X-Men. In her pre-teen years she was kidnapped by the sorcerer Belasco and turned into a demonic sorceress, who overthrew him and took control of his demonic pocket dimension, Limbo.

Ever since she has been its on and off ruler, periodically losing control to Belasco or one of the stronger demons of Limbo, and regaining her throne afterwards. Within the dimension of Limbo she is the Sorceress Supreme. Magik is also a long standing member of the X-Men, having started out as a member of the teenage New Mutants during the 1980s.

entities.name: Rat God
entities.description:
The Rat God is a fictional monster created by Richard Corben for his comic book series of the same name, where it serves as the mysterious deity venerated by the people of Lame Dog, Massachusetts.

Native to the woods in the vicinity of Arkham, the Rat God resembles a bear-sized rodent with a bare rat skull for a head. Its origins are unknown, but it has been alive since prehistory. This carnivorous beast devours humans and demands sacrifices of its cultists, which seem to be somehow linked to it. Many citizens of Lame Dog in the early 20th century displayed rat-like facial features themselves. The Rat God is also served by a swarm of oversized rats. Additionally, it might be associated with a type of fungus that revives the dead bodies of its followers, allowing them to live again for several generations.

The Rat God can dig under the ground at prodigious speed. It is strong enough to charge at an accelerating car and topple the vehicle, suffering no apparent damage from the collision. entities.name: Madame Renee
entities.description:
Brenda Goff, better known as Madame Renee, is a character who appears in several of the Arkham Detective Agency stories by C. J. Henderson and others.

After a career as a dancer in her younger years, Brenda Goff came to the realisation that the natural shelf-life of a professional dancer would not provide her with a steady income for the rest of her days. Deciding to make use of her natural psychic talents, she changed her name to Madame Renee and cultivated her naturally-Middle Eastern looks along with a faux accent to become a professional medium.

Since then she has developed a working relationship as a consultant with the Arkham Detective Agency, and Frank Nardi in particular, who she seems to have something of a soft spot for.

At some point in her life, Madame Renee gave birth to an unnamed daughter who is now of college age. She is stated to be worried about being able to afford her daughters university fees.
entities.short_description: Brenda Goff, better known as Madame Renee, is a character who appears in several of the Arkham Detective Agency stories by C. J. Henderson and others.

entities.name: Luke Robinson
entities.description:
Always a great dreamer, years ago Luke discovered the allure of the Dreamlands. He had climbed down the Seventy Steps of Light Slumber, faced the judgment of Nasht and Kaman-Thah, and walked through the Doors of Sleep; from then on he spent every night delving into its secrets. He wandered the sleeping world exploring all that he could, and discussed the reality of the place with its denizens before stumbling across the greatest truth of all: the Dreamlands were a real place, and one could travel there, if one knew how.

Gathering up his meagre possessions and setting his affairs in order, Luke made his way to the portal he had been told of and passed through, thinking that he would never again see the waking world.

However, word came to Luke that something catastrophic was happening in Arkham, that an evil from before time was rearing its ugly head once again. So, collecting his things for a second time, Luke prepared to leave the Dreamlands, to return to the waking world and prepare to defend his old home.

In Graham McNeill's 2012 novel, while living in the city of Oriab, Luke encountered Henry Cartwright, an amnesic dreamer whose body was dying in the waking world. He travelled back and located Cartwright's companions, who made their way to the Dreamlands - with help from the Terrible Old Man - and saved the poor man.(: Bones of the Yopasi)

entities.name: Roiling Gas-Cloud
entities.description:
The Roiling Gas-Cloud is a fictional entity created by American author and games designer Kevin A. Ross for the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. It first appeared in "Thunder in the Blood", a scenario included in the supplement End of the World (Triad Entertainments, 1994).

The Roiling Gas-Cloud is one of five Lesser Other Gods from the Court of Azathoth that appeared during a summoning of Azathoth near San Lucas. It appears as a humonguous greenish-grey roiling cloud of gas that voraciously devours all that it can find with an assortment of tentacles, entrails and partially formed limbs. (: End of the World)

Category:Outer Gods Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works

entities.name: Zoey Samaras
entities.description:
Zoey Samaras, the Chef, is a fictional character who appears in several of Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Files products based on the expanded Cthulhu Mythos.

God had spoken to Zoey ever since she was just a child- six years old to be precise, on the same night that He had also taken her parents away in a calamitous fire. He told her that she was to be His earthly warrior, protecting the innocent whilst making the evil answer for their crimes.

Ever since that day, God had continued to speak to Zoey, especially when times were hard; His presence gave her both comfort and the strength she needed to do the things He asked of her. On more than one occasion, He even pointed her in the specific direction of one who needed to be taught His justice, and every single time she prevailed.

Then one day, God told Zoey to gather her things and travel to Arkham; there, she would face the greatest challenge of her life. God did not speak to Zoey again but, doing as she was bid, she set her sights on Arkham, hoping that to rid the town of its festering evil would once again bring the voice of the Almighty back in to her life.
entities.short_description: Zoey Samaras, the Chef, is a fictional character who appears in several of Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Files products based on the expanded Cthulhu Mythos.

entities.name: Hank Samson
entities.description:
Hank Samson, the Farmhand, is a ficitonal character created by Fantasy Flight Games as a part of their Arkham Horror Files line of Cthulhu Mythos-related content.

Never the most cerebral of men, Hank has spent his whole life life working on the farm. When one day in the fields he spotted a colossal bird attacking the cattle, he didn’t think twice before picking up the nearest thing he could use as a weapon and killing it.

Since news got out about the incident, things have started to go bad for Hank: his Pa has disappeared, and word has reached him that a mysterious man is on his trail.

Arkham Horror states that Hank worked his whole life on the family farm, whilst Eldritch Horror has him as an itinerant worker.

entities.name: Julie Sands
entities.description:
Julie Sands is a fictional character created by Dan Wickline in 2012, first appearing in issue #1 of the 1st volume of Grimm Fairy Tales Presents: Call of Wonderland by Zenescope Entertainment.

Julie Sands is a studious young woman in college who spent much of her time alone in a library until she happened across a journal written by H. P. Lovecraft. Unfortunately for Julie, she was unaware of the dark secrets in her past. She and her friend Salome Gray were dragged into the madness of Wonderland. They vanquished their foes and returned to Earth, but were soon drawn back into Wonderland by the power of the Queen of Spades, who needed them to fill the role of the Queen of Hearts in Wonderland.

entities.name: Carl Sanford
entities.description:
Carl Sanford is a fictional character from the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. He appears in Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu role-playing game, and in Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham Horror Files-related content.

The High Priest of Arkham's Silver Twilight Lodge, Sanford is a tall, slim man with an air of breeding about him. An antiquarian by trade, he holds a degree of influence in nearly every organisation in the city. Despite his standing in the community, there are many who fear the man, and rumours abound regarding the unwholesome deeds perpetrated in both his name and that of the Lodge.

Sanford was first introduced in Shadows of Yog-Sothoth as the central antagonist, working behind the scenes of the Order of the Silver Twilight, and using other "Lords of the Silver Twilight" to raise the island of R'lyeh and possibly to even wake Cthulhu, depending on the player's intervention. Canonically, this fails, but Sanford escapes and then reappears in Masks of Nyarlathotep as a secondary antagonist in the China chapter. In Cults of Cthulhu, he is listed as an example "Deathless Master" (a leader of the global Cthulhu cult, coequal to the "deathless Chinaman" of The Call of Cthulhu, whom the book names Hui Qiang), or maybe even a direct agent of Cthulhu, but the book leaves the exact interpretation up to the Keeper.

During the events of the novel, Sanford inducted Phillip Avery into the Lodge as a way to gain the services of the Mi-Go known as Mr. Stone and his Byakhee servants. (: Feeders from Within)

entities.name: Trish Scarborough
entities.description:
Trish Scarborough, often simply referred to as the Spy, is a fictional character created by Fantasy Flight Games as part of their Arkham Horror Files series of Cthulhu Mythos-related content.

Something of a prodigy, Trish excelled at everything she turned her hand to as a child, which caused eyebrows to raise when she settled down in a seemingly-mundane job with a commercial code company as an adult.

What nobody had realised was that the company was in fact a front for something far more sinister: Trish had been recruited by "The Bureau", a shadowy organisation purporting to be part of the government, and she now works as a covert operative.

However, recently Trish has begun to suspect the motives of her employers, and wonders who is really pulling their strings- the government, or perhaps forces from beyond our world…

entities.name: Scat
entities.description:
Scat is a recurrent character who appears in the Cthulhu Mythos works of the late American author Michael Shea.

An intelligent, pretty young woman. Called a "nervy little minx, bright as a button," and a "bright kid, merry and invulnerable." Scat is described as looking

She is a sex worker in a more run-down part of San Francisco, and has a voracious appetite for the work of weird fiction writers like H. P. Lovecraft and Clark Ashton Smith. She describes herself as "a hooker that reads."

Scat first stumbled across the forces of the Cthulhu Mythos when she and Dee - the owner of a local bookstore which she frequented - accidentally ate cookies laced with cannabis. The ingestion of the drug brought the two to the attention of a supernatural killer in service to Dagon and, although they were able to defeat the creature, were forever changed by the encounter.
entities.short_description: Scat is a recurrent character who appears in the Cthulhu Mythos works of the late American author Michael Shea.

entities.name: Scathach
entities.description:
Scathach is a character from Gaelic mythology introduced into the Cthulhu Mythos in the story "October Surprise" by Kevin L. O'Brien. In the Mythos story, she is described as the daughter of Hziulquoigmnzhah and Klosmiebhyx and the sister of Ysbaddaden.

In Gaelic mythology, Scathach was a warrior-queen and sorceress. She is considered to be the legendary founder of Scotland in some tales and also figures prominently in the Ulster Cycle of Irish history and folklore. Her name means "The Shadowy One" in Gaelic.

Category:Other Supernatural Beings Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works

entities.name: Claus Schmidt
entities.description:
Professor Claus Schmidt is one of the main characters from the novella Ire of the Void written by Richard Lee Byers and published by Fantasy Flight Games.

Schmidt had been a rising star in the field of theoretical physics in his native Germany, and had actually been a protégé of Albert Einstein at one point in his career. After he began to espouse radical theories on the nature of gravity and the possibility of dimensional travel, his reputation took something of a downturn, and he decided to pursue his research alone.

Believing that in certain places across the globe the barrier between our dimension and others was thinner than others, Schmidt looked into inexplicable disappearances worldwide (reasoning that these disappearances were the result of cosmic gateways), and found that one of the largest concentrations of these was in the town of Arkham, Massachusetts. Packing his bags, he made his way to the United States in order to study this phenomenon in the field.

Upon reaching Arkham, Schmidt was befriended by an elderly lecturer in astronomy from Miskatonic University named Norman Withers, who agreed to help him in exchange for Schmidt’s assistance with his own problem: the fact that six stars had simply vanished from the sky overnight. The two scientists visited some of the sites of the disappearances, and obtained data from the first two which appeared to support Schmidt’s theory. Unfortunately, at the third site, something emerged from the portal which they had been investigating and dragged him off to another plane of existence.

entities.name: Shabbith-Ka
entities.description:
Shabbith-Ka is a Lesser Outer God which appears in the H. P. Lovecraft-inspired Cthulhu Mythos. Created by Jeff Moeller, it appeared in the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game scenario "What Goes Around, Comes Around," first published in The Unspeakable Oath #8/9, and later included in the collection The Resurrected III: Out of the Vault.

Shabbith-Ka manifests as an amorphous blob of glowing purple energy; staring at the entity for long enough may allow the viewer to discern the outline of a rudimentary face, although what effect such an action might have on the person's sanity is enough to make one shudder.

The entity's worshippers summon it through the use of a particular spell, which is employed in the form of a song. When summoned, anyone not under the protection of an Elder Sign or actively singing the summoning spell will be attacked and consumed by it. It achieves this by absorbing the person into its "body," leaving nothing behind but a purple-tinged husk, which quickly disintegrates into ashes. Due to the nature of its form, physical weapons are useless against Shabbith-Ka.

When exposed to an Elder Sign, or if it has simply run out of viable prey, Shabbith-Ka retreats back to its lair at the centre of the universe, either by blasting through space at an incredible velocity or simply fading away into the void.

entities.name: Amanda Sharpe
entities.description:
Amanda Sharpe, the Student, is a character created by Fantasy Flight Games for their Arkham Horror Cthulhu Mythos setting.

A 2-year student at Arkham's prestigious Miskatonic University during the late 1920s, Amanda has been having nightmares of an ancient entity sleeping beneath the waves. These dreams were sparked by the sight of a painting hanging in the university’s halls, and have had a negative impact on her schoolwork.

In Graham McNeill's novel Ghouls of the Miskatonic, Amanda and her friend and roommate Rita Young were kidnapped by a cult of Cthulhu worshippers who intended to feed the pair to their pet ghouls. Fortunately, the two were saved by an unlikely band of heroes, including Rex Murphy and Finn Edwards.

First introduced in Fantasy Flight's Arkham Horror Second Edition Core Set, Amanda Sharpe has since appeared in several other of the company's releases, including Eldritch Horror and Arkham Horror: The Card Game, and a plastic model of Amanda was created for the Arkham Horror Premium Figures series. Her character was expanded on significantly in Graham McNeill's novel Ghouls of the Miskatonic, and she was included as a playable investigator character in Jonathan Green's 2024 gamebook The Darkness Over Arkham.

entities.name: Sheila
entities.description:
Sheila (also known as The Chosen One) is a fictional hero created by Sam Raimi for the 1992 comedy-fantasy film Army of Darkness, the third installment of Raimi's Evil Dead franchise.

Sheila was a maiden in 1300 AD who first hated the time displaced Ash Williams and then fell in love with him. A Deadite possessed her and she turned into "Bad Sheila". Upon the defeat of Evil Ash and the Army of Darkness, she was freed of the Deadite and witnessed Ash's return back home to his own time.

Another version married Ash Williams who decided to stay in 1300 AD. This version had lost her right hand, and battled Deadites alongside her husband. Pregnant with his child, they married. Unfortunately during the reception party, a drunken Ash spoke the words "Klaatu Barada Nikto" which sent him to 1350 AD.

In another reality, after Ash returned to his time, she was convinced by the Wise Man and Lord Arthur to help them create a team to continue the teachings of the Promised One. She became a teacher to what would eventually become the 21st century's Supernatural Military-Adjacent Response Team (S.M.A.R.T).

entities.description:
Shimba is a fictional deity mentioned in the Cthulhu Mythos short story "The Stairs in the Crypt", by Lin Carter.

Nothing is known about Shimba, other than that it is a benevolent god of shepherds worshiped in monasteries in ancient Hyperborea. A remarkably agreeable deity, the monks of Shimba are allowed to indulge in hedonistic consumption of food and drink, and live in great comfort. (: "The Stairs in the Crypt")

It's unknown whether Shimba is a real entity within the context of the Mythos. Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Other Supernatural Beings

entities.name: Shimmering Liquid
entities.description:
The Shimmering Liquid is a fictional entity created by American author and games designer Kevin A. Ross for the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu. It first appeared in "Thunder in the Blood", a scenario included in the supplement End of the World (Triad Entertainments, 1994).

The Shimmering Liquid is one of five Lesser Other Gods from the Court of Azathoth that appeared during a summoning of Azathoth near San Lucas. It appears as a fully plastic but slightly translucent and shimmering liquid that is constantly changing shape while absorbing all manner of victims, no matter their form or size. (: End of the World)

entities.name: Shuggob
entities.description:
Shuggob is a fictional character created by Lin Carter for his Cthulhu Mythos short story "In the Vale of Pnath".

Shuggob is an elderly ghoul sage who lives alone in a stone house surrounded by a garden of moss and lichens, with a hedge made of mottled fungi, in the part of the Dreamlands known as the Vale of Pnath. He is extremely knowledgeable about magic and skilled in the craft of potions.

Somewhat unusually for a ghoul, Shuggob is a soft-spoken individual of gentlemanly demeanor and scholarly inclinations. He is amicable and receptive to strangers, offering them food and drinks of the type generally consumed by his species, i.e. made from human flesh and blood.

In terms of physical appearance, Shuggob is tall and lean. His skin is grey, cold to the touch, and rubbery, and his hands are surprisingly strong. He is so ancient that parts of his face have been eaten away by maggots, making his speech difficult to understand at times. Eibon attributes this state of partial decomposition to Shuggob's extreme age and "questionable diet". (: "In the Vale of Pnath") Category:Characters Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Extra-Dimensional Characters

entities.name: The Signalman
entities.description:
The Signalman is a ficitonal character in Caitlin R. Kiernan's Tinfoil Dossier series, the only character who appears in all three books. He is a senior agent of the shadowy organization known as Albany, a cynical and burnt-out alcoholic who is nonetheless one of the agency's most effective assets. He has a reputation as "the one who never flinched," and as "one of the last of Albany’s True Believers, a stone-cold MiB, the agency man through and through." He is introduced as one of the main characters in Agents of Dreamland (2017), plays a minor but pivotal role in Black Helicopters (2018), and is again a prominent onstage figure in The Tindalos Asset (2020).

The character's full name is never given; his nickname comes from the railroad watch he always carries, manufactured by the Elgin Watch Company of Elgin, Illinois, in 1888. In The Tindalos Asset, we learn that his first name is Quentin. He has an apartment in the hills above Santa Monica, California.

He is born in 1960, in Birmingham, Alabama. When he is eight years old, in 1968, he watches a late-show movie on TV, The Star Maiden, that has a profound effect on him.

His career with Albany begins in 1981. By 2011, he is partnered with the supernatural assassin Ellison Nicodemo, who is also his lover. A botched attempt to terminate the Mythos-powered serial killer Jehosheba Talog leaves Nicodemo severely traumatized.

entities.name: Silent One
entities.description:
The Silent Ones were a group of creatures which appeared in Mark McLaughlin's 2004 short story "Toadface".

Each of the three Silent Ones were roughly eighty feet in length, with heads similar to that of a snake yet sporting fish-like faces. They had fat bodies, tentacles in place of arms, and massively thick legs akin to those of an iguana. Although they were stated to possess gills, they seemed to be capable of comfortably surviving on land, at least for a short period of time.

The three Silent Ones slept in an ancient ruined temple (said to be reminiscent of a gladiatorial arena) within the aquatic Deep One city of Y'ha-nthlei just off Innsmouth harbour. The one known as G'hlaballa had its body inhabited by the ghost of a man known as John Masters who used it to kill the Deep One Toadface before heading back to the ocean to feed on whales.

The origins of the Silent Ones, how long they had lain dormant in their temple, or indeed how they even came to rest there, remains a mystery, although it is possible that they may have been either gods of the Deep Ones or Great Old Ones, as Toadface stated that by possessing G'hlaballa's slumbering form, Masters was committing an act of blasphemy.

entities.name: Simon of Gitta
entities.description:
Simon of Gitta is the protagonist of a series of Cthulhu Mythos stories by Richard L. Tierney featuring an alternative history set in the days of Ancient Rome.

Simon is an ex-gladiator turned sorcerer, using his skills with sword and sorcery alike to combat Mythos entities and the Roman Empire. He first appeared in "The Ring of Set", published in Swords Against Darkness #1 in 1977, though written in 1960.

Tierney loosely based Simon of Gitta on the biblical figure of Simon Magus, inspired by Jack Palance's portrayal of the character in the film The Silver Chalice (1954). The stories incorporate aspects of the historical religion of Gnosticism, meshing its lore with that of H. P. Lovecraft and his circle.

Tierney's Simon of Gitta stories are collected in The Scroll of Thoth: Simon Magus and the Great Old Ones, a Chaosium publication edited by Robert M. Price, and in Sorcery Against Caesar: The Complete Simon of Gitta Stories, from Pickman's Press.

entities.name: Court of Azathoth
entities.description:
The Court of Azathoth is a place mentioned in the Cthulhu Mythos. Sometimes it is called "the Final Void". Its relationship to the Last Void is unclear.

The Court of Azathoth, also known as the "Mouth of Madness", is located at the center of the universe, beyond time and space. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath, : Malleus Monstrorum (2006 edition))

The Court stands on a plane beyond space and time, serving as the abode for the Blind Idiot God Azathoth, "the foolish Daemon Sultan." There, the almighty Outer God remains dormant by the sounds sung by amorphous flute players. Both Nyarlathotep and Yog-Sothoth are known to visit the Court of Azathoth to review the state he is in after some time.

Court of Azathoth is only chaos, going beyond dimensional space, time, and matter, without form or location. (: Fungi from Yuggoth). Also, it is also said that Azathoth is “beyond angled space.” (: The Whisperer in Darkness).

entities.name: Cancerverse
entities.description:
Cancerverse is a fictional universe in the Marvel Multiverse, one of the realities conquered by the Many-Angled Ones. It appeared in The Thanos Imperative mini-series in 2010.

In this reality, Death was defeated by Life. A dying Captain Mar-Vell was seduced by the Many-Angled Ones into making a pact with them, who cured him of his cancer. After convincing his closest allies and friends to join him, twisting and corrupting them, they killed Thanos, the Avatar of Death. As a result of that ritual, which also destroyed that universe's cosmic aspect of Death, Life itself became an Eldritch abomination. Without Death to keep Life in check, it absorbed everything that would otherwise have been destroyed or killed and it grew like a cancerous tumor.

This unnatural "eternal life" was fueled by the power of the Many-Angled Ones, and Lord Mar-Vel, as the Cancerverse's Avatar of Life, was determined to spread the plague of undeath throughout the Multiverse. His first target was the Prime Reality (Earth-616), which he assaulted through a tear in reality known as the Fault. They would have succeeded if not for the actions of 616's Thanos and the Guardians of the Galaxy, who brought their universe's Death into the Cancerverse, temporarily weakening it and crippling the invasion. As the entity Death had to return to their reality, the Cancerverse was able to recover.

The Cancerverse features corrupted versions of the Marvel Universe's leading super teams, including the Revengers (Avengers), the Defenders of the Realm (Defenders), the Ex-Men (X-Men) and the Ftaghn Four (Fantastic Four).
entities.short_description: Cancerverse is a fictional universe in the Marvel Multiverse, one of the realities conquered by the Many-Angled Ones. It appeared in The Thanos Imperative mini-series in 2010.

entities.name: Celestial Toyroom
entities.description:
The Celestial Toyroom is a dimension created by the BBC in 1966 for Doctor Who.

The Celestial Toyroom is the realm of the Great Old One, the Celestial Toymaker, a remnant of its original universe and an integral part of the entity. The Celestial Toymaker could not survive long outside of this reality, due to the rules which were set down in his own home universe. He resides in the "Toy Shop" which unlike the rest of the realm is actually connected to him. Everything else can be destroyed except for the Toy Shop. A void surrounds the Toy Shop and anyone who attempts to leave, find themselves in a loop reentering it.

Interestingly, several of the entities appearing within the Celestial Toyroom seem to be fictional creations with their own independent "life", similar to Dreamlands entities.

entities.description:
The Dark Circus is a dimension created by the BBC in 1988 for Doctor Who.

The Dark Circus is the Gods of Ragnarok's dimension, which appears as an arena consisting of grey stone slabs that have inscriptions. Entrance to it is usually through a well on Segonax, though they can also create a bridge for others to enter the Circus. Gladiators are lured to the Dark Circus, where the Gods feed on the entertainment.

entities.description:
The Deadlands is a fictional dimension in the Ash vs Evil Dead universe which first appeared in 2018 in the episode 7 of season 3, "Twist and Shout".

The Deadlands is the shadowy mirror version of the real world. Humans who have been killed by Deadites or other evil beings or objects, end up in the Deadlands where they are preyed upon by a shadow demon. It is to here that the Dark Ones were originally banished from Earth.

entities.name: Dimension
entities.description:
The concept of different dimensions is present throughout the writings of H. P. Lovecraft and the cosmic horror genre as a whole. The term is often used to describe universes or planes of existence different from our own, usually very alien in nature or following different laws and having different matter than our own universe. For example Cthulhu is from a different universe/dimension as he is described as being made of a different type of matter, as well as the Mi-Go. The Dreamlands are a famous example as well.

Dimensions can also be interpreted as higher spatial dimensions, which as seen in "Through the Gates of the Silver Key", go up until "archetypal infinity". Gates are a series of highly transcendental planes of existence which themselves surpass the very concept of higher dimensions. An unknown amount of gates exist, but there is stated to be a "multitude". The Ultimate Gate transcends all dimensions, universes and planes of existence and is where the Court of Azathoth is located in the "Ultimate Void", where the Outer Gods reside.

Fictional dimensions are often treated as places similar to "parallel worlds" or pocket dimensions, small and finite bounded other worlds. However sometimes the term is used less accurately or more poetically in Mythos works. For example the entities in "From Beyond" are visible when an attunement takes place. This attunement is treated as accessing a different dimension by most authors using it in their own pastiches. However, the original story deals with vibrations or frequencies so in that sense treating different frequencies as different dimensions is not correct. This is why some later writers deliberately obscure the intended nature of the "other dimensions" by using poetical or literary terms such as "realm" or "world" rather than "dimension". Dimension is the most scientific sounding of the common terms and in later Lovecraft, for example "The Dreams in the Witch-House", when magic-as-unknown-science has more or less replaced the supernatural, the term "dimension" is used in its applicable meaning from physics. entities.name: Dreamlands
entities.description:
The Dreamlands (also known as the Dream Realm) are a fictional setting created by H. P. Lovecraft for a series of stories, known as the Dream Cycle, set in a world that people enter through their dreams. It is a vast, alternate dimension or universe, with lands, seas, creatures, civilisations, and an extensive Underworld.

The Dreamlands are for the most part a mirror-image of our waking universe, having, as far as can be determined, the same planets, stars, and other cosmic geographical features. However, there are numerous races, civilisations, and beings existing in the Dreamlands that do not exist in the waking universe, such as the Zoogs, Gugs, Ghasts, moon-beasts, and others.

In keeping with the dimension's nature as the consensus of Earth's dreams, it is easier to travel to distant places including other planets or the Moon than it would be in the physical waking world. The journey may still be long or have requirements to be met but travel to distant "locations" in the Dreamlands is relatively commonplace.

Also, the Dreamlands usually refers to the Dreamlands of Earth; however the overarching Dream realm includes a "Dreamlands" for every world inhabited by intelligent life. For example if Mars still had intelligent life, as some writers suggest, it too would have a Dream realm of its own and those falling asleep and dreaming on Mars would enter the same Dreamlands but in a vastly distant and presumably different set of entry points to those of Earth's Dreamers.

entities.description:
Egyptica is an extra-dimensional realm created by Mark McLaughlin and Michael Sheehan, Jr. for their Egyptian-themed contributions to the greater Cthulhu Mythos.

Existing on a separate plane of reality to Earth, Egyptica was said to have been created by the Outer God Nyarlathotep for his followers and their descendants, who dwell there to this day. Access to it is protected by a thick, swirling green fog shot through with bolts of lightning, and it appears to be divided into several sub-regions, including:

Transportation is provided by huge floating pyramids and Egyptian-style barges, likely powered by the magic seemingly possessed by all Egypticans.

entities.name: Elysia
entities.description:
Elysia is an extradimensional plane of existence in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos. It first appeared in Brian Lumley's novel The Transition of Titus Crow, part of the Titus Crow series.

The home of the ancient and inscrutable Elder Gods, the eternal enemies of both the Great Old Ones and the Outer Gods, Elysia is impossible to describe in its entirety. Whilst portions of it resemble endless forests, other areas are simply vast, nearly-empty oceans, and it features many cities which hover above its varied landscape, each as individual as the god or race which inhabits them.

What is known of Elysia is that it is an incredibly difficult dimension to locate. This may be due to the fact that it is protected by the unimaginably vast powers wielded by the Elder Gods, or simply that they have hidden the routes to it so well that only the most intelligent creatures in the multitude of parallel worlds which exist can even begin to fathom where to begin looking for them.

The first amongst the Elder Gods, Kthanid holds his palace in what is assumed to be the centre of Elysia. A vast, crystalline structure, it contains not only his living quarters, but on occasion residences for those races who serve him. He also keeps a supply of “Time Clocks” in a great chamber, machines whose capabilities can transcend time and space, and which he loans to lesser creatures in his employ in order to carry out specific tasks.

entities.name: Far Realm
entities.description:
The Far Realm is a Lovecraftian-like eldritch dimension from the fictional universe of the Dungeons & Dragons pencil-and-paper roleplaying game by Wizards of the Coast.

The Far Realm is a plane of madness, which is very far from the material plane. Which consists of an infinite number of layers of finite size. Layers that are very thin from a mile in thickness at most to an inch at the thinnest, with 10 ft separating each layer. Which are transparent and highly morphic. Entities and landmarks within the Far Realm are multidimensional, simultaneously existing on multiple layers at once.

It's a plane with forests of tentacles vegetation, viscously syrup-like air, drifting colossal multi-layer beings with the smallest being city-sized, falling globes that burst releasing horse-sized ticks, rivers of milky white fluids, etc. Neither time or gravity exists in the Far Realm. Inhabited by a number of species including Aboleth, Illithid, Beholder, kaorti, and carrion crawlers. Many Aberrations are also created here. Visitors usually go mad and all are twisted into gruesome creatures. It threatens all of the realities in the Multiverse. The rulers of the Far Realm are the Uvuudaums, whose very presence would make most creatures insane.

entities.name: Flickering Realms
entities.description:
The Flickering Realms is a fictional dimension created by Marvel Comics, which first appeared in Spider-Woman Vol 1 #44 "Vengeance!". It is known for being the realm of Chthon, as well as inhabiting the N'Garai.

The Flickering Realms (aka, the Dimension of the Darkhold) was created by the Elder God known as Chthon. The dimension has no map, due to its constantly changing landscape. One may cross stones, then swamps, followed by snow, and then sands; in which the snow burns like fire and the stones bleed. The only thing that is constant in the dimension is danger. It also contains the dimension of the N'Garai, which is full of demons.

entities.name: Gate
entities.description:
The Gates are incredibly vast levels of existence. The exact number of Gates is not known, only that there is a "multiplicity" of them.(: Through the Gates of the Silver Key)

The Ultimate Gate is the final Gate that is absolutely limitless and boundless from the perspective of beings from lesser Gates. It is guarded by 'Umr at-Tawil, an avatar of Yog-Sothoth itself. Past the Ultimate Gate lies the Ultimate Abyss, and is the home of Yog-Sothoth.

Randolph Carter passed all the Gates, including the Ultimate Gate, on his journey to meet the All-in-One, and where he saw his infinite duplicates.

entities.name: Heavenly Realms
entities.description:
The Heavenly Realms has historically been part of Buddhist cosmology. The Heavenly Realms of the Cthulhu Mythos was created by Chaosium for the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game in 2005.

The Heavenly Realms are located above Mount Semura, and can only be reached via specific spells and portals. The heavens are stacked in infinite dimensional layers. It's not a place for either the living or the dead, and humans are rarely welcomed with open arms by the gods residing there. Like humans, the gods of the Heavenly Realms have emotions and desires. Therefore depending on the mood of the god, a human guest may be struck by an angry god or seduced by a lustful one. Living in the Heavenly Realms are the gods of ancient China and Japan, the Taoist Immortals, and avatars of the Mythos (e.g. Aku-Shin Kage, one of Nyarlathotep's forms). It's a dimension which is either adjacent to the Dreamlands or completely separate.

It is not yet clear what if any connection may exist between the gods of the Heavenly Realms and the old gods of Earth now known as the Great Ones who reside in the Dreamlands.

K'gil'mnon is a fictional alternative reality or dimension that appeared in the short story "His Hour Upon the Stage" by J. B. Lee, published in the e-zine Nightscapes in 1998. It is depicted as a "nightmare realm" which seems very nebulous, perhaps similar to a small galaxy. It is home to and ruled by the Outer God Kaalut, accompanied by his parasitic insectoid servants, the Gharoides. The story does not mention any other entities inhabiting K'gil'mnon.

The Land of Fiction first appeared in an adventure involving the second incarnation of The Doctor. It was later stated as having been created by the Gods of Ragnarok for their own entertainment, but eventually they grew bored of the Land of Fiction and abandoned it. The dimension is inhabited by characters from various works of folklore, mythology, and fiction.

entities.name: Last Void
entities.description:
The Last Void is a fictional "location" created by H. P. Lovecraft and E. Hoffman Price for their short story "Through the Gates of the Silver Key." Its relationship to the Final Void, another term for the Court of Azathoth, is unclear.

In "Through the Gates of the Silver Key," Lovecraft and Price refer to the Last Void as that which is beyond all matter, and reality - transcending "all earths" and thus by implication all parallel worlds, alternative histories. The Last Void is thus, in current physics terms, either the Base Reality - or complete nothingness incapable of definition.

In the context of the story, it is clearly something inspiring both awe and fear. The story deals with the annihilation of individuality among many other themes and so it is not inappropriate to see the Last Void as a true baseline in the writings of Lovecraft but also in the broader Cthullhu Mythos, beyond any individual versions of any of the concepts or creatures written about, and since it is also beyond the Dreamlands it forms a kind of hard boundary within which the entirety of all the expanded Cthulhu Mythos takes place. It is the end of all invention, as it were.

Whether the resemblance of the Last Void to the annihilation of the ego and consciousness in Zen, certain Buddhist and Hinduism beliefs and in Jungian philosophy is coincidental or not is unknown.

entities.name: Marvel Multiverse
entities.description:
The Marvel Multiverse is a fictional multiverse created by Marvel Comics, which is inhabited by the Many-Angled Ones. It is the setting for two ongoing on-again, off-again comic series published by Marvel Comics, the What If? series (1977+) and the Exiles series (2001+). It was also the stage for an epic cosmic horror story which was the "Time Runs Out" event published in 2014-2015, as well as the issues leading up to the event, mainly within New Avengers Vol. 3 (issues #3-6 and 13-22 in 2013-2014).

The Marvel Multiverse is an infinite one (per the One Above All, who rules the Multiverse), in which each action that an individual takes creates a new reality, even something as simple as scratching your nose (as proven by Thanos and confirmed by the One Above All). In the early 21st century, Earth alone had billions of future timelines and the largest known multiversal temporal government (the Congress of Realities) had representatives from millions of realities. There have been a few known multiversal-level incidents which threatened the Marvel Multiverse or made changes to it, most recently when the Beyonders (a trio of omnipotent beings from a dimension beyond the Multiverse) nearly ended the Multiverse (the "Time Runs Out" event). It was destroyed at the end of the conflict, but was later restored.

The Marvel Multiverse is one of an unknown number of Multiverses that make up the Megaverse, which in turn is one of an unknown number of Megaverses that make up the Omniverse. Other Multiverses that are known to exist to the higher-level beings of the Marvel Multiverse include the DC Multiverse, the Transformers Multiverse, the Doctor Who Multiverse, and the Capcom Multiverse. Sometimes, there is interaction between the Multiverses, which result in temporary new realities or permanent realities that come about due to the merging of a universe from each Multiverse.

The Old Ones are scattered across this Multiverse with some living in the positive universes, beings that are powerful enough to pose a threat to a world to those that pose a threat to the entire universe. In the space between the infinite realities is where many of the Old Ones live or exist, from which they attempt to corrupt and conquer those realities. Any world or universe which is conquered by them gradually decays and dies. One such universe was called the Cancerverse, where the abstract entity known as "Death" was killed and nothing died. It was a universe corrupted by the Many-Angled Ones and life ran riot, like a cancer.

entities.name: Mirror Dimension
entities.description:
The Mirror Dimension is a fictional dimension in the Evil Dead universe which was later retconned as first appearing in the 1987 movie Evil Dead II, although it was not identified as the Mirror Dimension at that time. Its subsequent comic book appearance (see below) is its true first appearance and where it received its name.

The Mirror Dimension is where the first Chosen One banished the Dark Ones and Deadites. The spirits of slain demons and Deadites live in this dimension until someone summons them to Earth, alongside the souls of those consumed by the Deadites. It's unknown as to who created the dimension. Entry to the dimension is via a portal created by a spell in the Necronomicon Ex-Mortis, a Deadite swallowing one’s soul, or being pulled into it by a doppelgänger via a reflective surface.

One can leave the dimension by two ways, a teleportation spell cast by a servant of the Dark Ones or if you were pulled in by the doppelganger, by returning to the same spot and switching places. It's implied that the dimension is somewhat sentient. Changing its appearance, using the "swallowed" souls that joined the group consciousness as inspiration. Those who are pulled into the dimension experience death over and over, in varying ways (e.g. melting, falling apart, being consumed / replaced by worms, etc). When a simulacrum of Ash Williams ended up in that dimension, it experienced or witnessed its death a million times.

entities.name: Prime Reality
entities.description:
The Prime Reality (a.k.a. Earth-616) is a fictional universe created by Marvel Comics which is inhabited by the Many-Angled Ones and Lovecraftian Elder Gods. It is the setting for most of the comic series published by Marvel Comics, with a few comic series focused on the universe itself (the cosmic character or team series). It has also been the stage of two cosmic horror stories, the Infinity Gauntlet event in 1991 and the Chaos War event in 2010. There were also several other universal level events, such as the Infinity War and the Infinity Crusade.

Within "known space" (the local group of galaxies) there have been various events and crossovers, ranging from those focused on a particular character or team (e.g., the Dark Phoenix Saga, the Brood Saga, the Thanos War, and Emperor Vulcan: The Rise and Fall of the Shi'ar Empire) to the intergalactic wars that altered the region's geopolitics (the Kree-Skrull War, Operation Galactic Storm, the Second Kree-Skrull War, Annihilation, Annihilation: Conquest, War of Kings, The Thanos Imperative, and Infinity).

The Prime Reality (Earth-616) is the mainstream reality of the Marvel Multiverse that is still expanding and currently contains billions of galaxies. Its existence is occasionally threatened by the super-genius and super-powered Thanos the Mad Titan and sometimes by someone else (e.g., the Lovecraftian entity Dormammu) and on occasion its existence is threatened by an entity or faction from another reality. In this reality, during the late 20th century and so far in the early part of the 21st century, it is usually someone from Earth or an alien who favors Earth, who saves the universe or "known space". Most of the time it is either the Silver Surfer, the Fantastic Four, the Avengers, or the X-Men (the latter three being from Earth).

The Old Ones have representation within the Prime Reality, either themselves or their minions. On occasion, those existing outside of the various universes (e.g., Shuma-Gorath and Slorioth) will manifest in the Prime Reality, though because of how incomprehensibly vast is their power, it is usually only the tiniest infinitesimal fragment of their being.

entities.name: Gulf of S'glhuo
entities.description:
S'glhuo is a fictional dimension which first appeared in Ramsey Campbell's short story "The Plain of Sound".

S'glhuo is another dimension that only exists in our dimension as sound. In certain places, such as the plain in the Severn Valley, the dimension overlaps into our own, creating the effect of walking through jelly. Sounds from our world correspond to objects in S'glhuo, and sounds in our world can create things both living and non-living in S'glhuo. The location in the Severn Valley corresponds to a city of pillars on a planet composed of sound. It is implied there are other planets made of sound in S'glhuo and that the dimension is home to Tru'nembra, an Outer God made from pure sound. In S'glhuo, our dimension is only perceptible as odor. Details on S'glhuo are given in The Revelations of Gla'aki, along with plans for a machine to contact the S'glhuoans.

It is not known if the blue skinned reptilians that live near the Severn Valley are the only type of S'glhuoans, but it is likely that the dimension is home to other life forms. The denizens of S'glhuo may be friendly or hostile, but seem to have knowledge of both advanced science and the Mythos. In their own world they are blue skinned, tall, boneless reptiloids, but in ours they are beings of pure sound.

entities.name: The Labyrinth
entities.description:
The Labyrinth is a Lovecraftian-like eldritch dimension from the fictional universe of the Hellraiser franchise. This realm is a place of extreme agony ruled by the Cenobites and their god, Leviathan. Existing outside our dimension, it's often compared to Hell as it's a place of endless suffering. Described as a vast, complex labyrinth, this realm has no clear exit. At its core lies Leviathan, the entity controlling the Cenobites. While sometimes called Hell, its exact nature and relation to traditional religious concepts remain uncertain.

The Labyrinth is a complex, multi-story maze filled with countless rooms and passageways. Outsiders cannot find their way through it. Inside, countless souls are trapped and subjected to endless, personalized torment by demonic creatures. Above the Labyrinth, a massive, geometric entity called Leviathan supposedly reigns, though its exact role remains unknown.

Hell, once a chaotic and entertaining realm according to the character Pinhead, has transformed into a more structured place since Angelique's era. While naturally a labyrinthine dimension, Hell is capable of changing its form based on the pleasures and pains of its inhabitants. Many believe it's not the traditional Hell of religious texts but a separate dimension that can be interpreted as either heaven or hell, depending on the perspective of those trapped within.

Hell, as depicted in the franchise, has evolved from a chaotic, pleasure-pain dimension into a more structured and less enjoyable place. While originally a formless realm shaped by the inhabitants' experiences, it's now often portrayed as a traditional hell. There’s speculation that it might not be the biblical Hell but a different dimension entirely, experienced as heaven or hell depending on the trapped soul.

entities.name: The Upside Down
entities.description:
The Upside Down is a dark and eldritch parallel dimension featured in the Netflix urban fantasy series Stranger Things. It is a twisted, decaying mirror image of the real world, specifically the town of Hawkins, Indiana. It is filled with grotesque creatures and an ever-growing, malevolent force known as the Mind Flayer. Once a parallel dimension, it was irrevocably altered when child psychic Eleven opened a gate between the two worlds, allowing the horrors within to seep into the human realm.

Since then, it has been a constant threat to Hawkins, with its influence growing stronger as the series progresses. The Mind Flayer, a powerful entity from this dimension, seeks to merge the Upside Down with the real world, creating a horrifying new reality.

entities.name: Tindalos
entities.description:
Tindalos is a fictional location, shown in some works to be a dimension, in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was first mentioned, through the title of their most infamous denizens the Hounds of Tindalos, by American author Frank Belknap Long in his 1929 short story "The Hounds of Tindalos."

Assuming that Tindalos is in fact a location and not the master of the Hounds of Tindalos, it may be inferred from the actions of the Hounds that it is a separate dimension.

In Richard Lee Byers' novella Ire of the Void, Tindalos is an alien dimension, one inhabited by not only the Hounds, but also Satyrs and fearsome Doels (in Long's story, it was already established that the Satyrs and the Doels are associated with the Hounds of Tindalos). Its geography consists primarily of floating roadways in bizarre geometric patterns, and the occasional land mass adorned with dome-shaped buildings. Despite the incomprehensible laws which govern this strange realm, it is not unnavigable by human beings, as shown when Norman Withers worked his way across the labyrinth of roadways and rescued the abducted Claus Schmidt.

entities.name: Wonderland
entities.description:
Wonderland is a fictional country which appeared in the children's novel Alice's Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll in 1865. Zenescope Entertainment reimagined it in 2007 as R'lyeh in its Grimm Fairy Tales comic series and its spin-off Wonderland.

Wonderland is the source of the world's madness (Never-Ending Dream). To prevent the madness from infecting Earth, mankind made a deal with the sleeping entity. In every generation, children are sacrificed so that it doesn't wake. The innocents who end up in Wonderland feed the Jabberwocky's undying cravings. The monsters of the world (e.g. Hitler and Jack the Ripper) were influenced by Wonderland.

Down the generations, it has been the responsibility of one family to keep Wonderland at bay. In the modern era, the Liddle family has been sacrificing their offspring, one of which was Alice Liddle. One ancestor refused to sacrifice his son, resulting in the Great Depression and World War Two. The essence of Wonderland slips through occasionally, resulting in war, insanity, etc., but far less than it would without the sacrifices.

Category:Dimensions Category:Locations Originating From Mythos-Adjacent Works

entities.description:
The Arinurian Streams are cosmic boundary markers of uncertain nature that separate the Milky Way galaxy from the distant worlds of Teloe and Cytharion, mentioned in the story "The Crawling Chaos" by H. P. Lovecraft. They were part of an apocalyptic vision of the future experienced by the unnamed narrator of the story under the influence of opium, so their literal existence may or may not be taken for granted in the context of the Mythos.

entities.name: Basalt Pillars of the West
entities.description:
The Basalt Pillars of the West are fictional structures in the Cthulhu Mythos. They were originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The White Ship".

The Basalt Pillars of the West are a pair of pillars of gargantuan size made of basalt (a dark volcanic rock) that rise from the ocean in the Dreamlands on the western edge of the world. The pillars form the gate of a monstrous cataract whose swift, resistless waters spill over the edge into the "abysmal nothingness" of planetary space. The pillars are shrouded in mist so that none may see beyond them until one sails through the pillars and the mists are lifted, at which point the current becomes too strong to escape. (: "The White Ship", The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

Basil Elton sailed through the Basalt Pillars aboard the White Ship on his search for the fabled land of Cathuria but never found it. (: "The White Ship")

Randolph Carter was taken to the Moon as a prisoner aboard a ship that sailed through the pillars and over the edge. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

entities.name: Carcosa
entities.description:
Carcosa is a mystical ancient city created by Ambrose Bierce for his short story "An Inhabitant of Carcosa". It is a central element of the horror fantasy story cycle The King in Yellow, by Robert W. Chambers, who places it in an apparently extraterrestrial landscape complete with two suns, strange moons, and black stars. In some of Chambers' stories, it is stated that the towers of Carcosa can rise behind the moon, as if the city itself was a celestial place - or perhaps a theatrical stage.

The King in Yellow also associates Carcosa with Aldebaran and the Hyades, as well as Hastur (originally the name of a god created by Bierce).

While the mythology of The King in Yellow was incorporated into the Cthulhu Mythos by H. P. Lovecraft in The Whisperer in Darkness, Carcosa itself was referenced in the Mythos stories of August Derleth and Donald Wandrei.

In the Pathfinder multiverse, Carcosa is a highly magical planet which contains a living city that is also called Carcosa. It's the home of Hastur, who resides in the monstrous Lake of Hali. When the light from Carcosa's star shines on another world's night sky, Hastur's power increases on that world. Carcosa is continuously expanding, absorbing the societies and cities of other worlds, serving as the fuel for Hastur's eventual ascension into the ranks of the Outer Gods, at which time he will consume and absorb Carcosa and its inhabitants. The city of Carcosa is a vast patchwork of the cities which it absorbed over the eons, each individual patchwork is a nexus, which may retain some of the properties of their original worlds. Some of the known nexuses include Neruzavin (flying polyp city), Bohlvari (shoggoth inhabited elder thing city), a technologically advanced city of skyscrapers (inhabited by robots and aliens), and an underwater city (inhabited by the undead).

A fabled land of otherworldly beauty that is thought to exist by many of those who live in the Dreamlands, Cathuria is regarded as a legend and is said to lie beyond the Basalt Pillars of the West. Basil Elton sailed beyond the pillars aboard the White Ship in his search for Cathuria but never found it. (: "The White Ship")

entities.name: Cytharion
entities.description:
Cytharion, also known as Cytharion of the Seven Suns, is a mystical realm located somewhere "beyond the Milky Way and the Arinurian Streams", mentioned in the story "The Crawling Chaos" by H. P. Lovecraft. Cytharion is somewhere adjacent to the realm of Teloe, both of which are described as beautiful utopias inhabited by benevolent deities and favored mortals.

Cytharion and Teloe were part of an apocalyptic vision of the future experienced by the unnamed narrator of the story under the influence of opium, so their literal existence may or may not be taken for granted in the context of the Mythos.

According to The Whisperer in Darkness and other sources, Nyarlathotep also dwells in a "world of Seven Suns", which is named Abbith in the expanded Mythos. However, Nyarlathotep is not mentioned in "The Crawling Chaos" (despite the story's title matching one of his most common aliases).

entities.name: Dylath-Leen
entities.description:
Dylath-Leen is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his novella The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath.

Dylath-Leen is a bustling trading port and one of the largest cities in the Dreamlands. As well as the usual boats, mule caravans and two wheeled carts that stream constantly through the gates and docks, Dylath-Leen is famous for the comings and goings of the mysterious Black Galleys.

The thin angular towers that line the dark streets of Dylath-Leen are built of black basalt and from a distance could be compared to the stones of the Giant's Causeway.

The streets and sea taverns along the wharves are filled with oddly robed sailors from across the earth and beyond. Though most of the locals' conversation is taken up with rumours about the Black Galleys they can be coaxed to help travellers like Randolph Carter who arrives looking for passage to Oriab.

entities.name: Earth-666
entities.description:
Earth-666 is an alternate reality that first appears in Marvel Comics' Secret Avengers Vol 1 #33 and appeared in the next two issues of that volume. The reason it's called Earth-666 is because in that reality, Earth is a world of the undead.

In this world there are no living humans or none are visible. The world is run by a totalitarian regime, in which "civilians" require permits for a variety of things. It's inhabitants included vampires, werewolves, ghosts, mummies, zombies, spider humanoids, fish-like humanoids, and squid-like beings. They prayed to or swore by, the Old One Shuma-Gorath and the Hell Lord Mephisto. Its superhuman defenders were the Undead Avengers.

Their god is an Undead Celestial (space god) and their objective is to spread the undead across the universe. Who possessed the Orb of Necromancy which they planned to us to help them in their goal of bringing the dead back to life throughout the cosmos. It was feared that if the rest of the cosmos found out about their agenda, they would come and destroy their planet. Located on their world was Shuma-Gorath's Ego Maze, or at least access to it via a portal.

Category:Planets Category:Locations Originating From Expanded Mythos Works Category:Extra-Dimensional Locations

entities.name: Falona
entities.description:
Falona is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The Doom That Came to Sarnath".

Falona is a region of the Dreamlands whose people are described as brave and adventurous, with yellow hair and blue eyes. When the city of Sarnath was destroyed, no one dared return to the site where it once stood until long after when adventurers from Falona made the distant journey there. They had expected to see what remained of the city, but all they found was the lake, the grey rock Akurion that reared high above the water, and the empty shore as if Sarnath had never existed. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")

They also discovered, half buried in the marsh, the green stone idol of Bokrug, the Great Water Lizard. The idol was later enshrined at the high temple in the city of Ilarnek and subsequently worshipped throughout the land of Mnar. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")
