entities.name: Ilarnek
entities.description:
Ilarnek is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The Doom That Came to Sarnath".

Ilarnek is a city in the land of Mnar on the River Ai in the Dreamlands. It was built by the same wandering tribes that built the Mnaran cities of Thraa, Kadatheron, and Sarnath. Early in their history, an important trade route was established between Sarnath and Ilarnek. Sarnath eventually conquered the neighboring cities and lands (including Ilarnek) and forged an empire. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")

After the destruction of Sarnath, the green stone idol of Bokrug, the Great Water Lizard, was found on the marshy lakeshore where the city once stood. The idol, which had been taken by Sarnath from the conquered city of Ib, was enshrined in the high temple at Ilarnek and was subsequently worshipped throughout the land of Mnar. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")

Ilarnek is a repository of lore pertaining to the beings of Ib written on papyrus, including their discovery of fire and their use of flame in rituals and ceremonies. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")

Ilek-Vad is a city-state in the Dreamlands. Its location is further than the Moon and it floats in the aether. The people of Ilek-Vad are very happy. They have no real contact with the rest of Dreamlands. They practise magic, use spells and relics of power. The land of Ilek-Vad contains six kingdoms. It is possible to access the city state by the Cerenarian Sea through tunnels. The Race of the Gnorri live in the sea near the Dreamlands city of Ilek-Vad.

entities.name: Olathoë
entities.description:
Olathoë is a fictional extra-dimensional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "Polaris".

Olathoë is a great fortified city of marble in the far northern kingdom of Lomar in the Dreamlands. It lies on the Plateau of Sarkis in a hollow between the mountains Noton and Kadiphonek. Olathoë faces external threats from a horde of ruthless conquerors known as the Inutos that appeared out of the unknown west. The city is also threatened by the gradual encroachment of a great advancing ice sheet that long ago displaced the Zobnarians, the ancestors of the Lomarians. (: "Polaris")

Olathoë's architecture makes extensive use of marble in its construction. The upper parts of the pillars are carved into the images of bearded men, and the public squares where people gather to converse contain many statues. As a city in a high northern latitude region, Olathoë experiences periods of continual daylight and darkness. (: "Polaris")

Olathoë is a repository for the grimoire known as the Pnakotic Manuscripts, as well as books that contain the wisdom of the Zobnarian Fathers. (: "Polaris")

entities.name: Oriab
entities.description:
Oriab is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his novella The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath, depicted as being a large island located in the Southern Sea of the Dreamlands.

Every month the people of Oriab trade "fragrant resin of Oriab’s inner groves, and the delicate pottery baked by the artists of Baharna, and the strange little figures carved from Ngranek’s ancient lava. For this they were paid in the wool of Ulthar and the iridescent textiles of Hatheg and the ivory that the black men carve across the river in Parg".

The Plateau of Sarkis is a plateau in the far northern kingdom of Lomar in the Dreamlands. The plateau is the site of the city of Olathoë, and is situated in a hollow between the mountains Noton and Kadiphonek. (: "Polaris")

entities.name: Pnath
entities.description:
Pnath is a ficitonal region or city briefly mentioned as having been conquered by the city of Sarnath in H. P. Lovecraft's short story "The Doom That Came to Sarnath". On the night of Sarnath's destruction, the king Nargis-Hei and his nobles were in the banquet hall of the royal palace, getting drunk on "ancient wine from the vaults of conquered Pnath".

By the time of Randolph Carter's visits to the Dreamlands, the vale of Pnath is a shunned area inhabited by the mysterious dholes. The floor is covered by half-eaten bones, as the Ghouls of the waking world use Pnath as a dumping ground to cast away "the refuse of their feastings", thrown from the edge of a crag that looms over the vale. Nodens' night-gaunt servants "flop unendingly in the dark betwixt the Vale of Pnath and the passes to the outer world". Any intruders found on Mt. Ngranek are captured by the night-gaunts and taken to the vale of Pnath to be left to their own devices. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

entities.name: River Ai
entities.description:
The River Ai is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The Doom That Came to Sarnath".

The River Ai is a river in the land of Mnar. When tribes of wanderers first arrived in Mnar they built the cities of Thraa, Ilarnek, and Kadatheron along the river. Other tribes, hardier than the rest, pushed farther up the river all the way to the shore of a vast unnamed lake. There they built the city of Sarnath at a place where precious metals were found in the earth. These important natural resources contributed significantly to Sarnath's immense wealth and power. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")

entities.description:
The River Narg is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The White Ship".

The River Narg is a sacred river that flows through the fabled land of Cathuria in the legends of those who live in the Dreamlands. On the green and flowery mountains of Cathuria stand temples of pink marble with silver fountains in their courtyards that flow with the scented and musical waters of the Narg. The river is said to be home to colorful varieties of fish not found outside Cathuria. (: "The White Ship")

entities.name: River Skai
entities.description:
The River Skai is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The Cats of Ulthar".

The River Skai is a river in the Dreamlands that originates on Mount Lerion. It flows through fertile plains, fields, and meadows, beautiful countryside, and peaceful farmland near the towns of Ulthar, Nir, and Hatheg. The river then continues all the way down to the city of Dylath-Leen on the Southern Sea. A smooth trade road used by merchant caravans runs along the river between the aforementioned towns and cities. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

Near Ulthar the river flows past the Enchanted Wood where a village of the zoogs is located in the central part of the forest. A great stone bridge also spans the river at Ulthar. The masons who originally built the bridge sealed a living human sacrifice within the central support thirteen hundred years before Randolph Carter first visited the Dreamlands. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

entities.description:
Rokol is a region or city that presumably was part of the empire of Sarnath. On the thousand year anniversary of Sarnath's conquest of the city of Ib, among the many who attended the celebration were princes of Rokol. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")

entities.name: Sarkomand
entities.description:
Sarkomand is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by H. P. Lovecraft for his novella The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath.

Sarkomand is an ancient, ruined city situated in the northern Dreamlands, in a valley by the Plateau of Leng, above an entrance to the underground Abyss sections of the Dreamlands. It is beside the sea, but the rocks are jagged; human ships do not go there, although Black Galleys sometimes do.

Out in the water is a mountainous granite island, with windowless dwellings and paths carved into the rock, inhabited by Moon-beasts and their slaves. (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

The city was "proud and pillared ... wondrous with high fanes and carven places", filled with pillars of black stone. It was a seaport. In modern times its stones and pillars are broken, and overgrown with weeds and grass.

entities.name: Sona-Nyl
entities.description:
Sona-Nyl, also known as the Land of Fancy, is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The White Ship".

Sona-Nyl is a coastal region in the Dreamlands of Earth. The dreamer Basil Elton lived there for a time before embarking on his doomed sea voyage aboard the White Ship in search of the fabled land of Cathuria. The harbor of Sona-Nyl is guarded by twin headlands of crystal that rise from the sea and meet in a resplendent arch. (: "The White Ship")

According to Elton's description, "in the Land of Sona-Nyl there is neither time nor space, neither suffering nor death, and there I dwelt for many aeons. Green are the groves and pastures, bright and fragrant the flowers, blue and musical the streams, clear and cool the fountains, and stately and gorgeous the temples, castles, and cities of Sona-Nyl. Of that land there is no bound, for beyond each vista of beauty rises another more beautiful. Over the countryside and amidst the splendour of cities rove at will the happy folk, of whom all are gifted with unmarred grace and unalloyed happiness." (: "The White Ship")

Elton continues, "for the aeons that I dwelt there I wandered blissfully through gardens where quaint pagodas peep from pleasing clumps of bushes, and where the white walks are bordered with delicate blossoms. I climbed gentle hills from whose summits I could see entrancing panoramas of loveliness, with steepled towns nestling in verdant valleys, and with the golden domes of gigantic cities glittering on the infinitely distant horizon. And I viewed by moonlight the sparkling sea, the crystal headlands, and the placid harbour wherein lay anchored the White Ship." (: "The White Ship")

entities.name: Teloe
entities.description:
Teloe is a mystical realm located somewhere "beyond the Milky Way and the Arinurian Streams", mentioned in the story "The Crawling Chaos" by H. P. Lovecraft. Teloe is described as a beautiful paradise inhabited by benevolent deities and favored mortals, with cities of amber and chalcedony, ivory bridges, and rivers of liquid gold bearing pleasure barges bound for the realm of Cytharion.

Teloe and Cytharion were part of an apocalyptic vision of the future experienced by the unnamed narrator of the story under the influence of opium, so their literal existence may or may not be taken for granted in the context of the Mythos.

entities.name: Thalarion
entities.description:
Thalarion is a fictional extra-dimensional location created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The White Ship".

Thalarion is a coastal city in the Dreamlands of Earth, also known as the City of a Thousand Wonders, a mighty city surrounded by grey stone walls that hide most of the frieze covered buildings and alluring sculptures. Its temple spires however reach into the sky, far enough for their peaks to be invisible to the naked eye. Within the walls its streets are littered with unburied bones.

A stone pier leads to the huge carven gate of Akariel.

Though many men enter none leave and the streets are home to daemons and mad things that are no longer men.

entities.name: Thraa
entities.description:
Thraa is a city in the land of Mnar on the River Ai in the Dreamlands. It was built by the same wandering tribes that built the Mnaran cities of Ilarnek, Kadatheron, and Sarnath. Sarnath eventually conquered the neighboring cities and lands (including Thraa) and forged an empire. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath")

Pearls from the coastal region of Mtal dissolved in vinegar produced in Thraa were considered a delicacy in Sarnath. (: "The Doom That Came to Sarnath") Category:Structures Category:Locations Originating From Lovecraft Circle Works Category:Extra-Dimensional Locations

entities.name: Ulthar
entities.description:
Ulthar is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "The Cats of Ulthar".

Ulthar is a village in the Dreamlands of Earth. Its people are known for their simplicity, superstitious nature and reverence of cats. In the village it was forbidden for any citizen of the land to harm or kill a cat, after the visit of mysterious dark people who resemble Romani from Earth, albeit overt worshippers of Ancient Egyptian style deities. (: "The Cats of Ulthar")

For those wise enough to not anger the large population of man-eating cats, the cobbled streets of Ulthar seem to be some of the most pleasant in the mythos. Surrounded by suburbs of "little green cottages and neatly fenced farms" the centre of the town is composed of pink buildings, topped with old, peaked, red tiled roofs, overhanging upper stories and numberless chimney-pots". (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

Above the town on the area's highest hill is the modest, ivy-clad stone tower of the Temple of the Elder Ones, home to priests and their ancient records under the watchful eye of patriarch Atal. Randolph Carter visited the temple during his search for Kadath.

entities.name: Unspace
entities.description:
Unspace is an extra-dimensional location in the fictional universe of Transformers by Hasbro and Takara Tomy.

Unspace is a realm of kaleidoscopic madness and anti-matter, a timeless non-space that exists beyond all reality. Cybertronians often use space bridges to travel through unspace as a means of teleportation. Some entities, such as Unicron and other multiversal singularities, can transverse through unspace at will by using avatars.

It is also home to the Elder Gods, a race of ancient evil entities of indescribable power. If someone is unfortunate enough to be stranded in unspace, they will likely suffer a fate far worse than death at the hands of the Elder Gods. (: Hasbro Transformers Collectors' Club issue #5, Ramjet's profile) Despite being trapped in unspace, the Elder Gods were able to influence the minds of sensitive beings in the material universe, including H. P. Lovecraft, who used his horror prose to channel their call. Although the clandestine organisation, Oblivion, killed him before he could summon them, Lovecraft's stories continued to spread throughout popular culture and the Elder Gods eventually broke free to invade the multiverse. (: Infestation 2)

A valley in the far northern kingdom of Lomar in the Dreamlands, the Valley of Banof can be seen at a distance from the Watchtower of Thapnen in the city of Olathoë. (: "Polaris")

entities.description:
The Vaults of Zin is a fictional location created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his fantasy novella The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath.

An enormous cavern complex located in the underworld, the Vaults of Zin lie near the cemetery of the Gugs, which opens onto a large cave which, in the words of its origin story, "is the mouth of the vaults of Zin, and the vindictive Ghasts are always on watch there murderously for those denizens of the upper abyss who hunt and prey on them." (: The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath)

entities.description:
The Watchtower of Thapnen is a fictional structure from H. P. Lovecraft's short story "Polaris".

The Watchtower of Thapnen is a tower in the Lomarian city of Olathoë in the Dreamlands. The purpose of the tower is to guard the narrow pass that comes up from behind Mount Noton, providing a defense against potential invaders that would use the pass to launch a surprise attack against Olathoë. In such a case, a signal fire would be lit at the top of the tower to warn the soldiers and thereby save the city from immediate disaster. (: "Polaris")

entities.name: Xura
entities.description:
Xura is a coastal region in the Dreamlands of Earth, also known as the "Land of Pleasures Unattained", which first appeared in H. P. Lovecraft's short story "The White Ship".

From the sea the lily-lined coastline appears idyllic, with beautiful groves as far as the eye can see from which harmonic singing and snatches of laughter can be heard. However getting closer the wind carries the lethal, charnel odor of plague-stricken towns and uncovered cemeteries.

entities.name: Y'qaa
entities.description:
Grey-litten Y'qaa, a.k.a. the abyss of Y'qaa, or the Cavern of Y'quaa is an underground realm inhabited by the primordial being Ubbo-Sathla, and the current location of the Elder Records. The location first appeared unnamed in Clark Ashton Smith's story "Ubbo-Sathla", while the name was coined by Lin Carter for his Xothic Legend Cycle.

In Carter's "The Descent into the Abyss", the realm of Y'qaa can be reached by the tunnels deep inside Mount Voormithadreth in Hyperborea, which suggests that it might be intended to be the abode of Abhoth, the "Source of Uncleanliness", as featured in Smith's "The Seven Geases". This could be an allusion to the similarity between Ubbo-Sathla and Abhoth, proposed by Gary Myers to be two different names for the same deity.

The alternate spelling Y'quaa is used in the 2020 edition of the Malleus Monstrorum, in which the cavern is associated with both Abhoth and Ubbo-Sathla.

A grey-litten abyss identified as multidimensional, "coterminous with many worlds and planes of existence", including Yarnak. Nevertheless, Y'qaa can be accessed by the interior of Mt. Voormithadreth, past the cavern of the Prototypes. Its entrance is guarded by K'thugguol, the Grand Shoggoth. Ubbo-Sathla dwells there with the Elder Records it stole from the Elder Gods. The legendary power of these tablets has tempted many sorcerers to brave the abyss and try to retrieve them, but none has been successful so far. (: "The Descent into the Abyss")

Yundu is a fictional extra-dimensional world created by games designer Phil Frances for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu gaming supplement H. P. Lovecraft's Dreamlands (1986).

Located somewhere in the depths of space in the plane of existence dubbed the Dreamlands, Yundu is the home planet of the bizarre flying creatures known as Wenelians and, possibly, their flying steeds the Phosphorescent Monsters.

entities.description:
Zakarion is a city in the Dreamlands and a repository for much of the lore pertaining to the lands of dream. This lore was written down by sages who once dwelt there, sages who were "too wise ever to be born in the waking world." (: "Ex Oblivione")

entities.name: Zar
entities.description:
Zar is a fictional coastal region in the Dreamlands of Earth and home to "the dreams and thoughts of beauty that come to men once and then are forgotten".

Its green shore is bright and beautiful with verdant tree-studded terraces rising up from the sea. The temples have gleaming white roofs and colonnades and stand amoungst a beautiful landscape of "forms and fantasies more splendid than any I had ever known; the visions of young poets who died in want before the world could learn of what they had seen and dreamed". However those who go there can never return home.

entities.name: Zobna
entities.description:
Zobna is a fictional location in the Cthulhu Mythos. It was originally created by the late American author H. P. Lovecraft for his short story "Polaris".

Zobna was a far northern kingdom in the Dreamlands that was eventually overwhelmed by the gradual encroachment of a great advancing ice sheet. The Zobnarians were forced to move southward and became the ancestors of the Lomarians. During their southward migration, the Zobnarians "valiantly and victoriously swept aside the hairy, long-armed, cannibal Gnophkehs that stood in their way." The wisdom of the Zobnarian Fathers, as the people of Lomar refer to their ancestors, is preserved in books in the Lomarian city of Olathoë. (: "Polaris")

entities.name: Atlantis
entities.description:
Atlantis is a legendary lost continent, usually supposed to have been located in the North Atlantic Ocean. It was believed to have hosted an ancient civilization that was destroyed and sunk beneath the ocean in a cataclysmic event. The myth of Atlantis was incorporated as a background element by H. P. Lovecraft and other Cthulhu Mythos authors; Robert E. Howard and Clark Ashton Smith, among others, set stories in pre-cataclysm Atlantis.

Though rarely the focus of Lovecraft's stories, Atlantis is mentioned numerous times.

The kingdom of Atlantis thrived for thousands of years. At its prime, it was a mighty empire, with a respected naval fleet. The Atlanteans enslaved ape-like creatures known as Gyaa-Hua and had diplomatic relations with the mother-continent Mu, which turned sour when the Atlantean General Bothon's army besieged the Muvian capital of Alu to abduct the Emperor's niece. (: "Bothon")

Alien gods were worshiped in Atlantis (: "The Last Test") and there are rumours that the cult of Ghatanothoa was present in it. (: "Out of the Aeons")

entities.name: Irem
entities.description:
Irem, or Irim, is a legendary city mentioned multiple times in the Cthulhu Mythos stories of H. P. Lovecraft, Robert Bloch, and August Derleth.

It was the City of Pillars visited by the Mad Arab in the deserts of Arabia.

Irem is first mentioned by Lovecraft in "The Nameless City", in which the narrator finds evidence of a sapient reptile species that flourished before mankind and built a city in the Arabian desert. One of the images in their murals depicts a human being torn to pieces by the reptiles. The narrator muses that the man in the picture might have been "a pioneer of ancient Irem, the City of Pillars", thus implying that the reptile inhabitants of the Nameless City might have been enemies of the human inhabitants of Irem.

Abdul Alhazred, the 8th century author of the Necronomicon who worshiped Yog-Sothoth and Cthulhu, claimed to have seen Irem, the City of Pillars, "and to have found beneath the ruins of a certain nameless desert town the shocking annals and secrets of a race older than mankind". (: "History of the Necronomicon")

entities.name: Mount Semura
entities.description:
Mount Semura has historically been part of Tibetan cosmology, a mythical mountain which was often identified with Mount Kailash in western Tibet. The Mount Semura of the Cthulhu Mythos was created by Chaosium for the Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game in 2005.

Mount Semura is a mystical mountain which is located within the Tibetan Himalayas. It is a vast floating mountain that is invisible to the human eye. Those who are deemed worthy can ascend to the base of the mountain via a set of transparent stairs. The mountain itself is a paradise of quiet green gardens and perfect weather. A great Tibetan-style temple sits at the top, its spire reaching so high that those in the surrounding areas often mistake it for the North Star. It is a place of esoteric knowledge, with its lamas and millennia-old beings spreading their knowledge to the world via their messengers.

entities.name: Thule
entities.description:
Thule is a legendary land described in Classical Greek literature as being to the far north of Europe. The name was applied to ancient lands in the fiction of Lovecraft Circle writers Robert E. Howard and Clark Ashton Smith, and its role in the Cthulhu Mythos was systematised in the tales of Lin Carter.

Thule was first mentioned by Pytheas, the first documented representative of the Mediterranean world to visit the British Isles. Pytheas' writings do not survive, but he is cited by Strabo as describing Thoulē as an island six days' sail from Britain, near the frozen sea.

The Roman poet Virgil refers in his Georgics to Ultima Thule--"farthest Thule"--which became an expression for any place beyond the known world.

In Smith's "The Double Shadow," a short story published in 1933 and set in the Atlantean remnant of Poseidonis, the narrator Pharpetron wishes that his master, the sorceror Avyctes, "had contented himself with the lore preserved from Atlantis and Thule, or brought over from Mu and Mayapan." He notes that "this should have been enough: for in the ivory-sheeted books of Thule there were blood-writ runes that would call the demons of the fifth and seventh planets, if spoken aloud at the hour of their ascent."

entities.name: Aldebaran
entities.description:
Aldebaran is one of the brightest objects in the night sky, a giant red star about 65 light-years away from our Solar System. Seen from Earth, it appears to be part of the Hyades, although it is in fact much closer. It was used by Robert W. Chambers in his work The King in Yellow.

August Derleth identifies it as the "place where the dark stars hang", the abode of Hastur (: "The Return of Hastur").

Aldebaran appears in the short story "Polaris" by H. P. Lovecraft. The unnamed narrator observed Aldebaran from the city of Olathoë in the Arctic region of Lomar in the Dreamlands. The red star never set but crawled low around the horizon during the extended polar night.

Aldebaran is visible in the sky above Kingsport during the events of "The Festival" by H. P. Lovecraft, making the narrator shiver as the star seems to balance itself on the spire of the church. The Byakhee, which debuted in that story, are revealed to be servants of Hastur in Derleth's The Trail of Cthulhu.
